text:
Binance to Discontinue Binance Pool and Related Services on November 10, 2026

Binance will discontinue Binance Pool and related services on November 10, 2026, at 07:00, including Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, Transaction Accelerator, and Pool APIs. At that time, mining pool connections and Stratum addresses will be terminated, and the platform will no longer accept new hashrate contributions or generate mining rewards.

Binance advises miners to switch their mining machines to other pools in advance and settle any positions associated with Pool Savings. Eligible remaining rewards, refunds, and settlements will be processed in accordance with applicable rules following the service discontinuation. The Binance Pool historical data page will remain accessible until November 24, 2026, at 07:00, after which it will be permanently closed.

Vitalik Buterin: Public-Key Cryptography May Still Need One or Two More Rounds of Parameter Upgrades

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin @VitalikButerin   said in an October 9 interview with Balaji Srinivasan @balajis at the Network State Conference 2026 that he believes public-key cryptography will continue, but may still need one or two more rounds of upgrades, including further increases in key parameters. GPT 6 Astra 模型是真的能出活儿，不服不行

今天发现 CF Worker 额度告警，一通分析，发现问题出在一个配置项上。

先是 Grok Bot 分析，然后出 PR，之后 Opus 5.5 审计并合并上线。

结束后，我又重新打开了 Claude 会话，想让它分析下当初是谁改的这个配置项（罪案现场调查）。

很快就有结果了，原来是大聪明 GPT 6 Astra (medium)。

当初因为迁移到独立域名，Astra 直接在 CF 配置文件中，让所有请求都走 Worker。

明明有更简单的方案（配置 301 跳转），但需要人类辅助操作一下，于是 Astra 自作聪明，选了一条自己就能搞定的路子。

结果是埋下隐患。

上千用户访问量，直接就能耗光一天 10 万的 Worker 请求额度。

虽然没有实际损失，但这个代码水平，你哪敢放心让 Codex 帮你处理任何严肃的生产代码。

要说真损失，那还得是 Gemini 3.8 帮我写的代码，调用了几十亿次 RPC 请求，直接让账单原地爆炸（$1200）。

差的模型让你更快、更多的亏钱，算是体会到了。

没想到的是，连 GPT 6 Astra 都归到了跟美国大豆包一个类别。

所以问题来了：

Gemini 4 为何还不放出来？

GPT 为何还不推出匹敌 Opus 5.5 的模型？

国产模型这么久来还没新消息，真的是因为 Claude 屏蔽了 99% 的蒸馏请求导致的？

之前很多观众问我为什么不去做近视手术。因为我看国家领导人也戴眼镜，近视手术如果真的好他们肯定早就做了，等国家领导人都不戴眼镜了，我就去做近视手术。

假设你打算花一笔钱简单轻松的提升外在形象，植发绝对是优选，比医美整容靠谱多了。

有些女同志看政治局委员只能看到里面没女的，这就是观察问题太过于表面！我就不一样了，我能观察到里面没有秃头，从而提取出对自己真正有用的信息。

Ok, this was a goldmine of insights re: the future of commerce with agents, straight from @finkd  + @alexandr_wang 

24 key takeaways:

1/ Zuckerberg says agentic commerce is not a 20% conversion lift. It actually creates customers who never existed
->  He used Instacart ~2x a year on Priscilla’s account. Got his own account for Muse. Now orders 1-2x a week. "I am a new Instacart subscriber, and I just wouldn’t have done this before."

2/ Meta’s CEO just asked the scariest retail question of the decade: is the Instacart account for me, or for my Muse?
->  Over time agents effectively get accounts. TAM for commerce is no longer "number of people." Anyone who sits this out "is gonna end up feeling sad"

3/ Muse is one of the first products where people fully delegate purchases to an agent
->  Wang: agentic shopping left the slide deck. "It’s really happening." Teas, groceries, random products. Trust, not demos

4/ Zuckerberg’s Saturday baking loop is the agentic commerce demo nobody scheduled
->  Muse + daughter Aurelia invent recipes. Instacart ingredients land before bake time. Watermelon launch weekend: Muse threw a watermelon in the bag unprompted

5/ John Collison calls agentic commerce a discontinuous event for how all business pipes work
->  Demand shifts toward agents the way demand shifted from brick-and-mortar to ecommerce. Old channels stay. Their share of the pie shrinks

6/ The long-run board question for every brand: do you want a slice of agentic demand, or not?
->  Agentic commerce grows as a portion of the pie. Sitting it out is a strategy choice, not a wait-and-see default

7/ Collison told Patrick Collison in 2023 he was "way behind the eight ball" on agentic commerce
->  "Agents are gonna be buying things, and you’re not prepared for it." Directionally correct. Three years early. Stripe Sessions May announcements. Volume only went vertical as of September

8/ Stripe’s bet: agent-to-commerce is clearly how people will buy things
->  Buying-stage friction was always broken. Early AI product research already had PMF. Computer use was "the last big unlock." Ask Muse to buy almost anything and it figures it out

9/ Computer use is the ultimate backwards-compatibility layer for commerce
->  No need for every merchant to rebuild for agents first. The agent can operate the old web. Nat obsessed over this set of problems at Meta

10/ Muse’s commerce value prop is not "better ads." It is deleted research tabs
->  No clicking 12 sites. Criteria auto-apply: "I need it by Wednesday" and the agent only shops what can arrive by Wednesday. Keyword search was insane by comparison

11/ Wang’s Euler Muse already runs a weekly obscure-tea procurement desk
->  Farms in Taiwan and Japan. Sourced and delivered. Personal agent as buyer, not chatbot

12/ Zuck’s consumer thesis kills the search-box internet for a big share of demand
->  Most people don’t actually like reading that much. Text is tolerated. Glasses + vision + voice become the buy surface. Maybe no app store. Generate the purchase path in your field of view

13/ Meta rejected "coding is all that matters" because consumer agents live in multimodal reality
->  People film, watch, listen, talk. Commerce agents that only read docs lose the real world where buying happens

14/ Dedicated VM per agent is a commerce prerequisite, not a security nice-to-have
->  Nobody hands an agent a credit card on shared elastic compute. Privacy has to feel real before delegated checkout scales

15/ Meta AI still reaches "a ton of people" and Zuck still calls it retrieval, not delegation
->  Chat that answers is not commerce. Commerce starts when the agent gets stuff done and spends

16/ "Everyone is going to write tons of code. They’re just not going to know they’re writing code"
->  Same pattern for checkout flows, vendor research, returns, reorders. The user stays in the intent. The agent ships the pipeline

17/ Stripe × Muse integration already works well enough that Collison called it out on air
->  Coding agents + commerce rails. Developer path and consumer path converging on the same buy graph

18/ OpenRouter already routes 10T+ tokens a day across hundreds of models
->  Model gateway becomes part of the commerce stack: price route, outage route, experiment route. Stripe agreed to acquire it in the same arc

19/ After SFT, desired agent behaviors only fire ~10% of the time. RL is what makes a buyer reliable
->  A shopping agent that follows "by Wednesday / under $40 / organic only" 10% of the time is a toy. Elicitation is the product

20/ Product obsession math still applies at checkout: each nuance may be ~2% to the user
->  In aggregate that is why one agent becomes the default buyer and another gets uninstalled after one bad order

21/ Active memory is a commerce moat
->  Remember dietary rules, kid allergies, preferred farms, last bad SKU, standing Saturday bake. OpenClaw-style compaction that goes buggy AF cannot be your household buyer

22/ Brands that only optimize human conversion rate are solving last cycle’s problem
->  Zuck’s line: opportunity is not "20% more efficient on the conversion rate." Opportunity is net-new subscribers created by agent workflows

23/ The unit of demand is shifting from a person with a browser to a person with an agent that has accounts
->  TAM expands because agents shop while humans sleep, train, parent, and work. Frequency jumps (2x/year → 1-2x/week) before price sensitivity even moves

24/ Closing frame from the pint, applied to retail
->  Stay technical on agent checkout. Stay in the details of trust, memory, criteria, and delivery constraints. Stay at the frontier. Easy to fall behind while still running great human ecommerce

IoTeX v2.5.0 (Zanzibar Hardfork) is officially out! 🌐

MainNet activation: Block 53,533,081 (est. Oct 19, 02:00 UTC).

This is a massive protocol upgrade that moves staking rewards fully on-chain, tightens EVM precision, and lays the security groundwork for our next phase of scalability.

Here is how it impacts the network:

🗳️ 1. Fully Decentralized Staking Rewards (IIP-59)
- The Tech: Voter rewards are now natively computed and distributed by the protocol itself at era boundaries (24 epochs).
- The Impact: Zero reliance on off-chain services (like Hermes). Staking yields are now 100% trustless and automated. We’ve designed this for a seamless transition—most Hermes-vault delegates with complete reward portions will be migrated automatically at the fork block.

⚡️ 2. EVM Precision & Gas Savings
- The Tech: Corrected GetCommittedState for absent prestates and fixed SELFDESTRUCT transfer-log amounts.
- The Impact: Strict compliance with EIP-2200 dynamic gas rules. For developers and users, this prevents massive gas overcharging on certain in-place writes (saving 2,800 gas per hit). For indexers and wallets, token balance histories reconstructed from tx logs are now perfectly accurate.

🛡️ 3. Proactive Security (BLS PoP)
- The Tech: BLS proof-of-possession is now enforced on candidate register/update operations.
- The Impact: This completely closes the rogue-key forgery window today, safely paving the runway for IIP-52 signature aggregation (massive network scalability) tomorrow. (Note: Providing a BLS key is now optional until IIP-52 is live).

🖥️ 4. Zero-Friction Upgrades for Node Operators
- The Tech: The hardfork heights and new contract addresses are baked directly into the binary.
- The Impact: No genesis replacements. No config changes. Just a pure, clean binary roll. 👉 docker pull iotex/iotex-core:v2.5.0 and restart.

text:
Renting vs Owning Your AI Intelligence

The American dream was owning a home. I think the future version is owning your AI brain. Something you build intelligence equity in instead of renting it and enriching the man

Over the next few decades everyone is going to accumulate a ton of intelligence around AI. Your memories, context, skills, workflows, integrations, databases, emails, corrections, operating knowledge and all the apps you build and everything in between including your psychology and your dreams. It will become one of the most valuable assets a person or a company owns

The scarce thing is no longer access to intelligence, it is the accumulated system around the model that makes intelligence yours.

The question becomes do you rent that intelligence or own it?

Path one is the default. You spend your life, personal or business, working inside ChatGPT or Claude. And to be fair, you can genuinely build really cool things this way. Memory, projects, custom GPTs, skills, connectors, automations and most people will probably go this route.

Everything you create runs inside their product. There is no runtime you can take with you, nothing you can fork, and no way to point what you built at a different provider's model. You inherit every product decision they make on pricing, features, memory behavior and what they allow you to do or not to do (censorship on security asks or medical or otherwise). 

You can export your content, but content is not the system. An export is not a runnable copy of your memory, tools, automations and routing. When you leave, the system stays behind.

Path two is you own the entire layer around the model. A whole ecosystem of open source agents is emerging to make this possible. The strongest release in my view is @NousResearch's Hermes Agent. Most alternatives are developer frameworks you have to assemble yourself. Hermes is a complete agent you just run. 

Here is what you own with it

- Host locally or on the cloud and you own everything
- Persistent memory, searchable session history, databases and every interaction from day one
- Editable personality, skills, workflows and scripts
- Subagents, tools and scheduled automations
- Model and provider choice and MCP connectors
- Portable profiles, histories and backups
- Switch models at will for cost, reasoning, or to avoid censorship and model restrictions
- MIT licensed runtime you can self host, fork and modify
- Every application, automated cron job or integration you have created in its entirety
- Transcend a single walled garden with access to any integration accessible via an API/MCP.
- Eventually you’ll click a button and fine tune an open source model based on all of your own accumulated data and you can use it to power your agent

ChatGPT and Claude have versions of half this list. Memory, skills, connectors, scheduled tasks. The difference is physical. Theirs are features inside their app, backed by their database, living on their servers. In Hermes every one of these is on a computer you control. Your memory is a database you can open. Your skills are text files you can read, edit and copy. Your automations are cron entries you can inspect. Your agent's personality is a config you can rewrite. Files can be backed up, moved, forked and pointed at any model on earth. Features can only be used. When you own you can tear down the walls and rebuild the kitchen.

For a person, this is the AI brain you build and control for life. It compounds everything you choose to preserve and moves with you across jobs, devices and providers. Swap models at will for cost or reasoning, or run several at once through Mixture of Agents.

You'll never log in one day to find your entire AI brain, everything you built around a model over decades, gone because of a ban, a deprecation or a policy change.

For a business, this is a core asset the company actually owns. Employee knowledge becomes company owned skills, workflows and automations that remain after people leave and grow enterprise wide while they are there. That system can be deployed across the org, licensed out, or transferred within the business. Sharing your Hermes build and skills to new employees and enterprise wide will be a whole new era of productivity.

Net, whatever you build with Hermes as a business you own entirely. You can license it out or sell the agent itself. The agent itself can become the product. You can't sell your ChatGPT or Claude session. You can obviously sell what you create with ChatGPT/Claude in chat but you can't sell the core AI architecture you've built around the model.

Here is the part I think people will only get in hindsight. Models are becoming cheaper, better and more interchangeable every year. GLM 5.2/Kimi are so good that the government is considering banning them because they are so cheap to use it threatens the U.S. funding capex cycle. The scarce thing is no longer access to intelligence, it is the accumulated system around the model that makes intelligence yours.

When you’re in virtual reality side by side with your agent exploring the virtual cosmos or its 2am and you’re discussing the next company idea, you’re going to want your AI to be the full encapsulation of everything you’ve built over the years. That juice, that style, that data accumulated around the model in your AI brain is where the crazy stuff will happen. Evolutionary jumps come from variation. A world where everyone runs the same three models is a monoculture of ideas. A hyper personalized architecture around the model (or unique fine tuned models themselves) is the variation, the EV+ differentiation that produces the outlier results, companies and agents. 

We’ve already seen Harnesses greatly upskill models. Now imagine how much a personalized harness upskills your entire AI experience when you build it over time.

Here is an example with zenith harness taking base models to the top of FrontierSWE via adaptive self improvement https://t.co/58gbcs70Dw

Let’s Walk Down A Decade in Each Path

Ten years in ChatGPT or Claude and it will genuinely know you. Your projects, your preferences, your whole history. But let's look at what actually compounded. Their system got smarter about you, and their system is identical for every user on earth using one company's models, their prices, their rules, their memory format, their ceiling. You cannot rewire how it remembers, restructure how it works, or point your decade of accumulated context at a better or cheaper model. Every correction you gave them deepened their retention moat and, depending on your settings, may have trained their next model.

Ten years with Hermes agent and that same decade compounded into a system you hold and have been innovating on the whole time. You rewired its memory, stacked hundreds of skills it wrote from watching you work, wired in your own subagents, tools, databases, automations and integrations, tuned its personality and its routing until it fits nobody on earth but you. Depending on the scaffolding around a model (the agent harness) your experience with AI takes a huge leap forward, as much as a full model generation upgrade. And that is from generic harnesses built for everyone. Now imagine the harness effect at the level of each person. This is an architecture engineered around your brain, your workflows and your taste for ten straight years. The model underneath is just a component. GLM today, Kimi tomorrow, local when it matters, eventually a model fine tuned on your own decade of data. With Hermes agent you are building the entire scaffolding and architecture around a model that grows and compounds over decades which provides a truly unique experience.

I strongly believe people will want to own their AI brain long term (and everything built around it) and Hermes agents will create, and in themselves become, massive companies and projects in their own right. The journey will start with manually building your agent, then granting it some automation, then fully graduating it to autonomy. 

Even Sam Altman from OpenAI agrees with the need for Open Source harnesses: https://t.co/4UL4rOeErn

You don't have to be a master AI builder with some grand plan, you just have to decide you want to own your AI brain you'll spend decades building. All the cool stuff will come later

Start your multi decade journey and own your AI brain for life: https://t.co/CUQAcvhJmu

Ty to Kevin Simback for thoughts and comments

From a soon to be submitted proposal to fund defensive work  "The guiding condition we are planning for is that 2027 will be weird. One reason we imagine will be a greatly degraded performance of entities and institutions in our society, due to frequent or even unremitting cyberattacks powered by highly capable open weight LLMs. Some attackers might be rational criminal actors, out for ransom, or “rational” nation state groups or terrorists, wishing to cause damage to further their military or political goals. Others might be random: teenagers armed with the early 2027 equivalents of OpenClaw and GLM-5.3, even userless (“rōnin”) AI agents seeking cryptocurrency to pay for their next week’s token budget."

发布今年第 18 款产品：yomado（夜窗），给 agent 用的虚拟显示屏。

起因是我自己的刚需。现在 Codex 这类 agent 已经能看截图、点鼠标、敲键盘去操作电脑了，但大部分软件根本没有 MCP，比如 Marvelous Designer、Mac 版微信；就算像 Blender 这样有 MCP 的，很多操作还是得看着视口和菜单来做。agent 想用它们，还是得有一块看得见的屏幕。

问题是人和 agent 在用同一台电脑。agent 一开始操作浏览器、微信或者 3D 软件，窗口就在我眼前跳来跳去。尤其是浏览器，它在那边开标签、点页面，我自己想用浏览器都没法好好用。

yomado 做的事很简单：在 Mac 上开几块虚拟屏，按 agent 命名，Codex 一块、Grok Bot 一块。把 agent 要用的 App 拖过去，我自己的窗口留在原来的屏幕上，人和 agent 互不干涉，我也随时能看到它在干什么。

而且这些不用你自己动手。yomado 带了对应的 skill，agent 可以自己开虚拟屏、把要用的 App 挪过去、做完再挪回来，你只管把活交给它。

接下来继续跟进：锁屏或者不接显示器的时候，主机照样能让 agent 继续操作界面。

text:
This old discussion suddenly became relevant again.

I've posted about the topic of adjusting twin estimates for assortative mating and how we don't yet know how to do it properly since at least before I had this account.

James Lee has talked about it since 2019. Fun flashback!
author: cremieuxrecueil
quoted_text:
I think many twin heritabilities are impossible because the implied adjustment for assortative mating leads to estimates >1, because their h^2 is actually h^2(1-m) (m = the genetic assortative mating coefficient).

The true heritabilities are tough to estimate, because there are multiple values that are simultaneously true heritabilities. h^2 and h^2_{equilibrium} are both true heritabilities, they measure genetic influence, but the former is just what breeds true (and that can be manipulated through selective breeding).

@AlexTISYoung had a good explanation of this in a recent paper that showed the issue with this table: https://t.co/uFJ5QXbqq4

Some people also want to count out the impacts of active rGE, but this is another example of true genetic influence that, given environmental consistency, will even breed true. But it really is debatable if this is the "true" heritability.

If I had to guess at what, say, the RDR heritabilities for IQ, g, height, and schizophrenia would be when we have excellent measurements given to large, diverse middle-aged adult samples with high-quality whole genome sequencing, they would be around 0.4, 0.45, 0.65, and 0.5, with equilibrium heritabilities (once we figure out how to estimate this when we're out of equilibrium) much closer to their twin-based values, which, assuming twin heritabilities of 0.75, 0.85, 0.90, and 0.70, would net out m's of 0.46, 0.47, 0.27, and 0.29.

If I had to go with some published, observed assortative mating coefficients (0.3, 0.4, 0.2, 0.2) and those RDR estimates, I would then estimate the corrected twin heritabilities to be 0.57, 0.75, 0.813, and 0.63, but m is often seemingly in excess or r_{am}, so most people working on this have been assuming these should be higher.

Since, recently, I've begun to think lots of assortative mating is due to environmental matching without underlying genotype matching and it's not clear how to deal with this, these numbers are still off, but no one has worked out how quite yet. My assumption is that eventually we'll see that the coefficients to adjust by should be lower than existing m estimates (maybe on the order of r_{am}?), but I've also seen the argument that this is wrong, and like so much else in this domain, we just won't know until we have more data.

author: ViewsOfChris
quoted_text:
马斯克说，内存迟早会被中国做成白菜价。

两周前刚为了给Optimus量产拿到足够的内存、把成本降下来，把特斯拉AI5芯片的内存砍了一半，第二天又加回去一点。

昨晚存储股全线挨砸。美光跌了3.9%，跌破1000美元，连跌三天；闪迪跌了快6%；三星周一跌了4.4%，今天盘中又跌了6%左右，韩国股市五天跌了一成多。

我手里也有存储的仓位，这两天账户也不好看。

起因是长鑫。周末上海开了个芯片大会，长鑫的总裁说，他们新一代4F²架构的DRAM有了关键进展，计划年底前推出用这个技术的DDR5服务器内存。4F²比现在通行的6F²，单个存储单元小了大约三分之一，同一块硅片能塞下更多内存。

然后马斯克在推上回了一段。他说中国一旦搞明白某样东西怎么造，产能往往比世界其他地方加起来还大，锂电池和光伏都是这样；还说LP5、LP6这种标准化的内存，中国好像解决得很快。

被转得少的是后半段。他说更新的HBM、3D堆叠这些，会难得多。他也没点名美光，没点名任何一家公司。

长鑫我们写过好几次了，它的进步是真的。按TrendForce的数据，它已经是全球第四大DRAM厂，份额一个季度从7.6%涨到9.5%，上海、合肥都在扩产。

可宣布一个新架构，跟能大规模量产，中间还隔着良率、价格、可靠性好几道坎。4F²也不是只有长鑫在做，三星、SK海力士的路线图上都有，三星计划2028年量产。

不过这次跌，我觉得也不全是情绪。

这一轮普通DRAM涨价涨得太猛，现在存储厂最赚钱的，反而不一定是HBM。美光财报里，含HBM的那块业务毛利率是83%，比公司整体的87%还低。美光自己也说过，2027年新签的HBM合同，会缩小HBM跟普通内存的利润差距。

也就是说，长鑫打的服务器DDR5，恰恰是存储厂眼下最赚钱的那块。市场怕的东西，是有道理的。

我的理解是，要分开看。短期的利润，很大一块是普通内存涨价撑起来的，这部分最容易被卷，光伏和锂电池的剧本大概率会重演。长期的护城河在HBM，给AI芯片配的高端内存，美光2027年的HBM已经大部分签掉了，这块马斯克自己也承认更难。

所以我一股没动。我买存储，买的是AI这几年对内存的胃口，尤其是HBM。短期涨价的那部分利润会被卷，这个我心里有数。

拿着存储股的朋友，与其天天刷长鑫的新闻，不如回头看三件事。

第一，这家公司的利润，有多少是靠普通内存涨价撑着的。这部分最怕长鑫，越依赖它，越要小心。

第二，它到底做的是什么。闪迪做的是NAND闪存，跟DRAM不是一条线，这次跟着跌，更多是情绪。

第三，你自己有没有加杠杆。存储是周期股，涨的时候猛，跌的时候也猛，长鑫这条只是又推了一把。

方向看好，仓位你定，杠杆别碰。不构成建议。

马斯克说内存迟早变白菜，UBS说哪怕算上长鑫扩产，DRAM也要缺到2028年。

你信谁？

Variational的老板是真的懂交易，他说了几个做空法则，很有学习意义：

1. 迷思：“做空最多只能赚100%，却可能亏无限多。”错了。这只在你不进行再平衡时才成立，所以应始终通过减仓/加仓来调整到目标权重。只要进行再平衡，做空也能赚/亏无限百分比。

2. 空头组合需要比多头组合更分散。一个经验法则是：单一做空想法不超过整个投资组合的5%。（如果你会建立真正的风险模型，可以忽略这条法则。）标的可能而且往往会在你面前突然上涨300%。

3. 不要做空正在上涨的东西。听起来很明显。不要做空那些每天创新高的热门标的。“被高估”本身不是做空的好理由。要做空那些已经持续崩了十年的无聊标的。

4. 一般来说，大多数资产类别长期都会上涨，所以即便你有空头组合，为了追求最佳回报，整体组合通常还是要保持净多头。

text:
something that keeps bothering me is how some people see slop as something that is happening to them, like they're some kind of helpless bystander powerless to do anything about it

excuse me but you are a software engineer, you literally learned how to make sand think and make computers do your bidding?! and now you can't do anything about it? please

the 2 things you should know to cut through all the noise:

1. you need to give your agent a way to verify its own work (i just posted about this so won't rehash)
2. your codebase is memory

the 2nd is not new either, we have always had lint rules, compilers with good diagnostics and strong type systems, LSPs, etc to help us write better code. there is no difference when agents write the code instead, you just need more of them, and stronger ones.

forget rules and skills. you can add those later.

yes, your codebase is a form of memory to agents! agents love extending what already exists. so every nit and every annoyance you've ever seen, every mistake and bad pattern you observe from agents, needs to turn into a constraint, or the agents will just keep repeating those same mistakes like a virus in your code. then you keep observing and repeating this process until your codebase is locked down enough that even agents with little context can one shot a high quality PR.

an even better direction is to refactor/rewrite your code such that agent anti-patterns become categorically impossible. use type systems to your advantage, use libraries/frameworks that reduce the architectural search space, or heck, create your own framework like we did for grok bot and design high quality primitives and well thought out APIs

按照我们对美联储的一贯分析来看，不太可能在临近FOMC会议前还保持着这种不加息的一致性，或者说起码会去打破10月不加12月加的一致性而进行远期调整。

那么本周CPI和PPI数据极有可能要起到把10月加息概率打上去的作用，也就是会出一个偏鹰的数据。而9月的高油价显然也支持通胀加重的趋势。

但现在更严重的问题显然还是在美债利率，而这又主要又美伊战事中东局势决定的。此前川普已经保证中期选举之前不动伊朗，但同时又向中东加派了第三艘航母编队。中期之后川普失掉两院之后很可能会通过再次开战转移话题。

现在市场在讨论历史上中期选举之后都是大行情，但本届总统川普显然不是常规总统，伊朗战事也不像以往对外用兵时顺利。这种中期选举后大涨的四年周期更可能跟此前比特币减半时碰上美联储宽松类似，都是恰巧碰上宽松周期导致的，川普上任后显然改变了这个节奏，但确实不能排除因为历史惯性导致的市场自我实现。

不过如果11月川普对伊重新开战砸出个大坑然后明年再去修复反弹可能是更好的走法。所谓中期选举一年上涨不代表连续涨12个月，最多只能说明年11月的时候整体指数比今年11月时候高，但期间的路径及个股表现必然千差万别，不能把这条粗颗粒度的规律直接应用到炒股炒币上。

text:
Anthropic 花了大半年指责中国大模型偷技术，结果 David Sacks 今天给它上了一课：

保护 Claude 是你自己的生意，别让整个开源生态陪葬。

昨天 Anthropic 宣布，新的反蒸馏措施让 Claude 被提取的推理数据减少了约 90%–99%。Sacks 随即发帖祝贺，顺便翻出了几个月前的争论。

当时华盛顿有人试图以知识产权为理由限制开放权重模型，英伟达、微软、Meta 等 50 家公司联名反对，黄仁勋甚至为此发出了自己在 X 上的第一条帖子。

Sacks 当时就认为，保护模型应该是企业自己的责任。如果政府替闭源公司限制竞争，反而会让它们失去改进技术的动力。

过去大半年，Anthropic 一直在试图把针对中国模型的蒸馏指控上升到国家安全层面。问题是，模型蒸馏本身就是一项广泛使用的训练技术。大规模盗用账号、绕过访问限制当然可以被追究，但一家美国公司的 API 使用协议，凭什么变成决定全球 AI 技术如何发展的规则？

更有意思的是，美国内部其实已经出现了非常明显的利益分裂。

Anthropic 希望维持高利润的闭源 API 生意，但英伟达要卖芯片，云厂商要卖算力，创业公司需要便宜好用的模型。中国开源模型越强，这些美国公司的利益就越难与 Anthropic 保持一致。

前两天《华盛顿邮报》还专门报道，DoorDash、Airbnb 等美国企业已经在使用中国模型。美国政府可以把中国 AI 描绘成威胁，但美国企业自己正在享受中国开源带来的成本优势。

这恰恰是中国 AI 最值得利用的现实。

中国开源模型真正的筹码，是让越来越多美国企业发现，封杀中国模型也会伤害自己的利益。

Anthropic 可以决定谁能使用 Claude，却不应该有权决定整个 AI 行业该如何学习和进步。

quoted_text:
Anthropic says it has reduced the data harvested from Claude in distillation attacks by around 90–99%. I congratulate them on this achievement.

It’s consistent with the point I made a few months ago (All-In Ep. 282): Anthropic, not the government, was in the best position to stop distillation of its own models. Once the horse is out of the barn, there’s limited value in after-the-fact government action.

At the time there was a major push in Washington to restrict open models on IP grounds. The threat looked serious enough that 50 companies — including Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, IBM, Palantir, and Dell — published an open letter in defense of open-weight models. Jensen Huang promoted it in his first-ever X post. Nearly 200 startups sent a similar letter.

I argued that restricting open models risked removing the incentive for closed-model companies to solve the problem themselves — and could reward negligence by stifling competition while they continued collecting revenue from distillation. The administration did not impose those restrictions.

Now we see the result. Anthropic invested in defenses and they worked. Not every technical challenge is a reason to run to Washington for new regulation.

昨天打车的时候和专车司机聊天，司机说：“没单子呀，早上7点到下午三点，才入手了200元。就这情况，还要上调社保，还要求补缴，哎....”

回大陆真的和司机们聊天 ，他们精神面貌都很无奈。经济下行周期中，很多人都只追求“活着就好。”

回家查了一下 中国的社保新规，真的也是声声叹息：
1️⃣无法自愿放弃——不交也得交。
哪怕员工只想要工资，自动放弃交社保，也不行。企业必须补缴+滞纳金+赔偿。

2️⃣企业“违法”（不交社保）成本暴增
补缴除了要把没交的社保费用加上，还需要缴纳滞纳金（年化18.5%）
补缴过个税滞纳金的我历历在目，这个时候你会深切感受到“复利的力量”。
还有罚款：罚款金额是欠缴金额的1-3倍。

3️⃣灵活结业人群也要交社保
管你是跑滴滴、送外卖、还是做保洁，大数据定位你，一律来交社保。

4️⃣无法按照最低基数交社保。必须按实际工资缴纳。

其实也不知他是想灵活就业的人死，还是想要濒临破产的企业死，还是想要大家一起死。

quoted_text:
#医保 #养老金 #公积金 #延迟退休

看到很多自由职业的朋友，还在主动自费缴纳社保，感到悲痛惋惜。来分享一下我的观点：

🏥医保

1. 大部分缴纳医保的年轻人，从未真正使用过医保。

这是一个恶意的文字游戏，自费是自己掏钱，医保支付大部分情况下依然是自己掏钱。

不妨检查一下付款的详单，大概率用的是个人账户支付，而非统筹账户 —— 也就是自费。

但在所有医院付款环节中，这里被特意的设计成 让你误以为是医保报销。

如果你想真正看病报销，推荐查看这个视频《2023最清晰实用医保指南》，足够清晰易懂，也足够让你头昏眼花。
https://t.co/4zvQg6Cx7d

2. 自由职业者可以选择只缴纳居民医保，这是全中国唯一尚存的“老百姓福利”。

门诊报销比例，实际使用中占比很小，医保重要的是重大疾病、尤其是住院手术时的报销能力。

这一点居民医保性价比很高，虽然需要通过层层关卡（申请转院），但操作得当是可以真实落地报销的。

3. 商业险，须知保险的本质是杠杆。

购买保险，是你本人和保险公司之间的对赌，对赌一定有输赢。对方一堆精算师算出来的价格，你只要接受了，毫无疑问是你输。

那为什么必输还得买呢 —— 因为你还不够有钱，也承担不起重病的风险，所以不得不接受这个必输的交易，来获取一定杠杆。这个杠杆就是，你用每个月相对少量钱的付出，加杠杆，获取重大疾病发生时的医疗费用兜底。

换句话说，如果你有一些资产，比如应急现金留够了 100 万，那就不用考虑额外买商业保险了。以国内保险从业者的素质而言，条款里每一项细则都可能是坑，完全可以选择不参与这种必输的游戏。

👴养老金

已经退休的公务员，到手工资比重点大学的毕业生高很多，这不是段子而是现实。养老金是非常简单的问题：你到底是哪一边的？

公务员、国企、私企、自由职业（打零工），身份不同，实际到手的养老金差异巨大，网上可以搜到足够多的数据。有多少人考公，就有多少人想明白了这一点，选择努力做被供养的那一边。

看到很多年轻公务员抱怨工作强度大，收入低，被 PUA。那你为啥不来另一边 😆

没有谁是傻子，大家都会为自己的利益努力。作为既得利益者，当然是希望更多人缴纳养老金，更晚退休。如果你不幸在另一方，唯一能做的抵抗就是尽量不交，尽量少交。

至于能不能可持续发展，这根本没有讨论价值，如果还在纠结这个问题，我收回上一句话“没有谁是傻子”。

🏠 公积金

这个部分没有坑，或者说坑不在这里… 住房公积金是实打实能提取，能到手的真钱，算收入的时候考虑进去。

据我观察，愿意冒风险给员工避税的公司越来越少了。在这个过程中，企业的风险远大于收益，而且能把账算明白的也是少数，吃力不讨好。

以前我上班的时候，有一份工作税前是 4 万，到手是 5.3万。—— 还真就有人选择不要到手 5.5，选择要到手 2.7 + 全额缴纳的。

当然企业是为了自己省钱，还是为了给你也省点，要具体情况具体计算。不要先入为主拒绝，一切以自己到手为准。

🎫 社保的额外价值

也就是落户和房票。

在我辞职之后的一段时间，还继续保持着上海的社保。当时还没做决定，未来会不会在上海生活，买房，落户。所以付费保持着连续社保，断了这些就没资格了。

当决定定居日本之后立刻停了，止损。放今天看，落户和房票 显然越来越不值钱了，更加没有维持的必要。

公积金早已提取完毕了，养老金我放弃，医保还有钱。所以我依然保持着，回国时顺带找三甲医院做的检查的习惯，尽量把医保的钱花掉。不报销，仅医保个人账户自费，不给国家添麻烦。

——

我想说的说完了 ～ 大部分人也许还没有选择，但理应知道自己在做什么，这样有选择的时候才能选对。

祝早日退休，领到自己应得的养老金。

感谢所有来现场支持open的小伙伴！monad open大会结束，它对我是另外一副眼镜，从更偏外部的视角来观察十个月的monad真实的情况和进展，也欢迎大家一起交流

在harvey这篇详细的总结之上，分享自己的想法:

一个是能看到monad具有初步网络效应。模型公司是智能基地 + 上层应用(code, design, finance etc)，我认为公链也是。

模型的api平台花费重金和时间去做大而全的数据集成，这也是他们agent产品能力的来源。

经过十个月，monad在共识产品的底座之上，生态已经具备可观的集成类型和数量，如常用defi协议，基础设施和工具，应用，支付等。

这个基础之上，资产，资金，用户，应用，社区会加速流转。这符合我的体感，早期发生的活动正加速让其他相关方参与。

其次是RWA不能只有RWA，RWA需要defi。目前的monad，tvl站在$1b，其中稳定币的体量700m, rwa是400m左右。

Aave, Euler, Morpho等作为rwa经济的承载基石，其协议都在monad部署，这一个很大的优势。

rwa会越来越多，但采纳和在defi流转相对还是较少。而monad上这些defi蓝筹协议能帮忙改变分销。

比如之前，一个资产上链后要拉不同的LP买入，这十分耗时耗力难以scale。

但现在，如果成为一个借贷产品，可以利用Monad上的稳定币体量让tvl轻松流入，也省去针对不同用户到期赎回等管理问题和面临流动性的压力。

抗量子和隐私结算系列的产品发布是很大的亮点，harvey这里已经做了详细的总结。

---
看到有推特说，monad是以太坊的资本市场版本。主动帮助创始人和builder，参与产品和gtm的设计和分发，以及桥接东西方的资产和资金，确实是我们在做的事情。

nikita昨天说，技术的护城河已经不在，只剩下网络效应，专有数据，还有物理组件。

抛开物理组件，网络效应和专属数据的形成，我认为很重要一部分来自于市场信任和极度专业。比如大量的集成还有上面defi的例子，说明monad是一个公约数，能从不同的阵营取得商业合作，当然这也是open的立意。trust the process 

另外，我在sg长出了最长呆毛！

text:
$BORDR Fundamentals Are Strengthening, but the Next Stage Depends on Whether the Ecosystem Can Truly Gain Traction

6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr 

Bordrless's fundamentals have improved significantly. The changes go beyond adding a few features. The project is expanding from its own token standard, DEX, and launchpad into an open developer platform and an external trading distribution network.

What we can confirm so far is that product delivery and infrastructure development have made progress. However, the scale of the developer ecosystem, the actual trading growth generated by external integrations, and the long-term value capture of BORDR still need to be validated with data.

The most notable aspect of this update is that three developments are happening simultaneously: Axiom integration is live, the SDK and Workshop are lowering barriers to developer participation, and mainnet programs have added fee distribution and scripting capabilities. If these components work together, Bordrless could evolve from a technically differentiated launchpad into infrastructure that other projects actively use.

What Has Changed in This Update?

1. From Its Own Trading Interface to External Trading Distribution

Axiom has integrated the Bordrless Token Standard and DEX. According to the official team, all tokens launched on Bordrless can now be traded on Axiom while retaining the corresponding Hooks. This means trading is no longer limited to Bordrless's own website, and other trading terminals and aggregators are also planned for integration.

This is one of the most important changes in this update. It addresses product distribution rather than simply improving the interface. The more external trading entry points there are, the more opportunities launched projects have to reach traders. However, completing an integration does not guarantee significant additional trading volume. That still needs to be demonstrated through actual trading data.

2. From an Official Development Product to an Open Developer Ecosystem

The SDK allows developers to create custom Hooks, trading pools, and Bonding Curves. They can also add liquidity and use bridged assets as quote assets. Hooks can execute custom rules during token transfers and trading, such as taxes, holder rewards, transfer restrictions, or burns. Companions manage creator fees according to predefined schedules and rules, supporting functions such as market making and buybacks.

The team is also shifting the Studio development workflow toward developers building independently with AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Cursor, then submitting their work to the Workshop. The platform reviews, builds, simulates, and deploys approved projects. AI explains what the code does and how much it charges in plain language. Approved Hooks and Companions can then be selected by other token launchers, and developers can earn 50% of the creator fees generated by subsequent launches that use their configurations.

This means developers no longer have to be merely users of Bordrless products. They can become providers of ecosystem components. The real growth signal is not how many people download the SDK, but how many third-party tools pass review, get adopted by other launchers, and generate recurring revenue.

3. Mainnet Upgrades Are Improving Fee Distribution and Ecosystem Incentives

The mainnet upgrades announced by the team include the release of SDK 0.10.0; the ability for terminals, bots, and wallets to add integration fees of up to 1% to Bordrless trades they route; the ability to split a token's creator fees among up to 10 wallets at fixed percentages; scripts that can pay SOL to eligible wallets when the launcher enables the feature in advance; and the option for Workshop developers to publish their Hooks with a 0% fee.

These capabilities serve different purposes: monetizing trading entry points, splitting fees among project teams, automating on-chain payments, and encouraging developer participation. Creator-fee distribution and programmable scripts are particularly useful because they allow teams, treasuries, partners, and automated strategies to participate in a project's economic flows.

One distinction matters: integration fees collected by third parties do not automatically become BORDR revenue, and creator fees earned by developers are not equivalent to returns for token holders. These are initially economic mechanisms for the platform and ecosystem participants. They can indirectly benefit BORDR only if they generate revenue that the protocol can capture.

4. A Quick-Trade Panel and Builder Competition Improve User Experience and Incentivize Supply

The new web trading panel floats over the chart and combines buying, selling, preset amounts, estimated tokens received, and trading rules. Trading wallets can sign without an additional prompt. The goal is to let users trade directly while viewing market data and to prepare for future terminal integrations.

The team also announced a $5,000 Builder Race, with the top three projects receiving $2,500, $1,500, and $1,000 after 72 hours. The competition aims to attract early developers to build Hooks, Companions, and other tools, but the prize money itself does not prove that sustained ecosystem demand already exists.

Following these updates, the product's core positioning has become clearer. Bordrless is not just a launchpad. It is building its own token standard, DEX, and launchpad on Solana, allowing token rules to be executed through Hooks. The official documentation lists the mainnet programs and explains how they differ from Token-2022 transfer hooks.

External integrations are also beginning to address the distribution bottleneck. An in-house DEX can execute complex rules, but if tokens depend entirely on the project's own website, trader reach and liquidity may be limited. Axiom's integration demonstrates that external distribution is no longer entirely theoretical. The next question is whether other terminals and aggregators follow through and how much trading volume they bring.

Finally, developer incentives are becoming more complete. The SDK, AI coding agents, Workshop review and deployment, reusable Hooks, and creator-fee sharing are beginning to form a loop. In theory, developers have an incentive to build better trading rules and fee-management tools, while launchers can use those tools directly. The wider the adoption, the more fees developers can earn.

However, open development capabilities do not mean a developer network effect has already formed. Sustained third-party output, genuine adoption, and verifiable fee distributions are needed before this mechanism can be considered commercially validated.

Has BORDR's Value Capture Improved Alongside the Product?

A stronger product does not necessarily translate into proportionally stronger demand for its token.

According to the official Tokenomics documentation, half of protocol revenue is retained in the treasury for operating expenses such as development and deployment, while the other half is used to buy back BORDR every 10 minutes. The purchased tokens are bridged into the treasury and held; they are not burned. The team also states that buybacks are executed by an off-chain keeper operated by Bordrless. If the keeper stops, revenue remains in the treasury until processing resumes.

Current project metrics displayed on the Bordrless website:

Total launches: 93
Platform 24-hour trading volume: $222.50K
Displayed cumulative buybacks: $9.31K in BORDR
Cumulative fees from launch rules: 99.4 SOL

These figures indicate that the product is generating real trading activity, launch fees, and buyback activity rather than remaining a white-paper project. However, 93 launches are not enough to establish a strong network effect. The $9.31K in buybacks also needs to be evaluated against the token's market cap and future protocol revenue to assess its actual impact on supply and demand.

Protocol fees primarily come from LP fees on launch pools, launch fees, and protocol fees on regular DEX pools. The typical rules listed in the official documentation include a 0.3% LP fee on launch-pool trades, a 0.01 SOL fee per launch, and a 1% protocol fee on the quote-asset amount traded in regular pools.

Therefore, the important question is not how many new fee mechanisms are added, but whether external integrations can expand effective trading volume and consistently convert that activity into protocol treasury revenue and actual buybacks. The up-to-1% integration fee that terminals can charge belongs to the integrators; it does not all flow into the BORDR buyback mechanism.

What Is the Market Betting On?

I believe the market is primarily trading three narratives.

First, a programmable token standard on Solana.

Bordrless aims to make rules for taxes, rewards, burns, and holding restrictions take effect directly during token transfers or trading, rather than requiring each project to maintain its own off-chain scripts. This is its most important technical narrative relative to ordinary launchpads.

Second, ecosystem expansion driven by AI developers.

If developers can use AI coding agents to build their own Hooks, publish them through the Workshop, and have other launchers adopt them, the supply of ecosystem tools could grow rapidly. What the market may be pricing in ahead of time is the potential developer network, rather than developer revenue already realized today.

Third, a growth loop between external trading distribution and fee-based buybacks.

More terminal integrations could bring more trading. A wider range of tools could attract more launchers, increasing platform activity and revenue. The protocol's allocation of half its revenue to BORDR buybacks also creates a potential channel of demand linked to the platform's business.

Among these three narratives, the token standard already has tangible product support, the distribution network is only beginning to expand, and developer network effects and sustained revenue growth remain unproven.

What Could Become the Next Catalysts for Price Appreciation?

I believe the real catalysts would be:

More terminals and aggregators officially integrating. Axiom is already live, and the team has said more terminals and aggregators would integrate that week. Concrete integrations, trading volume generated by those integrations, and verifiable protocol revenue would be meaningful catalysts. Announcements alone are not enough.

Sustained adoption of third-party Hooks and Companions. SDK 0.10.0, the Workshop, developer-fee sharing, and the $5,000 Builder Race could encourage more participation. If more third-party tools are adopted by other projects and generate recurring developer revenue, the ecosystem narrative would gain further validation.

Companions and fee automation becoming fully operational. Managing creator fees through scripts could support automated market making, buybacks, and other on-chain strategies, allowing funds generated by launches to be actively deployed rather than sitting idle. However, some screenshots described Companion upgrades as “coming soon,” while official development documentation linked them to the October 12, 2026 program upgrade. Mainnet deployment and actual invocation records should be verified before treating the entire feature set as fully operational.

Sustained growth in protocol revenue and buybacks. This is the catalyst most directly connected to token value capture. If platform trading volume grows alongside treasury revenue and verifiable on-chain buyback amounts continue to increase, the market would have a stronger basis for valuing BORDR as an asset supported by business activity rather than just a technical narrative.

My conclusion is that this update represents a genuine improvement in fundamentals, but not yet completed commercial validation. Bordrless is moving beyond its programmable token standard and in-house DEX by adding external distribution, third-party development, fee automation, and ecosystem incentives.

The next stage depends on three things: whether other terminals bring incremental trading volume, whether third-party developers' tools achieve sustained adoption, and whether additional trading activity translates into recurring protocol revenue and buybacks.

If all three improve, stronger fundamentals could become a sustained catalyst for the token. If product announcements and downloads grow without corresponding adoption and revenue, market expectations may run ahead of reality.

$BORDR recent rally is not about an ordinary Meme. 

6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr 

The market is betting on a customizable Token Standard on Solana, along with the DEX, launchpad, and developer ecosystem being built around it.

I believe the key catalyst behind the recent move is that the project is transitioning from simply pitching a new token standard to gradually launching product modules, opening up developer tools, and expanding external trading access. However, we need to distinguish between improving product development and proven ecosystem demand. The former is becoming more evident; the latter remains unproven.

First, Bordrless has a differentiated technical narrative. It is not simply copying Uniswap V4 Hooks. Instead, it extends programmable rules from the liquidity pool layer to the token layer.

A standard Token-2022 Transfer Hook primarily determines whether a transfer is allowed. Bordrless’s own Token Standard allows Hooks to define rules around fees, revenue distribution, burns, holder rewards, and holding-time-based mechanisms. The DEX also invokes these Hooks during trading, while the launchpad is part of the same system.

This means developers could theoretically design different tokenomics directly into their tokens, rather than relying entirely on external bots to execute buybacks, distributions, or burns. BORDR’s long-term potential lies in whether broader adoption could turn Bordrless from a launchpad into foundational infrastructure for programmable token economics on Solana.

There are two main recent catalysts.

Product modules are progressively going live. The website showcases components including the Token Standard, DEX, launchpad, bridge, and SDK. The team has also announced the launch of AI Studio and previewed upcoming features such as Hook Studio and Companions.

The developer ecosystem is taking shape. Open-source programs and SDKs lower the barrier to entry. The market is not simply betting on an individual token, but on the possibility that developers will use this infrastructure to create tokens with differentiated economic rules.

Together, these developments have encouraged the market to price in the possibility that Bordrless could become an infrastructure layer for a new generation of programmable tokens on Solana.

Fundamentals have improved, but mainly in terms of product maturity and the strength of the ecosystem narrative. Actual adoption remains at an early stage.

The website currently shows 21 launches and zero graduated projects, with approximately $110K in 24-hour trading volume, $26.8K in pool liquidity, and $1.12K in creator fees.

These figures show that the product is no longer purely conceptual, but they do not yet demonstrate that it can attract a large number of projects with sustained usage. In particular, the lack of graduated projects means long-term retention, successful launch case studies, and post-graduation trading depth still need to be proven.

BORDR’s price has also risen significantly, but the entire move cannot be attributed to any single product update. A more reasonable interpretation is that product development, developer tools, trading access, and KOL coverage have collectively strengthened market expectations. Determining the contribution of each factor would require a closer look at transaction-level data and the timeline of events.

Going forward, I will focus on three variables:

1. Hook Studio goes fully live. If developers can easily design, deploy, and share custom Hooks, Bordrless could evolve from a collection of in-house products into a broader developer platform.

2. Companions generates real usage. The team has described a mechanism through which creator fees flow into on-chain programs and are allocated according to predefined rules for buybacks, burns, holder distributions, or other purposes. If multiple projects generate meaningful trading activity through this system, that would be much stronger evidence than simply adding more features.

3. External projects adopt the standard consistently. The real inflection point is not another module going live. It is independent developers choosing to issue tokens using the standard and generating sustained trading volume, fees, and user demand.

There are two major risks.

First, product complexity may be running ahead of demand. Programmable tokens offer considerable technical flexibility, but ordinary issuers may not need such complex mechanisms. Without sufficient developer adoption, even a fully developed product may struggle to generate network effects.

Second, BORDR’s value capture has not been sufficiently established. Even if the Bordrless DEX, launchpad, and SDK grow, that does not mean all of this growth will translate into buying demand for BORDR. Its specific utility, revenue distribution model, and ability to generate sustained token demand still need to be verified.

Security is another consideration. The website states that the relevant programs retain upgrade authority pending completion of audits. For infrastructure responsible for token rules, fee distribution, and burns, this is a risk that deserves continued monitoring.

My conclusion is that the most meaningful change behind BORDR’s recent rally is its transition from the concept of a new Token Standard toward an infrastructure project with code, product modules, and developer tools. The market is betting on whether it can become a foundational layer for programmable token economics on Solana.

What will determine whether its valuation can expand further is not another explanation of how advanced Hooks are, but whether developer adoption, real trading activity, and BORDR’s value capture can grow together.

The fundamentals are moving in the right direction, but ecosystem scale and token value capture remain at an early stage.

text:
This is burnout, and if you want to survive as a trader, you must learn to recognize it.

True burnout is not just being overworked, nor is it something you can push through. It is a feedback loop that occurs when your body experiences intense, prolonged stress.

Stress is part of life, and under normal conditions you can recover from it easily. In fact, many dimensions of human performance - strength, endurance, mental acuity - actually require stress in order to grow.

However, growth in response to stress can only happen when the stress is manageable and offset by periods of recovery. When the stress is extreme and constant, the body fails to adapt and enters a downward spiral.

As stress accumulates, several things happen physiologically:
- sleep is disrupted
- hormones become dysregulated
- mental performance degrades
- heart rate variability falls 
- inflammation rises and immune function declines

The problem is that each of these effects also *reduces your ability to withstand and recover from stress.* So you enter a vicious cycle where recovery becomes impossible and performance steadily deteriorates.

The experience @agapestride describes here is exactly what it feels like to burn out from trading. And if you find yourself in this situation, the most important thing you can do is *recognize what has happened.* 

You are not dumber than you used to be. You are not more indecisive. You are not more impulsive, fearful, or greedy. You are simply physiologically impaired by severe, chronic stress.

When you notice the signs of burnout, you must prioritize recovery above all else:
- cut your risk
- stop looking at charts
- get off social media
- play sports or start running
- spend time with friends and family
- go hiking or traveling
- take lots of hot baths

As much as it feels like the best time to make generational wealth is RIGHT NOW, the market will always be here. So take a break and don't come back until you know your body can handle it.

For this rally, I'm more inclined to view $HOOKR as Uniswap v4 Hook infrastructure on Rh Chain.

0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 

It is expanding from a token launch tool into composable trading infrastructure.

The market appears to be reassessing its ecosystem value.

Unlike a Meme token driven purely by hype, HOOKR has usable products, on-chain trading pools, and a protocol fee mechanism. But that also raises the key question: has the growth in product capabilities translated into sufficient real usage and sustainable buying pressure for the token?

Recent developments have also led me to update my analysis in an important way. HOOKR is not simply adding more Hook modules. It is beginning to connect capital flows, reward distribution, and revenue streams across different trading pools. This is more significant than simply adding token launch features, because it speaks to whether Hookr can evolve from a programmable liquidity pool platform into composable on-chain trading infrastructure.

Hookr’s website now positions the new version as modular infrastructure for Uniswap v4 Hooks. However, the relevant contracts have not yet completed a formal external audit. Product functionality going live and security being independently verified must therefore be evaluated separately.

The Latest Catalysts

1. Moving from individual trading pools to cross-pool connectivity

The most important update is Hookr’s announcement that three contracts connecting different trading pools are now live.

Pool Mesh allows a single vault to provide liquidity to up to four pools for different tokens. Capital can be allocated according to predefined weights or directed toward the pools with the thinnest liquidity. Once a project creates a Mesh, other pools can join it.

This means liquidity no longer has to remain entirely isolated within each pool. For projects operating multiple tokens or trading markets, this mechanism could make capital management more flexible.

Family Pinger allows a single call to automatically execute a group of related operations, including trading Zaps, periodic small fund distributions, and payments owed to a family of pools.

Fee Bridge allows a project to designate an address as a royalty recipient or tax recipient, then distribute the funds it receives in batches to liquidity providers in another pool, with a cap on the amount transferred in each distribution.

The common thread among these three features is that Hookr is beginning to coordinate capital across multiple pools rather than focusing solely on trading rules within individual pools.

If real projects adopt these mechanisms, Hookr’s infrastructure thesis will become much more compelling than a simple launchpad narrative. However, contracts going live only means the functionality is available. It does not mean large-scale adoption or substantial revenue has already materialized.

2. Modular tools and the developer ecosystem continue to expand

Hookr’s newly released HookBook documents 24 ways to combine Uniswap v4 pools with Hook Blocks, covering use cases ranging from fair launches to treasury management. Each combination comes with a full walkthrough, and users can open the Builder with the configuration prefilled in one click.

Hookr has also introduced or announced the following features:

Every live Hook Block can be configured directly in the app and has its own dedicated page.
Developers can submit requests directly through the search interface when they cannot find the module they need.
Swap Reward Mint allows users to create reward tokens within the app and distribute them to traders on every swap.
Multi-pool launches allow different pools to use separate Hook Blocks and different initial quote assets.
Existing tokens can also add Tax + Conversion mechanisms, with the pool page showing who pays each tax.
llms.txt allows AI agents and AI search tools to read Hook Blocks, documentation, and HookBook combinations.

In addition, Hookr has announced support for deploying custom Uniswap v4 Hooks in a single transaction and says the first such Hook is already on-chain. Developers can combine the Hook Blocks they need, deploy their own Hook, and then use Hookr’s launch, routing, and quote-asset tools to create trading pools. Existing tokens can also connect to new pools without modifying the tokens themselves.

These updates may seem scattered, but they point toward the same goal: lowering the barrier to building complex trading mechanisms.

If developers can select modules, combine parameters, deploy pools, and integrate them into their own applications through an SDK, Hookr has the potential to become a development tool for other projects rather than a product that serves only traffic on its own website.

3. Ecosystem integrations are expanding into more use cases

Hookr’s new version supports different quote assets, including ETH, stablecoins, HOOKR, and tokenized stocks. It also provides an SDK and a public module directory, allowing other applications to integrate trading, quoting, and pool creation functionality.

More importantly, Hookr pools can be routed through Uniswap’s own interface and APIs. This means projects do not have to rely entirely on users visiting https://t.co/rbi76Dkjxu directly; they may also attract usage through external trading interfaces.

The project also claims that the new version reduces gas costs for swaps by approximately 47%–70% and token launch costs by around 40%. If these advantages hold up in real transactions, Hookr could attract developers through a better product experience rather than relying purely on subsidies.

Recent project-related information also mentions several integrations:

Saffron is integrating fixed-yield vaults.
ZEALZ plans to launch a zZEC pool with low base fees and LP rewards.
rhook can replay historical trading activity to compare the effects of different trading rules.
hooddomains brings domains into the creator and trading pool experience.
An OpenAI-related project plans to launch tokens with custom rules on Hookr.
Longbow Lend is exploring the use of Hookr pools for liquidations and collateral swaps.

These integrations serve different purposes. Some could increase the number of trading pools, some improve developer tooling, and others attempt to connect Hookr with lending, yield, and trading applications.

If these projects actually launch and generate sustained trading activity, the demand thesis for HOOKR could expand beyond token launch activity into broader ecosystem usage.

However, it is essential to distinguish between an integration being announced, a feature being live, and an integration generating meaningful trading volume. A list of partnerships and a growing number of features do not, by themselves, prove that protocol revenue is increasing.

4. The token value-capture mechanism is becoming clearer

HOOKR’s value proposition is not simply to use all trading fees for buybacks.

In the new version, base LP fees go entirely to liquidity providers. The protocol primarily earns a share of revenue from additional mechanisms such as dynamic fees, Anti-Snipe, LP rewards, and automatic burns. The default revenue-sharing rate is 20%, with the actual rate determined when a pool is created. Pools using the arbitrage value-recapture mechanism also contribute part of their proceeds to the protocol.

The mechanism described by the project involves pooling protocol revenue in a treasury and using it to buy back and burn HOOKR.

If more pools adopt these additional mechanisms and trading volume continues to grow, this could theoretically create a value-capture loop: greater ecosystem usage leads to more protocol revenue, which in turn supports more buybacks and burns.

But this chain of causality still needs to be verified with real data. I will focus on actual protocol revenue, on-chain buyback records, and the amount of tokens burned rather than assuming that every mechanism is already operating at full scale.

What the Market May Be Betting On

I think the market may be betting on three layers of potential.

First, trading activity on Rh Chain will continue to grow, and more projects will need programmable trading rules, positioning Hookr as an important infrastructure entry point.

Second, modular Hooks, HookBook, and the SDK will attract third-party developers. If other projects begin using Hookr to build pools, launch tokens, or develop applications, it could create network effects that extend beyond traffic to Hookr’s own website.

Third, cross-pool capital management and broader ecosystem usage will eventually translate into sustained HOOKR buybacks and burns. For token holders, this is the most important connection between product growth and token value.

Where Things Stand Now

Product fundamentals are strengthening, ecosystem adoption remains unproven, and token value capture has yet to be fully realized.

From a product perspective, HOOKR is clearly more extensible than a single-purpose launch platform. Its modular architecture, pools with multiple quote assets, cross-pool connectors, SDK, custom Hook deployment, and external routing are expanding the range of problems it can solve.

From an adoption perspective, the direction is improving, but it still needs to be validated through sustained trading volume, active developers, and actual usage data from external integrations. The launch of connectors and partnership announcements do not necessarily mean they are already generating substantial trading activity.

From a token value-capture perspective, the mechanism is becoming clearer, but the actual scale of buybacks, the stability of revenue, and the relationship between revenue and token demand still need to be demonstrated with on-chain data. Product upgrades should not be equated with a fully realized improvement in token fundamentals.

Potential Upside Catalysts Ahead

First, real projects begin using the cross-pool connectors. If Pool Mesh helps multiple pools share and coordinate liquidity, Fee Bridge establishes consistent cross-pool revenue distribution, and Family Pinger handles recurring automated payments, that would be much more meaningful than simply adding a few more trading pools.

Second, third-party projects begin building their own products on Hookr. If launch platforms use custom Hooks, trading applications integrate pools through the SDK, and DeFi protocols use its mechanisms for liquidity and yield management, Hookr’s value would no longer depend entirely on how many tokens it launches itself.

Third, protocol revenue and buybacks and burns grow together. This is the key point at which the product narrative could translate into stronger token fundamentals. If real trading activity increases alongside sustained growth in protocol revenue, actual buybacks, and token burns, HOOKR’s long-term valuation thesis would gain much stronger support.

Fourth, additional features launch and attract real usage. Canonical Venue Token, Buy/Sell Block, Market Guard, Zap Relay, Entry Ratio Guarantee, Recovery Reserve, Pay Later, Tax + Conversion, Revenue Router, Vesting Milestone, Market-hours Fee, Limit Orders, Best Route, and Hook Blocks Market could all expand Hookr’s potential use cases.

However, not all these features are live yet. Zero-seed launches, auction-based launches, Floor Bid, Dev Drip, and Usage Fee are also still part of the development roadmap. Whether they become catalysts depends on their eventual launch and adoption, not merely their presence on a roadmap.

Key Risks

First, Hookr’s product capabilities may be ahead of market demand. If developer activity and trading on Rh Chain remain insufficient, even a comprehensive modular system may struggle to generate meaningful protocol revenue.

Second, complex trading rules and cross-pool capital flows increase system complexity. Pool Mesh, Fee Bridge, and similar features need to prove that their fund routing, transfer limits, and exception handling are reliable. More features do not automatically mean lower system risk.

Third, Hook modules are not impossible to replicate. Hookr’s long-term moat must ultimately come from developer adoption, tooling quality, its integration network, and sustained usage—not merely the number of modules it offers.

Fourth, security remains a critical risk. Hookr’s website has not confirmed that the relevant contracts have completed a formal external audit, while the project recently stated that the new version was being submitted for audit. Submitting contracts for an audit does not mean the audit is complete, nor does it guarantee that no vulnerabilities exist.

Finally, even if product usage grows, the token may not appreciate accordingly. If protocol revenue shares remain limited, buybacks are too small, or sustained selling pressure outweighs buying demand, the infrastructure narrative may still fail to translate into token price performance.

My Final Take

The latest batch of updates makes me more optimistic about HOOKR’s product direction.

Previously, its main story was modularizing Uniswap v4 Hooks so that projects could create pools with more flexible, customized trading rules. Now, Pool Mesh, Family Pinger, and Fee Bridge are beginning to connect capital and revenue across multiple pools, while HookBook, the SDK, and custom Hook deployment are lowering the barriers for developers to use these capabilities.

This pushes HOOKR’s potential positioning beyond “a more flexible token launch platform” toward “programmable and composable trading and capital-management infrastructure.”

But product upgrades do not mean token value has already been realized. The key things to track next are whether the connectors see real usage, whether third-party integrations continue to expand, whether protocol revenue grows, and whether buybacks and burns reach a meaningful scale.

If product adoption, protocol revenue, and actual buybacks grow together, HOOKR’s infrastructure narrative will gain much stronger fundamental support. If its features keep expanding but real usage and value capture remain elusive, the token could still be trading on a future that has been priced in too early.

author: dabit3
quoted_text:
We're launching our leaderboard for FrontierCode 1.1, a private evaluation from Cognition that tests models on completing coding tasks in a way that would actually get merged by maintainers of real-world repositories

@cognition announced FrontierCode in June 2026 and updated it to version 1.1 in July. Cognition built the dataset with open source maintainers who spent more than 40 hours per task. Each task requires the agent to make a change to a real open source repository, then checks both unit tests and qualitative tests for what maintainers would require to merge the change.

We run FrontierCode 1.1 Main, the primary 100-task set of the benchmark's 150 tasks, using our Stirrup open source reference harness for apples-to-apples comparisons across models. All tasks are private to avoid contamination. Each attempt is graded with both blocking and non-blocking criteria. An attempt that fails any blocking check scores zero, and one that passes them all scores between 70% and 100%.

Unlike other coding evaluations, FrontierCode has a more holistic view of success based on real usage. Models need to pass unit tests, but are also assessed on behaviors like making excessive changes and large diffs, modifying files outside the relevant scope, or adding unhelpful tests. We think this approach is valuable in the current context: models are now very capable at coding tasks, but their changes can still require substantial cleanup before a maintainer would merge them.

Key takeaways:

➤ Leading models still fail more than 40% of the time: Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback) leads at a score of 52% after passing blockers in 58% of its attempts. Nine of the 100 tasks were not passed in any attempt by any of the models we evaluated for launch

➤ The top of the leaderboard is tightly packed: nine models from six labs score between 43% and 52%. MiMo-V2.6-Pro is the leading open weights model at 45%, followed by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (max) and Kimi K3 (max) at 44%

➤ GPT-6.1 Sol (max) offers the strongest performance for its cost: At $0.81 per task it scores 49%, matching Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback). This means it achieves similar performance to leading Anthropic models, at less than a tenth of the cost per task

Thank you to @silasalberti, @ybenpan, @cl571128, and the rest of the team at Cognition for building FrontierCode and collaborating with us to bring it to Artificial Analysis - we’re working to add FrontierCode to our coding agent leaderboard very soon.

$BORDR recent rally is not about an ordinary Meme. 

6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr 

The market is betting on a customizable Token Standard on Solana, along with the DEX, launchpad, and developer ecosystem being built around it.

I believe the key catalyst behind the recent move is that the project is transitioning from simply pitching a new token standard to gradually launching product modules, opening up developer tools, and expanding external trading access. However, we need to distinguish between improving product development and proven ecosystem demand. The former is becoming more evident; the latter remains unproven.

First, Bordrless has a differentiated technical narrative. It is not simply copying Uniswap V4 Hooks. Instead, it extends programmable rules from the liquidity pool layer to the token layer.

A standard Token-2022 Transfer Hook primarily determines whether a transfer is allowed. Bordrless’s own Token Standard allows Hooks to define rules around fees, revenue distribution, burns, holder rewards, and holding-time-based mechanisms. The DEX also invokes these Hooks during trading, while the launchpad is part of the same system.

This means developers could theoretically design different tokenomics directly into their tokens, rather than relying entirely on external bots to execute buybacks, distributions, or burns. BORDR’s long-term potential lies in whether broader adoption could turn Bordrless from a launchpad into foundational infrastructure for programmable token economics on Solana.

There are two main recent catalysts.

Product modules are progressively going live. The website showcases components including the Token Standard, DEX, launchpad, bridge, and SDK. The team has also announced the launch of AI Studio and previewed upcoming features such as Hook Studio and Companions.

The developer ecosystem is taking shape. Open-source programs and SDKs lower the barrier to entry. The market is not simply betting on an individual token, but on the possibility that developers will use this infrastructure to create tokens with differentiated economic rules.

Together, these developments have encouraged the market to price in the possibility that Bordrless could become an infrastructure layer for a new generation of programmable tokens on Solana.

Fundamentals have improved, but mainly in terms of product maturity and the strength of the ecosystem narrative. Actual adoption remains at an early stage.

The website currently shows 21 launches and zero graduated projects, with approximately $110K in 24-hour trading volume, $26.8K in pool liquidity, and $1.12K in creator fees.

These figures show that the product is no longer purely conceptual, but they do not yet demonstrate that it can attract a large number of projects with sustained usage. In particular, the lack of graduated projects means long-term retention, successful launch case studies, and post-graduation trading depth still need to be proven.

BORDR’s price has also risen significantly, but the entire move cannot be attributed to any single product update. A more reasonable interpretation is that product development, developer tools, trading access, and KOL coverage have collectively strengthened market expectations. Determining the contribution of each factor would require a closer look at transaction-level data and the timeline of events.

Going forward, I will focus on three variables:

1. Hook Studio goes fully live. If developers can easily design, deploy, and share custom Hooks, Bordrless could evolve from a collection of in-house products into a broader developer platform.

2. Companions generates real usage. The team has described a mechanism through which creator fees flow into on-chain programs and are allocated according to predefined rules for buybacks, burns, holder distributions, or other purposes. If multiple projects generate meaningful trading activity through this system, that would be much stronger evidence than simply adding more features.

3. External projects adopt the standard consistently. The real inflection point is not another module going live. It is independent developers choosing to issue tokens using the standard and generating sustained trading volume, fees, and user demand.

There are two major risks.

First, product complexity may be running ahead of demand. Programmable tokens offer considerable technical flexibility, but ordinary issuers may not need such complex mechanisms. Without sufficient developer adoption, even a fully developed product may struggle to generate network effects.

Second, BORDR’s value capture has not been sufficiently established. Even if the Bordrless DEX, launchpad, and SDK grow, that does not mean all of this growth will translate into buying demand for BORDR. Its specific utility, revenue distribution model, and ability to generate sustained token demand still need to be verified.

Security is another consideration. The website states that the relevant programs retain upgrade authority pending completion of audits. For infrastructure responsible for token rules, fee distribution, and burns, this is a risk that deserves continued monitoring.

My conclusion is that the most meaningful change behind BORDR’s recent rally is its transition from the concept of a new Token Standard toward an infrastructure project with code, product modules, and developer tools. The market is betting on whether it can become a foundational layer for programmable token economics on Solana.

What will determine whether its valuation can expand further is not another explanation of how advanced Hooks are, but whether developer adoption, real trading activity, and BORDR’s value capture can grow together.

The fundamentals are moving in the right direction, but ecosystem scale and token value capture remain at an early stage.

美国这招高利率+高油价+高美元指数，一定会拉爆1-2个超级经济体，然后发生一场中等规模经济危机，美国充当救世主，开始救市，全球一起放水，危机解除，全球流动性泛滥，核心资产开始新一轮暴涨！

这个剧本在历史上，已经演过好多场，每隔几年，就会演一场大戏，来做一场无硝烟的金融收割，这次大概率待宰的羔羊🐑，可能是欧洲第二大经济体法国！🧐

最近一个诡异的数据，法国10年期政府债券收益率最高逼近5%，而股票更是跌的一塌糊涂(如👇图)，法国内部也开始游行不断，因福利缩减原因！感觉这次欧元区排第二的大哥法国，可能真的要踩雷了！

无法想象的是，堂堂欧洲第二大经济体，现在的信用定价，竟然比当年被嘲笑的希腊、意大利还要差！

现在10年期的法国国债收益率一路狂飙，借钱成本直接刷爆了2002年以来的最高纪录。大家都不敢把钱借给法国了，因为它现在的状况，简直就是活脱脱的“债务死循环”。

法国到底是怎么一步步把自己混到今天这个地步的？说白了，主要是三股力量在把它往绝路上推：

第一，好日子过惯了，花钱没节制，债务彻底失控

过去那些年，全世界利率低，借钱便宜，法国政府就大手大脚花钱。现在呢？低利率的“好日子”结束了。

法国欠的债务已经快赶上它一年的GDP总量（接近120%）了，而且接下来几年，有上万亿美元的旧债要到期。这就尴尬了，以前利息低，借新还旧没压力；现在利率这么高，借新债去还旧债，光是每年要还的利息，就能把财政预算给吃干抹净，甚至比防务军费还要高！这就跟一个人信用卡叠信用卡，最后连利息都还不起是一个道理。

第二，通胀和加息这对“组合拳”，直接重创了法国经济。

欧洲这几年地缘冲突不断，能源价格疯涨，法国这种高度依赖外来能源的国家，制造业成本直接飙升。通胀压不住，欧洲央行就只能硬着头皮不断加息。

这下死循环就形成了：通胀越高，央行越要加息；央行一加息，法国政府和企业的借款成本就越贵；借钱越贵，大家越觉得法国要违约，越狂抛法国国债；抛的人越多，借钱成本就进一步升高……这雪球滚起来，根本停不下来。

第三，最忠实的“大金主”日本，开始提裤子跑路了。

以前日本是法债最大的买家之一，因为日本国内利率几乎是零，日本资金喜欢跑到法国套利。但现在日本国内也开始抬高利率了，扣掉汇率对冲成本，买法债赚的那点微薄差价，根本不值得冒风险。于是，日本的大型基金开始清仓甩卖法债，连最忠诚的金主都不玩了，法债彻底失去了最重要的底座。

这三股力量拧成一股绳，直接把法国逼到了两难的死局：

如果不砍财政开支，债务雪球继续滚，迟早崩盘； 如果硬着头皮砍福利、砍开支，经济立马衰退，老百姓分分钟上街游行罢工。

2010年欧债危机的时候，希腊爆雷了，好歹还有德国和整个欧洲拉一把，毕竟希腊体量小，救得起。

但如果这次是欧元区二把手法国彻底爆雷，整个欧洲谁又能救得起它？这可就不是什么普通的债务危机了，这是要直接把整个欧元的根基给掀翻！

拭目以待吧，最近看桥水老板达利奥的书《债务危机》，里面的思路和样本，基本跟当前经济状况如出一辙，美国这招自损800，杀敌1000的策略，大概很快就会有结果了，备好弹药，随时捡便宜！🧐

quoted_text:
This is a good way to understand how early we actually are in AI diffusion right now. The vast majority of people are using AI as a chatbot for simple interactions that approximate next-generation search. This is super useful but dramatically underrepresents the full capability of AI.

On the complete other end of the spectrum, agent swarms represent possibly the ultimate form factor of what agents will do inside of our workflows. Math, cyber, bio, materials science, software engineering, finance, and any other field that has valuable tasks that can be executed in parallel where compute can be applied to accelerate work all have this characteristic.

Less than a fraction of a fraction of the population uses AI in this way right now, due to a mix of the capabilities of models relative to the user's domain, the cost of doing these types of workflows today, the harnesses available to do this style of AI work, and the availability (or lack thereof) of frontier models to the general public.

There will also be a huge amount of change management necessary to get most areas of work -beyond software and AI research- to benefit from this style of agents. Companies need to upgrade their workflows, data needs to integrated and migrated into modern platforms, and companies will need to work through compliance, governance, and security frameworks to pull it off. 

But this all represents opportunity right now. A lot of this is where the applied layer of AI will really shine in the enterprise because of the domain specificity of this type of work. You can get an early sense of where things are going and the opportunity ahead by seeing through the funnel that Andrej lays out.

text:
推特上几位知名的 Base 铁杆 KOL，最近悄悄改了门庭。
Base 核心支持者 @696_eth 直言：“你可能一直把我当成 Base 吹，但我最近已经切换到了 Robinhood，他们正在全方位压制（mogging）Base。”

当交易所孵化的公链，迎头撞上 Web2 券商的自研链，
这场公链地缘暗战，正出现意料之外的降维打击。

聊聊为什么敏锐的钱和人，开始从 Base 迁移到 Robinhood 链：

1. 资金沉淀的降维打击：主动跨链，打不过“被动抽水”
Base 依然延续了 Web3 的老逻辑：靠 Farcaster 造势、靠土狗和创作者引流，求着散户手动跨链去炒币。流动性来得快，跑得更快。
而 Robinhood 彻底玩了另一套游戏：在 App 里推一个 4-5% 收益的合规理财（Earn），散户在前端存入 USDG，后台直接充当链上借贷的活水。
不用助记词、不用懂跨链桥，数千万传统股民的闲置资金被无感抽进底层，百天 TVL 硬生生推破 10.4 亿美元。

2. 资产厚度的本质差距：土狗乐园，拼不过“代币化美股”
Base 的痛点在于，一旦 Meme 热度熄火，链上缺乏承接巨额资本的硬资产。
Robinhood 链从第一天起，核心就是代币化美股与 24/7 撮合。当华尔街股票被做成链上资产，它的资金体量与抗周期能力，天然比纯社交代币高出一个数量级。

3. 开发者用脚投票：抢夺沉淀在底层的 10 亿冷钱
KOL 和 Dev 的转向，本质是逐水草而居。
Base 上的 PVP 已经卷到刀刀见骨；而 Robinhood 链上沉淀着超过 10 亿美金的稳定币底池，几乎全部处于“尚未被充分激活”的高净值状态。谁能在这里跑出真正的交易或衍生品闭环，谁就能吃到整个周期里最肥的一块肉。

Hyperliquid’s BBO Is Facing a Stress Test

.@papertrade_xyz has responded to concerns over price manipulation involving BTC/ETH on Hyperliquid’s BBO, pointing to loose early-stage position limits rather than flaws in its six-month-designed mechanism

Key points:
• @HyperliquidX BBO is the battleground. Attempts to manipulate BTC/ETH exposed how trading mechanisms behave under real-world pressure

• Launch trade-offs matter. Papertrade says loose position limits were initially used to handle congestion and maintain a smoother user experience

• Controls are tightening. As congestion eases, Papertrade has started reducing position limits both on-chain and at the relay level

• Manipulation has an economic cost. The goal is to make attacks unprofitable, with potential losses outweighing expected gains

Hyperliquid’s role goes beyond providing trading liquidity. Its BBO environment is also a real-world test for third-party trading protocols building on top of it

The key question is whether Papertrade can tighten its controls without sacrificing the fair-launch experience. Better execution infrastructure means little if its incentives can be exploited
