Almost missed this milestone which is quite huge if you think about it.

The biggest moat of blockchains is network effect.

If you have many isolated networks, the combined network effect is smaller than if all the liquidity were on a single network.

But if you bring atomicity between L1 and L2 → liquidity movements become instant → you can reaggregate liquidity with more safety and speed → better prices and UX

On Morpho, you could imagine being able to do Multi Market Offers ACROSS CHAINS on Midnight for instance 👀

This way you'd connect @ethereum to @base @RobinhoodApp chain, and any other L2s together so they share liquidity and provide better rates for end users.
author: MerlinEgalite
quoted_text:
Ethereum Just Solved a Piece of L1-L2 Fragmentation

Ethereum just hit an important milestone for its L1 + L2 ecosystem.

The Ethereum mainnet completed its first atomic transaction between L1 and L2.

In simple terms:
• L1 and L2 can coordinate in the same transaction instead of acting more like separate networks
• Less fragmentation → Apps and liquidity across different Ethereum layers can work together more easily
• Better user experience → Cross-layer actions could become faster and simpler

Why does this matter?
Ethereum has many L2s, but liquidity and users are often split across them.

Atomic composability could help make these layers feel more like one connected Ethereum ecosystem.

This is only the first step, but it could be an important piece of Ethereum’s long-term scaling roadmap.

text:
"If I got my Ledger from the US, am I safe?"

I dunno, but here's a list of other Ledger incidents over the years that might have impacted you 

🔴 2018 (MCU address-spoofing exploit): Security researcher Saleem Rashid demonstrated that an attacker with brief physical access could reflash the non-secure microcontroller (ST32) on a Nano S to spoof recipient addresses directly on the screen while bypassing the Secure Element check.
🔴 2020 (Database breach and cover-up): An exposed marketing API key and compromised Shopify integration leaked user data. Ledger initially downplayed it, claiming only 9,500 people were affected. Months later, the full database leaked on RaidForums, exposing home addresses, phone numbers, and names for 272,000 customers alongside 1M+ emails. It triggered years of death threats, home invasion attempts, and SIM-swapping. Ledger refused refunds or compensation.
🔴 2021 (Poisoned replacement mailers): Attackers used the leaked physical addresses to mail counterfeit Nano X units directly to victims' homes. The packages included realistic packaging, tampered circuit boards with embedded flash drives, and letters directing users to enter their 24-word seeds into a fake desktop client.
🔴 2021 (Nano X battery failures): Batches of newly shipped Nano X devices arrived with dead batteries and charging errors ("battery temperature too high/low"). As community forums filled with complaints, customer support went largely unresponsive for weeks.
🔴 2023 (Ledger Recover and deleted tweet): Ledger rolled out a subscription service to split, encrypt, and back up seeds to third-party custodians over the internet. This revealed that the proprietary operating system (BOLOS) could export private keys via firmware updates, contradicting years of marketing that keys could never leave the Secure Element. When backlash erupted, official support tweeted: "Technically speaking, it is and has always been possible to write firmware that facilitates key extraction... You have always trusted Ledger." They deleted the tweet hours later, and executives publicly dismissed user concerns by claiming critics simply misunderstood hardware wallets.
🔴 2023 (Connect Kit npm supply-chain hack): A former employee fell victim to a phishing attack, allowing a hacker to hijack Ledger's npm registry credentials. The attacker pushed malicious versions of @ledgerhq/connect-kit, injecting a wallet-draining script across major Web3 front-ends (including SushiSwap and https://t.co/4mWriSEyFA) that stole roughly $600,000 before being caught.
🔴 2023 to 2024 (Rogue app store drainers): Fake "Ledger Live" apps repeatedly bypassed moderation on the official Microsoft Store and Apple App Store, remaining active for weeks and draining hundreds of thousands of dollars from users while Ledger was criticized for sluggish takedown enforcement.
🔴 2024 to 2026 (Data breach class actions): Multiple multimillion-dollar class action lawsuits were filed in the US (including a $500M filing in New York), alleging gross negligence in securing user data and failing to take adequate remedial measures after repeated leaks.

text:
为什么美股经常在中期选举后上涨？③ 🧐

华尔街有一个持续70多年的规律：

1950年到2022年，美国19次中期选举，每次选举后的12个月，标普500全部上涨，平均涨幅约15%。

不管哪个党赢，美股似乎总能在选举后迎来一轮上涨。

比如2022年，美国通胀一度冲到9.1%，美联储激进加息，美股大幅下跌。

但从当年中期选举到一年后，标普500反而上涨了约14.5%。

为什么会这样？

————————

第一个原因，不确定性消退。

选举前，税收、监管等政策悬而未决，投资者难以判断企业未来的经营环境，只能要求更高的风险补偿。

选举结束，国会格局明朗，政策走向更容易判断，市场风险溢价可能下降，股票估值也就有了修复空间。

所以对市场来说，结果是否符合预期，有时候比谁赢更重要。

————————

第二个原因，股市的周期性修复。

富达统计显示，总统任期第二年，也就是中期选举年，美股平均回报约5%。

到了第三年，平均回报提高到14%。

因为选举年往往伴随政治不确定性和市场波动。等悲观情绪消退，股价就可能反弹。

比如2002年互联网泡沫破裂，以及2018年贸易摩擦和加息引发市场调整之后，美股都在次年迎来上涨。

当然，这也离不开经济周期和美联储货币政策的影响。

————————

第三个原因，华尔街有时候喜欢一个办事没那么容易的国会。

如果总统所在政党同时控制参众两院，重大政策更容易推进。

但如果失去其中一个议院，就可能形成“分治政府”。

税收、监管等重大改革的推进难度提高，企业现有的经营规则也更容易延续。

当然，政治僵局也可能引发预算和债务上限危机，给市场带来新的风险。

————————

不过，19次全部上涨，也有一个容易忽略的问题：

美股本身就具有长期上涨的趋势。

企业盈利增长、经济扩张，以及标普500持续调整成分股，都在发挥作用。

所以，中期选举只是影响股市的其中一个因素。

而2026年还有一个特殊情况：

美股已经提前涨了。

截至10月初，标普500年内上涨超过10%。

过去很多中期选举年，美股先经历震荡，再在选举后修复。但今年，市场已经提前跑了一段。

如果选举结果符合预期，部分利好可能早就反映在股价里。

接下来如果想复制历史上平均15%的选后涨幅，还需要企业盈利继续增长，或者美联储进一步降息。

This is very directionally aligned with what I’m seeing in enterprises

Most start with the Anthropic/OpenAI approach but it stalls out, some internal champions are born but 80% of the org still barely scratches the surface with it

So those enterprises need to bring in FDEs if they want to drive real transformation and gain edge from AI, otherwise the change ends up being more incremental while those that really lean in gain the edge

The Palantir approach requires a bigger commitment as you’re taking on a full platform deployment, but you get the benefit of owned intelligence, just with a sticky vendor platform as you mention

Enterprises can also get there with a Databricks/Snowflake at the data layer with AI on top, which could be OpenAI/Anthropic or a more agnostic approach to model providers 

So enterprises have options, and I don’t think one necessarily wins out over the other because EVERY enterprise needs to go down one of these paths to remain relevant and it’s not a one size fits all market

And then you have smaller enterprises, those that can’t afford the expensive Palantir deployment and don’t want to lock in to a closed source lab

That’s where many independent AI transformation partners can step in (talking my own @codos_ai book now)

Because the one constant theme regardless of approach is the level of change this drives within enterprises and the need for external support to go through it

Some will self-navigate but there’s a massive industry of service and software providers that has existed to help companies navigate change and there’s never been a bigger transformation catalyst in our lifetimes than AI

So who wins? Everyone that can provably add value to enterprises during this period

text:
🔥 Project Analysis - @WalrusProtocol 

@SuiNetwork seems to be getting serious about the data business

Most people still think of @SuiNetwork as a fast L1, but lately I'm seeing them put much more attention into data infrastructure, especially for AI

And I think this direction could be much more interesting than another race for faster transactions since most already done it 

The latest move is a $30M investment into DATA Network, which has already recorded over 250M data contributions and processes more than 3M receipts daily

Instead of building another AI platform from scratch and hoping users show up, Sui is bringing an existing data network into its ecosystem

@datafdn plans to migrate to Sui, while @WalrusProtocol will become the default storage layer for DATA Foundation applications

For those unfamiliar, Walrus is a decentralized storage network developed by @Mysten_Labs, the team behind Sui

A blockchain can record ownership and transactions, but storing huge amounts of videos, documents and AI training data directly onchain isn't very practical

Walrus handles those large files while applications can use Sui to manage the transactions and permissions around them

And I can see why this could matter for AI

Imagine an AI company purchasing thousands of datasets to train a model. It needs access to the original files, records of who contributed them and a way to check what it's allowed to use

With DATA Network handling contribution records and usage rights, Walrus storing the files and Sui managing transactions, more of that process could happen within the same ecosystem

For data contributors, this could make it easier to track how their work is used and how they get paid

For developers, it reduces the need to build separate systems for storage, ownership and payments

Walrus is also working on persistent memory for AI agents, allowing them to retrieve information from previous sessions rather than repeatedly starting from scratch

The potential market goes beyond crypto trading activity, which is what I like about this direction

But the economics of $WAL are still a different story

Storage is paid in $WAL at around $0.023/GB/month, and the token is also used for staking to secure the network

That's a real use case, but storage is cheap by design. Walrus needs a lot of paying customers before those fees become meaningful

Current storage revenue is only around $3.7K per month, while roughly 52% of the 5B maximum $WAL supply is circulating

And those 250M contributions from DATA Network don't automatically translate into 250M paid storage transactions on Walrus

I like the idea of bringing an existing user base into the infrastructure instead of waiting years for organic adoption

But I want to see how much actual storage demand follows the migration, especially with more $WAL supply still waiting to unlock

For Sui, I think the longer-term opportunity is building an ecosystem where AI companies can access data, manage ownership and pay contributors without having to piece everything together themselves

Walrus could become an important part of that

I'm more interested in the direction Sui is taking than in chasing $WAL just because of the AI narrative

The next few months should tell us whether these partnerships can finally turn into paying customers

quoted_text:
If Democrats lose in 2026, they lose for a DECADE.

Here's why.

The real fight isn't this election. It's the 2030 Census — the count that redraws every House seat and every Electoral College vote for the entire decade after it.

And here's the part nobody tells you: the Census does not count citizens. It counts TOTAL population. Every person in the state. Voter or not. Legal or not.

That's why the border was never just about compassion. 10M+ people entered under Biden, and they landed heavy in blue states — California, New York, Massachusetts, Colorado. 

Every single one of them inflates those states' seats and electoral votes. 

People who cannot vote, deciding who governs people who can.

Now run it the other way.

Republicans win 2026. Deportations continue. Americans keep fleeing blue states for Texas and Florida. By 2030, the blue-state numbers FALL — and the red-state numbers climb.

The latest 2030 projections, off the Census Bureau's own 2025 estimates:
Texas +4 seats
Florida +2
California -4
Illinois, New York, Oregon, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island — -1 each

That's roughly a 20-electoral-vote swing toward red America.

Win 2026 and the map itself moves. A redder House. A redder Electoral College. New paths to 270 all over the Sun Belt. Democrats wouldn't just lose an election — they'd lose the decade.

22 days out. This is the most important midterm of our lives, because the winners hold power while the 2030 Census gets decided.

Vote Republican. Win the decade.

text:
Robinhood 链：被冷落了一场发布会，换来 CEO 亲自救场。

HOOD Summit '26 上，Robinhood 讲了很多东西，
唯独 Robinhood Chain 几乎没怎么提。

链上的人坐不住了。

今天凌晨 1 点，CEO Vlad Tenev 在 X 上开了 30 分钟 AMA，
1500+ 条回复，问题最集中的就是一个：
“为什么不聊 Robinhood Chain？”

接下来 3 个多小时，官方的动作很密集。拆开看：

1. Vlad 正面认错：“我们哪儿也不去”

一位用户直接说：“为什么发布会不讲 Robinhood 链？很多币圈用户觉得被辜负了。”

Vlad 的回复：
“这个反馈很公平。Summit 要讲的内容太多，但 Robinhood Chain 是我们的重点，我们哪儿也不去。早期来建设的开发者对我们很重要。很快会有更多消息。”

1500+ 赞，是整场 AMA 互动最高的一条回答。

CEO 亲口说“公平”，这个姿态本身就是信号。

2. 链的定位：只做代币化真实资产

有人问 Robinhood 链打算怎么提升使用量。

Vlad 的回答很直接：
Robinhood Chain 为代币化真实资产（RWA）和围绕它的应用而建，
使用量跟着效用走：好资产、好开发者，再接进数百万用户已经在用的 Robinhood 产品。
More to come。

另一个问题是会不会扶持链上头部项目（资助、上线、支持）。
回答：“我们要最好的开发者，并且正在投入。详情很快公布。”

翻译一下：开发者扶持计划大概率在路上。

3. 官方补课：百日成绩单

AMA 结束后 1 个多小时，@RobinhoodCrypto 发了 100 天长文：

· 190+ 只股票代币上线，持有人突破 20 万，覆盖 120+ 个国家，是所有链里最快的
· 股票代币 DEX 交易量 150 亿美元
· Morpho 上存款超 10 亿美元
· 上线以来日活交易者 L2 第一，TVL 超 10 亿，DEX 累计交易量 990 亿美元

结尾一句：“下一个 100 天，现在开始。”

再过一个半小时，又补了一条：
“Robinhood Chain: just getting started.”

LONG 的 Nate、Pons 的 Ozzy，转发和引用一个没落下。

4. 另一条线：AI 交易代理即将上线

AMA 里被问得第二多的，是 Robinhood Agents。

· 什么时候上线？“很快，我们在谨慎推出，先做好再交到所有人手上。”
· 会不会大家都用同类策略，放大市场波动？“代理围绕每个用户自己的目标运作，内置护栏，最终决定权在你。”

Vlad 自己的判断：这是投资方式的下一个大转变。

总结与思考：

这两天官方的打法，是一次很标准的危机公关：
先认错，再表态，然后用数据和口号把情绪接住。

但细看会发现，所有关于链的回答，结尾都是同一类话：
“More to come”“More to share soon”“More details soon”。

态度给足了，干货一条都没有。

开发者扶持计划什么时候落地，
以及 “More to come” 到底兑现成什么。

兑现了，Robinhood 链会迎来第二波；
一直是“很快”，情绪迟早会再次被消耗掉。

$HOOD

非投资建议

text:
下一个 HYPE 究竟在哪？

越来越多人开始寻找“下一个HYPE”，哪里有积分，哪里可能空投，哪个永续合约平台还没有发币，哪个项目能复制Hyperliquid的上涨？

昨天我们讨论，Hyperliquid的持仓规模已经超过OKX，但当日成交量仍有明显差距

这提醒我们，支撑HYPE回购的，最终不是平台讲了多大的故事，而是用户有没有持续交易，协议能不能持续获得收入

所以，寻找下一个HYPE之前，不妨先问：Hyperliquid到底做对了什么？

交易员选择平台，首先要考虑的是能不能顺利成交

盘口深度够不够，大单滑点高不高，下单是否稳定，保证金和仓位管理是否方便。空投可以吸引人来，但奖励结束以后，能把交易员留下来的，仍然是产品本身

有人愿意留下来交易，平台才有持续的手续费；这些手续费能够进一步传导到代币，回购才不只是一次性的宣传动作

今天的收入截图，正好把这条逻辑拆开了

据链上数据统计，Hyperliquid的协议收入约为14.1亿美元，其中原生永续合约贡献约88.5%，现货累计贡献约5040万美元，HIP-3永续合约约2960万美元，USDC储备收益约2320万美元

这不是净利润，也不能把每个统计项目都视为同一种现金收入，但收入结构已经说明：Hyperliquid目前最主要的收入来源，仍然是它最核心的交易业务

不是先把生态规划得足够大，再等用户出现

而是先让一项核心产品被持续使用，再逐步增加市场和收入来源

这也是为什么，“下一个Hyperliquid”不能只看积分人数、空投热度和发币后的市值

还要看，去掉奖励和补贴以后，有多少人愿意继续在这里交易？

同样创造1美元费用，HYPE对应的市值是不是更低呢？

Hyperliquid最近30天App Fees约为1.58亿美元，HYPE流通市值约为190亿至220亿美元

两者相除，大约是120至139倍

SOL约为154至158倍，ETH和BNB都超过1000倍

表面看，HYPE的费用与流通市值之比确实比较突出

但这里不能直接得出“HYPE最便宜”的结论

首先，这个倍数是流通市值除以30天费用，不是市盈率

其次，生态里的应用费用，不一定属于底层代币持有人，也不一定全部进入协议回购。不同平台的费用分配和价值传导方式，并不相同

只看费用有多少，还没有回答：这笔钱最后归谁，又有多少能够转化成代币需求？

Hyperliquid值得讨论的，恰恰是它已经建立了一条从交易活动到协议收入，再到HYPE回购的路径

寻找下一个HYPE，至少要同时回答三个问题：奖励结束以后用户还会不会留下，真实使用能不能创造收入，这些收入又能不能持续传导到代币

只复制积分、空投和发币，并不等于复制了Hyperliquid

下一个HYPE，也许不是那个最会让人期待空投的项目

而是那个空投结束以后，用户仍愿意留下来付费使用的产品

普通人成长最快的捷径，就是少走别人已经走过的弯路。你今天遇到的问题，地球上早就有人踩过坑、找到过答案，临摹就是最快的学习方法之一

text:
昨天大盘往下探，无论是链上还是山寨都出现了大幅度的回撤，我相信后面还是有波行情的，大盘能回调后继续涨，一级可以恢复元气

$Pons 从0.9 一路下杀到现在的0.29，这一波套住了很多人，我也是从0.45的价格一路每日定投，目前成本约在0.33

分析下跌问题：

Pons真正的核心在于销毁机制，Pons对每笔交易收取1%的手续费，其中30%归协议所有，而协议中80%的资金用于购买并销毁 $PONS 

这一机制启动后，到9月初，大约30%的供应量被销毁，让 $PONS的价格上升到约0.9$

最核心原因是销毁机制只有在人们持续发行代币的情况下才能发挥作用，发行量从每天约3.6万枚代币骤降至约6千枚代币，平台收入下降了约88%
收入减少意味着回购减少，也就意味着价格无法维持在高位, 而随着市梦率一下子被打破，价格也是扛不住压力一起倾泻

不过我依然认为这个是优质资产，调整完毕后会有新的大浪在后面， 而上 Robinhood 交易所只是时间问题

Pons 注重合规并且喜欢和时间做朋友，从Defillma 上的数据来看，收入上已经成型触底反弹的信号（并不一定反应在价格）

后续随着大盘的企稳，越来越多想在牛市赚钱的人涌入链上，代币发行增多，收入增加，回购增加，形成新一轮的飞轮

text:
AI 好不容易把服务器内存炒成了暴利生意，中国厂商就准备进来卷了。

昨天长鑫公布了 4F² DRAM 架构的进展，计划年底推出相关服务器 DDR5 产品。美光跌了近 4%，闪迪跌了近 6%，三星和 SK 海力士也跟着跌。

我觉得很多人还没意识到长鑫这次选的切入口有多狠。

TrendForce 有组很有意思的数据，今年一季度，64GB 服务器 DDR5 的单晶圆盈利已经超过了 HBM。AI 抢走大量存储产能，普通 DRAM 也跟着缺货，仅第一季度合约价格就环比暴涨了 93%～98%。

过去全球 DRAM 市场长期由三星、海力士、美光三家主导。AI 的爆发又让它们获得了极强的定价权，连原本周期性很强的普通内存都能卖出惊人的利润。

而长鑫现在已经占到全球 DRAM 营收的 9.5%，上一季度还只有 7.6%。更重要的是，它开始从消费级内存向利润丰厚、认证门槛更高的服务器内存进军。

当然，4F² 的技术进展距离稳定量产还有很长的路，服务器客户也不会轻易换供应商。但只要长鑫能够真正进入这块市场，三巨头就得重新考虑定价和扩产策略。

马斯克说 HBM 更难，我觉得他说得没错，只不过华尔街担心的是另一回事。

中国制造过去最可怕的能力，就是把原本拥有极高利润的产业，硬生生卷回成本竞争。光伏、锂电池都发生过类似的事情。现在存储行业可能也要面对这道题了。

如果长鑫最终能够把服务器 DDR5 的价格打下来，AI 行业的利润分配可能会发生一件很有意思的事，过去靠卖铲子赚走大部分钱的存储巨头，要开始把利润还给买铲子的人了。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined. We saw this with lithium batteries and solar, for example. 

SpaceX is a rare counter-example, where its mass to orbit is roughly an order of magnitude greater than the rest of the world, BUT China now does a majority of non-SpaceX mass to orbit. SpaceX is an anomaly in the matrix. 

Maybe RAM will be different, but RAM was a low margin commodity only ~3 years ago. LP5 and LP6 are designed to a common standard that China seems to be solving fast. 

Newer HBM architectures and things like an SRAM layer below logic and 3D stacking RAM on top of logic while finding a way to keep the logic cooled will be harder to solve.

72 hour update on reseller CryptoBilis incident  🔽

As the investigation continues, we are working with relevant authorities. The volume of impacted devices is limited. We know this is concerning, especially for those directly affected, and we are reaching out to impacted users.

To date, all confirmed cases related to the disclosed draining incident of Oct 9th, 2026, involve devices sold through the Southeast Asia reseller CryptoBilis. Our systems and direct sales channels remain unaffected. 
We take the CryptoBilis situation seriously and are actively investigating.

We encourage impacted users to reach out to Ledger Support through official channels and file complaints with their local law enforcement authorities. As a reminder, CryptoBilis has confirmed having ceased all sales of hardware wallets.

We are reminding our authorized resellers and distributors to source products only through authorized channels and never to restock returned products.

Also, we strongly advise users not to purchase from unauthorized resellers, where the risk of buying suspicious, counterfeit or modified devices is important as nothing operates under ledger security guidelines.

Security isn’t static and this incident underscores why we continuously review and strengthen our distribution and anti-tamper processes. 

We are continuously improving that work now and events like this strengthen our resolution: reviewing authorized reseller controls, advancing hardware protections, and cooperating with authorities. Thanks to @SEAL_911 for their collaborative support and all their efforts.

This is an ongoing threat that doesn’t just impact Ledger, but the whole ecosystem, and we are calling others in the space to work with us on making improvements for users.

We believe in jointly working with researchers, other vendors and partners on improving industry chain-of-custody practices and anti-tamper techniques. Raising the bar on physical supply-chain integrity benefits the entire ecosystem. If you have relevant information, contact security@ledger.com.

For CryptoBilis buyers: do not initialize unused devices. If already set up, move to a new seed on a device from Ledger. If you have concerns that your device was impacted by the CryptoBilis incident, please contact Ledger Support through the official site: https://t.co/JUcWwJO9iF. 

Ledger Support is available 24/7 to answer your questions and concerns.

Scammers often try to take advantage of incidents like this. Rely only on official Ledger channels. Ledger will never call you, DM you, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase.

APAC led global growth in on-chain transaction volume. Over that same period, however, its most established hubs steadily raised their barriers to entry.

So, which APAC market is "winning crypto"?

Vietnam ranks highest for builder conviction in our six-market analysis. Yet it ranks last overall on the Builder Sentiment Index (BSI), which gives greater weight to the conditions businesses need to operate.

How does the most optimistic market end up at the bottom?

That's one of the questions behind the 2026 APAC Crypto Infrastructure Map report, co-authored by ARC and @PreferencesAI, with insights from our network layer at @arcthecommunity.

Pairing qualitative field research with large-scale synthetic modelling, the report examines six markets: Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea, Thailand, Malaysia and Vietnam.

It covers nine sectors: Stablecoins, RWA/DePIN, DeFi/prediction markets, AI, centralised exchanges, funders/VC, macro, robotics and launchpads.

The analysis looks at what it takes to build a crypto business, from licensing and banking access to capital, institutional infrastructure and talent. It also examines builders' expectations and whether conditions are improving.

Hong Kong and Singapore lead the BSI rankings, supported by their strengths in institutional infrastructure and capital depth. Vietnam ranks last despite leading on conviction, reflecting gaps in the infrastructure businesses need to operate once licensed.

The report also explores where each hub's strengths lie. Depending on your priorities, its findings point towards:

- Hong Kong for institutional issuance
- Singapore for raising and holding capital
- South Korea for reaching users at speed
- Vietnam for testing consumer product-market fit
- Malaysia for a faster, realistic path to licensing
- Thailand for tax-efficient retail distribution

The full ARC × PreferencesAI report drops on Wednesday, 14 October.

I have made $2,300 just by holding an NFT in big 2026

Here is how Standard Reserve actually works and how people make money from it.

Their entire system revolves around:

- $STANDARD
- Bank Charters
- Branches
- ETH reserves
- Dynamic emissions
- Buybacks and burns

First, understand the difference.

$STANDARD is the currency, a Charter is your license to operate a bank.

(Branches are what generate income)

Simply holding $STANDARD earns you nothing so you need a Charter with active Branches to receive newly issued tokens.

I only minted the NFT and that was enough to give me a charter, but fyi NFTs are not tradable (in paper)

There were originally 1,000 Genesis Charters.

Each bank can operate up to 10 Branches.

How much can a banker earn?

The protocol starts with a base emission of 700,000 STANDARD per day.

But it adjusts that amount depending on ETH flowing into or out of its Uniswap pool.

Currently:

Emission multiplier: 0.35x
Actual emissions: 245,000 STANDARD/day
Active Branches: 3,419
Earnings per Branch: ~72 STANDARD/day
At $0.288: $21/day

But here we have a problem especially if you are farming

To withdraw your accumulated STANDARD, you must permanently close a Branch.

You lose its future income.

There’s also an exit fee, currently at 4.87%, which can reach 60% when too many bankers leave.

Every three days, the protocol measures net ETH flow.

More ETH entering = potential emission increases.

More ETH leaving = emission cuts.

During expansion, protocol fees help accumulate reserves, including tokenized gold.

During contraction, the protocol uses ETH to buy back STANDARD and burn it.

- 70% of protocol fees go to the active vault.
- 15% goes to permanent protocol-owned liquidity.
- 15% goes to the team.

Branches create another source of demand.

Bankers need to buy expansion licenses using STANDARD.

100% of the tokens spent are burned.

(The latest auction sold 25 licenses, closing at 5,669 STANDARD each)

So bankers expanding their operations directly reduce the token supply.

Basically atm I’m earning money just trying an experiment inside RH 

We will see if an automated monetary system can create enough demand to sustain its own token.

But even looking at how Robinhood is doing these days, I’m confident for the future.

Will keep holding (NFA)

text:
Any L2 is free to become an L1, and vice versa.

But if your L2 always had various human/social vectors of censorship you didn't bother to improve, then what are we doing here?

The threat of AI or quantum breaching elliptic curves in a way that harms crypto users remains purely theoretical. Also, any such attacker would have to breach one user at a time.

But the threat of sequencer censorship or security council upgrades harming all users at once is very real.

And BTW, an L1 with concentrated token ownership (which is almost guaranteed here) is similarly vulnerable. 
An L2 that can unilaterally decide to become an L1 is bound to become a centralized L1.

author: toly

text:
i love writing. i never let agents write for me. whether it's docs, or tweets, or shitposts, or even prompts (okay maybe that one's harder as agents manage other agents) 

there's a simple reason for that: i still strongly believe that writing is thinking. it's a skill i hope to never give up. it's also important to me that whatever i say is always authentic, mistakes and all. my favorite posts are the ones that i just full send without any editing

i suspect it also helps with prompting. being able to clearly express what i want, and knowing the vocabulary i need to be able to direct my agents does seem to make for more effective usage of agents. in the same way that engineers have an advantage when we prompt agents to write code, because we are intimately familiar with the words that make up the discipline

knowing the right word incantations to get an agent to produce a desired goal almost feels like spellcasting. as models get more capable, and that input box looks more and more like a magic box that can output anything, words become the interface between you and the genie

there may come a time when we give up the keyboard in exchange for brain-computer interfaces. but until then, i'm writing every word.

text:
Last month, the contracts powering Magic Eden were exploited to the tune of millions of dollars. I was lucky enough to be in a position to rescue a good portion of that, but it highlighted the danger of leaving approvals open as adversaries get access to better and better tools for finding holes in contract logic. 

Today, Blur announced that they will be deprecating their frontend. 

I've investigated Blur and found no exploits within the current contracts. However, the Blur contracts are upgradable, meaning that they could turn malicious at any time.

They currently have eight figures worth of NFTs approved to them. The safety of those NFTs effectively hinges on the opssec of the Blur team, which appears to be disbanding at this time. 

If you have open approvals to Blur, I recommend you remove them immediately. Use https://t.co/3zfwoDIeZV  or similar to ensure that you are protected in case of a contract exploit or later upgrade.

Don't wait. The time is now.

昨晚 ARCUS 与 RH LIGHTER 又一个重要的发现：对冲刷量，决定成本的不只是策略，还有交易的时段。

  同一套参数，周末期货休市时每 10 万成交只亏 2.2U，期货一开盘就跳到 11U，差了 5 倍。

下面是实测。

 1、结构：Arcus 做空 SPY 永续，Lighter 做多同等数量，价格风险对冲掉，只刷成交量。

 2、 执行：Arcus 挂 maker 单（0 费率），成交后 Lighter 立刻 IOC 对冲。每轮持有 8–12 分钟，入场和出场都要等基差合适才挂单。

 3、 结果：一晚 11 轮，Arcus 成交约 21 万，两边合计磨损约 7U/10万，手续费为 0。

 4、 为什么时段影响这么大：成本主要来自 maker 成交后、对冲完成前那几秒的价格变动。周末 Arcus 价格冻结、期货休市，几乎没有这种变动；行情一活跃，挂单就容易在不利价位被吃掉。之前 QQQ 在工作日盘中甚至到过 17–22U/10万。

 5、 所以接下来工作日只在美股休市的平静时段刷：速度慢一点，但磨损能压在预算内。

$HYDX “Stocks 2.0” narrative has a real-world basis, but for now, its strongest aspects are the sector thesis and product concept. I don't think its commercial revenue has been validated yet.

0xaa5751ff3fb61e613993b2eb4eab1fce017081fc 

HyperDex is not simply trying to bring U.S. stocks onto the blockchain. It aims to integrate tokenized stocks, cross-chain trading aggregation, thematic investment portfolios, and token launches into a single platform. If these components can form a complete ecosystem, its positioning could expand from a trading tool into a financial gateway for stocks and other real-world assets on-chain.

The reason this vision is attractive is that it attempts to connect several previously fragmented markets:

Different stock issuers distribute assets across different chains, forcing users to find separate trading venues.
Buying individual stock tokens provides exposure to a single asset, while thematic baskets can combine multiple assets into one investment.
If lending, yield strategies, and a launchpad are added, these assets would not merely be traded but could also be used to build additional financial products.
If these businesses eventually generate verifiable fee-based buybacks, burns, or holder income for HYDX, platform growth could translate into token value.

This is the main idea behind the market's “Stocks 2.0” narrative. However, among these four points, the product interface and basket functionality have support from existing product pages, while the complete commercial flywheel has not been validated to the same extent.

The First Layer of Evidence: Tokenized Stocks Are Becoming a Real Industry

On July 1, 2026, Robinhood announced the launch of the Robinhood Chain public mainnet, positioning tokenized real-world assets as an important direction for its ecosystem. On October 8, Reuters also reported that Securitize had launched a blockchain-based stock trading service covering publicly listed companies such as Apple, Nvidia, and Microsoft.

This suggests that the market is gradually moving beyond the question of whether stocks can be tokenized toward how these assets can be traded, combined, used as collateral, and put to work.

However, tokenized stocks from different issuers do not necessarily provide the same legal rights, underlying backing, or redemption mechanisms. Tokenization does not automatically mean holders possess all the shareholder rights associated with traditional stocks.

For HyperDex, industry growth creates two main opportunities.

The first is demand for trading access. When tokens representing the same company exist across different issuers and chains, users need to compare prices, liquidity, and cross-chain costs. Aggregators can handle this complexity on their behalf.

The second is demand for financial products. Once tokenized stocks can be transferred and traded on-chain, investment portfolios, collateralized lending, strategy products, and other applications can potentially be built on top of them.

Therefore, “Stocks 2.0” is not an entirely baseless concept. The tokenization of real-world assets has genuine industry momentum. What still needs to be validated is whether HyperDex can capture enough trading activity and market share within this industry.

The Second Layer of Evidence: HyperDex's Product Suite Is Not Just an Idea

HyperDex currently positions itself on its official website as an aggregator for tokenized assets, covering stocks, ETFs, commodities, private credit, and government bonds, while advertising support for more than 50 chains. Its homepage features quote comparisons across DEXs and bridges, aiming to provide cross-chain trading through a single interface.

Its current product strategy can be divided into three components.

1. Stock Aggregation: Handling Fragmented Liquidity for Users

The website lists assets from issuers such as Robinhood, Ondo, xStocks, and Coinbase, alongside quote comparisons across chains and DEXs. The goal is to eliminate the need for users to research which chain a particular stock token is on, who issued it, and which bridge or liquidity pool they need to use.

The real competitive advantage should come from better execution prices, lower transaction costs, and higher routing success rates, rather than simply supporting more chains.

2. Tokenized Baskets: Moving Beyond Individual Stocks to Thematic Investments

The official basket page displays 27 baskets, 142 tokenized stocks, and 4 chains. These include themes such as AI photonics, Neocloud, AI power, robotics, and the Magnificent 7. The page also lists 18 index baskets, approximately $21.6 million in total value, and around $117,300 in 24-hour minting and redemption volume.

The appeal is that these products lower the operational barriers to portfolio investing. Instead of purchasing a dozen stocks individually, users can select a single investment theme.

However, these figures should not be counted directly as HyperDex's own TVL, revenue, or user count. They represent the baskets and aggregated data displayed on the platform, including products from other issuers. HyperDex's value lies in its trading access, discovery, and aggregation services. The entire value of the underlying assets cannot be attributed to the platform.

3. Hyper Agent and Launch: Letting Ordinary Users Interact with Financial Products Through Natural Language

The official website now promotes Hyper Agent, which supports Swap, Earn, and Launch through a chat interface. This shows that the product aims to lower the operational barriers to cross-chain trading and asset creation.

If future data demonstrates that users can reliably execute actual trades, portfolio investments, or token launches through the Agent, HyperDex could move closer to becoming a comprehensive financial gateway. However, there is not yet enough independent data to establish the actual trading volume, retention rate, or launchpad activity generated by the Agent.

Together, these three components make HyperDex more interesting than a simple tokenized-stock trading interface.

However, product breadth does not equal a competitive moat. Cross-chain aggregation, stock baskets, and AI trading interfaces can all be replicated by competitors. Ultimately, HyperDex must build an advantage that retains users through better execution, actual adoption, or greater capital efficiency.

The Third Layer of Evidence: Market Valuations for the Project Are Generally Above $10 Million

This valuation scenario is understandable, but two different questions need to be separated.

The first question is: How much could the platform be worth if the business scales?

If HyperDex eventually becomes a major gateway for tokenized stocks from multiple issuers, its business could encompass trade routing, cross-chain services, thematic investment baskets, collateralized lending, and new asset issuance.

That is a broader business scope than a single launchpad. Its potential value would come from multiple businesses contributing traffic, revenue, and users, rather than depending on a single popular token.

The second question is: How much value would these businesses generate for HYDX?

The evidence here is considerably weaker. Even if a platform generates substantial trading volume, much of the value may remain with underlying issuers, DEXs, bridges, or other partner protocols. The platform token does not necessarily capture a corresponding share of that value.

Therefore, the industry-wide scale of tokenized stocks, the total value of baskets displayed on the website, or the possibility of a future launchpad business cannot directly establish that HYDX should be valued at $10 million or more.

A reasonable valuation analysis needs to answer four questions: How much trading volume can the platform capture? How much net revenue can it retain? How much of that revenue actually flows to HYDX? And can this value capture be sustained over time?

The Most Important Counterargument: The Product Narrative Is Large, but Traceable Revenue Remains Small

I checked HyperDex's revenue and trading aggregation data on DeFiLlama. The page currently shows the following public metrics, which represent a snapshot at the time of the query:

Fees and protocol revenue over the past 30 days: $435.28
DEX aggregation volume over the past 30 days: $51.5K
Cross-chain aggregation volume over the past 30 days: $148.6K
Traceable holder revenue over the past 30 days: $0

These figures are important because they reveal the project's current stage: its product coverage and future potential are substantial, but the traceable trading volume and revenue have not yet reached a comparable scale.

Therefore, fee-based buybacks and burns, as well as stock-related income for holders, should not yet be treated as fully validated value-capture mechanisms. The actual execution of buybacks, the source of buyback funds, the holder distribution contracts, and records of actual payments all need further verification.

What Could Drive the Next Price Appreciation?

I believe the market may be betting on three developments, although their levels of validation differ.

First: Growth in Tokenized Stocks and HyperDex Becoming a Major Aggregation Gateway

This is the largest long-term narrative. As more issuers and chains join the market, aggregation and thematic baskets could gain more use cases.

The real catalysts would be sustained growth in actual trading volume, a better trading experience than competitors, and user retention—not simply adding more supported chains to the website.

Second: Hyper Agent, Baskets, and the Launchpad Forming a Complete Business Loop

If users can discover an investment theme, purchase the corresponding stock basket, execute trades automatically through an Agent, and create new assets, HyperDex could potentially attract both investors and asset issuers.

The validation points are the number of trades actually executed by the Agent, whether basket minting and redemption volumes grow, whether the launchpad achieves sustained issuance and trading activity, and whether these businesses generate additional protocol revenue.

Third: Data-Verified Value Capture for HYDX

This could have the most direct impact on the token's valuation logic. If the project consistently discloses actual buybacks, burns, and holder income—and these amounts grow alongside platform activity—the market would have a clearer basis for connecting business growth to token demand.

Furthermore, given the potential market size and breadth of the business, a $10 million market cap is not an unimaginable figure. However, it cannot yet be considered a valuation justified by the fundamentals.

To support that valuation, we first need to establish three things: whether HyperDex can capture a meaningful share of the market, how much net revenue the platform can retain, and how much of that revenue can be consistently converted into value for HYDX.

One competitive issue deserves particular attention: HyperDex can have a broad range of businesses, but breadth alone does not create a moat. It must demonstrate that it can attract and retain users from existing trading aggregators, cross-chain tools, and stock-basket products, rather than simply combining several popular concepts on one website.

My conclusion is that the “Stocks 2.0” narrative has a genuine industry foundation, and HyperDex's product suite supports that direction. However, HYDX is currently closer to a bet on future business expansion than a mature platform token backed by established revenue.

What matters most going forward is not how many additional features are introduced, but whether actual trading volume, revenue, basket assets, launchpad usage, and on-chain buybacks and holder income grow together.

If these metrics improve consistently, a valuation above $10 million would have a stronger foundation.

text:
People want a tiger put down in Yorkshire because some idiot jumped into its pen. That is ridiculous.
The tiger is only in Yorkshire because we put it there. Tigers do not live in Britain. Someone decided a Yorkshire zoo or wildlife park needed one, so they imported it, built a pen, and charged people to look at it. Then a person climbed or jumped the barrier on purpose and got too close. Now the argument is that the tiger has to die for doing what a tiger does when a human suddenly appears in its space.
That makes no sense. The animal did not choose to be in a concrete enclosure in the middle of Yorkshire. It did not invite anyone in. We created the whole setup—the captivity, the barriers, the viewing area—and then someone ignored the only rule that keeps people safe. Killing the tiger does not fix any of that. It just means the animal pays for human decisions it had nothing to do with.
Yorkshire is not tiger country. Keeping one here already requires constant human management. When the arrangement goes wrong because a person enters the pen, the answer should be better fences, clearer warnings, or a serious look at whether we should be keeping large exotic predators in British enclosures at all. Instead, the loudest response is to demand the tiger’s death as if that restores some kind of order.
It does not. It just lets everyone pretend the real problem was the animal rather than the series of choices that put a tiger in a pen and then let someone jump into it. That is not a serious way to deal with risk. It is people refusing to own their own folly and looking for something else to blame.

text:
Back the market, not just the debt. Price the shock, not just the spread. 

That was one of my key messages when I spoke about financing and  investing in Africa, at the AIM Summit, the leading alternative investment summit, being held in Dubai, UAE. Several hundred decision makers were in the room: hedge funds, sovereign wealth funds, private equity firms, family offices, other asset allocators, and government officials.

The question I was asked: is the main problem for Africa (and other frontier markets) the level of debt, or the cost of borrowing?

My answer: it's not how much Africa owes. It's what it costs, who funds it, and what the borrowing builds.

An example: Africa's borrowing spread fell from about 900 basis points to about 330. Yet yields still rose to 8.77%.
Africa did its part. Africa didn't get riskier. The world got more expensive. Treasury yields are now at 5.4%. The spread is what Africa controls; the base is what Washington controls.

So how should African countries read this environment? Three points.
 
1. This is a new global investment regime, not a storm that will pass. Higher interest rates, expensive energy and selective capital are here to stay. Money now has a price, and it chooses its destinations carefully. Africa should plan for it, not wait for the old world to return.

Many African economies carry moderate debt but pay spreads that reflect fear rather than fundamentals. I call this the “prejudicial premium”.

2. Selective capital is not absent capital. It flows to clarity: credible reforms, transparent frameworks, bankable projects.

Excellent successful examples: the $12.5 billion Bishoftu International Airport in Ethiopia, one of the 10 largest in the world when completed, has drawn interest from financiers in the U.S., China, Europe, Japan, the Middle East and Asia. Same for Dangote's successful $20 billion oil refinery in Nigeria.
 
3. Africa must reduce its dependence on foreign, dollar -denominated debt.
 Africa has a $4 trillion domestic pool of capital. Putting it to work means: • deeper domestic capital markets • local currency funding • pension and insurance pools investing at home • listed companies that give investors a way in

My message to African economies:

Don't ask only, "How much do we owe?" Ask: What does it cost us? Who funds us? What does it build?

text:
这是我对目前主流模型的排名，这是一个综合性的排名，而非单纯智力比较。（当然，我也有张纯智力的排名图，我会放在评论区做比较）

我考虑的维度有：智力、性价比、速度、易用性

无论怎样，Opus 5.5 毫无疑问是#1，A档我给到 Fusion(Opus 5.5+SWE-2)，Fable 5.1 和 Astra

B档有 SWE-2 、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、Haiku 5.5。他们不是最顶尖的模型，但其中 SWE-2 有非常强大的 coding 能力，而 deepseek和 haiku 有着非常快的速度。而且他们同样都有大的惊人的额度。

C 档中 Step 5 算是新出现的模型。它的智力水平和同档其他模型差距不大，但速度非常快，而且模型额度很大；6.1 Sol 在 Codex 几乎不是一个能用的模型，但考虑到在第三方 Agent 中表现不错，所以给到 C。其他都是老生常谈，GLM 和 Kimi 只需要一次更新。

G 档由 Grok 4.7 独占。我从来没见过这么弱智的模型，连一句正常话都说不出来，额度还少。建议直接用 Grok 4.6，这个模型还是不错的。

text:
Update from Ledger Donjon on the CryptoBilis investigation 🔽

@DonjonLedger is investigating Ledger signers sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, that contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Ledger confirmed this on October 10th for one affected user's signer. All confirmed fund losses tied to the incident disclosed on October 9th involve signers sold through CryptoBilis. We have not verified a drain linked to a signer bought elsewhere. CryptoBilis has confirmed it stopped selling Ledger signers while the investigation continues.

Based on the Donjon's analysis of the attack, the implant sits inside the enclosure and reads the data shown on the screen. During setup, the signer displays the 24-word recovery phrase. When the implant detects these screens, its microcontroller decodes the words and transmits them over LTE using a provisioned eSIM. The implant is a separate component. It does not modify the Secure Element or the Ledger operating system, and it does not alter transactions or signatures.

The Donjon will analyze the signers it receives and will share more as the investigation continues.

We have not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost. Figures circulating online come from third parties and Ledger has not fully verified them. If your funds were drained and you have not contacted us, please do so through Ledger Support so we can include your case. We are also reviewing reports of implants in other signers and locations. We will continue to share information as the investigation progresses. Rest assured the Ledger team is going above and beyond to leave no stone unturned to investigate this situation to the strongest possible outcome.

If you bought a Ledger signer from CryptoBilis and have not set it up, do not set it up and contact Ledger Support. If you have set it up, transfer your assets promptly to a new signer with a new recovery phrase. Do not enter or restore any recovery phrase on a signer bought from CryptoBilis. Never enter your recovery phrase into a website, app or form.

If you lost funds or hold a tampered signer, contact Ledger Support at https://t.co/QzukOZdEzq and file a report with local law enforcement. Do not send the signer to anyone before speaking with Ledger Support or local law enforcement. If you lost funds, coordinate with law enforcement before opening the signer. Researchers and others with relevant information can write to security@ledger.com.

If you did not buy from CryptoBilis and want to inspect the inside of your signer, the guide is at https://t.co/Bh9DHQulIv. Use caution and make sure your recovery phrase is backed up first, because opening a signer can damage it.

Ledger will never call you, message you directly, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase. We will update this post when we verify new information.

text:
为什么美债利率下跌？半导体科技股反而下跌？
传统理论认为利率下跌利好股票，但这只是第一层。
这次的原因是债券市场认为，AI融资是推高美债收益率的关键原因，如果AI降低融资额度，虽然对半导体不利，但是对降低美债收益率是有效的，市场很显然在表示：AI融资引发的半导体可持续增长和美债收益率，只能二选一。
市场选择美债而不是半导体。

Pacing is out the window. For it to work, every American lab needed to be on board, Mark Zuckerberg has repeatedly made it clear that he is not interested. Mark has a staggering amount of compute and has been all in on compute capex for years; even in the face of some investor opposition he never stopped building his infra once. text:
I found a critical safety issue in one major new consensus protocol in the blockchain sector.

The protocol had been formally verified, HOWEVER the formally verified protocol is not the same as the pseudocode.

This appears to be the same scenario that OpenAI has run into with Navier-Stokes.

If this had gotten into production it could have triggered a catastrophic failure, since only a small portion of stake could have broken safety.

The protocol in question is Fast Tendermint. It lets a single Byzantine validator (out of 5f+1) make honest validators decide different values. With 2 validators, equivocation is not even required.

Paper with two fixes and proofs: https://t.co/vj5Qdtwebx

Disclaimer: The authors also specified they consider the formally verified protocol the source of truth.

Last week, Robinhood Chain turned 100 days old.

In the history of TradFi, which took generations to change, that’s a blink of an eye. Onchain, where markets move from idea to existence overnight and assets reach people in milliseconds, a lot can happen — and a lot has.

Robinhood Chain was built to close that gap.

100 days is early days in the life of a new chain, but our initial growth says a lot about why we built it.

✔️ 190+ Stock Tokens are live, and they reached 200K holders faster than on any chain yet. That’s people in 120+ countries gaining exposure to U.S. equities, access that’s still out of reach for billions of people around the world.

✔️ $15B in Stock Token DEX volume proves what’s possible once utility is brought onchain and made composable: new liquidity, new features, and, on Robinhood Chain, pairings people never imagined. 

Giving builders the tools to experiment, form new communities, and ship globally is why building onchain is so powerful and unique. 100 days of Stock Tokens in DeFi has made that clear. From perps to agents and lending markets, the opportunities are out there for anyone who wants to build.

✔️ $1B+ deposited on Morpho on Robinhood Chain. Lending and borrowing, open to anyone, in a world where 1.3 billion adults still don’t have a bank account.

✔️ Robinhood Chain has been the #1 L2 for daily active traders since launch, with $1B+ in TVL and $99B+ in cumulative DEX volume. None of this would be possible without everyone who came here to build and every trader who jumped into the trenches from day one.

Rome wasn’t built in a day (or 100 days), and Robinhood Chain won’t be either. We have more work to do, and we’re excited about what’s next. 

More users, more experiments, more milestones, and more reasons why TradFi and DeFi building on the same rails unlocks a better, more open future for finance.

The next 100 days starts now.

text:
During the research for this project, Opus agents made an interesting discovery: a LIDAR scan of the aircraft carrier.

On their own initiative, they realized that in 2024, Washington State DNR did an aerial LIDAR survey... which included Puget Sound. 

"Could this LIDAR data include the Nimitz?" they wondered. They investigated. Sure enough, they matched raw LIDAR point data to what could only be a huge ship. 

It was the Nimitz. 

Nimitz was alongside at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard in Bremerton, Washington, for a maintenance period. She happened to be under the survey aircraft's flight path, so she's in the public Geospatial data.

(sources in comments)

With that public-but-buried data, Opus was able to match the model to nearly-exact dimensions from the laser scan.

How much other data like this is hiding in plain sight?

text:
ReplaySSM now runs in production in GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3, and ships in TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, FlashInfer, and SGLang!

It speeds up standard decoding (up to 1.47x) and speculative decoding (up to 2.1x), and now also enables a low-precision SSM state whose rounding error never propagates through the recurrence.

Building on our earlier ReplaySSM work, we collaborated with @NVIDIA to pin down what the method really unlocks. Caching SSM inputs instead of the state is what ReplaySSM does. What it changes is that computing the output and updating the state can be separated during decoding. All three gains follow from that separation.

Joint blog post, paper, and code with @NVIDIA and @tri_dao 👇

为了那点百来 U 的 LP 奖励和平台积分，一直死扛到今天
结果打开钱包，U 全没了，账户里剩下的全是 PONS，几千刀蒸发

这个剧本在 Pump fun 时代就演过无数遍，但很多人还是没看懂

给没接触过链上 LP 的朋友人话补充几句：
- 做 LP 就是给池子提供两种币，吃手续费和一些项目方给的额外奖励
- 价格暴跌时，池子会自动把你的 U 换成跌麻的那个币
- 换句话说，价格跌得越凶，你手里的 U 就越少，烂币就越多
- 看着是百分之几十年化，一次价格腰斩就全赔进去，还倒亏

发射台币跌到「APY 看起来还很高」的时候，往往就是最危险的时候
APY 看着高，一次腰斩全还回去
LP 奖励救不了价格，积分也救不了

❚ Vlad Tenev 一句「哪儿也不会去」，把评论区吵翻了

就在刚才，Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev 在 X 开 AMA 聊 HOOD Summit '26。一开口就 19 万阅读、2144 赞，社区热度不低

一个叫 justhodlthebag 的老哥第一时间下场质疑：
「为什么你一句 RobinHood Chain 都没提？加密领域有很多用户感到失望」
这条质疑 1.7 万阅读、209 赞，踩到了一堆人的痛点

Vlad 当场回了一段，原话大意：
「公平的反馈，峰会涵盖了很多内容」
「但 RobinHood Chain 对我们来说是重中之重，我们哪儿也不会去」
「那些早早现身的建设者对我们很重要，很快会有更多分享」

这条回复 12.6 万阅读、1438 赞、293 转，评论区快吵翻了

单看文本好像也没啥
但「哪儿也不会去」这几个字在加密圈分量很重
我们这个圈子最怕的从来不是跌价，是 soft rug
人没了，TG 不回了，推特不发了，筹码慢慢阴跌，一拖就是一年半

CEO 在价格最惨、社区质疑最大的时候亲自开麦承诺「我们不走」，是另一种意义的止跌信号

Flap 在 BNB 链上也走过类似路径：冷启动 -> 社区质疑 -> CZ 催化 -> 二段起飞

这种时间点的高管表态，通常对应着一次链级别生态的底部？

❚ 几个可以提前思考的点

1/ RH 的分发优势，一般 L2 比不了
Robinhood 本身是美股券商，核心用户 2800 万+ 规模
一旦链上功能和 Robinhood 主端打通，哪怕只接入 10% 的用户，对现在整个 RH 链生态都是降维打击
对标 MetaMask 之于 Linea，Robinhood 之于 RH 链是同一个逻辑，但量级大一个数量级

2/ 「加大对早期建设者投入」里藏着的信息
Vlad 原话特意提了「早早现身的建设者对我们很重要」
翻译过来就是，之前跟 RH 链走到现在的项目方，大概率会有额外的资源倾斜
PONS、STONK 作为 TVL 和交易量都留在链上的头牌，排在最前面

3/ 「更多细节即将公布」通常不是客套
加密圈 CEO 用这几个字，往往对应着两周内会有具体动作
可能是生态基金、可能是主端功能、可能是新合作
注意观察官方账号接下来两周的动作

❚ 我的参与方式和保留

我手里有 PONS 现货，深度套牢
现在的策略不是加仓抄底，也不是割肉认输，不建议持有LP

- 如果真有二段，币又会被池子提前卖掉，吃不满涨幅。两头都不划算。
- 如果没有二段，LP 只是在下跌里被池子不断换成更多 PONS，那点奖励覆盖不了

不如直接拿现货，涨跌都看得明白

Vlad 这次是真续命，还是又一次公关表态，还得看接下来两周有没有真东西。我不建议任何人无脑冲，只建议大家别再做 LP 送钱了

text:
好一个黑暗森林！
从2020到2026，币圈反复证明：买到币只是开始，保得住、拿得出，才算过关。

放在CEX：
怕被盗、被冻结、被挪用；开了杠杆，还得怕爆仓。
你以为账户里是资产，出事后才知道，也可能是债权。

换成硬件钱包：
不开源，担心黑箱；开了源，也不能保证实物没被动过手脚。还会被加元件！

你买保险柜，别人往里面加窃听器。
还有假设备、掉包设备、预设助记词、物理攻击、假配套软件。
再加盲签、恶意授权、忘记PIN、丢失备份、忘记passphrase。
你防住别人，也可能成功防住自己。

用PC钱包：
假安装包、木马、远控、剪贴板劫持，轮番上场。
钱包文件被偷，弱密码遭离线破解；硬盘坏了、系统重装，没备份又是一道死题。
随机数生成再出问题，助记词长也未必救得了你。

用Web钱包：
托管型，要信平台；非托管型，也得信送到浏览器里的代码。
假域名、搜索广告、官网被篡改、恶意脚本，都能把“恢复钱包”变成“交出秘密”。
你以为网页长得一样，就是同一个钱包。

用插件钱包：
假的会偷，真的也可能被投毒。
2023年Ledger Connect Kit出事；2025年底Trust Wallet官方插件2.68版本遭供应链攻击。
你以为更新堵漏洞，这次更新却给钱包开了洞。

用手机钱包：
防假App、防恶意软件、防云端泄露，还得防自己忘记iPhone解锁码。
如果最终只能抹掉手机，而钱包恢复材料仅存在本机、又没有可用备份，币还在链上，你却没了入口。
记得Apple账户密码，不等于拿得回钱包秘密。

认真做备份：
截图进云相册，文件进网盘，助记词进密码管理器。
LastPass旧泄露事件的盗币后果延续多年。
你以为事情过去了，别人只是还没破解完。

转个账：
剪贴板换地址，地址投毒污染记录，假二维码换收款人。
2024年有人误转约6800万美元，后来退回；2025年又出现近5000万USDT的同类事件。
你核对首尾，骗子也专门给你做了相似首尾。

冲个MEME：
假官宣、假背书、刷量拉盘、限制卖出、高额卖出税、抽池、砸盘。
代币一个没少，本金却没了。
你以为自己是早期投资者，别人把你当退出流动性。
群里喊“钻石手”，后台忙着卖出。

玩DApp、跨链、DeFi：
骗签名、骗授权，桥出事、池子出事、管理员密钥出事。
你保住私钥，没保住存进去的本金。
旧授权还可能一直有效：你忘了项目，它还握着花你代币的权限。

遇到“稳赚机会”：
假量化、假套利、假挖矿、假质押。
先让小额提现，再诱导大额充值；最后收税费、解冻费、保证金。
你以为遇到贵人，对方以为等到客户。

用上AI：
黑客也有AI。
辅助找漏洞、写恶意程序、做假网站、定制钓鱼，再配上伪造声音和视频。
你用AI研究怎么赚钱，黑客用AI研究怎么拿走你的钱。
把钱包权限交给AI代理，还得防提示注入。
你让AI读网页，黑客把网页写成了给AI的指令。
强私钥没被AI“算破”，秘密却可能被你授权交出去。

丢币后想追回：
假客服、假侦探、假恢复专家继续收费。
第一拨骗你的币，第二拨骗你想拿回币的心。

躲过线上，还有线下：
抢劫、绑架、胁迫转账。
密码学扛得住计算，人未必扛得住暴力。

就算没人偷、没人骗：
助记词丢了，密码忘了，文件坏了，多签凑不齐人，分片凑不齐份数。
甚至人走了，家人根本不知道怎么取。

丢币的道路千万条，总有一条等你疏忽。

买币时以为自己是投资者。保币后发现，还得兼任安全专家、硬件验货员、合约审计员、档案管理员和保镖。如今，还得管好AI的权限。

Serenity的最新观点

1. 存储：风险收益比最好

$MU 、三星、SK海力士：需求可见度延伸至2030—2031年，长期合同锁定产能，部分可能有价格底线。

三星：据称70%产能锁定至2031年，2027E PE仅约3倍。
$SNDK ：2030年前后毛利率有望超过80%。

② 光通信：2027—2028年最具爆发力

$LITE 产能据称售罄至2029年，基本面极强，但估值偏贵。
$AAOI 光模块产能快速扩张，收入和利润有望数倍增长。
$SIVE 规划超1亿单位激光器产能，ASP上涨带来巨大盈利弹性。
$MTSI 2027年扩产，受益于光电器件供应瓶颈。
住友电工、古河电工：光通信供应链潜在受益者。

3. AI芯片：需求依然极其强劲

$NVDA FY2028收入增长预期约70%。
$AVGO  2027—2028年增长预期极高，供应受限。
 $MRVL：FY2031收入目标700亿—900亿美元。
$INTC：CPU供给瓶颈值得关注。

4.算力租赁：短期谨慎，中期关注拐点

$IREN：Anthropic大单利好，但巨额CapEx和ATM融资压制股价。
$NBIS：类似案例，签约后市场未立即认可，收入兑现才可能触发重估。

⑤ 高估值软件：谨慎

$CRWD、$PLTR：避险资金涌入，但估值已经过高。
$GLW、$RMBS：不能简单与拥有稀缺产能的光通信公司同等定价。

Serenity的核心结论：

存储看确定性，光通信看利润弹性，算力租赁等融资结束和收入兑现。

AI产业链正在从普涨转向分化，真正值得买的是产能稀缺、掌握定价权、盈利拐点临近、前瞻PE快速压缩的公司。

当前市场最大的机会，可能恰恰来自无差别杀跌造成的错杀。

Sure... Random train of thoughts on markets now, optics like $LITE / memory + $IREN / Anthropic. 

On Memory: 

- Demand visibility on $MU / Samsung / SK Hynix extend into 2030-2031. 

Samsung has LTAs covering 70% of their capacity into 2031 (likely with SK Hynix type price floors)... and their operating profit is already absurd.  

There's a consensus that shortage in 2027 will be much more severe than 2026... Even $SNDK expends gross margins to exceed 80% entering 2030. 

You're going to hear Acer and other CEOs that want memory prices to go down cite bear cases like CXMT/YMTC, and Chinese players. 

But just looking at supply procurement that $NVDA is doing + hyperscalers, demand visibility is absurd for the next 5 years. And by that time, cumulative FCF coming in from these take/pay + pricing floor contracts might exceed some of their entire marketcaps so it feels like there's some baseline.  

Near-term is always volatile (IV dropped a ton across $EWY to $DRAM to $MU), so people with call options likely got nuked, along with underlying prices. 

But if Samsung is 3x 2027E, has 5 year LTAs with 70% of capacity committed from hyperscalers, and price floors, it's kinda hard to see these names suffer a sustained crash...   

For optics: 

- $LITE is literally sold out into 2029, starting discussions into 2030.  With demand visibility lasting into 2031… with hyperscalers largely funding the capacity buildout.  

Their 2028 Greensboro fab expansion was ~$5B in UHP laser capacity revenue alone, yet it’s basically allocated toward $NVDA (50%+ with options for more) and co from channel checks. 

Existing supply chain bottlenecks are extremely severe as optical content/XPU skyrockets entering 2027-2028.

So everything from DSPs/TIAs, photodiodes, lasers, InP/SOI substrates, wafers (epi, SOI, etc) are expected to go brrr. 

And what does that imply to anyone else with enormous amounts of capacity coming online like $AAOI + $SIVE + $MTSI capacity expansion in 2027? Or other players like Sumitomo / Furukawa? 

But again it's not quite the same situation as memory since the BOM % is extremely low in a cluster... If micron/samsung raised another 2000% hyperscalers would go bankrupt. But doing that for InP substrates seems possible. Or a 100% increase on CW laser content. 

I actually thought $LITE was overvalued at $100B+ MC, relative to capacity expansion on your smaller optical players to their respective MCs. So I chose to position accordingly (But lumentum does deserve premiums for demand visibility). 

For the companies leading the charge like $NVDA / $AVGO / $MRVL:

- Nvidia has 70% forward revenue growth FY2028 which is supply constrained growth. 
- Broadcom 100% Y/Y for 2027/2028 which is also supply constrained growth. 
- Marvell FY2031 upgraded guidance to $70B-$90B from $46B analyst projections... 

They all seem to be very happy.... and read through on demand for next 2-3 years is enormous (also echoing what $INTC CEO said today on the panel with $AVGO CEO).  

So you have overwhelming growth on memory + photonics + from the leaders... But the nuance is not everything in the AI supply chain get the same economic benefit. 

HBM/Laser/CPU/MLCC and other players in the bottlenecks look to be printing money. And seem to be the largest beneficiaries of the current bottlenecks. 

Test players are also getting price hikes + capacity allocated by players like $NVDA, but economic impact seems a tad lower than other players since forward P/E for many I modeled were still in the 45x+ range even if you hiked prices like 10-30%. 

As for capex intensive players... there's some like $IREN ($25-30B for 2027) that despite a deal with Anthropic ended up dropping.  I don't think markets seem to appreciate players spending a lot of money + ongoing financing (think they're like halfway through their $6B ATM). 

Just some hopium for $IREN investors, $NBIS also signed a deal with $META at the start of the year (but markets didn't care at all, since Nebius dropped to ~$70-80 at the lowest point?). 

But did 6 months later, as the time to revenue inflection gets closer and you're past the ATM/capex window, markets would likely care more. 

I don't think it's irrational but at the same time, the fundamentals have improved from Mirantis acquisition to others. I also think it was known for awhile it was either OpenAI/Anthropic from CEO comments earlier too? 

But either way to be a more risk-off environment where funds seem to be rotating to larger names as a flight to safety.

$CRWD / $PLTR  as just two example, but my take is that the valuations of these rotations are reaching clown levels. And that certain AI supply chain beneficiaries in comparison are undervalued now. 

I was thinking markets would just rotate to names that are extremely profitable like Samsung or names that have <2X P/E, so it was surprising to see $KOSPI and some legacy memory players get sold off today. 

Since all of this is colliding with uncertainty about sht macro environments and renewed sustainability concern of AI capex/commitments from frontier labs like OpenAI/Anthropic from due to that FT piece recently. I've always been sounding the alarm about the contractual backlog OpenAI has with $CBRS, $MSFT, $ORCL and others earlier in the year. But OpenAI did just raise $122B or so , so I don't quite think they're at risk of going down anytime soon. 

I also don't think overall capex can just exponentially go up, but even if it stalls / hovers around a certain point or even drops...

Capex toward certain areas like optics will still explode as hyperscalers fight over allocations when CPO scale up comes about, but might drop in others where more capacity comes online like test or DRAM. So it's a lot more nuanced than capex down = everything down or vice versa.   

I also slightly agree with community agreements that open weight models wouldn't lessen demand on AI infrastructure (otherwise $NVDA wouldn't be funneling funds into Reflection), but all the contractual obligations that Anthropic has might get messy if their models/company get cannibalized. 

Either way, I'd expect some of these frontier lab valuations to likely compress but I do think Jensen knows what he's doing though to avoid contagion.

But basically: 

- Extremely difficult market now, can't just throw money at any AI supply chain company like $GLW and expect it to go up. There's cause for concern of rate hikes mixed with financing per $AVGO CEO but not to the point you just blindly sell off everything.

Also I think markets are stupid and ties baskets together so that leads to mispricing + individual buying opportunities with certain chokepoints too.

If capacity + demand is visible and forward p/e compresses like $AAOI to single digits off hundreds or thousands of percent growth from hyperscalers off $471m transceiver revenues and hundreds of thousands of monthly ELSFP capacity. Or $SIVE coming online with 100M+ laser capacity + multiple foundries with ASP hikes on lasers. I wouldn't lump them into other AI supply chain names in IP like $RMBS or others. 

My take is that AI supply chain beneficiaries with closer inflection points, demand visibility, and forward P/E compressing due to economic leverage would likely outperform medium term despite current volatility. 

TLDR: 
- Memory strongest risk/adjusted return with LTAs + pricing floors extending to 2030's + buybacks. 
- My opinion is that optical supercycle for 2027-2028 with CPO/NPO is going to look absurd relative to capacity coming online of smaller suppliers. 
- Overwhelming fundamentals/growth colliding with sht macro + media scares
- Markets are stupid and groups things in baskets and sells them all off together or buys overvalued names, creating short/long opportunities

I'd give a prayer to people on short term options given underlying drop + IV decline, but there could be a reversal... who knows. Most valuable thing right now is time.

The teams and I are focused on the CryptoBilis incident.

If you bought a Ledger signer from CryptoBilis and have not set it up, do not set it up. If you have set it up, transfer your assets promptly to a new signer with a new recovery phrase. Ledger will never call you, message you directly or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase.

Ledger is reviewing its reseller controls and anti-tamper protections. We invite researchers and other vendors to work with us on tamper-detection and chain-of-custody practices. quoted_text:
Update from Ledger Donjon on the CryptoBilis investigation 🔽

@DonjonLedger is investigating Ledger signers sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, that contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Ledger confirmed this on October 10th for one affected user's signer. All confirmed fund losses tied to the incident disclosed on October 9th involve signers sold through CryptoBilis. We have not verified a drain linked to a signer bought elsewhere. CryptoBilis has confirmed it stopped selling Ledger signers while the investigation continues.

Based on the Donjon's analysis of the attack, the implant sits inside the enclosure and reads the data shown on the screen. During setup, the signer displays the 24-word recovery phrase. When the implant detects these screens, its microcontroller decodes the words and transmits them over LTE using a provisioned eSIM. The implant is a separate component. It does not modify the Secure Element or the Ledger operating system, and it does not alter transactions or signatures.

The Donjon will analyze the signers it receives and will share more as the investigation continues.

We have not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost. Figures circulating online come from third parties and Ledger has not fully verified them. If your funds were drained and you have not contacted us, please do so through Ledger Support so we can include your case. We are also reviewing reports of implants in other signers and locations. We will continue to share information as the investigation progresses. Rest assured the Ledger team is going above and beyond to leave no stone unturned to investigate this situation to the strongest possible outcome.

If you bought a Ledger signer from CryptoBilis and have not set it up, do not set it up and contact Ledger Support. If you have set it up, transfer your assets promptly to a new signer with a new recovery phrase. Do not enter or restore any recovery phrase on a signer bought from CryptoBilis. Never enter your recovery phrase into a website, app or form.

If you lost funds or hold a tampered signer, contact Ledger Support at https://t.co/QzukOZdEzq and file a report with local law enforcement. Do not send the signer to anyone before speaking with Ledger Support or local law enforcement. If you lost funds, coordinate with law enforcement before opening the signer. Researchers and others with relevant information can write to security@ledger.com.

If you did not buy from CryptoBilis and want to inspect the inside of your signer, the guide is at https://t.co/Bh9DHQulIv. Use caution and make sure your recovery phrase is backed up first, because opening a signer can damage it.

Ledger will never call you, message you directly, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase. We will update this post when we verify new information.

author: madhavjha
quoted_text:
I am a member of the Norwegian Nobel Committee.

There are five of us. Five people, appointed by a parliament most of the planet could not find on a map, who decide, once a year, which human being the world has agreed to call good.

I know. I know. I think about it on the tram.

We meet in a building on Henrik Ibsens gate, a street named after a man who wrote almost exclusively about people discovering they are frauds, which nobody on the committee finds funny except me. There is a room with a long table and the portraits of the dead laureates looking down, Mandela, the Dalai Lama, a great many earnest men in spectacles, and one portrait we do not discuss, which is Kissinger, 1973, awarded while the bombs were still falling, after which two of our predecessors resigned and the satirist Tom Lehrer said political satire was now obsolete. We keep him on the wall. A reminder. Every family has the uncle.

It is October in Oslo, which means the sun gives up around four in the afternoon like a civil servant, and it rains the particular Norwegian rain that isn’t quite falling, just hanging there, judging you. I arrive with wet shoes. I always arrive with wet shoes. There is coffee, because this is Norway and there is always coffee, we drink more of it per person than almost anyone alive, and someone’s wife has sent kanelboller, the cinnamon buns, and we sit, five Norwegians, damp, caffeinated, sugared, and we decide the moral standing of the entire species.

Let me tell you how it actually works, because the world imagines a cathedral and it is, I promise you, a book club with a mandate.

287 nominations this year. 208 people, 79 organizations. Anyone can nominate, that’s the secret nobody understands: a professor, a parliamentarian, a former laureate, so the “nominee” list is meaningless, it’s a suggestion box, and every autumn some congressman nominates his own golden retriever and the press writes “SHORTLISTED.” Nobody is shortlisted. There is no short list the public ever sees. There is us, and the coffee, and the rain, and the portraits, and a Norwegian stubbornness that is older than the prize itself.

We read reports. The institute’s advisers write them, thick dull documents, and we argue. Our chairman told the BBC once that in the final meeting “there is a high temperature.” High temperature, for a Norwegian, means someone slightly raised an eyebrow and then apologized for it. We don’t do high temperature. We do a long silence, and then Kristin says “well,” and everyone knows exactly what “well” meant, and it’s settled. That’s our shouting. “Well.” You’d have to be raised here to hear the violence in it.

Now. This year. I will not say the name, because we never say the name, but you know the name.

A certain head of state wanted this prize the way a child wants a thing in a shop window, which is to say loudly, and in public, and with the full belief that wanting it was itself the argument. He said he deserved it. He said he’d ended eight wars, a number that grew most times he said it, like a fish. He had other heads of state phone us. Israel’s prime minister posted it on the internet, “Give him the Nobel.” The leaders of Cambodia and Pakistan announced they’d nominated him, as though announcing it were part of it, as though we tally mentions. A man flew around the globe collecting endorsements for a Norwegian committee the way you’d collect signatures for a petition to the council about a noisy dog.

And here, uff da, is the detail I treasure, the one that makes me smile into my coffee. The nomination deadline is the 31st of January. He took office on the 20th. So for all the phone calls, all the posts, all the gilded lobbying, the only nominations that could possibly count for this year’s prize were filed in the first eleven days of his term, before he had, by his own arithmetic, ended a single one of the eight wars. He campaigned all year for a prize whose window had shut while he was still hanging up his coat. We didn’t have to reject him. The calendar did. We just watched. Norwegians are very good at watching. We have long winters.

People think we sit there weighing his deeds. We don’t. That’s the thing I can’t make the world understand. We’re not grading his homework. We don’t owe anyone the prize for a ceasefire, however real, however loud the announcement. “He made peace” is not a sentence that ends in a medal, the way he believes it does, the way he believes every good thing ends in his name on it. The will of a dead Swede says the prize goes to whoever did the most for fraternity between nations. A dead Swede, I should add, who made his entire fortune inventing dynamite and selling arms, and spent his last years horrified at his own obituary, which called him a merchant of death, and so bought his way to immortality as a man of peace. The whole prize is one guilty arms dealer’s attempt to launder his name. We are, all of us, administering a dead man’s public relations. I find this clarifying. It keeps me humble. It should keep everyone humble, and it keeps, by my count, no one humble at all.

So who did we give it to?

An eighty-five-year-old woman. A judge. Born in Durban, under apartheid, granddaughter of a Tamil man who came to South Africa as indentured labor, a bus driver’s daughter from the poor Indian quarter, who became the first non-white woman to run a law practice in her province, who defended Mandela’s people when defending them was dangerous, who sat on the Rwanda tribunal and the court at the Hague, and who, at eighty-five, is right now a judge weighing whether a genocide is a genocide. When we told the world, our chairman said the rule of law “underpins the system we have set up to ensure peace,” and that “peace requires justice.” She wasn’t even in Oslo. She was in Nuremberg. In courtroom 600. The actual room where they tried the Nazis. You cannot stage that. God staged that, and God, it turns out, is a better satirist than any of us.

She did not phone us. She did not post. No prime minister demanded it for her on the internet. She had, as far as our deliberations are concerned, the one qualification the loud man could never manufacture, which is that she wanted the work and not the medal. The medal finds those people. It flees the ones who chase it. This is not a rule we wrote. It’s just the only pattern the hundred-odd years of our mistakes has ever shown.

The reaction from across the ocean was immediate. His spokesman posted that we “place politics over peace.” Ja. Perhaps. We’re five damp pensioners in a rainy city; of course it’s political, it was always political, it was political when we gave it to a sitting American president nine months into his first term for the promise of things he had not yet done, and we have been quietly embarrassed about that one for fifteen years, so believe me, we had a particular reason this year to prefer a woman with fifty years of verdicts behind her over a man with eight wars in front of him and a deadline already behind him.

Here is what he will never understand, the thing I’d tell him on the tram if he ever took one. We are the one prize he cannot buy, cannot post his way to, cannot have a friendly dictator phone in for him. Not because we’re incorruptible, nei, we’re as vain and wrong and human as the portraits on our wall. But because the entire point of the thing, the only power a small cold country’s book club has ever held, is that it goes to the person not performing the wanting. The moment you demand it, you’ve proven you don’t understand what it’s for, and proving that is itself the disqualification. He ran the most expensive campaign in the history of the prize and the campaign was the reason. He was never losing to Navi Pillay. He was losing to the concept.

It’s dark now. Four o’clock dark. The buns are gone. Kristin said “well” an hour ago and we all went home. I’m on the tram with my wet shoes, and somewhere across the water a very powerful man is explaining to a camera that the prize is rigged, that we’re corrupt, that he’ll win it next year, and he genuinely might, we’re only five idiots and we’ve been wrong before, Kissinger is still on the wall.

But not this year. This year an old woman in Nuremberg, in the room where the law once stared down the exact kind of man who thinks wanting a thing loudly enough should make it his, got a phone call she didn’t ask for.

That’s the job. We don’t reward the man who ends the war and announces it.

We reward the woman who spent fifty years deciding what a war was.

He’ll never see the difference. That’s rather the whole point of him.

Takk for i dag. I have to change trams.

11 年刑期，6.1 万枚比特币，敛财 400 亿的钱志敏和被“原价打发”的受害者。

轰动全球的比特币跨国洗钱案最近迎来了关键判决。

英国高等法院正式裁定：这批查获的 6.1 万枚比特币的财产追索权，应适用中国法，而非英国法。

这就意味着，英国政府或许成了这起世纪大案的最大赢家，而中国那 12.8 万受害者却只能被“原价打发”。

因为适用中国法，受害者大概率只能按当初被骗的法币“本金+利息”去追偿。当年钱志敏卷走 400 亿后以不到 3000 元的均价扫货，这批比特币被动锁仓 7 年暴涨了近 200 倍。

如今扣除清退受害者本金后剩下的数百亿暴利，受害者一分钱拿不到，极大概率会直接落入英国政府的口袋。

更具讽刺意味的是，这场漫长的官司还伴随着巨大的市场回撤。

去年 11 月钱志敏在伦敦获刑时，比特币还在 10 万美元上方，这批大饼估值一度逼近 66 亿美元。

如今随着币价回落到 8 万美元附近，在各方还在为利益怎么分争得不可开交时，这笔资产已经在周期波动里凭空蒸发了十几亿美元。

一切都有种宿命的感觉。

当年那个揣着假护照、妄想买下欧洲城堡当女王的洗钱主谋，最终倒在了一家 Airbnb 的床上。

而真正为这场狂欢买单的十几万受害者，熬了 7 年，终究还是被无情地隔离在了加密红利之外。

text:
New post on Eth Research!

Informed Diffusion: making home builders publish fast

By:
- cskiraly

🔗 https://t.co/zx53WpdWlf

Highlights:
- Today’s whole-payload gossiping advantages datacenter builders: in a mixed network a datacenter builder reaches p99 in ~1.8s for 1 MiB, while a home builder takes ~4.2s; in an all-home network it’s ~6.3s, threatening decentralization if only datacenters can publish on time.
- Informed Diffusion is built as four tiers (a stack of small “cards”): Tier 1 pipelines by chunking and early-forwarding; Tier 2 reduces duplicates by mixing push and announce/pull; Tier 3 uses erasure coding so any K of 2K chunks reconstruct the payload; Tier 4 adds neighbor-aware scheduling and source/uplink-aware behavior.
- Tier 4’s main wire change is a per-peer HAVE bitmap (plus asking by index) carried in existing gossipsub control messages; most other improvements are local client policies (canceling duplicates at send time, sending rarest chunks first, aiming pushes, pacing announcements, windowing in-flight chunks, etc.).
- Simulation results (500 nodes, 1 MiB) show Tier 4 delivering within the ~3s budget with large margins: p99 ~0.63s (all-home), ~0.58s (home builder in mixed network), and ~0.41s (datacenter builder in mixed), while also cutting average bandwidth to ~1.7 payload copies per node in all-home (vs ~4.4 today).
- The design is robust under stress in the tested scenarios (loss, withholding/silent nodes up to half, uplinks as low as 10 Mbps, payload sizes 128 KiB–2 MiB), and is positioned as a general large-object diffusion approach beyond just Ethereum execution payloads (e.g., BALs, PQ signatures, proofs, large transactions), with an intended follow-up to unify broadcast with sampled diffusion (FullDAS-style).

ELI5:
Imagine you need to share a big file with lots of friends, but your internet upload is slow. If you try to send the whole file to many people at once, everyone gets it late and you waste data sending duplicates. This post proposes a smarter way: split the file into small pieces, let people forward pieces immediately, mostly “announce” what you have and only “send” when it’s helpful, add extra repair pieces so you don’t get stuck waiting for one missing piece, and keep a tiny checklist of what each friend already has so you don’t resend the same pieces. With these tricks, even someone on a home connection can spread a 1 MiB payload across the network fast enough.

Realizing something was wrong, the victim contacted family and friends and feigned illness to buy time. After receiving a request for help from the victim’s family and friends, we worked with police to pinpoint their location using phone-related leads concerning those involved, photographs the victim had taken along the journey, and a photograph of a food delivery order. We ultimately helped secure the victim’s rescue

Police subsequently took those involved in for questioning and continued examining their immigration records, travel in border areas, and possible involvement in irregular border crossings. The investigation remains ongoing

The window for intervention before victims are transferred across the Thai–Myanmar border is extremely narrow. Once they have been taken across, rescue becomes very difficult.
