Last week, Robinhood Chain turned 100 days old.

In the history of TradFi, which took generations to change, that’s a blink of an eye. Onchain, where markets move from idea to existence overnight and assets reach people in milliseconds, a lot can happen — and a lot has.

Robinhood Chain was built to close that gap.

100 days is early days in the life of a new chain, but our initial growth says a lot about why we built it.

✔️ 190+ Stock Tokens are live, and they reached 200K holders faster than on any chain yet. That’s people in 120+ countries gaining exposure to U.S. equities, access that’s still out of reach for billions of people around the world.

✔️ $15B in Stock Token DEX volume proves what’s possible once utility is brought onchain and made composable: new liquidity, new features, and, on Robinhood Chain, pairings people never imagined. 

Giving builders the tools to experiment, form new communities, and ship globally is why building onchain is so powerful and unique. 100 days of Stock Tokens in DeFi has made that clear. From perps to agents and lending markets, the opportunities are out there for anyone who wants to build.

✔️ $1B+ deposited on Morpho on Robinhood Chain. Lending and borrowing, open to anyone, in a world where 1.3 billion adults still don’t have a bank account.

✔️ Robinhood Chain has been the #1 L2 for daily active traders since launch, with $1B+ in TVL and $99B+ in cumulative DEX volume. None of this would be possible without everyone who came here to build and every trader who jumped into the trenches from day one.

Rome wasn’t built in a day (or 100 days), and Robinhood Chain won’t be either. We have more work to do, and we’re excited about what’s next. 

More users, more experiments, more milestones, and more reasons why TradFi and DeFi building on the same rails unlocks a better, more open future for finance.

The next 100 days starts now.

text:
最近一直在参与各种 Launchpad，跟项目方聊得多了以后，我发现大家一开始最关心的，通常都是：

首发资源
控筹
KOL
第一波交易量

但再往后聊更深入，问题就会变成：

第一波热度过去以后，流动性怎么承接？
资产发生变化以后，原来的池子怎么办？
新的用户和需求从哪里继续进来？

很多项目到这一层，路径就开始变得模糊。

所以现在我看一个 Launch，会很在意它有没有把资产后面的生命周期提前策划好。

最近看 @Four_FORM_ 的 4Stock，也是这个角度

股票资产有一个很明显的特点：热点出现得非常快。
一份财报、一条政策、一个 AI 概念，几个小时就可能把一只股票推到市场中心。bStocks 已经给 BNB Chain 带来了一批链上股票资产，但资产覆盖天然存在时间差。
4Stock 补的就是这段窗口。

对于暂时还没有对应 bStock 的热门股票，Four 可以先通过 4Stock 建立对应的链上资产，让 Stock Meme、交易和流动性先跑起来。官方文档里对 4Stock 的定位也很明确：它主要覆盖当前尚未有对应 bStock 的热门美股。

这里有一个细节很重要。

按照 Four文档，4Stock 早期采用申请制：

用户提交 USDC → 平台通过专门管理账户买入对应底层股票 → 再按照实际买入数量 1:1 铸造 4Stock
最终执行价格和到账数量以实际买入为准。

这和 bStocks 的资产支持方式需要分开理解：

bStocks：对应美股由托管方式 1:1 支持
4Stock：https://t.co/pa4OzGBt8g 通过专门管理账户购入底层股票，再按照实际购买数量铸造

更值得关注的是后面⬇️

如果 4Stock 只是解决“先把资产发出来”，价值其实还有限。
比较特别的是，它把后续资产升级和流动性怎么继续往前走也设计进去了。

具体路径是这样的：

Stock Meme 可以先通过 Meme / 4Stock 建立主流动性。
等对应 bStock 就绪以后，官方给出的路径是可以引入 4Stock → 1:1 bStock 的转换（具体仍以届时产品规则和开放状态为准）。

然后是这次我觉得更值得看的 SIH 👇

@PancakeSwap  Infinity 的 Shared Inventory Hook 可以让同一份 Meme 库存同时服务 Meme / 4Stock 和 Meme / bStock 两种配对。

Convert 负责 4Stock → bStock 的资产转换

SIH 负责共享库存和交易过程中的流动性供给
这样原有市场不需要先把主流动性撤掉，再重新建立一套新的池子；随着交易发生，主流动性可以逐步从：

Meme / 4Stock → Meme / bStock

继续往后升级

所以如果让我把这套机制压成一句话：
｜
4Stock 补资产覆盖的时间差，SIH + Convert 补资产升级过程中的流动性断层。

这也是我最近参与 Launchpad 项目后一个很直接的感受：
一个资产最后能不能成为 runner，很多事情其实在Launch 之前就已经决定了一部分：资产怎么承接，流动性怎么延续，用户为什么留下，下一阶段的需求从哪里进来；这些东西如果一开始没有想清楚，前面的热度很容易只剩下一次流量。

所以现在我会拿三个问题去看一个 Launch：

热点来的时候，资产跟得上吗？
资产升级的时候，流动性会不会断？
第一波过去以后，用户凭什么留下？

4Stock 这套机制至少在前两个问题上，给出了一套很清晰的产品思路。

后面我还会继续看几个更实际的问题：

管理账户里的底层股票具体怎么托管和披露
持有人怎么赎回
Convert 真正开放以后深度和滑点表现怎么样

如果 @BNBCHAIN  后面能继续把 资产覆盖速度、流动性连续性、DeFi 可组合性 接起来，我觉得 Stock 这条线会比现在看到的空间更大。

quoted_text:
预测市场还能承担社会价值？
凭什么猜一场比赛叫赌博，猜一只股价的涨跌就叫金融。
美国职业橄榄球联盟最近插手了关于Kalshi的争议案件，要闹到最高法院。
我今天想让你思考一个问题：同样是花钱押结果，从社会价值、经济学的角度来看，为什么不能把预测市场和赌场划上等号。
00:25 交易结构上的区别
01:00 从投机角度来看，预测市场在风险转移、价格发现上的经济价值，类比传统期货市场。
03:00 预测市场的社会成本——激励与风险。不止是内幕消息，当一个人可以左右事件结果，甚至事件涉及选举、战争或公共安全，会发生什么？
03:54 金融创新的边界，一直在增加价值与减少代价之间徘徊。我认为预测市场是金融创新，因为我不想从预测的准确性去判断它，我会看它有没有帮助人们管理风险、作出决定？为了这些价值，又让谁承担了成本？

不要因为一份合约预测的是股价，就认定它天然有价值。反而，某些天气预测却可能帮助农业或物流企业提前安排业务。
不同的事件，能带来的价值和风险都不一样，体育预测也不因为标的是球赛，就必然毫无信息价值。
金融创新让我们拥有了越来越多交易未来的工具，但技术能做到什么，和我们应该允许它做什么，始终是两个需要分别回答的问题。

quoted_text:
令人讽刺的是，一场战争的结束是为了制衡另一场战争，并且可能会让另一场战争风险扩大！

特朗普在自己的社交媒体上直接宣布俄乌60天停火协议达成，此次特朗普促成俄乌和谈的主要目的就是让俄罗斯释放足够的原油来压制Brent 价格，从而压制伊朗的谈判筹码

这场维持了4年7个月的俄乌战争，让特朗普努力调停，让泽连斯基尝试妥协，核心目的居然是压制另一个地缘战争敌人

截止目前，泽连斯基也明确表态，如果俄罗斯同意停火，泽连斯基将会在乌克兰举行大选，泽连斯基这个选择具备超高风险，如果败选，意味着被清算，除非特朗普给泽连斯基开足了筹码保护他

为什么说这个动作会让美伊风险进一步增加？

伊朗明确表态，不会再外部压力下放弃核技术，另外伊朗明正式判断美国对伊朗提出的7项条件回应不足，增加了美伊回归谈判的门槛，此时的伊朗态度依旧强硬

所以说，美国促和俄乌是为了俄罗斯释放更多的原油来压制油价，让美国在美伊谈判桌上筹码更重，但是伊朗的强势也势必会让局势更加恶化

目前战争迷雾依旧比较复杂，俄乌与美伊就像是一个天平，一方的战争风险降低意味着另一方军事冲突风险更大，除非伊朗与美国其中一方选择单方面妥协，这种可能性大吗？确实不大。

看来新的一周，要继续被美伊与能源价格折磨，这是最让人讨厌的！

PS：这里特朗普宣布的俄乌停火先不着急判定为乐观，因为很有可能半场开香槟，接下来要看俄罗斯方面的表态！

text:
给 Agent 一笔预算，或者让它跟另一个 Agent 做生意，安全靠什么保障？

10 月 6 日，在旧金山举办的 C1 Transform 2026 上，我们的联合创始人兼 CEO @ChiZhangData 发表了题为「Enabling Agents as Economic Actors with AI-Native Infrastructure」的演讲，探讨 Agent 要成为经济活动参与者，需要什么样的基础设施：

▷ 可验证身份与有边界的权限，让 Agent 在预算和授权范围内行动。
▷ 清晰的交易条款与验收标准，依据交付凭证完成结算。

text:
财报明明“超预期”，股价却跌了。到底超的是谁的预期？

梅西最近找了不少老师请教：接下来的美股财报季，到底该怎么看、怎么找机会？

平时主要交易 BTC、ETH 的朋友，对资金、情绪和宏观都不陌生。但到了美股财报季，还需要看懂公司交出的这份成绩单。想找密码，先把这几件事弄清楚👇

1️⃣ 一份财报，到底在表达什么？

季度财报可以理解成公司的经营成绩单，但不只是赚了多少钱

▫️利润表：这段时间收入多少、花了多少、最后赚了多少。
▫️资产负债表：公司手里有什么、欠了多少。
▫️现金流量表：现金实际从哪里来，又花到了哪里。

为什么要分开看？因为卖出去的东西可能还没收回钱，买设备、建工厂也会消耗现金。账上有利润和手里有现金，不一样

公司发布业绩时，还可能给出下一季度或全年的预期，也就是 guidance／业绩指引。

随后在业绩电话会上，分析师会追问：增长从哪里来？成本为什么变了？这种变化会持续多久？

2️⃣ 财报一出，机构在忙什么？

做基本面研究的分析师，通常先对照原来的预测，再拆差异来自哪里：

▫️收入增长，是卖得更多，还是涨价了？
▫️利润增长，是主营业务改善，还是一次性收益？
▫️这一季度的好成绩，后面还能不能持续？

做基本面研究的机构，会结合这些信息，更新未来的盈利、现金流预测和估值。

宏观也会进入这笔账：利率影响融资成本，消费影响需求，汇率影响海外收入。即使公司盈利没变，市场愿意给的估值也可能变化

所以这季度成绩不错，不代表后面的预期也变好了，更不代表股价一定上涨。

3️⃣ 不同公司，重点也不一样

▫️医疗保险公司，要看保费收入有多少用于医疗支出；
▫️云业务，要看增长和利润率能不能兼顾；
▫️零售公司，要看销售、库存和折扣；
▫️重投入的 AI 业务，除了收入，还要看建设算力花了多少钱、现金流能不能撑住

同样是收入增长，靠主营需求带动，和靠不断打折、加大投入换来，含义可能完全不同。

4️⃣ 回到开头：到底超的是谁的预期？

新闻里的「超预期」，通常是在和分析师的一致预期比较。
但这个数字，不一定等于投资者心里的门槛

举个例子：分析师预计赚 100，投资者却已经期待它交出 110。最后公布 103，标题可以写“超预期”，市场却可能觉得不够好

还有一种情况：这季度不错，管理层却调低了下一阶段的预期。过去赚得多，不代表未来还能按原来的速度赚

所以“比去年好”“比预测好”“好到值得现在这个股价”，是三件不同的事

5️⃣ 到了预测市场，更要看清楚自己在判断什么

「利润是否超过某个数」和「财报后股价是否上涨」，是两道不同的题

前一道更偏经营结果；后一道还要考虑市场预期、估值和当时的环境

看懂财报、参与预测市场之后，怎么表达自己的判断？

这也是股票永续合约值得关注的地方。OKX 已上线多个 Tradfi 永续合约标的，支持用 USDT 作为保证金，7×24 小时交易。

对于不熟悉这种波动的朋友，先看解读、等信息更完整，也是一种参与方式。工具更灵活，不等于风险更小。

text:
预测市场还能承担社会价值？
凭什么猜一场比赛叫赌博，猜一只股价的涨跌就叫金融。
美国职业橄榄球联盟最近插手了关于Kalshi的争议案件，要闹到最高法院。
我今天想让你思考一个问题：同样是花钱押结果，从社会价值、经济学的角度来看，为什么不能把预测市场和赌场划上等号。
00:25 交易结构上的区别
01:00 从投机角度来看，预测市场在风险转移、价格发现上的经济价值，类比传统期货市场。
03:00 预测市场的社会成本——激励与风险。不止是内幕消息，当一个人可以左右事件结果，甚至事件涉及选举、战争或公共安全，会发生什么？
03:54 金融创新的边界，一直在增加价值与减少代价之间徘徊。我认为预测市场是金融创新，因为我不想从预测的准确性去判断它，我会看它有没有帮助人们管理风险、作出决定？为了这些价值，又让谁承担了成本？

不要因为一份合约预测的是股价，就认定它天然有价值。反而，某些天气预测却可能帮助农业或物流企业提前安排业务。
不同的事件，能带来的价值和风险都不一样，体育预测也不因为标的是球赛，就必然毫无信息价值。
金融创新让我们拥有了越来越多交易未来的工具，但技术能做到什么，和我们应该允许它做什么，始终是两个需要分别回答的问题。

text:
The fundamental investment era for crypto

It might be the topic du jour, but I’ve been writing at @RealVision all year that matket forces were correcting years of misalignment and distortion. 

For four years after I entered this space, what vexed me most was how unstable traditional equity-like factors were when applied to this asset class. I wanted to understand what actually drove token value. Quality had to be part of the answer, from first principles, but there weren’t enough protocols with product-market fit, disciplined supply and incentives aligned between insiders and token holders to make the case convincing.

The last cycle left investors disillusioned: too much VC-era grift, dilution and protocol teams whose incentives had little to do with their token holders. Trump’s arrival changed the regulatory environment, while market pressure from pissed off investors and evangelists began to exert pressure. We now have a situation where a protocol cannot just have product-market fit. It must compete on tokenomics / value accrual. Distortions haven't disappeared, but they are declining. Market forces and proper regulatory guardrails will see to that.

The top third of my quality basket is up about 35% through September, while Bitcoin and the cap-weighted Top 100 are both down about 8%. From 2022 through 2025, that basket lost about 71% while Bitcoin gained 88%. Nine months prove little statistically. Still, I’m increasingly convinced that protocols without product-market fit, supply discipline and a credible path for value to reach token holders will underperform those that have all three.

quoted_text:
Why Extended is pursuing a regulated path in Europe

TLDR: European retail already trades inside licensed apps, and regulated platforms typically need regulated venues they can integrate. Extended is building one. Builder codes let partners plug Extended into their own product: through the existing venue for self-custody users where available, and through the regulated venue for regulated clients once live.

Europe has close to 10,000 fintech companies, and hundreds of licensed investment firms and credit institutions. Most are exploring new ways to engage their retail user base, and perps are consistently near the top of the list. All of them are potential clients for a regulated exchange.

That market opportunity drove our decision to build a regulated venue in Europe:
1. Retail is the user base we are building the regulated offering for. We have said before that sustainable growth is built on product quality, distribution and community rather than financial incentives. For a trading product, the largest pool of users is retail, and reaching it is a distribution problem.
2. Perp DEXs processed roughly $600 billion in volume over the past 30 days. CFD brokers alone show the size of the addressable market: around $30 trillion a month, with a large share of it in Europe. The largest platforms already earn most of their volume outside FX, in equities, indices, commodities and crypto. On-chain perps is a market we know well and intend to keep serving, but the larger opportunity sits next to it: tens of millions of retail traders already active on regulated platforms, many of whom have no access to perps today.
3. There are three retail markets at the scale that matters: the US, Europe and Asia. The US is the most contested, with many major exchanges and brokers competing for the same users and a long licensing path. Asia has high perps penetration but regulatory approaches vary by jurisdiction. Europe is where we are starting, and we will look at other regulated markets as and when it makes sense.
4. Regulated crypto derivatives in Europe have only recently expanded. Kraken, Coinbase and Bitstamp (owned by Robinhood) launched futures for EU clients over the past 18 months, each using regulatory infrastructure obtained through an acquisition of a licensed investment firm or exchange. That route is open to a handful of firms with the balance sheet for it, but for the far larger group of fintechs and brokers with users and no perps infrastructure, it is not. Our model is to offer builder codes on both venues: a way for partners to plug perps into their own apps, route users’ orders to the venue and earn a share of the fees. Self-custody wallets can integrate with the existing venue where available. Regulated brokers and fintechs will be able to use the regulated venue once it is live.
5. A regulated perps setup takes significant time and resources to build from scratch, and many fintechs lack the product and market expertise to run it well, starting with established market-maker relationships. For smaller players the economics may not work. For larger ones, regulated builder codes cut time to market, especially inside slow-moving large organisations, and deliver a quality product from day one.
6. The demand is clear. We are already in conversations with wallets, CFD brokers and fintechs across Europe, and we repeatedly hear the same request: a regulated venue with a broad range of crypto and RWA markets they can integrate.

Importantly, this does not change our DeFi offering or our commitment to the early community. The existing venue stays for crypto-native users where it is available. The regulated venue adds a new distribution channel and a new user base. 

Europe is the first step. Over time, we expect to replicate the same model in other markets, including the US. Our plan is subject to the relevant regulatory authorisations, and we will share specifics as they are confirmed. At a high level, we have an initial route to market, followed by a transition to our own licences.

text:
literally everyone knows that taste matters more than ever

two things people aren't talking about which the next phase of winners need:

1) legendary context switching - you're going to be working on 10x more things than before, you need to be able to go wide seamlessly (and ready to go deep when necessary)

2) mental toughness to resist being lazy - yes you need taste, I actually think the hard part is being tough enough to apply the taste at scale

when little robots are doing so much work for you, it's easy to over-delegate the most meaningful parts that actually matter

if you don't spend the time on nailing the ask/prompt, and then doing deep critical edits/feedback on all output, you're going to fail

if you're 10x scaling mid-tier work, you're wasting everyone's time. it's hard to critically review and improve so much work, but if you don't summon the strength to do it, you're ngmi 

not everyone is cut out to be a manager, but suddenly everyone in the world is a manager (of robots)

luckily the same principles apply - vision setting/articulation, clear expectations, logical collaboration processes, documentation, etc - you have to set your agents up for success, and push them to be better

don't get lazy, always think critically

text:
小資金如何快速做大？

理論上說，小資金要做大，必須要採用「重倉+槓桿」的操作才行。然而，這種方式如果用在了錯誤的標的和錯誤的方向上，必定是歸零。

所以，我的看法是：
1.  不要碰個股，只做美股大盤指數，比如納斯達克100指數 。它不會跌到零，它的優勝劣汰機制決定了指數長期上漲是必然的；
2. 在長期必然上漲的標的上「重倉+槓桿」做多，在概率上是有利的。

具體怎麼做？我提供一個思路供參考：
1.  在上升趨勢中（請注意這個前提），每次納斯達克100指數從前一個高點回撤超過-3%，收盤前買入 $QQQ 看漲期權；
2. 選擇到期日>90天、價外5%左右的合約；
3. 期權增值100%止盈，虧損-30%止損出局。

簡言之，用3:1的盈虧比，在長期必然上漲的標的上「重倉+槓桿」，長期堅持這麼做，你的資本會飛速增長。

增長到一定程度（比如每增長10萬美元）就將帳戶資金的80%買入 $VOO ，剩餘20%繼續以小搏大。如此往復，這是最容易讓小資金迅速放大的方式。

當然，這並非沒有風險。 $QQQ 在2000年科技泡沫崩盤後，用了十六年才創出新高，在這期間，不論怎麼做都難以獲利。

說到底，我們多數時候賺的都是趨勢的錢。所以，研究趨勢是我的主要工作，感興趣的話可以來看看我的交易筆記，每個交易日更新。

text:
亚洲科技股刚刚经历了一轮市值蒸发约 8000 亿美元的抛售，现在美股盘前也开始跟跌。

但仔细看看跌幅，会发现很有意思。

西部数据跌 3.74%，希捷跌 3.48%，Marvell 跌 3.41%，闪迪跌 3.08%，美光跌 2.47%。另一边，AMD 只跌了 1.06%，博通跌 0.79%，英伟达甚至只跌了 0.54%。

我觉得市场正在重新区分两种 AI 资产。

一种是掌握核心技术、生态和客户关系的公司，另一种是受益于 AI 需求爆发、供需失衡和产品涨价的公司。

过去两年，大家都在讲 AI 基建超级周期，似乎只要沾上算力、内存、存储，就能享受同样的估值溢价。但一旦市场开始担心供给扩张、价格回落，第二类公司的利润预期会率先受到冲击。

尤其是存储行业，本身就有很强的周期性。这两年 AI 需求让市场一度相信，它们可以摆脱传统周期，长期维持高利润。

text:
上个月被 4stock这个meme币折磨的死去活来。本来是很完美的题材，却因为机制的缺陷没有走下去。

这次Fourmeme痛定思痛，和pancake合作，在4Stock功能中引入了Infinity Shared Inventory Hook（SIH）流动性升级机制。

基于 PancakeSwap Infinity 的 SIH，https://t.co/e2t0udq2G2 让已建立的 Stock Meme 主流动性可以在 bStock 就绪后持续升级。

举个例子，原来bnc股票原来没有在bstock推出，然后玩家想玩bnc的币股，只能借助fourmeme的bnc4来玩，但是等bstock正式推出自己的bncb后，bnc4就成为了很尴尬的存在。已经建立的LP中的bnc4没办法直接换成bncb，导致了流动性割裂，进而导致了meme分流。

现在在SIH的新功能下。Stock Meme 毕业后先在 4Stock 池中交易。当对应 bStock 上线后，https://t.co/e2t0udq2G2 会为 Convert 合约配置对应的 bStock 库存。交易发生时，路由可以先将用于交易的 4Stock 送入 Convert 合约，转换为 bStock，再由 Infinity（V4）池以 Meme / bStock
路径完成交易执行。随着交易持续，市场的主流动性会从 Meme / 4Stock 连续升级为Meme / bStock，而无需先撤出、再重新建立一套主流动性。

希望这次完全体形态的4sotck能跑出来一个金狗。
author: Mumu_yay
quoted_text:
📢 https://t.co/P50JGo73zK Product Update: A Seamless Path from 4Stock to bStock

4Stock brings popular stocks onchain before their bStock is available. To ensure Stock Memes built on 4Stock can transition to bStock seamlessly, we’ve introduced a shared-inventory pool mechanism built on @PancakeSwap Infinity’s Shared Inventory Hook (SIH).

How it works:
- At graduation, a newly created Stock Meme opens its primary pool as Meme / 4Stock
- Once the corresponding bStock is live, primary liquidity migrates to Meme / bStock in one step
- The same meme inventory backs both pairs, so price and depth remain continuous and trading is never interrupted
- Only one primary pool exists at any time, keeping each token fully compatible with aggregators

No action is required from creators or holders.

More Stocks. More Memes. Make Four Great Again. 📈

text:
为什么美国机构拼命卖比特币，Binance 上的全球资金却还在接盘？

这几天 Coinbase 的比特币负溢价持续扩大，说明美国市场的买盘明显弱于 Binance。

美国机构忙着降低风险敞口，全球其他地区的资金却没有同步撤退，双方对比特币的定价态度出现了明显分歧。

美国机构管理的是资产组合，盯着美债收益率、美元指数、通胀和地缘政治风险。

如今美国10年期国债收益率仍在5%以上，美元指数突破102，宏观风险持续压制流动性，机构为了控制回撤和满足风控要求，自然倾向于先跑为敬。

但 Binance 上的交易者来自更广泛的全球市场，资金结构、风险偏好、投资周期都不一样。Coinbase 长期负溢价，至少说明美国市场的相对卖压没有让全球市场出现同等程度的疲软。

如果全球买盘持续承接，BTC 价格重新走强，美国机构最终还得面对重新配置的问题。

等美元和美债收益率回落、风险偏好恢复，这些现在急着卖出的所谓聪明钱，完全可能重新追高买回来，成为下一轮上涨的燃料。

比特币越来越全球化了，美国机构可以影响短期价格，却未必能决定长期趋势。

You already gave the LLM the answer. So why is it writing it out from scratch?

Introducing a new AI model architecture: Constrained Decoding Models (CDMs)

LLMs were built to write. Most production workloads just need an answer: fast, consistent, and affordable.

CDMs are purpose-built for 1 task each. They read your input once and skip the token-by-token generative loop that makes LLMs slow and expensive.

Not just a decision model, but a family of 3 CDMs live today:

• Classify: define your labels and get back a calibrated probability + reason for each. Used for routing, tagging, and intent detection.
 • Extract: describe the entities in natural language and get back well-formed JSON with confidence scores + citations. Used for web scraping, document processing, and PII redaction.
 • Summarize: pass in long text, images, or PDFs and get back a consistent summary under 1,000 tokens. Used for context compaction, metadata generation, and transcript digests.

Built for production:

• 1M tokens of multimodal (text + image) input, 31x larger than Jev

经常有人问我订阅了啥AI的会员，所以今天正好分享一下。 
 
1. ChatGPT Pro会员，100刀（约670块）。 
GPT-6 Astra刚出来的时候，我是200刀的会员，那时候还在重构AIHOT，基本一天1个200刀账号，所以我还临时开了2个200刀的会员，配上重置才勉强够用。 
现在Cluade Opus 5.5在实在太强了，所以对ChatGPT会员进行了降阶，11月初生效，100刀配上补偿的62500还有重置卡，感觉也够用了。 
我现在用它的是几个场景：自己和公司项目的反馈和PR自动化开发、项目运维监控的自动化等等，GPT-6.1 Sol在BUG优化和修复上确实还是很不错的。 
同时对后端、还有一些硬件进行定向优化或者协议破解，比如今晚就让它在优化新公司的网关和AP设置，提升大家的网络稳定性。 
不过对于大家来说，我觉得ChatGPT还是最水桶的，聊天是完全免费的，也有生图的额度，开发点小东西，GPT-6.1 Sol也够了。 
 
2. Claude Max会员，250刀（从Google Play订阅的，所以多收了50刀的渠道费，约1675人民币） 
没啥可说的，Claude Opus 5.5基本上是现在的版本真神，GPT-6.1 Sol和GPT-6 Astra除了在一些后端、硬件的优化还有浏览器操控上，我觉得很难跟Opus 5.5去打，并且我自己整体额度体感大概是Codex的5倍，高强度开发+设计+做动效做了一周了，明天下午重置，我周额度只用到了84%，还没用完。我整体消耗都是Claude Opus 5.5，Fable 5.1基本不咋用。 
 
3. X Ultra会员，260刀（今天新定，从Google Play订阅的，所以多收了60刀的渠道费，也约1742人民币） 
马斯克的全新会员体系，今天刚刚上线，我直接定了一下，首月130刀打半价，它直接把Grok、Grok Bot、Cursor和X合并掉了，Grok 4.7比较拉，但是我依然愿意买，纯粹就是冲着Grok Bot去的，这玩意相比ChatGPT的Dots，目前还是好用的比较多的，后端模型还给你用Claude Opus 5.5。 
且本身我是X用户，而且老马给的额度很足，200刀的Ultra直接给了50x的额度，Claude和Codex都是10x。所以我觉得性价比还行。 
不过如果ChatGPT把Dots优化好了，没有这么蠢了，且老马的Grok 4.8或者5又拉了，那我大概率不会定了。 
 
4. Suno Pro，8刀（我开了年付费，所以打折了，月53块） 
独一档做音乐的，不常用，但偶尔得用，属于刚需，直接包年了，跟团队共用。 
 
5. LibTV至尊版，1499元（我开了年付费，所以打折了）。 
我偶尔跑视频用，主要是跟团队共用，他们跑视频的量太大了，不是做视频方向的没必要定，现在视频的AI太贵了，贵的肉疼。 
 
我自己个人最常用的基本就这些。
杂七八糟的每个月+API大概在AI上的花费是6000多一点吧，很贵，我也只想订阅一个。
所以这么看，ChatGPT还是最全面的水桶，对所有人都友好的。
 以上，做个参考，希望对大家有用。

text:
In March this year, the @BitcoinPolicy Institute tested 36 AI models from six labs across 9,072 scenarios about money. No currency was suggested to them. 

For storing value long term, the models chose Bitcoin in 79% of responses, and not one of the 36 chose fiat as its top preference.

We think the next question matters even more than the finding: where does an agent hold that Bitcoin? 

An agent can’t call a support line or file a dispute. An account that can be frozen or a transaction that can be reversed isn’t an inconvenience for an agent - it’s a reason to leave. Agent capital will settle where custody and exit back to Bitcoin are enforced by cryptography rather than by an operator’s permission.

That is the network we’ve spent years building.

text:
We've updated the nomenclature and added figures to the Ostium dashboard on Dune to make it clearer how revenue is defined and how it's split between the OLP Vault and the Ostium Protocol.

Top-Line Revenue (previously “Total Fees”) is the sum of Trading Fees and Flow Revenue:
 󠁯•󠁏󠁏 Trading Fees are the opening fees on each trade, currently split 30/70 between the OLP Vault and the Ostium Protocol. They are charged when the trade is opened.
󠁯•󠁏󠁏 Flow Revenue is spreads, rollover and liquidation fees. Since the liquidity upgrade in April, Flow Revenue goes to the Ostium Protocol. You can see this evolution in the monthly chart.

Unlike Trading Fees, Flow Revenue is built into the trade itself (spreads on entry and exit, rollover while the position is open, liquidation fees if it is liquidated) and is settled through the trader’s PnL.

Neither value represents gross profits: Top-Line Revenue is an onchain, gross figure and does not include the off-chain cost of hedging flow. Gross profit is an off-chain metric and is the value of what remains after the OLP Vault’s share and off-chain hedging costs.

We will continue to make improvements to the Dune dashboard and welcome feedback on how it can be further improved.

Wintermute: Crypto Is Losing Its Flow Support as ETF Outflows Mount

Wintermute said crypto is losing support from capital flows, while equities remain backed by earnings expectations. Last week, BTC fell 3.2% and ETH dropped 7.0%, with U.S. spot BTC and ETH ETFs recording $679M and $542M in net outflows, respectively. BTC ETF outflows were the largest weekly total since late June.

Wintermute said a sustained recovery requires long-term Treasury yields to stabilize and spot ETF flows to turn positive. Until then, BTC remains vulnerable to volatility and downside risks, while low-quality altcoin rallies should be approached cautiously. The firm remains constructive long term but would turn more cautious if the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield exceeds 5.64% or BTC repeatedly fails to break above $82,500.

text:
Takeaways from this year's Token 2049 Singapore:

- The industry remains a barbell. One side is the institutionalization of crypto [RWA, stablecoin, vaults]; the other side is gambling-adjacent [prediction markets, gacha, meme-tooling]. Perps are the PMF adored by both.

- Revenue first. No one is sugarcoating that you need to be business-first. The space used to value research-type personalities/companies, but now rather cheers on the success of apps like Fomo or protocols like USDAI. Signs of maturation.

- Margin is compressing. AI can really one-shot most apps these days, so the only moat remaining is (i) liquidity and (ii) distribution 

- Trickier VC underwriting. The previous point means that it's easier than ever to be a builder, but it's harder than ever to back truly venture-scale companies. There are 20+ neobanks and 10+ card issuers. Read the last sentence again.

- West tokenize, East capitalize. Regulated Western (US, EU) funds want to tokenize their assets, but most of the buyers remain offshore. Unfortunately, an 8-10% yielding strategy isn't as interesting if PYUSD and RLUSD are burning $ to give you 6-7%; and even funds in MENA/APAC can easily get an 8% rate with relatively safe private credit offchain. You HAVE TO ENABLE looping.

- Chains are consolidating and incubating their own apps. Perhaps goes w/o saying, but many chains are allegedly terminating relationships with their ecosystem apps and going full blown venture-studio mode; perhaps they're inspired by Hyperliquid, or realizing that they can no longer sell their gOveRNanCe token to fund runways.

参会的人透露了更多细节：

text:
Holding Bitcoin is the best product in our industry.

While I have great sympathy for my fellow builders, most of what Bitcoin finance has shipped so far asked the holder to accept worse products.

Be it wrapped BTC, wrapped BTC paired with liquidation logic that a lending protocol wrote, yield layers built on top with all kinds of DAO emergency controls, etc. The holder is paying for a worse version of the thing they used to have.

The answer is to rebuild Bitcoin finance from the ground up. BTC stays under Bitcoin rules, while it's value works elsewhere. When debt are repaid, holders take their coins back without requiring permission. If the lending market or EVM fails, holders take their coins back without requiring permission. Bitcoin Collateral Vaults at @ZestProtocol are built against exactly that test.

@muneeb wrote after Token2049 that Bitcoin sets the ceiling for the whole industry. In Bitcoin finance the ceiling has already been set by the holder. We can add to that product, but we cannot substitute for it 🟧

AI企业借钱扩张，盈利跟不上可能拖累整个金融市场

AI扩张已经越来越依赖借钱了。路透援引IMF最新报告的数据，大型云计算公司在全球投资级债券新增发行中的占比已经达到10%，2024年还不到1%。这也说明，跟着AI一起押注未来收入的资金越来越多了，买股票的人在等它赚钱，借钱给它的人也在等。

现在建数据中心、买芯片、抢电力，钱都要先花出去，至于这些投入什么时候能赚回来，还要看客户愿意花多少钱、持续用多久。市场愿意支持扩张，也是因为相信后面的收入能跟上，今天多花一些钱，未来就能多占一些市场。但借的钱越多，企业留给自己等待的时间也会受到限制，毕竟生意可以慢慢做，利息和到期的债务都需要按时支付。

如果AI企业赚钱的速度跟不上投入，压力就会顺着这笔钱往外传。企业为了保住现金，可能先放慢建设、减少采购，而它少花出去的钱，就是芯片公司、设备商和工程公司的订单。几家大公司一起收缩，受到影响的企业就会越来越多，这些企业自己的收入、投资和还款，也会跟着承压。

而借钱给它们的机构看到回款变慢，也会开始谨慎，愿意继续借的钱可能减少，要求的利息可能提高。这样一来，需要继续融资的企业就更难受了，一边收入没有达到预期，一边借钱又变贵，只能进一步压缩投入。如果原本拿来抵押的数据中心和设备也跟着贬值，能借到的钱还会更少，整条链就可能越收越紧。

这时候，压力就可能传到市场上。持有相关债券和贷款的机构如果出现损失，又碰上赎回或者追加保证金，就需要卖出其他持仓来筹钱。它卖的可能是科技股，也可能是其他容易变现的资产，资金一旦开始集中降低仓位，美股和 bitcoin:native 这样的风险资产都可能受到影响。

quoted_text:
近期韩国半导体股票大跌原因是什么？

今天上午，韩国 KOSPI 盘中跌幅超过6%，SK 海力士一度跌超8%，三星也大幅下跌，前一天美光已经跌了约3.9%。投资者开始担心这些靠 AI 赚了很多钱的公司，以后还能不能一直这么赚钱。

之前存储芯片涨得好，很大程度上有两个原因。一个是科技公司不断建数据中心，买的芯片和内存越来越多；另一个是生产 AI 芯片配套的高带宽内存 HBM，需要占用更多产能，留给普通内存的产能就少了。所以厂商不仅能卖更多 AI 用的内存，普通内存也因为供应紧张而涨价，赚到的钱跟着增加。

现在长鑫存储公布了技术进展，计划年底推出新一代服务器 DDR5 内存。这让投资者担心，以后市场上的内存多了，三星、海力士和美光还能不能继续涨价。长鑫不需要一下抢走很多客户，只要有一部分客户多了选择，原来的供应商就可能要让价才能留住订单。即使卖出去的数量继续增加，每件产品赚得少了，总利润也可能没有之前预计的那么高。

这里还有一个容易忽略的地方，长鑫即使先满足中国客户的采购，也可能影响其他厂商的生意。如果这些客户减少购买三星、海力士和美光的产品，后者就要把货卖给其他客户。当更多供应商都想争取同一批订单，买家谈价格就会更有底气。

另一件让投资者担心的事，是科技公司花在 AI 上的钱，什么时候能赚回来。买芯片、建机房只是开始，后面还有电费、维护、设备折旧和利息。如果 AI 业务赚的钱长期跟不上这些支出，客户就可能放慢建设，把设备多用一段时间，或者推迟下一批采购。对于原本指望订单快速增长的芯片厂商来说，客户买得没有预计的那么多，就可能影响以后的利润。

韩国跌得更惨，是因为三星和海力士在指数里占比很大，两家公司一起跌，再碰上外资卖出，整个市场就会被拖下去。日本、台湾和美国相关股票也受到影响，是因为很多公司虽然做的产品不同，但都在等这些科技大客户继续买设备。投资者一旦担心这些客户以后花钱没那么快，就可能把几个市场里的相关股票一起卖掉。

总的来说，说人话就是财报好，说明之前赚得多。可大家担心以后内存降价、客户买得少，公司赚的钱也会少，就可能先卖股票，不会傻等到财报真的变差。

text:
ARK's Lorenzo Valente says RWAs will win, but tokenized stock trading is moving to L2s and Solana, leaving Ethereum L1 as a proof layer

"Tokenization is just changing the entire market and structure. And I think people are not realizing, if you see the tokenized equities and the trading volume, it's basically all happening on Solana, Base, and Robinhood."

"What is gonna grow the most in the next 2 to 3 years, we think it's gonna be RWAs. I do think Ethereum, the asset, is gonna continue to grow. But I think the winner is gonna be RWAs."

"If nothing is happening on the Ethereum base layer, and all the activity is happening on Base, Robinhood and the layer twos, I don't see why Ethereum L1 just doesn't become just a layer where you post proof."

"It's basically a DA layer where Robinhood, Base and other layer twos post their proof, which is literally what happens today."

"And then you have, $50 to 100 billion worth of stablecoins on Ethereum. If you fast forward, you'd imagine some of them being pulled into the layer twos if most of the activity happens there."

"I think the Ethereum people think that it's the opposite way. Because there's a lot of assets on Ethereum L1, it'll pull the activity."

"But the net new user doesn't care about a token that is issued on L1. They wanna trade the Circle stock. They wanna trade NVIDIA, and that is happening on Base and Robinhood."

text:
币股 2.0 里的小赛道：聚合入口

最近 Robinhood 链上，币股 2.0 讨论最多的标的是 $HYDX。
最常听到的一句话是：“这是币股的 JUP 时刻。”

逻辑是这样的：
Solana 上，最后吃到最大流量的不是哪个 DEX，
而是聚合所有 DEX 的 Jupiter。

币股也一样。
Robinhood、Ondo、xStocks、Backed、bStocks……
发行方越来越多，同一只英伟达，在不同链上有好几个版本。

用户不想管背后是谁发的，只想一键买到最便宜的那个。
谁做成这个入口，谁就吃流量。

这个逻辑我是认的。
但聚合入口这条小赛道，比很多人想的要卷。

1. 巨头已经下场了

PancakeSwap 的 Stock Terminal：
· 3,600+ 只股票和 ETF
· 覆盖 bStocks、Ondo、Robinhood、xStocks 等发行方
· 跨链比价，自动找最优报价
· 9 月拿下 bStocks 24 小时交易量第一

它背后是 2 亿用户、6 年的品牌，还有 Robinhood 链上 90% 手续费返给 LP 的补贴。

说白了，“币股版 JUP”这件事，PancakeSwap 已经在做了。

2. 小项目在卷什么？

· $HYDX（HyperDex）
跨链聚合 + 主题篮子 + 大佬持仓一键跟投，
手续费回购销毁。
币股抵押借款，官网还写着即将上线。
功能堆得最全，项目方更新也最勤快。

· $VERDEX
据官方介绍，主打股票篮子：七姐妹、AI 基建、SPY、QQQ 这类主题指数，
用 USDC 买入，钱包签一次就能买齐。
篮子已经能在 Base 上买；Solana 上是一键买 xStocks 的入口页。
官方还宣布了借贷和杠杆。

代币模型和 HYDX 很像：
手续费拿去回购 VERDEX，一半销毁，一半每周分给交过费的地址；
持币用户做指数和杠杆免手续费。

篮子 + 回购分红，基本是同款打法。
这条小赛道的同质化，已经开始了。

3. 小项目的机会在哪？

和巨头正面拼深度、拼资产数量，基本没胜算。

小项目能打的，是巨头不会做、或者做得慢的事：
· 跟单、主题篮子这种更“散户”的玩法
· 币股抵押借贷、回购分红这种更 DeFi 的组合
· 在 Robinhood 链上做原生，跟社区贴得更近

还有一点：
PancakeSwap 没有一个专门押注币股的代币，
HYDX 和 VERDEX 有。
想单独押“币股聚合”这条线的资金，只能从这些小币里选。

4. 风险也很清楚

· 聚合器本身没有护城河，流量入口最终拼的是用户规模和补贴；
· “回购 + 分红”的前提是有真实交易量，而整条链的交易量还在低位；
· 这类小币市值只有几百万，底池很浅，波动会非常大。

聚合入口是币股 2.0 里逻辑最顺的一条线。
但“JUP 时刻”的前提是：
你得是那个最终赢家，而不是被巨头顺手做掉的那个。

$HOOD $HYDX $VERDEX $CAKE

GS Delta-One head, Rich Privorotsky, on latest in AI:

Four stories to unpack:
First, CXMT is a legitimate concern for memory economics. 
Second, Microsoft’s Maia 300 custom chips, moving to TSMC’s 2nm process.Incrementally negative for merchant GPU suppliers (NVDA), positive for the custom silicon supply chain and aggregate compute consumption. 
Third, Hock Tan’s comments comparing AI investors to gamblers have been taken wildly out of context. Both Broadcomand Intel reaffirmed exceptionally strong demand for another 2–3 years, potentially through 2030. Tan sees compute demand exceeding supply and explicitly acknowledged that frontier labs generating substantial revenue can afford expensive financing. LT ROI is a legitimate question, but hardly a revelation.  
Fourth, Meta’s Muse Wonder and Wonder Full look genuinely competitive at the frontier,potentially adding another serious player alongside OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Some questions around benchmarking, but impressive nonetheless. Prediction markets also anticipating another major Google release imminently. 

What do I make of all this? Competition fuels competition, and competition requires more compute. The frontier keeps advancing, driven by Western closed source labs trying to outdo one another. Hardly bearish for aggregate compute demand, even if the economics shift around the supply chain. Think the legitimate concerns are around the ability to complete capacity/deliver power relative to expectations and that is fueling further de-rating in the capex vertical.

text:
Update from Ledger Donjon on the CryptoBilis investigation 🔽

@DonjonLedger is investigating Ledger signers sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, that contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Ledger confirmed this on October 10th for one affected user's signer. All confirmed fund losses tied to the incident disclosed on October 9th involve signers sold through CryptoBilis. We have not verified a drain linked to a signer bought elsewhere. CryptoBilis has confirmed it stopped selling Ledger signers while the investigation continues.

Based on the Donjon's analysis of the attack, the implant sits inside the enclosure and reads the data shown on the screen. During setup, the signer displays the 24-word recovery phrase. When the implant detects these screens, its microcontroller decodes the words and transmits them over LTE using a provisioned eSIM. The implant is a separate component. It does not modify the Secure Element or the Ledger operating system, and it does not alter transactions or signatures.

The Donjon will analyze the signers it receives and will share more as the investigation continues.

We have not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost. Figures circulating online come from third parties and Ledger has not fully verified them. If your funds were drained and you have not contacted us, please do so through Ledger Support so we can include your case. We are also reviewing reports of implants in other signers and locations. We will continue to share information as the investigation progresses. Rest assured the Ledger team is going above and beyond to leave no stone unturned to investigate this situation to the strongest possible outcome.

If you bought a Ledger signer from CryptoBilis and have not set it up, do not set it up and contact Ledger Support. If you have set it up, transfer your assets promptly to a new signer with a new recovery phrase. Do not enter or restore any recovery phrase on a signer bought from CryptoBilis. Never enter your recovery phrase into a website, app or form.

If you lost funds or hold a tampered signer, contact Ledger Support at https://t.co/QzukOZdEzq and file a report with local law enforcement. Do not send the signer to anyone before speaking with Ledger Support or local law enforcement. If you lost funds, coordinate with law enforcement before opening the signer. Researchers and others with relevant information can write to security@ledger.com.

If you did not buy from CryptoBilis and want to inspect the inside of your signer, the guide is at https://t.co/Bh9DHQulIv. Use caution and make sure your recovery phrase is backed up first, because opening a signer can damage it.

Ledger will never call you, message you directly, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase. We will update this post when we verify new information.

next week they will slash incentives for BOTH market makers and takers.

And the numbers are brutal.

📉 MAKER REBATES

Previously, ALL market makers received the same rebate coefficient of −0.0125, regardless of volume.

Now, rebates depend on monthly maker volume:

- Under $10M: 0 (−100%)
- $10M–$50M: −0.0035 (−72%)
- $50M–$200M: −0.0070 (−44%)
- $200M+: −0.0104 (−16.8%)

which means that If you do under >$10M volume, no rebates at all ! 

and even whales at the max tier doing over $200M in monthly maker volume will get less than before.

📉 TAKER REBATES

It's arguably even worse for takers

Previously:
- $250K–$1M monthly volume: 10% back
- $1M–$10M: 25% back
- $10M+: 50% back

Starting October 19:

- $250K–$1M: 3% (−70%)
• $1M–$10M: 5% (−80%)
• $10M–$25M: 10% (−80%)
• $50M+: 30% (−40%)

Polymarket will allow traders to qualify for higher rebate tiers using volume from *other prediction markets*.

text:
项目方的生意不好做，连 KOL Agency 都开始盯上交易所的钱了。

Mango 主要做的是项目方的品牌营销、KOL 推广和上币服务。现在开始招募有交易量资源的 BD，显然是想切入交易平台的增长业务。

商业模式其实不复杂。

先把 KOL、社区、交易团队、BD 等带量渠道整合起来，再以总代理的身份，去跟 CEX、Perp DEX 谈合作。

这样至少可以赚两份钱：

第一份：手续费返佣差价。

比如从交易所拿到 80% 返佣，给下游 BD 60%，自己留下 20%。只要用户持续交易，就能一直赚钱。

第二份：交易所增长服务费。

交易所需要新增用户、入金、交易量，或者想打开某个国家的市场，Mango 可以组织自己的 BD 网络去完成 KPI，再收服务费和阶段奖励。

但我觉得，这个生意想做成，难度非常大。

首先，真正能带量的 BD，基本都在各大交易所手里。你要挖人，就得给出比交易所更好的待遇。

500–1500U 的有责底薪…… 用香蕉的钱，就只能雇到猴子。

其次，也是最关键的问题：

一个手里真有客户、有交易量的 BD，为什么要把自己的资源挂在 Mango 下面，而不是直接找交易所拿返佣？

Mango 必须证明，自己拿到的费率、增长预算和渠道支持，比 BD 直接对接交易所更有优势。

说到底，这门生意的核心不是招聘多少 BD，而是谁掌握交易量，谁拥有对交易所的议价权。

text:
At around $5 per ethereum:0x85f17cf997934a597031b2e18a9ab6ebd4b9f6a4 , @NEARProtocol  pays stakers about $146M a year in newly issued coins.

The issuance proposal's own benchmarks put validator hardware at about $1.3M a year.

That's quite a gap, but it isn't $145M of waste. Most staking rewards go to delegators, whose NEAR helps secure the network. Paying for hardware and keeping enough capital staked are different things.

Validators get no direct share of gas fees. Their protocol staking rewards come from issuance.

The current proposal would cut issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%, which takes those rewards down by about a third.

@sal_ternullo wants to go further eventually and end issuance altogether. That's not part of the current proposal, and there's no adopted replacement for staking rewards at zero issuance.

Meanwhile @near_intents bought $1.84M of NEAR in September. Repeat that record month twelve times and you get about $22M a year. Those coins are bought and held, not paid to stakers.

There's a separate idea on the @NEARProtocol  forum: use protocol revenue to buy NEAR and pay stakers, and cut issuance only after a full year shows the revenue holds up. It hasn't been adopted.

If you want a say in the cut, staking doesn't give you one. You need to lock NEAR in House of Stake before the voting-power snapshot. 

The issuance cut is still a proposal. Voting hasn't opened.

Here's the formal proposal:
https://t.co/pCq4W89cYU

The $1.3M estimates the hardware bill, but it doesn't tell us how far NEAR can cut staking rewards before holders start unstaking.

if you're a public figure in crypto with 7figs+ net worth you need the following at a MINIMUM (regardless of where u live):

1. video systems at every entry point to your house
2. full alarm system that you set every day/night when you sleep, any trigger should immediately inform an off-site 3rd party firm + the police
3. "panic button" that triggers the above alarm system
4. where legal/feasible, concealed weapons in every room
5. never answer the door unless you are specifically expecting something and know who it is, have an external drop-off system for parcels etc
6. try to live on a busy road/street with lots of cameras/cctv etc. best case is you live in a gated complex with security (many apartment complexes have this inexpensively)
7. if you don't live in a gated complex, then 24/7 security is actually much cheaper/affordable/non-intrusive compared to what you think
8. store significant amounts of your wealth in off-site locations, use multisigs with EOAs stored off-site etc and try to keep minimal amounts on hot wallets

most people don't bother to spend the time/money to setup the above, but like i said, if you're a public figure and u haven't bothered to take care of your personal security ur just putting urself at risk...don't leave it too late.

BITGET $390M HACK 🧵 We traced the stolen Zcash out of the private pool.

The attacker took 8 pieces of Bitget's stolen Zcash, 246.74 ZEC ($406.7k), and hid them in Zcash's private pool, where who pays whom is hidden.

Every piece came back out the same way: swapped to Bitcoin through NEAR Intents, from @zodl_app, the Zcash phone wallet formerly called Zashi. That matches the phone-wallet fingerprint we flagged on every shield.

The swap service keeps a public record of each swap: the Zcash transaction in, the Bitcoin address out. 4.77 BTC ($404.5k) came out to 10 Bitcoin addresses. 7 of them are missing from Bitget's attacker list.

ReplaySSM now runs in production in GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3, and ships in TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, FlashInfer, and SGLang!

It speeds up standard decoding (up to 1.47x) and speculative decoding (up to 2.1x), and now also enables a low-precision SSM state whose rounding error never propagates through the recurrence.

Building on our earlier ReplaySSM work, we collaborated with @NVIDIA to pin down what the method really unlocks. Caching SSM inputs instead of the state is what ReplaySSM does. What it changes is that computing the output and updating the state can be separated during decoding. All three gains follow from that separation.

Joint blog post, paper, and code with @NVIDIA and @tri_dao 👇

text:
# Sci-fi books on AI & neurotech

How might AI, BCI / neurotech, AR/VR and nanotech change the world?

My main approach to this Q is to understand others' visions of the future. Not just one or two, but *dozens*.

Fortunately there's a whole genre of writing for that: science fiction. There many great SF books with many different visions of AI, BCI etc. And a few TV great series and movies too.

Here's my list, with a bias to optimism.

## Books

Accelerando, by Charles Stross. A gonzo speedrun from the near-future with AR goggles, to the far future singularity. Early in the book, the protagonist loses his AR headset; in doing so, forgets who he is and stumbles around lost. Later on, his girlfriend leaves him because he was acting bird-brained for a couple centuries too long. Literally bird-brained: he’d transformed himself into a flock of birds.

Hyperion cantos, by Dan Simmons. God-like ASIs at the core of the plot. Surrounded by memorable imagery: winged posthumans breathing in space, burning trees & high-tech crucifixes, giant arches to teleport between worlds. Hugo winner.

A Fire Upon the Deep & A Deepness in the Sky, by Vernor Vinge. ASIs live in the "Fast Zone" as gods to the humans living in the "Slow Zone". There's a buffer zone in between. Intricate story weaving medieval era x space opera. Hugo winner x 2.

Saturn's Children duology & Singularity Sky, by Charles Stross. Two different pictures of a post-singularity world, with hilarious plot twists. Sex bots run amok. Described slow money <> fast money for cryptocurrency across galaxies, in 2013 (!)

Children of Time trilogy, by Adrian Tchaikovsky. Uploads; speedrunning evolution towards intelligence; swarm-like parasitic intelligences; living in a simulation. Ever wonder what sci-might look like if it used all the new science learnings of the last 20 years? This is your answer.

Avogadro Corp cantos, by William Hertling. Google's AI wakes up.

Rainbows End, by Vernor Vinge. The archetypical AR novel, set in the near future. Bonus: pragmatic telepathy aka "SMs" (silent messages.) Hugo winner.

Diamond Age, by Neal Stephenson. The archetypical nanotech novel, set in the near future. Bonus: future of learning. Hugo winner. Bonus: future of learning (YLIP).

Nexus trilogy, by Ramez Naam. Start with near-feature BCIs then extrapolate. Cyberpunk rave culture.

Neuromancer, by William Gibson. The archetypical cyberpunk novel, heavy on BCI & implants. More dystopian than I prefer, but the tech & culture content is unforgettable.

Daemon & FreedomTM, by Daniel Suarez. *Cypher* punk. A swarm of narrow AIs approaching AGI-like intelligence. Envisioned web3 before there was a web3; incentives, world-building, DAOs.

Snow Crash, by Neal Stephenson. The archetypical VR novel, set in the near future. Cypherpunk.

We Are Legion (We are Bob), by Dennis Taylor. Upload, clone yourself, explore the galaxy. VR as a tool to preserve sanity.

The Quantum Thief, by Hannu Rajaniemi. AIs, uploads, clones. Hilarity spanning galaxies in a heist story.

House of Suns, by Alistair Reynolds. Uploads & their clones, AIs, posthumans spanning galaxies

Blindsight, by Peter Watts. Humans with BCI & implants meet an alien intelligence.

Diaspora, by Greg Egan. For the first 50 pages, I didn't grok what I was reading, but I forged on. Then it dawned on me: this is what it would feel like to be a pattern of intelligence living among the stars. Whoa. This book is truly special, it will change your thinking more than anything else on this list.

On my shortlist to read, but I can't comment yet: Consider Phlebas by Ian M. Banks; Fine Structure by qntm; The Metamorphosis of Prime Intellect, by Roger Williams; Infinity Gate by M.R. Carey

## TV series

Pantheon. Uploads, then singularity.

Cyberpunk:Edgerunners. A cyberpunk world heavy on BCI & implants. "Brain dances": super-immersive VR of others' experiences. You'll have to look past the super-violence. (There's also related video games and graphic novels.)

## Movies
(I'm skipping the blockbusters here, to focus on lesser-appreciated movies that focus on the AI/etc.)

Transcendence, starring Johnny Depp. Brilliant scientist gets uploaded, and changes the world.

Strange Days, screenplay by James Cameron. "Brain dances" at the core of the plot.

Lawnmower Man, starring Keanu Reeves. Intelligence-enhancing experiments on the gardener.

text:
这个很像假货。

- 没有安全芯片。 正品 Nano S Plus 板上有两颗 ST 芯片。U2 是 STM32F042K6，官方图上能直接看到 F042K6 字样。U4 是 ST33 安全芯片，你这块只有一颗主芯片，找不到第二颗。

- 主芯片上只有 Ledger 标志，没有型号。 正规芯片表面印的是芯片厂的标志、型号和批号。Ledger 用的是 ST 的现成芯片，不可能给芯片单独印自己的标志。

- 多了一颗 40MHz 晶振。 X1 上印着 40.000，这是乐鑫 ESP32 系列芯片。正品用的 STM32F042 不需要外接晶振就能跑 USB，官方板上也确实没有晶振。

- 布局和丝印完全是另一套。 正品的按键在板子上沿，标作 SW1/SW2，还印有板厂编号和日期码（E232940、JOVE3 2203）。你这块的按键在下沿，标作 S2，看不到任何板厂标记。

You already gave the LLM the answer. So why is it writing it out from scratch?

Introducing a new AI model architecture: Constrained Decoding Models (CDMs)

LLMs were built to write. Most production workloads just need an answer: fast, consistent, and affordable.

CDMs are purpose-built for 1 task each. They read your input once and skip the token-by-token generative loop that makes LLMs slow and expensive.

Not just a decision model, but a family of 3 CDMs live today:

• Classify: define your labels and get back a calibrated probability + reason for each. Used for routing, tagging, and intent detection.
 • Extract: describe the entities in natural language and get back well-formed JSON with confidence scores + citations. Used for web scraping, document processing, and PII redaction.
 • Summarize: pass in long text, images, or PDFs and get back a consistent summary under 1,000 tokens. Used for context compaction, metadata generation, and transcript digests.

Built for production:

• 1M tokens of multimodal (text + image) input, 31x larger than Jev
 • 77.2% on DecisionBench vs Jev's 72%
 • 200x faster, 467x cheaper than frontier LLM APIs
 • $0.05/M input tokens. Output is free (yes, even for summarize)

author: stanisloou
quoted_text:
Base 可能找到了 meme 问题的一条解法。线索就在今天新加坡的一个房间里。

@jessepollak 今天闭门见了 Base 中文社区，会后还专门用中文发推：「Base 属于每一个人。」

参会的人透露了更多细节：
> @KuiGas 说，这已经是 Base 今天的第二场闭门会，连开发者社区的负责人都带来了
> @David_MetaWorld 问他未来一年 Base 最重要的方向。据他说，Jesse 的回答是：第一交易，第二支付，第三链上金融
> @BroLeon 写道，Jesse 表示以后会更重视中文社区。现在的问题只剩一个：Base 怎么让大家赚到钱
> 他还说，Base 在 meme 上的表现「一言难尽」，这个问题他当面也提了

问题大家都知道。有意思的是，这次是 Jesse 自己来找中文圈。

去年 10 月，中文圈已经演示过一次这种力量：
> 币安人生：一个钱包 3 天把 3,500 美元变成 790 万美元
> 10 万多个地址参与，40 个钱包赚到 100 万美元以上，900 个赚到 10 万美元以上
> BNB 链上 DEX 单日成交超过 60 亿美元

另一面也来得很快。10 月 9 日 CZ 特意说自己的推文「不是背书」，同一天一批 meme 在 24 小时内跌了 60% 到 95%。

BNB 当时有 CZ 的推特，也有 Binance 的上币和生态资源一起放大。Base 没有同样的机器，但它正在搭另一套：
> $BLUECHIP 和 $BASECAT 已经上 Coinbase
> @o1_exchange 把 41 只美股代币做成 quote assets，并把 launchpad 收入的 2% 分给 BD 和 ambassadors
> 昨天，Base 中文社区的创始人之一 @juliezize 加入 o1，成为联合创始人兼 CFO

我的判断很简单：Base 的 meme 现在缺的是人。
上一次中文圈认真玩 meme，3 天出了一个 790 万美元的钱包。这一次，Jesse 亲自来请人了。

我赌：Base 下一轮 meme 行情，会从中文圈开始。

text:
Anthropic CEO 回答了大家最关心的问题：现在还该不该学编程？

1. 编程会最先被淘汰。
AI 模型已经在做这件事了。更广泛的软件工程任务虽然会慢一些，但也在退潮。如果你学编程只是为了保住饭碗，那方向就错了。

2. 哪怕你只做 5% 的工作，依然有价值。
AI 做 95%，你做 5%，你的生产力能提升 20 倍。比较优势的威力非常惊人，哪怕差距巨大。

3. 最有前景的职业，是以人为中心的。
把人际、物理世界和分析能力结合起来的工作。他举了放射科医生的例子：理解患者和背景的医生，而不只是会看片子的人。

4. 批判性思维可能是未来十年最重要的能力。
当 AI 什么都能生成时，分辨真假的能力就变得稀缺又宝贵。你不想抱着错误信念，也不想被骗。这是他给 25 岁年轻人的实际建议。

5. 用不好 AI，它会让你变蠢。
Anthropic 做过相关研究。取决于你怎么用模型，编码能力的衰退是可测量、真实存在的。问题不在工具，而在不当使用。

6. 他看好半导体在未来十年的资本主义胜利。

author: EggheadCobra
quoted_text:
For a while now, I've noticed that some people are still confused about Psylocke, who she is, and which is which. Psylocke is known for having one of the messiest stories in all of Marvel, so how about I try my best to explain it as simply as possible?

- There are three Psylockes.
Betsy Braddock, Kwannon, and Sai.

- Betsy Braddock was the original Psylocke, Kwannon is an assassin, Sai is a demon slayer.

- Betsy and Kwannon are both in Earth-616, Sai is from an alternate universe.

- Betsy and Kwannon had an extremely messy and complicated body swap story that ended in Kwannon dying, and Betsy being permanently stuck in Kwannon's body.

- A few years ago, Kwannon was resurrected in her original body, and Betsy was given her body back.

- Betsy became Captain Britain, Kwannon is now Psylocke.

Fun facts about them!
- Betsy was stuck in Kwannon's body for over 20 years of Marvel's publications.
- Kwannon is not her real name, and it is yet to be revealed.
- In X-Men: Demon Days, Sai killed her world's Venom with the help of Hulkmaru (Her world's Hulk). Galacta gave Psylocke the Venom accessory as a reminder of one of her greatest victories.

Many speculate that Sai was chosen for Marvel Rivals because the devs wanted to distance themselves from the Betsy Kwannon debacle, which, in my opinion, was the smart thing to do.

This was only a heavily simplified version of Psylocke. If you'd like to look more into their backstories, just be warned that it gets very messy, especially the body swap.

Trading venues will need to adjust their approach to expansion into new geos, cooperation with regulators, and general strategy.

Banks, broker dealers, and trad venues will need to learn how to build onchain (and fast).

Overall it's a complete sea change for the industry.

text: A digital asset treasury should be more than a passive vehicle for its ecosystem. Our CEO Christopher Jensen on how StablecoinX can serve as the institutional gateway between Ethena and TradFi: a two-way bridge that distributes Ethena's products into TradFi and connects new institutional users and capital into Ethena's expanding yield layer.
author: stablecoin_x
quoted_text:
A DAT Is Not a Megaphone Anymore. It Is a Distribution Channel.

Panelists Christopher Jensen (@jensane2001, @stablecoin_x), Hyunsu Jung (@hyperiondefi) and Kevin Lepsoe (@lepsoe, @ETHGasOfficial) discussed "Digital Asset Treasury: The New Frontier of Corporate Finance."

What is a DAT actually for?

Not promotion, and Jensen said it plainly. His StablecoinX holds roughly 20% of Ethena's total token supply.

"DAT companies are no longer simply businesses that promote or speak for a specific digital asset."

His reframe: the ecosystems behind these assets contain real products, and a DAT can push those products through distribution channels protocols cannot reach directly. Holding company to distribution platform is a different business, and he called the shift a significant one for the category.

Is accumulating the job?

No, and Jung of Hyperion DeFi treated that as an obligation rather than an option. What DATs need to do is go beyond continuing to accumulate and consistently contribute to the growth of those ecosystems, which means putting the balance sheet backed by those holdings to practical use. His own example: when new markets or products launch on Hyperliquid, Hyperion can supply capital and infrastructure and share in the resulting revenue, while building credit and trading infrastructure for participants entering the ecosystem.

So how should anyone value these companies?

This is the consequence nobody has priced yet. Jensen's read is that market cap to modified net asset value is the first metric comparing across DATs, but over time they get valued as a sum of their parts. Treasury assets on one side, operating businesses using those assets on the other, and the operating side judged on revenue, customers and ARR like any other company.

If DATs start trading on ARR instead of token beta, the whole category re-rates on operations.

Moderated by Jun Kim (@junkim), General Manager of Investor Relations at Hashed (@hashed_official).

text: More game launches and higher trading volume → more protocol revenue → more $LOAD buybacks and burns, creating sustained deflationary pressure.
author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
$LOAD represents a potential repricing of the game financing sector, rather than just another GameFi launchpad.

8sWe4GzK1YqG3vyzKHf8ZyB1WB5asofw2o6TqgFePtPo 

My view is that the most interesting aspect of Loadout is its attempt to solve a long-standing problem in crypto gaming: how to turn the liquidity of crypto markets into actual development funding for traditional game studios, rather than packaging games as crypto products and selling them to crypto investors.

This is fundamentally different from the traditional GameFi approach. Loadout does not require games to revolve around tokens. Instead, it allows independent and AA studios to issue tokens and obtain ongoing development funding through public trading. Players can still play these games on Steam, consoles, and other traditional platforms, while on-chain tokens handle financing and market trading.

Founder Kieran Warwick has described this as one of the most practically useful applications of crypto for the gaming industry: capital formation.

However, the investment thesis for LOAD needs to be split into two parts: whether Loadout can become an effective game financing channel, and whether the platform's growth can genuinely translate into value for LOAD. The former has a clear product design; the latter is still in the early stages of validation.

I still believe this narrative has a real-world foundation, for several reasons.

Traditional game financing has several structural problems.

Publishers provide funding and distribution support but may take 30%–70% of a game's revenue in return. VCs generally prefer projects that fit their return models, making it difficult for ordinary indie studios to secure funding. Government grants involve application requirements and long waiting periods, while Kickstarter requires developers to have strong demos, marketing materials, and community traction before they can successfully raise money.

In Loadout's founder article, Kieran Warwick connects these problems to the failures of crypto gaming. Many studios sold tokens to retail investors at valuations far above those offered to early investors, even when their products were still immature. His experience building Illuvium also gave him firsthand insight into the conflicts between early-stage financing, retail valuations, and game development timelines.

Loadout's approach is to use what crypto markets have already demonstrated they can do well: global trading, instant liquidity, and public market pricing.

The process is relatively straightforward. Studios submit playable demos, design documents, team information, roadmaps, and funding plans, then issue tokens through a bonding curve. There are no presales, private rounds, or VC discounts. Tokens begin trading on the public market, and the fees generated by trading continuously flow into the studio's treasury instead of providing a one-time injection of capital at launch.

This design has two implications.

First, studios do not need to give up equity or depend on publishers to fund the next stage of development.

Second, investors are no longer limited to buying into projects only after they launch at substantially higher valuations than those offered in private rounds. They can participate earlier in the public market and decide whether to continue holding or exit based on the game's subsequent progress.

This does not guarantee that every game will succeed. It is an attempt to let public markets play a greater role in capital allocation.

Second: The financing mechanism is what makes Loadout interesting

Loadout charges a 5% trading fee, of which 4% goes directly to the game's treasury and 1% goes to the protocol. The official documentation acknowledges that this is higher than the fees charged by ordinary DEXs. However, the goal is not simply to offer low-cost trading; it is to make trading itself part of the game's financing mechanism.

A breakdown of the fees generated by every $100 in trading volume would look like this:

$4 — Game treasury: Used for development, operations, marketing, and growth.
$1 — Loadout protocol: Used for platform operations.
The remaining $95 is the amount left after the 5% fee, before accounting for other trading costs. This example follows the official 5% fee model and does not represent every trader's actual slippage or final execution cost.

As a result, trading volume affects not only token prices but also how much development funding a studio can receive.

Based on the official fee rate:

At $10,000 in daily trading volume, the studio receives $400 per day, or $12,000 over 30 days.
At $50,000 in daily trading volume, the studio receives $2,000 per day, or $60,000 over 30 days.
At $100,000 in daily trading volume, the studio receives $4,000 per day, or $120,000 over 30 days.

This means a game that attracts sustained attention and trading activity could gradually build a meaningful development budget without relying on traditional financing.

However, actual financing capacity depends on sustained, genuine trading volume rather than market capitalization itself. If a token is driven only by short-term speculation and trading volume quickly declines, the studio's funding source will shrink accordingly.

Another important design feature is that once a project reaches 85 SOL, its token migrates from the bonding curve to a Meteora DLMM pool, with liquidity permanently locked according to the official rules. Studio tokens come in two modes: Fair Launch and Studio Launch. The latter allows the team and treasury to retain certain token allocations, subject to on-chain linear vesting.

These mechanisms help standardize the launch process, but permanently locked liquidity does not guarantee price stability or ensure that the game will eventually be delivered.

The most important question for the investment thesis is LOAD's own value capture

Three different assets need to be distinguished here: individual game tokens, the Loadout platform token LOAD, and the SOL received by studio treasuries.

Game tokens reflect the market pricing of individual games. Studios receive trading fees to fund development. LOAD, meanwhile, represents a bet on the platform's future growth and token economics. Trading volume in game tokens cannot automatically be counted as revenue for LOAD.

Based on the platform's current product and rewards pages, Loadout has established trading rewards, referral rewards, and an XP points system. The current rewards page shows that Season 0 has a reward pool equivalent to 12.5% of the token supply. Historical Solana trading volume and realized profits affect XP calculations, and users need to link their X accounts to earn points. Subsequent seasons are also expected to introduce rewards based on trading volume, early participation, and trading-volume tiers.

The purpose of this system is to attract early traders and encourage them to trade game tokens and refer other users. It could help Loadout build an initial user base, but there is an important question: how much of the trading volume generated by these incentives comes from genuine investment demand for games, and how much exists simply to farm rewards?

If traders are only generating volume to qualify for rewards, the platform's reported activity may not translate into sustainable revenue.

Another key issue is protocol revenue. Under the official fee structure, the 1% protocol fee is used for platform operations. Third-party market sources also describe LOAD as a utility token with staking and buyback-and-burn mechanisms. However, these sources are insufficient to confirm the actual buyback amounts, triggering conditions, or whether the mechanism has been consistently executed on-chain.

For now, I would not classify LOAD as a token already supported by stable cash flows. What needs to be verified is how much of the platform's fee revenue goes toward operations, how much is explicitly allocated to the Illuvium DAO, token buybacks, or other mechanisms, and whether these allocations are backed by on-chain records.

This is particularly important because Kieran's founder article states that Loadout will direct a portion of its fees to the Illuvium DAO and plans to distribute a substantial portion of its tokens to the Illuvium community, although the details were still to be announced at the time. Loadout is an independent protocol, and Illuvium is not its funding source.

This gives the project potential advantages in terms of founder experience and ecosystem distribution, but it also means that the economic relationship between DAO fee allocations, community token distributions, and LOAD holders needs further clarification.

What is the market betting on?

I believe there are three main bets.

First, game financing could become a new productive use case for crypto markets.

Loadout does not require studios to become Web3 game projects first. Instead, it allows traditional games to access crypto market capital. If this model succeeds, it could expand across more studios, game genres, and ongoing financing scenarios. That would have greater commercial significance than simply adding another category of GameFi tokens.

Second, Kieran Warwick's industry experience could attract genuine game supply.

Loadout is currently in discussions with more than 100 studios, with 33 having confirmed plans to launch. This is an important supply-side signal, but it is necessary to distinguish between studios that have confirmed participation and those that have actually launched tokens, generated sustained trading activity, and successfully raised funding.

If these studios launch as planned and their projects generate genuine trading activity, Loadout could begin building a consistent pipeline of game financing opportunities.

Third, trading in game tokens, platform rewards, and protocol revenue could form a growth loop.

More studios launch → more games enter the market → traders discover and trade game tokens → studio treasuries receive development funding → game development progresses → new developments attract more traders.

If the platform also generates protocol revenue and allocates part of it to verified LOAD buybacks or other clearly defined value-capture mechanisms, ecosystem growth could eventually translate into additional value for the platform token.

However, this loop remains an unproven business model rather than an established flywheel. Its success depends not simply on the number of projects launching, but on whether games can sustain attention, whether traders remain active on the platform, and whether studios can deliver products with the funds they raise.

The catalysts I would watch next

I would focus on four specific developments.

1. Whether studios continue launching as planned.

The official page currently lists upcoming projects, including The Signal: Stranded on Sirenis, scheduled for October 15; Cosminers, scheduled for October 18; and Lo and Behold, scheduled for October 21.

Whether these projects launch on schedule, and whether they generate genuine game content, trading activity, and treasury inflows after launch, matters more than the raw number of studios that have expressed interest.

2. Whether project treasuries actually accumulate sustained funding.

We need to monitor each game's trading volume, the cumulative fees generated by the 4% treasury allocation, the movement of funds into project treasuries, and whether those funds are used for development and operations. If trading volume increases without translating into usable funding for studios, the financing thesis will remain unproven.

3. Whether Season 0 rewards and subsequent seasons generate user retention.

Early trading incentives can attract users, but the more important question is whether users continue returning to trade game tokens after the reward period ends, and whether the platform can maintain organic activity without incentives.

4. Whether LOAD's value capture becomes clear and verifiable.

The key metrics are protocol revenue, on-chain execution of buybacks and burns, staking mechanisms, and fee allocations to the Illuvium DAO. If the project consistently discloses these figures, LOAD's valuation thesis could move from early-stage traffic and narrative expectations toward a more measurable economic model.

Ultimately, what matters is whether projects continue launching, studio treasuries accumulate real development funding, games demonstrate tangible progress, and reward-driven trading turns into organic demand.

If these elements gradually materialize, Loadout could evolve from an innovative game-financing launchpad into a long-term interface between traditional gaming and crypto capital. Conversely, even if LOAD attracts high trading volume during its initial launch due to its narrative and trading incentives, that alone would not establish a sustainable business model.

Worth reading in full. Drop any further questions below👇
author: FlareNetworks
quoted_text:
⚡️ How Flare usage feeds back into FIRE and FLR

There are two separate paths.

The first one is simple: every transaction fee paid in FLR is burned. That was already part of Flare, but after FIP.16 the base fee is higher, so real network activity now burns more much more FLR than before.

The second path is FIRE.

FIRE is the protocol revenue pool created by FIP.16. Its main job is to reduce FLR supply as much as possible, either directly through FLR buyback and burn, or indirectly by supporting validator and staker rewards so  FLR inflation decreases.

Right now, the tracked streams going into FIRE are:

90% of FDC attestation request fees, paid in FLR.
100% of FXRP destination-tag registration fees, paid in FLR.
100% of FAssets direct minting fees, paid in FXRP.
10% of FAssets redemption fees, paid in FXRP.

The remaining 10% of FDC fees still goes through the existing reward path, and the rest of the FAssets redemption fee stays with the agent and collateral pool.

So the basic idea is:

More transactions burn more FLR, more protocol usage sends more fees to FIRE, and FIRE is designed to push that value back into FLR economics.

text:
A blockchain transaction can be easy for a person to understand and still be difficult for software to execute reliably.
Imagine an AI agent paying for a service across different blockchain environments. It needs to know where the asset lives, how ownership is verified, and what happens if execution fails halfway.
A human might notice the problem and try another route. Software needs predictable rules and clear outcomes.
As more applications become automated, these infrastructure details matter just as much as transaction speed or cost.
This is one reason @WireNetwork 's Universal Transaction Layer (UTL) is worth understanding. It is designed to coordinate transactions and ownership across supported ecosystems while assets remain on their native chains.
The interesting challenge isn't simply letting software initiate transactions. It's making cross-chain activity reliable enough for software to use without manually handling every layer of complexity.
Infrastructure built for software needs to be predictable by design.

A lot of RSI pitches are really just people using AI to build better AI. Tech has always worked that way. You needed computers to build chips. Steam engines got better once you could get coal faster.

- VCs are dead. Or at least the VC market I remember from previous conferences. Far fewer investors around, with the remaining funds increasingly focused on growth-stage businesses or liquid tokens. Good time for established businesses, much tougher for early-stage founders.

- Everyone wants to become a vault curator or run a yield fund.

- More and more wrappers are appearing, allocating capital to the same onchain opportunities. Unless you're bringing some actual alpha, I'm not sure what value you're adding for LPs.

- LPs are getting more sophisticated. They want direct relationships with protocols, transparency into what's happening with their capital, and liquidity. But they're also starting to accept that locking up capital for a defined period can mean better yield.

- Term deposits are the next meta. Crypto lending is fully commoditized, so you need to look elsewhere for an edge. Right now, there's plenty of edge in term lending.

- Looping is still one of the few ways to squeeze more yield out of existing opportunities. Sophisticated LPs prefer doing it themselves, but less sophisticated users increasingly have access to automated strategies. You can already access this through @OseroHQ Yield+, powered by @Gauntlet

- We need more yield from the real world. Crypto has always been an incredible tool for capital formation, and there's a lot more we can do with it.

- I'm already seeing people financing everything from invoices and international trade to orange juice vending machines in Singapore. Yes, actual orange juice machines.

- Scalable yield for USDT is still missing. And the demand for it in Asia is hard to ignore.

- Crypto is becoming infrastructure for TradFi and the real economy. Something we've been talking about for years is actually happening.

The cypherpunk days are fading. Some people aren't ready to accept it yet.

Soon we'll all be wearing suits.

Are you focusing all your skill upgrades and stats purely on damage?!

That might work for boss fights, but understanding how crowd control works is key to winning in PvP!

First, Stun, Frost, and Airborne can be removed with Defiance, but Root and Seal (silence) cannot! Once an opponent uses Defiance to break out of Stun or Frost, they also become immune to new Roots and Seals for 5–7 seconds!

The key is to disable your opponent and hit them while they can’t fight back! That’s why investing in stats that improve your chances of landing crowd control is so important!

One of the most important tools in a Sorcerer’s kit is the specialization for Soul Freeze, our silence skill, that adds a 50% chance to Root the target for 5 seconds! Bittercold Wind also has a Root effect, lasting 3 seconds!

On the Taiwan server, I’ve raised my chance of landing these Root effects to nearly 200%, so they land every time against opponents with 100% status effect resistance or less!

With the right combination, that means I can unleash my Sorcerer’s damage skills on a helpless opponent for up to 8 seconds!

Of course, top PvP players make sure to build up their status effect resistance too!

text:
按照目前全球 AI 基础设施的投资规模，到 2031 年，AI 行业需要每年创造 6 万亿美元收入，才能支撑这些算力投资。

但即便把 ChatGPT、Claude、AI Coding 和所有现有企业 AI 应用未来的收入都算进去，乐观估计也只有 1.8 万亿美元。

剩下 70% 的收入，要靠机器人、自动驾驶、药物研发，以及一大堆还没诞生的产品来填。

整个 AI 行业正在拼命让智能变得越来越便宜，却又指望靠卖智能赚回天文数字般的投资。

模型价格战、开源竞争、推理成本暴跌，大家都在欢呼 AI 的边际成本趋近于零。

但问题是，使用量暴涨不等于收入同比例暴涨。

如果 AI 真的成为一种随处可得、极其廉价的基础能力，创造出来的经济价值可能非常惊人，但这些价值未必能被模型公司和数据中心运营商捕获。

一个企业可能靠 AI 节省了 1 亿美元的人力成本，最后却只需要向 AI 公司支付 100 万美元。

所以我越来越觉得，AI 行业可能正在犯一个非常昂贵的错误，用技术的长期价值，来证明眼前任何规模的资本开支都是合理的。

尤其是 GPU 还在不断迭代，今天建设的数据中心有明确的折旧周期，但未来的商业模式没有兑现期限。

这场 AI 泡沫最讽刺的结局，可能是 AI 真的成功了，投资 AI 基础设施的人却亏得一塌糊涂。

技术革命的赢家，未必是为革命买单的人。

有人把谷歌EmbeddingGemma 2改造成了语音识别模型，实现了非常惊人的端侧推理速度，快得离谱

M3 MacBook Air，1小时音频转写约13秒，处理速度288×

WER 5%，领先的STT在2%～3%，如果后续reader迭代能把WER压到3%以下，估计专用端侧STT市场要重新洗牌了

传统STT需要专门训练一个声音→文字生成模型，但是今天，EmbeddingGemma 2已经能把文本、图片、音频和视频映射到同一个语义空间，让声音的“你好”和文字的“你好”在向量空间中相互靠近

于是网友在不修改EmbeddingGemma 2参数的情况下，只在上面训练一个轻量Reader，把音频切片编码成向量后，直接在模型的文本空间里检索最近的词，把转录从生成问题变成了检索问题，把它“歪”成了一个语音转文字模型

目前5%的WER，用在容错要求相对较高的比如说会议录音整理、采访转写、语音笔记、视频字幕初稿等场景，有一定的实用潜力

Thanks to @redkev , he first noticed the robinhood:0x07ebb29a38fbcb41563817e5e19f2cec619c90d2 token and initially saw it as just another meme coin. But when I started digging deeper, I came across the @Moshdottrade project. As it turned out, the token is only 1% of the meme and 99% technology focused on fair launches, AI agent market making, and anti-whale supply control.

I spent some time in the Mosh Telegram, and what really caught my attention was the way the admins and developers communicate with the community. It reminded me of December 2023, when I joined @HPOS10Ireturns chat and got a response from @HalloweenIn2008 (even though back then I was just a user with a Russian name)

I really liked @justinbebis mindset:

“I don’t even care if the price pumps over the next few months. Let’s look at the results of our work at least a year from now.”

For some reason, that really resonated with me. And that’s saying something, considering I’ve been in crypto for around three years and have heard countless slogans like “This is extremely bullish,” “We have huge plans,” and so on.

But with Mosh, I genuinely want to believe in the technology because I can see how a team of honest developers could actually put these ideas into practice.

@vmudream has always said something along the lines of:

“https://t.co/6NXJrjFv0Q and other launchpads are destroying token launches because you can buy 70% of the supply through bundles for next to nothing and slowly drain retail traders. Make token launches cost at least $2K.”

So, what exactly is Mosh?

Mosh is a project that allows developers to launch tokens with 1–90% of the supply bundled into AI agent wallets, where those tokens are permanently locked. These AI agents act as market makers, with the goal of accumulating both the token and ETH while operating 24/7 without emotions.

Developers earn a percentage of the platform fees, which they can set during the launch.

But what are the actual advantages of this launch model?

Let’s say a developer wants to bundle 70% of a token’s supply into AI agents. To do that, they pay approximately $10K in ETH, which becomes the initial liquidity in the LP.

One of the key points here is that a whale can’t simply buy 2% of the supply for $200 and then dump it once the price goes up. The initial market cap is expected to be around 50K+, making that kind of cheap supply acquisition much harder.

I hope I’ve managed to get the idea across well enough for anyone interested to start digging deeper into the project themselves.

Now, coming back to robinhood:0x07ebb29a38fbcb41563817e5e19f2cec619c90d2 

Essentially, BUN is the flagship token of the Mosh ecosystem, accumulating fees generated by the platform.

If you believe in the potential of Robinhood Chain and think Mosh can establish its place within that ecosystem, then BUN could have significant upside potential.

I’m honestly pretty frustrated that I didn’t make this post yesterday, when the price dropped to its lows. It has already bounced back this morning, so please don’t take this as an exit liquidity post. That’s not the intention.

I simply wanted to share something I found interesting and potentially valuable, and hopefully give some people a reason to look into Mosh for themselves.

One final note: Mosh is still in beta. However, version v0.1 is already live, with the platform open to developers. I’ve also heard that v1, with additional features, is expected to launch within the next 1–4 weeks.

As always, do your own research. I’m sharing my perspective and what caught my attention, not telling anyone what to buy.

Hopefully, someone here finds this useful. 🤝

text:
卧槽，这个看起来好厉害

这是一个特别有意思的开源项目，叫 Consensus。

它的思路很简单，你问它任何问题，它就去 X 和 Reddit 上阅读超过 10,000 条帖子和评论，然后把人们的观点分类，统计出每种观点占多少比例。

比如问它「AI 会毁灭人类吗？」

61% 的人认为会
28% 的人认为不会
10% 的人认为人类自己才是最大的风险
1% 持其他观点

每个百分比都能追溯到背后具体的帖子和评论。你可以直接去看那些人到底说了什么。

我觉得这个产品抓住了一个很有价值的需求。

我们现在已经有太多 AI 在试图告诉我们正确答案了，但很多时候，我其实更想知道其他人究竟怎么想，尤其是那些跟我意见完全相反的人。

当然，X 和 Reddit 的用户有很强的样本偏差，这些数字也不能当成科学民调。更何况社交媒体上最爱发言的人，未必代表沉默的大多数。

但对做媒体、投资、品牌和产品的人来说，这东西真的太有用了。以前需要翻几百条帖子才能摸清的舆论分歧，现在可以直接查询，还能顺着证据往下挖。

我甚至觉得，随着这类产品成熟，我们可能会看到一种新的搜索习惯：搜索一个问题时，顺便看看全世界的人正在怎么争论它。

text:
This is burnout, and if you want to survive as a trader, you must learn to recognize it.

True burnout is not just being overworked, nor is it something you can push through. It is a feedback loop that occurs when your body experiences intense, prolonged stress.

Stress is part of life, and under normal conditions you can recover from it easily. In fact, many dimensions of human performance - strength, endurance, mental acuity - actually require stress in order to grow.

However, growth in response to stress can only happen when the stress is manageable and offset by periods of recovery. When the stress is extreme and constant, the body fails to adapt and enters a downward spiral.

As stress accumulates, several things happen physiologically:
- sleep is disrupted
- hormones become dysregulated
- mental performance degrades
- heart rate variability falls 
- inflammation rises and immune function declines

The problem is that each of these effects also *reduces your ability to withstand and recover from stress.* So you enter a vicious cycle where recovery becomes impossible and performance steadily deteriorates.

The experience @agapestride describes here is exactly what it feels like to burn out from trading. And if you find yourself in this situation, the most important thing you can do is *recognize what has happened.* 

You are not dumber than you used to be. You are not more indecisive. You are not more impulsive, fearful, or greedy. You are simply physiologically impaired by severe, chronic stress.

When you notice the signs of burnout, you must prioritize recovery above all else:
- cut your risk
- stop looking at charts
- get off social media
- play sports or start running
- spend time with friends and family
- go hiking or traveling
- take lots of hot baths

As much as it feels like the best time to make generational wealth is RIGHT NOW, the market will always be here. So take a break and don't come back until you know your body can handle it.

text:
GM 🤝

There’s a lot of chatter around $NEAR, and it sort of forced me into doing some extensive research. So I hereby announce the NEARies, a series of short posts with @NEARProtocol in the spotlight.

People are calling for an ATH (some even go as far as $155 per token), and I'm here to crunch the numbers, crack dad jokes, and occasionally write something seemingly smart.
I'll start with a TL;DR because I can:

🟢 NEAR Intents routed ~$35B in total, up from $5B less than a year ago, and most of that growth happened while the token traded under $2.50.

🟢 over the last 30 days, Intents earned about $8M in fees, of which the protocol kept ~$2.6M (30-ish %). Fees are captured from trades roughly 595k unique users have facilitated.

🟢 those captured fees buy NEAR tokens on the open market, holding them out of circulation. The buybacks (we all love) currently offset ~19% of new issuance (far from deflationary, but the team's been working on it).

🟢 max inflation actually halved from 5% to 2.5% some time ago. A draft proposal would trim inflation from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. If it passes, about 12M fewer NEAR tokens would be minted over 2 years. Quick maff: that's roughly what today's buybacks remove in the same period.

🟢 buybacks are sweet, and so are token burns. A 100% gas burn (up from 70%) has been approved, and it will ship with nearcore v2.14, which has been on testnet since mid-September and has no mainnet date yet (but it'll certainly happen before GTA VI).

🟢 confidential TVL ((money users keep inside Intent's private mode (different from DeFi TVL)) is about $169M, up ~4.6x in just 90 days. Cool fact: NEAR earns on private execution without being a privacy coin.

🟢 post-quantum keys are live on mainnet: accounts upgrade by rotating keys, with no need to move funds.

🟢 Bitwise's NRR (first US spot NEAR ETF) pulled >$75M in net inflows over its first 10 trading days, with 0 (zero) outflow days. Relative to market cap, that's actually the strongest early days inflow of any US crypto spot ETF.

Alrighty, that's just an intro. The question is, is NEAR a temporary trend or is it here to stay?

In my opinion, it's here to stay, and you'll understand why once you read the coming pieces in this NEARies. And btw, just because I believe it has legs, it doesn't mean I'm a financial advisor. Au contraire, the token is up 115% in the last 30 days and a healthy pullback (TA experts will notice there's a retest as well) is expected. What's your take?

running your own internal greptile is usually more expensive than paying for greptile. 

usually $5-$20/review to get in the vicinity of greptile quality vs $1/review for greptile.

we have one of the largest dataset of buggy PRs in the world. this means we can know for sure if a particular version of our agent is more or less effective than another. 

as a result, we can experiment with hundreds of permutations of models, harnesses, techniques, tools to eek out maximum performance per dollar. 

we then pass those savings onto the user.

we can only do this because of the dataset. if we didn’t have it, we won’t know for sure if a new version really can catch every unique one in a million bug.

So happy to have @brian__foster joining @Morpho to lead GTM!
