This is truly the start of a new era for onchain finance.
author: Morpho
quoted_text:
I’m excited to share that I’ve joined @Morpho to lead all things commercial as Head of GTM.

@PaulFrambot and team are visionaries and world-class builders. It’s a privilege to team up with them.

What’s Morpho?

Morpho is an open credit network that enables people and agents to build customizable onchain lending, borrowing, and yield products.

Morpho protocols, smart contracts, and blockchains are the infrastructure making it possible. Morpho is a pure technology layer, with composability and security at the center of its design.

The why

Morpho makes it dead simple for our partners - fintechs, brokerages, exchanges, and banks - to build revenue-generating products that help their users put their assets to work. In parallel, this helps unlock new distribution for lenders and asset issuers.

Historically, spinning up credit products meant building pricing, risk and liquidation systems from scratch, and spending months on integrations before the first loan went out.

Morpho collapses this into open infrastructure: liquidity, rates, and liquidations run onchain, in markets anyone can access.

We’re growing

More than $17B is now deposited on Morpho protocols, up 3.4x since the beginning of 2025.

So far, BTC, USDC, ETH  and other stablecoins have anchored most of that growth. But these assets have also laid the foundation for what's coming next, by getting institutions comfortable with onchain infrastructure…

The onchain collateral supernova

…Now, Wall Street is racing to tokenize treasuries, funds, credit, and equities. “Crypto native” collateral will keep growing, but the tokenization wave has the potential to be orders of magnitude larger.

Onchain credit markets will accelerate tokenization growth because they make tokenized assets more productive: they becomes programmable collateral that people can borrow against 24/7, in seconds.

In the not so distant future, we’ll have tens of thousands of tokenized assets and $ trillions more in value onchain. Humans and agents will flock to the fastest and most composable system.

In credit, Morpho is poised to be that system.

First orders of business

It’s day one for me, but it’s already clear a lot of my work will rhyme with what I focused on over the last 7+ years scaling Coinbase’s institutional and infrastructure businesses: helping make our partners successful.

Over the next few weeks, I’ll be on a listening tour. If you’re working on credit products - as a fintech, lender, curator, asset issuer or something else - drop me a line. We want to hear from you and help you grow.

Last but not least: we’re hiring! …Across GTM and beyond. Come get in touch if you’re as excited about the Morpho vision as I am.

Let’s go.

- API docs [https://t.co/1JedjYXLvH]
- About Morpho [https://t.co/lJfsBSGeF4]
- Our recent $175M raise from a16z, Ribbit Capital, Paradigm, Apollo, and others [https://t.co/bWXe59WRpJ]

text:
一个 4B 模型，学会「怎么改 Agent」之后，在没见过的任务上，平均改得比 35B Teacher 还好。

这篇工作有意思的地方是把「如何改 Harness」本身训练成了一种可以迁移的能力。

系统里有两个角色：

Solver 负责做任务，Proposer 观察执行结果，再修改 Solver 的 Harness，包括模型调用、工具使用、信息流和控制逻辑。

训练阶段，Proposer 用 RL 学习哪些修改真的有效。

到了新任务上，两个模型的权重全部冻结，Proposer 只根据执行反馈继续改 Harness。

在 21 个训练时没见过的 Reasoning Gym 任务上，4B Proposer 的平均修改得分从 0.32 提升到 0.62，超过 35B Teacher 的 0.56。

还有就是它只训练过单次修改，却能在测试时连续迭代。

在未见过的 MuSiQue 上，独立修改平均只有 0.15，连续改 10 轮后达到 0.27；在两个未见 QA benchmark 上，连续修改甚至超过了从 80 个独立方案里挑出的最好结果。

所以 Harness 自进化再往前一步会变成训练出一个会持续改工作流的 Agent。

它学到的，是一种改进方法本身。

text:
我觉得 AI 创业的终局，可能是亲手干掉自己的客户。

刚看完一份旧金山过去 60 天完成 A 轮融资的 24 家创业公司名单，其中最让我感兴趣的，是 Epsilon Health。

这家公司拿了 2760 万美元融资，直接把 AI 软件和医生结合起来，经营放射影像诊疗业务。

还有 Jack & Jill，融资 6000 万美元，用 AI Agent 直接撮合求职者和雇主；Kastle，融资 2680 万美元，把 AI 劳动力带进银行后台；Sela，融资 2100 万美元，让语音 Agent 承担房贷销售工作。

以前创业公司给医院卖软件，赚的是医院的 IT 预算。现在 Epsilon Health 干脆自己做医疗服务，直接进入医院原本的收入市场。

招聘、金融、企业服务也一样。

过去 SaaS 公司想的是怎么让客户多买几个 Seat。现在 AI 公司开始思考，既然 Agent 已经能完成一部分工作，我为什么还要把软件卖给你，让你来赚最终客户的钱？

过去一家软件公司的天花板取决于客户愿意花多少钱买工具，未来它可能直接参与瓜分整个行业的收入。

反过来看，这份名单里还有 Sapiom、Raindrop、Vals AI、AIUC，分别给 Agent 做支付、监控、评测和保险，四家累计融资已经达到 2 亿美元。

我反而对这类公司有些担心。随着基础模型平台不断完善，这些功能中有相当一部分可能被逐渐内置。

但一家真正经营医疗服务、拥有行业客户和合规能力的 AI 公司，OpenAI 再发几个新模型也没法轻易取代它。

下一批最值钱的 AI 公司，可能根本不会以软件公司的面目出现。它们会是一批成本结构被 AI 彻底改造过的传统企业。

以前大家担心 AI 会抢走员工的工作，现在看来，AI 创业者可能连老板的生意都想一起抢了。

UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!

text:
扎克伯格就是一部 All in 史。

2004 年，哈佛宿舍里写出 thefacebook，退学 All in 创业——那年他 19 岁。

2006 年，雅虎开价 10 亿美元收购，他拒绝了。董事会觉得他疯了，他说 Facebook 值更多。后来证明他是对的。

2012 年，13 个人、零收入的 Instagram，他花 10 亿美元买下，全硅谷都说他疯了。今天 Instagram 是 Meta 的现金牛。

2014 年，190 亿美元买下 WhatsApp，创下当时科技收购纪录；同年 20 亿美元买下 Oculus，提前十年下注 VR。

2021 年，他把公司改名 Meta，All in 元宇宙，Reality Labs 烧掉数百亿美元，股价一度腰斩，华尔街喊他下课。他没回头。

2023 年起 All in AI：Llama 开源掀桌子，2025 年组建超级智能实验室，为顶尖研究员开出上亿美元签字费，GPU 有多少买多少。

2026 年 9 月，Muse 上线——个人 AI 助手，10 天登顶美区 App Store，把 ChatGPT 挤下第一，22 天 500 万下载，比 ChatGPT 快一倍还多。元宇宙烧掉的几百亿，终于在 AI 上看到了回头钱的影子。

别人的人生是复利，他的人生永遠是all in。
author: minglaugodel
quoted_text:
快进的听完了，比孙哥硬核多了，几个很有趣的观点总结一下：

1. 1000-2000亿美元先押注：模型未出炉就承诺巨额资本开支，Zuckerberg认为只要AI整体成功，算力可转售，风险低于账面。

2. 模型即产品：Muse故意去掉模型/effort选择器，真正产品是模型的记忆、执行能力与人格，而非传统UI。

3. 个人智能体差异化：刻意避开纯编码竞赛，重点做多模态个人智能体（Active Memory + Active Focus），针对消费场景。

4. 极小研究团队：MSL核心研究约100人，强调人才密度。Llama 4后彻底重启，无硬性deadline。

5. 对齐逻辑不同：优先高可靠执行用户指令，不做道德说教，强调隐私酌情处理（discretion）。

6. 代理商务已启动：用户已把采购委托给Muse，收入路径含订阅 + 帮用户省钱/赚钱的抽成 + API/企业。

7. 不会赢家通吃：蒸馏让能力快速下沉；各实验室执行有起伏；生态倾向多玩家，目标尽快把Wonder能力压缩到Spark并免费分发。

8. 基础设施自建有利：1GW运营约150亿美元/年、建设500-600亿美元。自建优于租云，芯片仍保值。

9. 分发优势明显：免费层用Spark覆盖海量用户，付费层先上Wonder；长期靠规模网络效应。

10. 决策风格激进：Zuckerberg一旦确信就大幅转向，MSL是典型表现。成败关键看Wonder能否快速转化为付费与交易规模。

从投资的视角看：短期资本开支压力极大，中长期取决于个人智能体商业化速度。Meta押注的是“模型能力 + 分发”而非单纯模型领先。

quoted_text:
I’m excited to share that I’ve joined @Morpho to lead all things commercial as Head of GTM.

@PaulFrambot and team are visionaries and world-class builders. It’s a privilege to team up with them.

What’s Morpho?

Morpho is an open credit network that enables people and agents to build customizable onchain lending, borrowing, and yield products.

Morpho protocols, smart contracts, and blockchains are the infrastructure making it possible. Morpho is a pure technology layer, with composability and security at the center of its design.

The why

Morpho makes it dead simple for our partners - fintechs, brokerages, exchanges, and banks - to build revenue-generating products that help their users put their assets to work. In parallel, this helps unlock new distribution for lenders and asset issuers.

Historically, spinning up credit products meant building pricing, risk and liquidation systems from scratch, and spending months on integrations before the first loan went out.

Morpho collapses this into open infrastructure: liquidity, rates, and liquidations run onchain, in markets anyone can access.

We’re growing

More than $17B is now deposited on Morpho protocols, up 3.4x since the beginning of 2025.

So far, BTC, USDC, ETH  and other stablecoins have anchored most of that growth. But these assets have also laid the foundation for what's coming next, by getting institutions comfortable with onchain infrastructure…

The onchain collateral supernova

…Now, Wall Street is racing to tokenize treasuries, funds, credit, and equities. “Crypto native” collateral will keep growing, but the tokenization wave has the potential to be orders of magnitude larger.

Onchain credit markets will accelerate tokenization growth because they make tokenized assets more productive: they becomes programmable collateral that people can borrow against 24/7, in seconds.

In the not so distant future, we’ll have tens of thousands of tokenized assets and $ trillions more in value onchain. Humans and agents will flock to the fastest and most composable system.

In credit, Morpho is poised to be that system.

First orders of business

It’s day one for me, but it’s already clear a lot of my work will rhyme with what I focused on over the last 7+ years scaling Coinbase’s institutional and infrastructure businesses: helping make our partners successful.

Over the next few weeks, I’ll be on a listening tour. If you’re working on credit products - as a fintech, lender, curator, asset issuer or something else - drop me a line. We want to hear from you and help you grow.

Last but not least: we’re hiring! …Across GTM and beyond. Come get in touch if you’re as excited about the Morpho vision as I am.

Let’s go.

"Our integrated system narrows millions of molecules down to a short list that's synthetically accessible. Not just promising in silico, but actually makeable before a single one is sent to the labs."

Traditional drug design often leans on decades of precedent and familiar chemistry. In Part 6 of our platform series, SVP of Drug Design Donovan Chin, Ph.D., explains how Recursion breaks that mold by getting a full computational design cycle up and running in about a day.

Our AI-native engine vastly increases the aperture for our chemists. Instead of relying solely on known binding pockets, they can efficiently explore entirely novel and complex chemical space. By leveraging our integrated data, the team can forecast non-obvious design hypotheses and predict how to synthesize molecules even when nothing like them currently exists.

This process begins by scoring binding affinity using advanced 3D structural models like Nesso-1. From there, the team runs hundreds of integrated models covering ADME, potency, advanced simulations, and AI retrosynthesis. This unified system rapidly filters millions of potential molecules down to a precise shortlist of high-quality candidates that are physically ready for the lab.

🚀 Follow along over the coming weeks as we continue this series, covering how Recursion maps biology, optimizes precision drug design, and closes the gap between patient and discovery.

text:
I’m excited to share that I’ve joined @Morpho to lead all things commercial as Head of GTM.

@PaulFrambot and team are visionaries and world-class builders. It’s a privilege to team up with them.

What’s Morpho?

Morpho is an open credit network that enables people and agents to build customizable onchain lending, borrowing, and yield products.

Morpho protocols, smart contracts, and blockchains are the infrastructure making it possible. Morpho is a pure technology layer, with composability and security at the center of its design.

The why

Morpho makes it dead simple for our partners - fintechs, brokerages, exchanges, and banks - to build revenue-generating products that help their users put their assets to work. In parallel, this helps unlock new distribution for lenders and asset issuers.

Historically, spinning up credit products meant building pricing, risk and liquidation systems from scratch, and spending months on integrations before the first loan went out.

Morpho collapses this into open infrastructure: liquidity, rates, and liquidations run onchain, in markets anyone can access.

We’re growing

More than $17B is now deposited on Morpho protocols, up 3.4x since the beginning of 2025.

So far, BTC, USDC, ETH  and other stablecoins have anchored most of that growth. But these assets have also laid the foundation for what's coming next, by getting institutions comfortable with onchain infrastructure…

The onchain collateral supernova

…Now, Wall Street is racing to tokenize treasuries, funds, credit, and equities. “Crypto native” collateral will keep growing, but the tokenization wave has the potential to be orders of magnitude larger.

Onchain credit markets will accelerate tokenization growth because they make tokenized assets more productive: they becomes programmable collateral that people can borrow against 24/7, in seconds.

In the not so distant future, we’ll have tens of thousands of tokenized assets and $ trillions more in value onchain. Humans and agents will flock to the fastest and most composable system.

In credit, Morpho is poised to be that system.

First orders of business

It’s day one for me, but it’s already clear a lot of my work will rhyme with what I focused on over the last 7+ years scaling Coinbase’s institutional and infrastructure businesses: helping make our partners successful.

Over the next few weeks, I’ll be on a listening tour. If you’re working on credit products - as a fintech, lender, curator, asset issuer or something else - drop me a line. We want to hear from you and help you grow.

Last but not least: we’re hiring! …Across GTM and beyond. Come get in touch if you’re as excited about the Morpho vision as I am.

Let’s go.

- Our recent $175M raise from a16z, Ribbit Capital, Paradigm, Apollo, and others [https://t.co/bWXe59WRpJ]

To address concerns about providing your seed phrase in the claims form:

Payy's ZK privacy architecture means the only person who knows your balance is you, using your seed phrase / private key. We can't know your balance without it.

We are requiring ID because given the known and potential vulnerabilities in Aztec’s ZK framework, we can't rely ZK proofs submitted from the wallet. This could and would lead to claims fraud. Requiring ID helps us reduce the chance of that.

Additionally, your Payy seed phrase was only ever used on your Payy Wallet. Given that all onchain funds from Payy were stolen, the seed phrase doesn't have value anymore, except to help us identify the amount of USDC that was in your wallet.

We know this isn't an ideal process, but it's the only way we can ensure the remediation process.

Please verify this information on our website: https://t.co/0kxELf95Hi

text:
중국 애들이 오픈AI 모델 베껴서 반값 떨이 모델 만드는 거 어떻게 막을 거냐고? 
샘 알트만의 솔직 고백 ㅋㅋㅋ

중국 AI 랩들이 OpenAI 증류(Distillation)해서 가성비 모델 찍어내는 거 어떻게 막을 거냐고 물어보니까 올트먼 성님이 입을 열었음.

결론부터 말하면 막을 방법은 아는데, 
그러면 AI 발전 자체가 막혀서 딜레마라는 거임 ㅋㅋㅋ

• 지식 증류(Distillation) 막으려면 창의성을 포기해야 함
제품 제공 방식을 바꿔서 모델을 베끼기 빡세게(harder to distill) 만들 수는 있다고 함. 
근데 그렇게 틀어막으면 오픈엔드한 창의성이나 유연성이 다 죽어버려서 유저 경험이 씹창남. 
올트먼 본인도 그런 극단적인 조치로 내몰리고 싶지 않다고 못 박음.

• 국가 안보 vs AI 기술 보급의 트레이드오프
미국이 기술 격차를 유지해서 국가 안보를 지키는 것도 중요한데, 사람들한테 AI 접근성을 풍부하게 뿌리는 것도 포기 못 함. 
어설프게 잠그면 정상적인 글로벌 경쟁이나 개발 생태계 자체가 타격받는다는 계산임.

• 진짜 병목은 돈이 아니라 공급망(웨이퍼)
돈? 금융 시장에서 투자금 땡겨오는 건 여전히 널려있어서 아무 문제 없음. 
문제는 실리콘 웨이퍼 공급이 존나 타이트해서 원가를 미친 듯이 밀어올리고 있다는 거임. 
즉, 자금 조달보다 하드웨어 제조 병목이 본체라는 소리.

결국 알면서도 안 막는 게 아니라, 
모델 꽁꽁 싸매면 AI 발전 속도가 뒤처지니까 어쩔 수 없이 딜레마 안고 가는 중임 ㅋㅋㅋ

text:
Sui Devnet Adds Post-Quantum Signature Support, Targets Mainnet Rollout in Q1 2027

Mysten Labs co-founder and chief cryptographer Kostas Chalkias announced that Sui Devnet has successfully processed its first native quantum-safe transaction, sharing the on-chain transaction record. Sui's core developer Mysten Labs has introduced ML-DSA-65 post-quantum signature support in Devnet release v1.82.0, allowing signed transactions to be submitted through the ExecuteTransaction API and verified through the VerifySignature API.

ML-DSA-65 is also supported in multisignature transactions, with additional integration into GraphQL and the Rust SDK. According to Sui's previously announced roadmap, native ML-DSA-65 accounts are expected to reach Testnet by the end of 2026, with native account authentication on Mainnet targeted for Q1 2027, subject to security audits and testing results.

60 个国家共同表态，反对在霍尔木兹海峡收过路费。除了欧盟 27 国，英国、日本、澳大利亚等国也加入了，连海峡另一边的阿曼都在名单里。

这些国家不愿意接受伊朗长期收费，因为石油和货物经过海峡要多交钱，最后增加的成本还是会落到企业和消费者身上。如果霍尔木兹可以这么做，其他重要海峡也可能有人跟着收费。这件事关系到各国自己的利益，所以即使对战争的态度不同，也能一起反对。

对伊朗来说，想在谈判中让其他国家接受它长期收费，会遇到更多阻力。船东为了安全通过而临时付款，不代表各国政府承认伊朗有权一直收钱。阿曼也支持这份声明，至少说明伊朗的收费主张还没有得到海峡另一侧国家的支持。

如果伊朗非要收费，各国可能继续谈判，也可能扩大制裁，冻结参与收费者的资产，禁止相关付款。欧盟此前已经制裁了参与收费和限制通航的伊朗相关人员及机构，受欧盟规定约束的企业和银行不能向这些被制裁对象提供资金。其他国家如果跟进，伊朗收钱就会更困难。

伊朗如果仍然坚持不交钱就不放船，船公司就可能选择停航、等待，也可能有船东在不违反适用制裁的情况下，为了减少损失而付款。只要船只的安全没有保障，一份反对收费的声明就不足以让船东放心通过。

各国可以通过谈判争取伊朗停止收费，也可能考虑加强护航。如果军舰保护商船通过时，伊朗继续拦截甚至攻击，就可能引发交火。这需要各国另外作出决定，支持声明并不代表已经答应参战。如果没有后续措施，伊朗仍可能继续收费，只是会面对更多国家的反对，以及进一步制裁的风险。

text:
研究了下SN26 Perturb，它也是做 AI 红队安全网络，但主要聚焦在图像识别领域。

计算机看世界的方式和人眼不一样。人眼看一张熊猫照片，哪怕上面落了一层薄薄的灰尘，你依然知道它是熊猫，但图像识别 AI 就不一定了。

只需给熊猫照片施加一层肉眼不可见的微小扰动（像素改动仅 1%–2%），人眼看着还是熊猫，但 AI 经过层层运算后，会认定这是一只长臂猿。

这种专门用来阴 AI 的图片，在学术上叫对抗样本。

SN26 现在就是专注这种经典攻击：在像素层面上施加极微小的数学扰动，而不是现实世界里的复杂盲区。本质上来看，它就是做这种针对固定图像识别模型的微小像素攻防演练。
 
联合创始人兼CEO Koyuki Nakamori , Koyuki Nakamori 之前是 OpenTensor Foundation AI 负责人，后面离开了基金会自己做子网。她同时还做了SN78 UMI 。

目前 ，SN26 自称进入产品阶段，矿工已经能用对抗数据微调出更鲁棒且更准的模型，目标大约 11 月上线产品。

可以保持关注 @perturbaix 、并期待一下！

text:
Ledger 自己承认，芯片认出了屏幕上的 24 个助记词

欧洲最大的消费电子连锁之一 MediaMarkt，今天把货架上全部 Ledger 产品端走了。下架的不是某个批号，是整条产品线，因为德国门店卖出去的两台 Nano X 被拆开后，里面都多了线缆和一块疑似 LTE 模块。

这事前几天还被当成东南亚一家经销商的意外。Ledger 确认被动过手脚的设备全来自 CryptoBilis 这家东南亚授权经销商，马来西亚、印尼、菲律宾三地，官方口径里只验证出一台机器里有未授权植入物。

所以 Ledger 今天把手法摊开讲了。那颗多出来的芯片藏在设备外壳里面，用户第一次初始化、屏幕上亮出 24 个恢复短语的那一刻，芯片里的微控制器就把这些词认出来、解码，然后通过一张 eSIM 走 LTE 移动网络发了出去。

24 个词就是钱包的总钥匙。谁拿到，谁在别的电脑上把钱包重建一遍，币就搬走了，你那台机器连都不用连。Ledger 还特意说了一句，安全芯片没动，系统没动，签名也没动，就是货在路上被人开壳塞了东西。

但德国这边根本不是东南亚的货。@0xJohannes_ 是个德国用户，他在 MediaMarkt 门店买了台 Nano X，拆开发现里面多了线缆和一个疑似 LTE 模块。自己都不信，10 月 12 日又跑去另一家 MediaMarkt 门店买了第二台，全程录开箱视频。

我把那段视频翻出来看了，画质糊得厉害，他从店里拿着全新机器出来，当场撬开，还是那几根多出来的线。两台，两家店，全中。他点名中间那一环是经销商 Aqipa，Ledger 的 CTO 自己也说不清 Aqipa 算不算直接经销商。

也就是说，脏货不只在一家经销商的仓库里。新加坡樟宜机场 Metapod 店卖的一台 Ledger Flex，买家 Ben Yorke 看外壳有划痕送去检测，门头沟前 CEO Mark Karpelès 拆开发现里面多塞了一块电路板，这机器一次都没用过。日本从 Amazon Japan、Yahoo Auctions 收来的部分 Nano X 也有植入。10 月 11 日还出了第一例 Stax 的植入报告，里面是 4G/LTE 模块加隐藏天线。

两台德国门店的货都验出同样的东西，MediaMarkt 母公司索性把全部 Ledger 下了架。正规电器连锁里塑封好的那台冷钱包，现在也没人敢保证它是原装。

text:
On October 10, 2025, $19 billion of futures was liquidated in one day. 

Days like that are when you find out how a venue prices risk.

If a $500 order and a $5M one-sided order get the same quote in a falling market, somebody absorbs the difference. 

Usually the LPs.

The D8X AMM prices market conditions into every quote. Flow that adds to the pool's risk pays more to get filled, which is how the pool is still standing the morning after.

After a cascade, what do you check first on a venue: open interest, funding or the insurance fund?

非美国人持有美国上市的 ETF，属于美国境内资产。持有人去世时，超过 6 万美元的部分可能被征收最高 40% 的美国联邦遗产税。

text:
最近 AI 自动开发的讨论很多 🤔。 决定开源我这个自动跨session通信的开发框架。 

先说下本人背景。纯血翻译系山顶洞人文科生。前半辈子连一个python 脚本都没有跑过。

起因是发现codex / Claude code都可以跨 session通信了，也就说我们可以把一个“session”理解成一个“agent”去管理。基于这个思路，把分工、验收的交给一个总管 agent 是完全可行的。我只要约束好功能优先级、合并优先级、功能规划等等大的方向就好了（当领导这块）。

于是给自己运行了 5 年的社区搓了一个网站， 7 天新增代码 10 万行，合并 668 次提交，后端合并 243 次，前端 180 次，还包括智能合约、telegram bot 等等都多个不同开发框架下的调研、设计和实现。

不管什么事情，我只跟总管对话。总管开 opus5.5 high 。其他开 sonnet5.5 medium，甚至haiku 5.5 high 。总管会自己分派任务、验收、处理合并优先级。对于很多需要我决策的事情，我也做了约束，要求所有session 上报给总管只有总管能跟我沟通。大大节省了我的注意力。

把他做成了一个 skill 形式。 /devteam root 设置总管session。 /devteam frontend 设置前端session ， /devteam backend 设置后端session …… 还有全自动测试session 、客诉处理 session 等等，只要你 token 够用可以搞无数前后端 session 并行开发。

感觉未来 session 这个概念会加速消亡，因为确实直觉上他就是 agent 分片。🤔 很多东西不管开发者自己怎么想，用户永远会以用户视角最简单的方式去理解。

text:
hi mr. mosby,

the initia team has been running an experiment -> incubate -> scale playbook across a few categories both in crypto and AI

Claude has made the "experiment" step much faster, so we've built tons of MVPs and scrapped many 

if we like something, we move to "incubate". we put together a team to build out the business, typically a mix between initia contributors and external folks who have a particular passion or strength for that business

some of the public incubations:
@TradeOnStrat: full-stack prop trading, best terms in the market
@init_ai: undisclosed humanoid project
@GlyphUniverseAI: write a prompt to fight others
@usebetbot: bet on tickers on the TL
along with a handful more that remain [redacted]

now all of these are relatively new, having been launched just a month or so ago. Yet some of them are showing signs of traction from metrics and user feedback. 

for those that do (like Strat) we now begin the arduous task of "scaling" the business aided by our treasury 

you might notice, not all of these are appchains... we still believe they lead to highest value capture but have drawbacks on distribution if you don't have it already

Each incubation has a path to using initia infra if certain metrics are hit and all of them will have a portion of rev flow back to initia.

in terms of the core initia infra business line, we continue to make product improvements, will have some tokenomics updates, and have a couple more onchain game clients coming online

ultimately, I believe dogfooding the infra through incubations yields the highest chance of winning overall, so that's where we're focused

text:
Robinhood 加密的官方X 账号 @RobinhoodCrypto 发帖公开欢迎一个偏冷门的生态协议 @metricxyz, 比较罕见。

Metric 能获得这个待遇，我认为跟它与RH Chain 定位的高度契合、能补强关键的底层infra 脱不开关系。

Metric 的定位是基于propAMM 机制的DEX，但它跟目前RH Chain 上的龙头DEX Uniswap 并不是零和竞争，而是要进一步做大现货市场的整体蛋糕。

propAMM 机制有别于传统的AMM: 传统AMM 可以理解成“先交易，价格再被交易推着走”；Metric 则是“先把真实价格引进来，再围绕它做交易”。前者特别适用于没有外部参考价的资产和长尾市场，后者则对RWA/ 股票代币化这类有真实外部市场价格的资产非常友好。

因为propAMM 机制下资产的价格主要由预言机引入外部参考价驱动，资产价格能快速跟随真实价格变动，价格更准、LP 风险更低、资本效率也更高。

引入Metric 后，可以跟Uniswap 形成比较清晰的互补分工：
Uniswap 提供基础和通用的流动性，而Metric 提供针对Stocks Tokens 的专业流动性。

一起把Robinhood Chain 生态做大做强。

author: edward_yu_var
quoted_text:
Small RL companies are the AI industry's equivalent of quant shops. Let me explain.

Both are small, secretive, full of brilliant people, profitable, and always one step from their edge disappearing.

The parallels:

- Secretive. Nobody publishes their signals. Labs won't say what they're training next, and vendors can't say who they sell to. Epoch calls the market "largely behind closed doors."

- Hunting alpha. For a quant, a trade stops working once everyone finds it. For these shops, a task stops paying once models can solve it (labs drop tasks at around 70% pass rate). Meanwhile, labs are building their own in-house. So they always have to find the next field.

- Deep Industry Connections. You need to know the problem cold to get in. Founders have usually worked at, or sold to, the labs. You can't define "correct" for fund accounting without having done fund accounting.

- They buy strange data. Quants buy satellite photos of parking lots. RL shops bid for enterprise data (eg $12.5M bid for Spirit Airlines historical data).

- Brilliant people. Quants hire math olympiad winners. These shops hire ex-lab researchers and real practitioners.

- Huge revenue per head. Jane Street made about $11M per employee in 2025. Proximal is about $5M. The tweet's company would be $20M.

- One narrow problem that makes something more efficient. Quants make markets more efficient. These RL shops make models training more efficient.

- High risk (for different reasons). A quant can lose millions in a day on a bad trade. An RL shop's risk is that one lab trains a model that makes their environments irrelevant, or brings the work in-house, and the revenue stops.

- Overfitting/reward hacking. A quant's nightmare is a strategy that looks perfect on historical data and fails live. An RL shop's nightmare is an RL grader that scores perfectly and trains the model incorrectly. 

- Infrastructure arms race. Quants pay for microseconds of speed. RL shops race to spin up thousands of disposable computers per training run.

Obviously there are as many differences between RL companies and quant shops, but right now the aura around them feels eerily similar. 

Curious to see how this market matures as robotics opens up a new surface, and whether the frontier labs end up absorbing them.

text:
Crypto is entering a period where partnerships and acquisitions are becoming increasingly important to finding product-market fit and entering new markets.

Building a blockchain requires significant investment in infrastructure, developers, distribution, and ecosystem development. Each additional market introduces local relationships and regulatory requirements. Combining capabilities with established partners can dramatically improve the economics and speed of execution.

We saw this firsthand with the acquisition of HashPalette in Japan.

HashPalette had built an established blockchain ecosystem around entertainment and digital assets. It also brought relationships with Japanese enterprises and the Osaka-Kansai World Expo.

The acquisition created a path to migrate Palette Chain and its applications onto a larger blockchain. It also introduced a token-exchange mechanism for existing holders.

That combination gave us a stronger position in Japan. HashPalette’s existing ecosystem could benefit from broader infrastructure, distribution, and technical capabilities.

The same pattern is now emerging elsewhere.

Sui Foundation announced a $30 million strategic investment in DATA Network, formerly Story Protocol. DATA will retire its independent blockchain and move its AI data provenance protocol onto Sui.

Its Trace registry has already recorded more than 250 million contributions. Walrus will provide the underlying storage infrastructure, while DATA retains its token and existing governance economics through the migration.

The transaction brings together complementary capabilities. DATA contributes an established application and its users. Sui provides network infrastructure, while Walrus contributes storage designed for large datasets.

Maintaining an independent blockchain carries costs that increase with technical complexity and competition. Protocol teams increasingly have to decide which capabilities are worth owning and which can be acquired through partnerships.

We’re seeing the same logic in traditional financial infrastructure.

Stripe acquired Bridge to expand its stablecoin capabilities. Mastercard acquired BVNK to connect digital assets with established payment networks. LayerZero acquired Stargate through a DAO-approved token exchange.

Each transaction combines assets that could take considerable time to develop independently.

The broader M&A data supports the direction, although the market remains concentrated. Disclosed crypto acquisition value reached approximately $9.7 billion in the first half of 2026, with a small number of large transactions driving most of the total.

I expect more protocol teams to confront these decisions as the market matures.

The most interesting question is where economic value ultimately accrues.

Tokens provide mechanisms for governance, coordination, and economic participation. Their long-term value depends on how those mechanisms connect to genuine demand and durable economic activity.

A protocol with meaningful distribution and a sustainable business model has more strategic options. Others may find stronger economics through partnerships, acquisitions, or migration onto established networks.

The next phase will require teams that understand how to combine equity, tokens, infrastructure, and real businesses.

Many of the legal and economic structures are still developing. Founders will need to understand what they are transferring, what token holders retain, and who controls the resulting network.

We’ve already seen how complicated these arrangements become when technology, ownership, and market access have to work together.

MFV is already guiding several portfolio companies through what we call capability partnerships. I expect more founders to face those decisions as the next generation of protocols begins to consolidate.

text:
near:native chain abstraction stack is what powers @near_intents and other cool features that have contributed to get market's attention to @NEARProtocol 

• one account
• real assets on other chains
• the very notion of managing different wallets in different chains abstracted

↓

the core piece of this puzzle is Chain Signatures

your NEAR account (or a smart contract) derives addresses on other chains via derivation paths. then an MPC network of nodes jointly signs the transaction for you.

no single party holds the full key.

you control native BTC, ETH, SOL, ZEC, etc. from a near-native account, not wrapped tokens sitting in a usual cross-chain bridge.

this difference is important for both efficiency and security reasons.

• bridges: lock funds → mint a wrapped token → bridge wallet has custody of the locked funds and becomes a honeypot → wrapped tokens inflates the market

• chain signatures: a NEAR account signs transactions executed by the MPC network in the target chain (no wrapped tokens doubling the total market cap). and the trust assumption shifts to the MPC threshold + NEAR’s validator set.

on top of that sits Intents.

• you say the outcome: “swap USDC for ZEC at the best price.”
• solvers compete to fulfill it in the best possible way

practical result for users:
• one human-readable, named account
• gas that can be paid in stablecoins held in any chain
• cross-chain actions without managing 5 wallets and seed phrases

for builders: one contract on NEAR can orchestrate actions across Zcash, Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and more. focus on the app logic instead of writing the same integration five times.

---

i’ve written about the stack before (including the trust model of the MPC keys). it’s not the same as pure self-custody of a single-chain key you can export anytime -- this is an important trade-off to understand.

it is still meaningfully better than most bridges and custodial routes for multi-chain use. the abstraction is real. the complexity is mostly hidden from the user, with strong security primitives and a well-defined trust assumption.

i run a NEAR validator: thecoding.pool.near
(stake with me via app.thecoding[.]dev)

and also a devops business on thecoding[.]dev, helping teams with technical content, documentation, and user/dev education.

Go down the rabbit hole 👇
author: Sharplink
quoted_text:
Last week I had the pleasure of sharing the stage with @ethereumjoseph at our Ethereum Ecosystem Summit alongside @token2049.

The topic was “Ethereum’s Next Decade: The Cryptographic World Computer,” moderated by @mcamarda0.

Over the past two weeks at KBW and Token2049, we’ve focused on what’s happening now: the convergence of stablecoins, tokenized assets, onchain finance and AI agents. There is a clear acceleration of institutional adoption.

Individually, each of these elements is transformational. Together, they form the catalyst for a financial revolution that will lead to a new era of economic growth and financial autonomy for investors and consumers around the world.

But what will Ethereum look like by 2035? On our panel, we had the opportunity to take a step back and think big.

Vitalik recently shared that the Ethereum ecosystem will transition from a traditional blockchain into a high-capacity “cryptographic world computer.” But what does this mean in practice?

Ethereum’s foundation of trust and security rests on participants’ ability to independently verify transactions and their outcomes. Its continued evolution builds on that strength, expanding its capacity to support the global financial system. Ethereum’s coming architecture will be leaner and more modular, using ZK proofs and virtual machines to verify results more quickly and cheaply. These advances will support stronger privacy alongside better performance, while further upgrades will strengthen the network against emerging quantum threats. As that foundation becomes faster, more scalable, more private and more secure, we can begin to envision how much further Ethereum can go.
Here’s what this means in practice.

Tokenization will bring the world's value onchain, but this is just the on-ramp. Onchain finance at near zero cost will be the utility layer. Zero-knowledge proofs will be the engineering that allows neutral trust at a global scale. We will live in a world where any asset can be traded 24/7 with deep liquidity and can settle in an instant. Tokenized assets will be the preferred form of collateral not just in DeFi but across traditional execution venues. Programmable assets and money that run on blockchain rails will allow billions of AI agents to sift through millions of data points and scenarios to make the best decisions for consumers. Billions of AI agents will leverage machine intelligence, financial literacy and unlimited attention. They will provide retail investors with the same capabilities and outcomes as the largest Wall Street institutions.

To fully realize this vision, Ethereum’s core principles and advantages will become even more important. The words credibly neutral, decentralized, and censorship resistant mean different things to different audiences. In practice, they will underpin the foundation of the new digital and agentic economy.

Indulge me to explain why I believe these principles are so critical:

Credibly neutral means a network where the core rules, transaction ordering, validation, and settlement are applied consistently without favoring any specific person, company, or agenda. When the world’s largest financial institutions move their infrastructure onchain, they require one that will remain stable and resilient over decades because market participants know the rules of the game will not suddenly be rewritten to benefit insiders. This is equally important because the billions of agents that are coming onchain will rely programmatically on Ethereum for the essential architectural backbone of a machine-to-machine economy.

Decentralization means a network where no single company, bank, or government controls the ledger or makes the rules. Decentralization will create a new type of trust that relies on self-executing smart contracts without the need to rely on human or corporate trust. This automated trust, combined with instant settlement of transactions, will lead to a massive reduction in financial market risk. Equally important, it will ensure the AI agents can seamlessly interact with different decentralized protocols. They can lend on one platform, borrow on another, and hedge derivatives, without always needing API keys or permission from corporate gatekeepers.

Censorship resistant means a technical and structural guarantee that anyone with an internet connection can create an account or broadcast a transaction without applying for permission from a centralized authority. In practice, it means that Ethereum applies the exact same mathematical rules to everyone. This is not a political slogan, but rather a prerequisite for the future onchain and agent economy. No one can be unbanked and no AI agent can be excluded from the new machine-to-machine economy.

We envision a future where the Ethereum ecosystem will form the global, decentralized settlement infrastructure for the movement of assets and transactions, a new internet of value. This design will make it more difficult for highly-placed intermediaries to exploit a lack of attention to collect rents. It will make it easier for billions of AI agents with unlimited financial attention to deliver value for investors and consumers around the world. 

At Sharplink, we have more conviction than ever that Ethereum is best-positioned to deliver this future, a value proposition that is hard to overstate.

ETH, held.

Conviction, held.

quoted_text:
Most of the recent math results were not reached by a swarm, the way Navier–Stokes was. I think that part got lost in the excitement around the release. OpenAI's unnamed internal model, which I'm going to call Aeon, reached most of them in one shot, from a single prompt, with no interruptions. This model did not even exist before the end of August, and it is still training. Notice how the returns are not dropping off? That chart is from a month ago. It is a log scale. What does Aeon look like now? 

On average, each result used three hours of thinking. Aeon was given 4000 problems to work on by OpenAI. How many more have been solved in the last three days? That number is not zero. 

It's like hearing notes in a song that is slowly rising. I don't think Pacing the Frontier was just about Hugging Face or hacking. They've seen how close we are to closing the loop, and as the hour draws near, their resolve begins to quaver. The last piece was model creativity, and I think that threshold was crossed internally by Anthropic and OpenAI in September. You see it in Opus 5.5, which gets it from Fable 5.5. You see it in the math results from Aeon.

All that was needed to start the event was the ability for models to think of novel ways to improve themselves. That was the last piece. This is directly analogous to the ability to think of strange, alien ways to solve math problems: solutions so inhuman that they are difficult to express in existing human terms, so the proof winds up incomprehensible. I think these same kinds of alien solutions are now being applied to model improvements internally. That's what all this recent consternation is really about. They see the invisible frontier. And they see what is about to happen.

text:
Last week I had the pleasure of sharing the stage with @ethereumjoseph at our Ethereum Ecosystem Summit alongside @token2049.

The topic was “Ethereum’s Next Decade: The Cryptographic World Computer,” moderated by @mcamarda0.

Over the past two weeks at KBW and Token2049, we’ve focused on what’s happening now: the convergence of stablecoins, tokenized assets, onchain finance and AI agents. There is a clear acceleration of institutional adoption.

Individually, each of these elements is transformational. Together, they form the catalyst for a financial revolution that will lead to a new era of economic growth and financial autonomy for investors and consumers around the world.

But what will Ethereum look like by 2035? On our panel, we had the opportunity to take a step back and think big.

Vitalik recently shared that the Ethereum ecosystem will transition from a traditional blockchain into a high-capacity “cryptographic world computer.” But what does this mean in practice?

Ethereum’s foundation of trust and security rests on participants’ ability to independently verify transactions and their outcomes. Its continued evolution builds on that strength, expanding its capacity to support the global financial system. Ethereum’s coming architecture will be leaner and more modular, using ZK proofs and virtual machines to verify results more quickly and cheaply. These advances will support stronger privacy alongside better performance, while further upgrades will strengthen the network against emerging quantum threats. As that foundation becomes faster, more scalable, more private and more secure, we can begin to envision how much further Ethereum can go.
Here’s what this means in practice.

Tokenization will bring the world's value onchain, but this is just the on-ramp. Onchain finance at near zero cost will be the utility layer. Zero-knowledge proofs will be the engineering that allows neutral trust at a global scale. We will live in a world where any asset can be traded 24/7 with deep liquidity and can settle in an instant. Tokenized assets will be the preferred form of collateral not just in DeFi but across traditional execution venues. Programmable assets and money that run on blockchain rails will allow billions of AI agents to sift through millions of data points and scenarios to make the best decisions for consumers. Billions of AI agents will leverage machine intelligence, financial literacy and unlimited attention. They will provide retail investors with the same capabilities and outcomes as the largest Wall Street institutions.

To fully realize this vision, Ethereum’s core principles and advantages will become even more important. The words credibly neutral, decentralized, and censorship resistant mean different things to different audiences. In practice, they will underpin the foundation of the new digital and agentic economy.

Indulge me to explain why I believe these principles are so critical:

Credibly neutral means a network where the core rules, transaction ordering, validation, and settlement are applied consistently without favoring any specific person, company, or agenda. When the world’s largest financial institutions move their infrastructure onchain, they require one that will remain stable and resilient over decades because market participants know the rules of the game will not suddenly be rewritten to benefit insiders. This is equally important because the billions of agents that are coming onchain will rely programmatically on Ethereum for the essential architectural backbone of a machine-to-machine economy.

Decentralization means a network where no single company, bank, or government controls the ledger or makes the rules. Decentralization will create a new type of trust that relies on self-executing smart contracts without the need to rely on human or corporate trust. This automated trust, combined with instant settlement of transactions, will lead to a massive reduction in financial market risk. Equally important, it will ensure the AI agents can seamlessly interact with different decentralized protocols. They can lend on one platform, borrow on another, and hedge derivatives, without always needing API keys or permission from corporate gatekeepers.

Censorship resistant means a technical and structural guarantee that anyone with an internet connection can create an account or broadcast a transaction without applying for permission from a centralized authority. In practice, it means that Ethereum applies the exact same mathematical rules to everyone. This is not a political slogan, but rather a prerequisite for the future onchain and agent economy. No one can be unbanked and no AI agent can be excluded from the new machine-to-machine economy.

We envision a future where the Ethereum ecosystem will form the global, decentralized settlement infrastructure for the movement of assets and transactions, a new internet of value. This design will make it more difficult for highly-placed intermediaries to exploit a lack of attention to collect rents. It will make it easier for billions of AI agents with unlimited financial attention to deliver value for investors and consumers around the world. 

At Sharplink, we have more conviction than ever that Ethereum is best-positioned to deliver this future, a value proposition that is hard to overstate.

ETH, held.

Conviction, held.

Ironically, this is a good reason why private equity firms like adding debt to their portfolio companies

Beyond just enhancing equity returns, a constant stream of interest payments tends to keep executives much more operationally disciplined in terms of their spend

While short term underperformance might be fine for a debt free business, companies with a massive debt load are forced to focus on cost cutting and margins so they can meet their quarterly interest payments

This obviously has second and third order effects, and can lead to underinvestment for the long run in some cases

But in majority of cases, CEOs and CFOs tend to execute much better with a little bit of debt on the balance sheet

text:
hi mr. mosby,

the initia team has been running an experiment -> incubate -> scale playbook across a few categories both in crypto and AI

Claude has made the "experiment" step much faster, so we've built tons of MVPs and scrapped many 

if we like something, we move to "incubate". we put together a team to build out the business, typically a mix between initia contributors and external folks who have a particular passion or strength for that business

some of the public incubations:
@TradeOnStrat: full-stack prop trading, best terms in the market
@init_ai: undisclosed humanoid project
@GlyphUniverseAI: write a prompt to fight others
@usebetbot: bet on tickers on the TL
along with a handful more that remain [redacted]

now all of these are relatively new, having been launched just a month or so ago. Yet some of them are showing signs of traction from metrics and user feedback. 

for those that do (like Strat) we now begin the arduous task of "scaling" the business aided by our treasury 

you might notice, not all of these are appchains... we still believe they lead to highest value capture but have drawbacks on distribution if you don't have it already

Each incubation has a path to using initia infra if certain metrics are hit and all of them will have a portion of rev flow back to initia.

in terms of the core initia infra business line, we continue to make product improvements, will have some tokenomics updates, and have a couple more onchain game clients coming online

ultimately, I believe dogfooding the infra through incubations yields the highest chance of winning overall, so that's where we're focused

Gm gm @cashcat_token @RobinhoodApp 

Feels good to be among the Top 10 holders of FOMO now. ❤️

But when it comes to $CASHCAT, this journey has always been personal.

I put my cash into CAT because I believed in it from Day 1. Not because the chart looked perfect, not because everyone was bullish, and certainly not because the price made it easy to hold.

Sometimes, you see something that clicks with your instincts. Something you believe has potential before the rest of the market sees it. And once that conviction is built, you stop letting every candle dictate your emotions.

I watched $CASHCAT fall to $37M, climb all the way to $300M, and turn the journey into an absolute roller coaster. Along the way, so many people got shaken out, sold at the bottom, and watched from the sidelines as the market proved how difficult it is to hold through uncertainty.

And I understand why. Holding is easy when you’re in profit. Holding is easy when everyone is cheering. The real test of conviction comes when the chart turns red, the noise gets louder, and everything around you tells you to give up.

I’ve been bullish on $CASHCAT at $30M, at $200M, at its ATH of $300M, and I’m still bullish at $123M.

My conviction was never built on a single price target. It was built on what I saw in this project and the belief that made me stay through every phase of the journey.

The market will always give you reasons to doubt. People will always have opinions. Prices will rise, prices will fall, and sentiment will change overnight. But you have to learn the difference between listening to the market and letting the market control your mind.

Sometimes, the biggest mistake isn’t buying too early. It’s letting fear convince you to abandon something you genuinely believe in.

I’m not here to tell anyone what to buy or when to sell. Everyone has their own risk tolerance and their own conviction.

I’m simply sharing my journey.

I believed when it was quiet. I believed when it was uncomfortable. I believed when the market tested everyone’s patience. And I continue to believe today.

Because real conviction isn’t proven at the top. It’s revealed in the moments when holding becomes the hardest thing to do.

Cut the outside noise. Do your own research. Trust your judgment, understand your risks, and never let someone else’s fear become your decision.

$CASHCAT has already taken us on one hell of a ride. And for me, this journey has always been about more than the price.

Conviction over noise. Patience over panic. Belief over temporary sentiment.

text:
Today we're launching MagicOS. And we've come to the conclusion that designers are NOT getting replaced.

most of the industry moved to the same answer this year: give the agent its own canvas, let it run, hand you the output. 

we made a different bet: the canvas should be yours and the agent is your collaborator. that’s MagicOS.

most AI design tools are a linear conversation: prompt, generate, iterate, repeat. a hundred prompts in, you might have a great final design, but the reasoning, rejected directions, and inspiration that got you there are buried in a chat log nobody will ever scroll back through.

MagicOS is a persistent, spatial canvas. Your PRD, inspiration images, design system, variations, rejected directions, final picks - all of it lives together, all in one place, instead of stacked on top of itself and lost.

it’s voice-first. talk to it in real time and watch work land directly on the canvas as you speak.

it’s also multiplayer. your whole team works on the same canvas together.

and it still runs on your design system and components because none of this matters if the output doesn’t look like your actual product.

three months ago, this was internal only at Magic Patterns, my co-founder's weekend project. it’s now live for everyone.

Design everything, everywhere, all at once.

最近研究了一番Citrini Research《Breaking The Wall》 文中提及的美股公司，然后再思考这几年，大力推进的美元稳定币，如今的RWA代币化，叠加从中受益的美股公司，其中确定性机会还是蛮明显的，让我们娓娓道来！🧐

最近无论是SEC还是CFTC，美国政府部门都在大力支持 RWA，其中有一件事很值得琢磨：

未来越来越多的人通过加密钱包参与金融市场，最后用的还是美元，只是换成了稳定币形式，买的还是美债和美股，加密也会有，但会被逐渐稀释掉！

交易入口变了，美国资产的销售范围反而扩大了。

从这个角度看，美国为什么愿意推动稳定币、支持资产代币化，就很容易理解了。

我认为，这里面藏着一条值得长期研究的投资线索：全球资金进入美元体系的方式，正在发生变化，其中衍生的金融服务，机会很多。

不过，方向看懂了，不代表随便买一家 RWA 公司就能赚钱。接下来，我讲讲自己的思考。🧐

先从一个普通用户说起。

假设一个海外用户，把一部分储蓄换成 USDC。

他的想法可能很简单：留一点美元，转账方便，随时可以交易。

但在发行人那一端，这笔钱对应着储备资产，其中包括短期美债。

也就是说，用户在钱包里存了一笔数字美元，背后可能就多了一笔美债需求。

用户未必研究过美国财政，也没有主动决定给美国政府融资。这笔需求，是随着产品使用自然产生的。

美国财政部在 2026 年 9 月披露，稳定币发行人已经持有接近 2000 亿美元的短期国债及其他临近到期美债。这才是稳定币对美国有吸引力的地方。

过去，美元的使用依赖银行、贸易和金融机构的网络。现在，钱包和应用也可以帮助美元触达用户。

当持有美元变得更方便，美元就多了一种争取全球储蓄的方式。

所以，我理解的稳定币逻辑是，全球用户需要一个方便使用的美元工具，发行人需要配置储备，美国因此获得更多潜在的短期债券买家。

这条逻辑成立，但别顺手把它推演成“美国债务问题解决了”。

稳定币主要影响短期美债需求。如果资金只是从原本持有美债的货币基金转进来，新增需求也可能有限。美国政府该付的利息，一分钱都不会因为上链而消失。

销售渠道扩大了，财政账还是要继续算。

再往下想一步。

一个人已经在钱包里持有美元，他接下来会做什么？

有人拿去支付，有人继续交易，也有人希望这笔钱产生收益。

这时，美债基金、美股、信贷产品，就有了进入同一个钱包的机会。

从美元余额，到美元资产，再到抵押、借贷和交易，一整套金融服务可以围绕这个用户展开。

美国推动 RWA 的长期利益，我认为就在这里：让全球资金更方便地进入美元资产，也更有理由继续留在里面。

这也让我重新理解了“美股代币化”。

很多人觉得，把美股搬到链上，让更多人来买，就能解决美股估值高的问题。

这个判断，我只认同前半段。

代币化有机会扩大买家范围，改善资产转移和使用方式。可一家公司的利润没有变化，原来卖 40 倍市盈率，上链以后仍然是 40 倍。

买起来方便，不代表买得便宜。

而且，更方便的交易渠道，同样方便卖出。

美股代币化解决的是一部分投资门槛和使用效率问题，估值最终仍然要由盈利来支撑。

美国监管也在沿着这个方向推进。2026 年 9 月，SEC 批准了部分代币化股票链上交易的临时、有条件豁免，但仍然设置了交易范围、规模和技术要求。方向已经能看见，具体业务还要一步步落地。

我觉得，RWA 更值得想象的变化，可能发生在买入资产之后。

今天，我们习惯把股票、现金、基金放在不同账户里。需要用钱时，再去卖出、转账，或者申请抵押融资。

如果未来合规的链上资产能够更方便地转移、抵押和结算，一份资产的用途就可能增加。

持有一份短期国债基金或者代币化美股，在获得收益的同时，还可能把它用于某些交易场景的抵押品，为生活支出或者消费市场提供更大支持。从投资角度看，这意味着服务机会和场景会增加。

发行的时候有人收费，持有期间有人管理，交易的时候有人提供流动性，融资的时候又需要风控和抵押品管理。

资产进入系统只是开始，后续被反复使用，才有机会形成持续收入，才能扩大金融服务范围，也会更有壁垒性的竞争优势，或许这就是美国在下一代金融技术优势上的大跃进。

沿着这条思路，再看图里的公司，就更有意思了。

我会先把它们放回各自的生意里，再看市值。

📍 $CRCL：掌握数字美元的发行和使用网络

Circle 市值约 214 亿美元。

2026 年 Q2，USDC 期末流通量约 733 亿美元。对 Circle 来说，这些余额背后的储备收益，是目前收入的主要来源。

它的长期空间，是让更多企业和用户持续使用 USDC，并愿意保留余额。

这里最值得关注的，是“钱留下来多少”，以及 Circle 最后能分到多少收益。

流通量增长是好事，但利率下降、渠道分成提高，都可能抵消一部分增长。储备资产也对应持币人的赎回权，不能当成股东可以随意使用的现金。

我对 CRCL 的判断：业务方向清楚，利润要看余额、利率和分成三件事，整体来看，目前高通胀粘性，高利率背景下，对CRCL是一件好事情，另外要留意ARC公链，对它产生的附加值影响，能否实现两条腿走路。

如果未来支付和基础设施收入能够做起来，它的收入结构还会更加稳健。

📍 $COIN：在多个环节参与收费

Coinbase 市值约 476 亿美元。

交易、托管、稳定币、Base，这些业务让它有机会参与资产上链后的多个环节。

2026 年 Q2，订阅与服务收入约 5.55 亿美元，占净收入的 48%。这个比例已经充分说明，多元化进程，Coinbase做的相当不错，毕竟Q2 交易收入也仅仅为5.99亿，基本旗鼓相当。

它的优势是业务覆盖比较完整：资产进来以后，可以保管、交易，也可以接入其他服务。

风险是，这些业务仍然受到市场活跃度、币价和利率影响。收入来源增加，并不意味着周期性已经消失，它跟BTC四年周期，依旧有高度相关性。

我会把 COIN 放在观察链上金融整体扩张的位置。

同时持有 $COIN 和 $CRCL，也要意识到，两家公司都参与 USDC 的经济分配，风险具有一定的重叠性，但目前这两家公司，我都持有中。

📍 $HOOD：用户入口本身就有价值

Robinhood 市值约 988 亿美元。

一家平台已经拥有用户、账户资金和交易习惯，再推出新产品，通常比从零开始找客户容易。

2026 年 Q2，Robinhood 有资金客户约 2840 万，平台资产约 3690 亿美元。这是它参与资产代币化的重要基础。

但最近Robinhood公链熄火，由于当初meme搞的太火爆了，市场褒贬不一，合规监管也开始盯上它，逐渐开始低调，但目前也太低调了，基本没啥讨论音量了。

其中我最看重 HOOD 的分销能力，但接近千亿美元的市值，也意味着市场已经为增长支付了不少钱。

未来做得好，还要比今天股价里预期的做得更好，投资回报才有空间，其实难度也是不小。

📍 $SECZ：负责把RWA代币化落地的工程师

Securitize 市值约 19 亿美元，业务与RWA代币化直接相关。

发行、登记、转让和资产服务，这些环节做得越深入，客户迁移系统的难度就可能越高。

但它最新一季的数据，却让人大跌眼镜：交易量同比增长 147%，收入却同比下降 5%。

这组数字，比任何“万亿美元市场”的故事都更有启发。

业务规模扩大，收入未必同步扩大。产品组合、收费方式和收入确认节奏，都会影响结果。

按行情平台过去十二个月收入计算， $SECZ 市销率约 30 倍，价格已经包含较高期待。

我会重点跟踪它，但最想看到的是持续的收入和盈利能力改善。

📍 $FIGR：有实际经营结果检验的 RWA 公司

Figure 市值约 64 亿美元。

它从房屋净值信贷等业务切入，把贷款发起、融资、出售和交易连接起来。

这个方向吸引我的地方，是客户采用产品有明确的经济理由：能不能节约成本，能不能提高资金周转效率。

2026 年 Q2，Figure 净收入约 2.26 亿美元，同比增长 113%，净利润约 8744 万美元。

到 Q3，初步披露的消费者贷款市场业务量约 51.19 亿美元，同比增长 107%。这是经营规模指标，不是收入，而且尚未包含 Kiavi 平台并购后的业务量。

它已经有收入和利润可以观察，但信贷业务始终要面对房价、违约率和融资条件。所以我会优先研究 FIGR 的经营兑现情况，尤其是增长过程中，信贷质量有没有变化，尤其值得关注。

📍 $BLSH：通过并购争取证券服务客户

Bullish 市值约 48 亿美元。

我更关注它拟收购 Equiniti 这件事。后者拥有证券登记和股东服务业务，能够帮助 Bullish 接近发行人及其资产。

但约 42 亿美元交易价值，包含承接债务和股票对价。里面机会和风险并存。所以研究 BLSH，必须把并购后的股数、债务和现金流一起算。

如果只拿今天的市值，对比未来并购后的利润，我个人认为还是偏向乐观的，值得重点关注一波。

📍 $BLK、 $WT：传统资管公司也在扩大产品的使用范围

BlackRock 市值约 1663亿美元，WisdomTree 约 33 亿美元。

它们原本就有产品、客户和管理能力。代币化可能帮助基金接入更多钱包、机构和交易场景。

两者的区别，在于体量。

BlackRock 的集团规模很大，RWA 即使增长很快，短期对总利润的影响也可能有限。买 BLK，主要还是在投资整个资管平台。

WisdomTree 的体量小一些，代币化业务的变化更值得跟踪。公司最新披露，相关 AUM 已接近 13 亿美元，年内增长约 65%，目前增速十分迅猛，反而更值得长期跟踪。

我的看法：这两家公司都有现有业务支撑，但不要把客户管理资产的规模，直接当成股东能赚到的钱。最终还是看费率、成本和净流入。

📍 $BHYP：单独看，它是持有 $HYPE 的基金

BHYP 是 Bitwise Hyperliquid ETF，并非上市公司股票。

基金净资产约 1.80 亿美元。这个数字是基金规模，不是 Hyperliquid 的估值。

它对应的是 HYPE 的投资逻辑：交易生态增长、费用分配、回购，以及代币供给变化。

我会把 BHYP 作为链上交易生态的独立敞口研究，不能直接套用上市公司的利润和市盈率框架。

把这些公司放在一起以后，我反而觉得，RWA 投资最容易犯的错误，是太早把行业前景算成自己的收益。

资产会上链，谁能赚钱，需要继续验证。

公司能赚钱，现在的价格是否合适，还要再算一遍。

这两步，少一步都不行。

图中前五个标的权重合计 84%，多个业务又受到加密市场活跃度、稳定币增长和风险偏好的共同影响。看起来买了很多名字，实际可能仍然在押同一个市场环境。

我更愿意按三个问题持续跟踪：

第一，客户有没有反复使用。

完成一次发行，和资产长期留在系统里交易、抵押、结算，价值差别很大。

第二，规模增长后，利润有没有留下来。

渠道分成、价格竞争和合规成本，都会影响最后的结果。

第三，公司做大以后，每股价值有没有增长。

融资、并购和股权激励持续增加股数，原有股东未必能完整享受到业务增长。

美国推动 RWA 的利益，我认为已经比较清楚了：让数字美元更好用，让美元资产更容易触达全球资金，再让金融服务围绕这些资产继续展开。

对我们来说，值得寻找的是其中能够长期留住客户、收取合理费用，并持续提高每股盈利的公司。

如果三年后，链上的资产规模翻了十几倍，你持有的公司却没有多赚多少钱，这笔投资仍然可能是失败的。

所以综上所述，我个人比较看好的标的： $CRCL, $HOOD, $SECZ, $COIN ，也是我目前持有的，但依旧要长期跟踪他们的收入增长，以及多元化带来的长期价值，DYOR🙏

Performed this Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy few days back with dense violin strings adhesions between liver and parietis,a case a Fitz Hug Curtis sybdrome causing chronic abdominal pain.
As a general surgeon few things should be noted in such a case-
1.The second port place ment is important and should be at around paper's or bit laterally instead of epigastric,to facilitate easy adhesiolysis.
2.All the liver-parietis adhesions should not be cut because in a way it provides retraction of the liver.
3.The main problem is widespread adhesions between all the structures around GB,rarely small bowel as well,where a gentle approach should be taken,although the Calot's anatomy is usually normal.
4. One of the issues is putting the Gall Bladder in retrieval bag as the space above liver cannot be used.

Today we are rolling out Gemini 4 Argon globally in the Gemini API, to Pro + Ultra in Gemini App, and Ultra subs in Antigravity!

Argon is a huge step forward for Gemini, and a labor of love. This model has been battle tested by over 100,000 people at Google over the last month, with so much new innovation, ambition, and hard work baked into this release. We rolled the model out to cyber defenders as part of our fairwind program and early access customers over the last 2 weeks, it has been amazing to see and talk to folks who are now using this model daily. Seeing the models writing capability, raw knowledge and persistence for coding, paired with new features like 1M token output when the model needs to work more has gotten me even more excited about our path ahead.

This is just the start of the Gemini 4 era. As you saw with 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, and 3.8 Flash, our iteration speed with Gemini is fast : ) Now with Gemini 4 Argon to work from, I am cannot wait to see the progress continue, and most importantly see what this new model enables for the world.

quoted_text:
Today, we're launching Sazabi version 1.0.

The reality of shipping software as a team in the age of AI is actually crazy.

Agents merging their own PRs. Hundreds of deployments per day. A codebase that is constantly changing. Junior developers with 10x or 100x leverage. 😵‍💫

I spent the last year building a safety harness for teams that ship with AI. It's called @sazabi.

The premise is simple:
1. You send us logs. 
2. We detect anomalies, investigate them, and send you back rich, actionable alerts about real problems in your app.

Sazabi helps you find issues before your users notice. 

No monitors or noisy alerts. Just pure signal. 

And today we're making it available for anyone to use.

text:
Interesting fact: as of today, this is powered by the most efficient and practical PIR scheme.

Under the hood, there is a ciphertext compression mechanism called packing.

A paper came out a month ago that optimized the packing throughput by 5x compared to the prior state of the art. It’s called ReInsPIRe.

The buffer introduced by the speed up has allowed us to reduce parameters controlling decryption correctness. The security parameters stay the same.

With more room for noise, we applied a number of tricks such as rounding encryption at the client/server boundaries, which reduced total bandwidth.

There are also GPUs involved for the matrix-vector multiplication of the database by the client query.

The results are sub 200KB total per-query bandwidth and sub 50ms server time on a 1.88 GB database.

The wallet PIR databases are sharded into chunks of under 500 MB. So, in production, the server time and bandwidth are even smaller.

text:
为什么我看好 $BORDR？因为它正在从一个代币，逐步走向 Solana 的基础设施。

真正让我看好 Bordrless 的，不只是它讲了什么故事，而是团队一直在持续交付。

从主网上线、DEX 发布，到 SDK 开放、无许可开发、Workshop 上线，再到 Axiom 集成落地，项目正在一步步把最初的构想变成真正可用的产品。

几个值得关注的进展：

• SDK 上线：让开发者能够基于协议构建自己的应用。

• Workshop 推出：开发者可以提交自定义 Hooks，并分享创作者费用收益。

• Companions 上线：支持链上创作者费用分配与回购自动化。

• DEX 与代币标准开放：让更多外部开发者参与构建 Bordrless 生态。

• Axiom 集成落地：这是一个重要进展，意味着交易不再局限于 Bordrless 自己的网站，相关代币可以通过外部交易终端进行交易，同时保留协议的 Hooks 功能。

• 持续升级主网：最新进展还包括多项功能更新、公开源码的可验证构建、SDK 发布，以及最高 1% 的集成费用机制，让终端、机器人和钱包有机会通过路由 Bordrless 交易获得收益。

这条发展路线很值得关注：

构建协议 → 产品上线 → 开放基础设施 → 吸引开发者 → 接入交易平台 → 建立集成激励。

这才是我真正关注的地方。

我看涨 $BORDR 的核心逻辑，并不是单纯押注一个热门叙事，而是押注它能否成为 Solana 可编程代币生态背后的经济层。

如果未来越来越多的代币发行、交易、Hooks、开发者工具、交易终端和应用接入 Bordrless，那么协议就有机会获得更多使用量，并形成更完整的经济循环。

根据项目公布的代币经济模型：

总供应量为 10 亿枚，团队称不会额外增发。
50% 的协议收入进入金库。
另外 50% 用于回购 BORDR，项目方称回购每 10 分钟执行一次。

如果这些机制能够持续运行，并且真实交易量和协议收入不断增长，那么回购机制的价值才有机会逐步体现。

当然，技术交付不等于商业成功，集成上线也不等于大规模采用。 后续仍需要观察真实交易量、协议收入、开发者增长、集成留存，以及回购机制的实际执行情况。

但对一个仍处于早期阶段的项目来说，我更愿意关注那些持续交付、开放技术并努力建立生态经济模型的团队。

Bordrless 已经展示出从协议到产品、从产品到集成的推进路径。

接下来真正值得期待的是：它能否让更多开发者和交易平台主动选择这套基础设施。

如果这个方向最终跑通，$BORDR 的想象空间就不只是一个 Meme 币的涨跌，而是整个生态能否持续创造价值。

我会继续关注，也期待下一阶段的交付。

$BORDR #Solana #Crypto

quoted_text:
My guess on the Polymarket airdrop: never. It doesn’t make sense when NYSE’s parent company is the biggest investor.

So why not just say there won’t be one? Because the airdrop hopes are what keep users trading.

A hypothetical pitch meeting 👇

INT. ICE BOARDROOM, NEW YORK. Mahogany. A Bloomberg terminal hums. A Polymarket founder in a hoodie faces a row of suits.

POLYMARKET: So we’re thinking about the next phase. IPO... or an airdrop.

ICE: What’s an airdrop?

POLYMARKET: We give free money to our users.

ICE: (long pause) Why?

POLYMARKET: Engagement.

ICE: And what do we get? We own 22% of the company.

POLYMARKET: You’d get some free money too.

ICE: From where?

POLYMARKET: From the token.

ICE: What’s the token worth?

POLYMARKET: Whatever people think it’s worth.

ICE: And what do people think it’s worth?

POLYMARKET: We’ll know after the airdrop.

ICE: We own the New York Stock Exchange. We have a building for exactly this. There’s a bell.

POLYMARKET: An IPO takes months. Lawyers, auditors, an S-1, the SEC...

ICE: And the airdrop?

POLYMARKET: A tweet.

ICE: (slowly) So why not just do it properly, with an IPO?

POLYMARKET: Because it’s more fun.

(Silence.)

ICE: Can we bet on it?

POLYMARKET: On what?

ICE: Whether the airdrop happens.

POLYMARKET: There’s already a market. 34% yes.

ICE: Who’s buying yes?

POLYMARKET: Our users. They’re farming the airdrop.

ICE: So they’re betting on getting free money from you...

POLYMARKET: ...by trading on the platform...

ICE: ...which generates fees for us...

POLYMARKET: ...so we don’t actually need to do the airdrop.

(The board exchanges glances. Someone slowly closes a laptop.)

ICE: Kid, that’s the best business model we’ve seen since 1792.

I like the framing that vibe coding an app is about as cheap as getting a free puppy.

I don't want to build my own coding harness because maintaining it at the edge of capability is more than a full time job. I want to "hire" great people to do that. 

This is what software is going to feel like ironically. You still pay monthly, but for the great updates. And for stuff that doesn't change much static (a personal todo app, etc) no reason not to build your own and very little value in paying others. 

In the end it feels a lot more like sports than locked in network effects. You go with the software team at the top of their game - and "hire" another one if they slip.

text:
“_______ is the new gold / oil” 

The expression that labels 
what asset is trending as the highest-value resource of each era

The Evolution since Gold 💰 :

- 1500: 🌶
Spices are the new gold.
Spices (especially black pepper, known as “black gold”) were among the most valuable commodities on Earth. They drove the Age of Exploration, global trade routes, and early colonial empires. 

- 1800: 🚂
Coal is the new spices. 
Coal powered the Industrial Revolution through steam engines, factories, railways, and iron/steel production, becoming the backbone of industrial growth and energy. 

- 1850: 🪔
Whale oil is the new coal.
Whale oil lit cities, streets, factories, and homes while serving as the premium lubricant for machinery. The whaling industry boomed as one of the world’s most valuable resources until petroleum replaced it. 

- 1910: 🛢
Crude oil is the new oil.
 Crude oil exploded in value with the automobile boom. Internal combustion engines and companies like Standard Oil made petroleum the backbone of energy and industry. 

- 1955: ⛽️
Gas / casual travel is the new oil.
Post-WWII car culture, suburbs, and the Interstate Highway System turned gasoline and personal mobility into the economic driver. 

- 1980: 🛍
Shopping is the new oil.
The 1980s saw the rise of malls, credit-fueled consumerism, and retail as a core GDP driver (U.S. consumer spending ~70% of the economy). 

- 2000: 👀
Attention is the new oil.
The attention influencer economy exploded with Web 2.0, Google, Facebook, and social media. Influence through influencers followed.

- 2015: 🤖
AI training data is the new oil.
Data for AI training became the new oil. It exploded with big data centers and AI agents (The Economist called data the world’s most valuable resource). 

- 2026: 💼
Life Management is the new oil.
AI agents, personal data, and life-optimization tools (calendars, health, finance, decisions) make managing your entire life the highest-value asset. 

- 2029: 💡
Innovative insight is the new oil. 
As AI handles routine tasks, human (and human+AI) creativity, novel insights, and high-value ideas become the premium resource. 

- 2031: 🚀
Searching for “the new oil” 
becomes the new oil. 
Exploration mapping and cataloguing of all life, expansion into space, underground undersea for finding resources opens the next frontier, with Helium-3 emerging as a critical fuel for clean fusion energy. 

Each wave shows the asset rising to dominance, peaking in economic power, then shifting to the next higher-value resource, with overall value and impact compounding upward across every era.

text:
Last week I had the pleasure of sharing the stage with @ethereumjoseph at our Ethereum Ecosystem Summit alongside @token2049.

The topic was “Ethereum’s Next Decade: The Cryptographic World Computer,” moderated by @mcamarda0.

Over the past two weeks at KBW and Token2049, we’ve focused on what’s happening now: the convergence of stablecoins, tokenized assets, onchain finance and AI agents. There is a clear acceleration of institutional adoption.

Individually, each of these elements is transformational. Together, they form the catalyst for a financial revolution that will lead to a new era of economic growth and financial autonomy for investors and consumers around the world.

But what will Ethereum look like by 2035? On our panel, we had the opportunity to take a step back and think big.

Vitalik recently shared that the Ethereum ecosystem will transition from a traditional blockchain into a high-capacity “cryptographic world computer.” But what does this mean in practice?

Ethereum’s foundation of trust and security rests on participants’ ability to independently verify transactions and their outcomes. Its continued evolution builds on that strength, expanding its capacity to support the global financial system. Ethereum’s coming architecture will be leaner and more modular, using ZK proofs and virtual machines to verify results more quickly and cheaply. These advances will support stronger privacy alongside better performance, while further upgrades will strengthen the network against emerging quantum threats. As that foundation becomes faster, more scalable, more private and more secure, we can begin to envision how much further Ethereum can go.
Here’s what this means in practice.

Tokenization will bring the world's value onchain, but this is just the on-ramp. Onchain finance at near zero cost will be the utility layer. Zero-knowledge proofs will be the engineering that allows neutral trust at a global scale. We will live in a world where any asset can be traded 24/7 with deep liquidity and can settle in an instant. Tokenized assets will be the preferred form of collateral not just in DeFi but across traditional execution venues. Programmable assets and money that run on blockchain rails will allow billions of AI agents to sift through millions of data points and scenarios to make the best decisions for consumers. Billions of AI agents will leverage machine intelligence, financial literacy and unlimited attention. They will provide retail investors with the same capabilities and outcomes as the largest Wall Street institutions.

To fully realize this vision, Ethereum’s core principles and advantages will become even more important. The words credibly neutral, decentralized, and censorship resistant mean different things to different audiences. In practice, they will underpin the foundation of the new digital and agentic economy.

Indulge me to explain why I believe these principles are so critical:

Credibly neutral means a network where the core rules, transaction ordering, validation, and settlement are applied consistently without favoring any specific person, company, or agenda. When the world’s largest financial institutions move their infrastructure onchain, they require one that will remain stable and resilient over decades because market participants know the rules of the game will not suddenly be rewritten to benefit insiders. This is equally important because the billions of agents that are coming onchain will rely programmatically on Ethereum for the essential architectural backbone of a machine-to-machine economy.

Decentralization means a network where no single company, bank, or government controls the ledger or makes the rules. Decentralization will create a new type of trust that relies on self-executing smart contracts without the need to rely on human or corporate trust. This automated trust, combined with instant settlement of transactions, will lead to a massive reduction in financial market risk. Equally important, it will ensure the AI agents can seamlessly interact with different decentralized protocols. They can lend on one platform, borrow on another, and hedge derivatives, without always needing API keys or permission from corporate gatekeepers.

Censorship resistant means a technical and structural guarantee that anyone with an internet connection can create an account or broadcast a transaction without applying for permission from a centralized authority. In practice, it means that Ethereum applies the exact same mathematical rules to everyone. This is not a political slogan, but rather a prerequisite for the future onchain and agent economy. No one can be unbanked and no AI agent can be excluded from the new machine-to-machine economy.

We envision a future where the Ethereum ecosystem will form the global, decentralized settlement infrastructure for the movement of assets and transactions, a new internet of value. This design will make it more difficult for highly-placed intermediaries to exploit a lack of attention to collect rents. It will make it easier for billions of AI agents with unlimited financial attention to deliver value for investors and consumers around the world. 

At Sharplink, we have more conviction than ever that Ethereum is best-positioned to deliver this future, a value proposition that is hard to overstate.

ETH, held.

Conviction, held.

text:
Robinhood 加密的官方X 账号 @RobinhoodCrypto 发帖公开欢迎一个偏冷门的生态协议 @metricxyz, 比较罕见。

Metric 能获得这个待遇，我认为跟它与RH Chain 定位的高度契合、能补强关键的底层infra 脱不开关系。

Metric 的定位是基于propAMM 机制的DEX，但它跟目前RH Chain 上的龙头DEX Uniswap 并不是零和竞争，而是要进一步做大现货市场的整体蛋糕。

propAMM 机制有别于传统的AMM: 传统AMM 可以理解成“先交易，价格再被交易推着走”；Metric 则是“先把真实价格引进来，再围绕它做交易”。前者特别适用于没有外部参考价的资产和长尾市场，后者则对RWA/ 股票代币化这类有真实外部市场价格的资产非常友好。

因为propAMM 机制下资产的价格主要由预言机引入外部参考价驱动，资产价格能快速跟随真实价格变动，价格更准、LP 风险更低、资本效率也更高。

引入Metric 后，可以跟Uniswap 形成比较清晰的互补分工：
Uniswap 提供基础和通用的流动性，而Metric 提供针对Stocks Tokens 的专业流动性。

一起把Robinhood Chain 生态做大做强。

author: felix_fan
quoted_text:
Part of @TrustWallet  engineering is available for other teams to build on.

It’s called Wallet Core: an open source library for creating and importing wallets, deriving addresses and signing transactions across supported blockchains.

A simple example: a developer can use it to derive a receiving address or sign a transaction inside their own app. Checking balances and broadcasting that transaction requires separate communication with blockchain nodes.

Wallet Core provides part of the foundation. Developers build their own application around it.

The value extends beyond Trust Wallet: other teams can reuse these components rather than implement each one from scratch.

I usually cover the updates people see in the app. This time, I wanted to highlight the code other builders can use, and the work that goes into maintaining and documenting it.

Credit to the Trust Wallet engineers and the wider contributor community. Making that foundation available to others is a contribution worth recognizing.

text:
Recently, @frostledger and I joined the Layer One podcast to discuss the Foundation's research agenda.

One interesting topic that came up: Validator pay is a genuinely hard problem, and most chains haven't actually solved it.

The real question is a two-sided market problem: what are network users actually willing to pay for validation, and what's the minimum validators need to be willing to provide it? We need some kind of equilibrium mechanism to find that price.

There's a second layer to this too. Validation is a public good, validators don't fully capture the benefit of the security they provide, everyone on the network does. Basic economic theory says that means it'll be undersupplied without some kind of subsidy.

Still working through the answer, but this is exactly the kind of question our research agenda is built to take on.

Not just for Avalanche, probably every proof-of-stake chain out there.

text:
Today we're launching MagicOS. And we've come to the conclusion that designers are NOT getting replaced.

most of the industry moved to the same answer this year: give the agent its own canvas, let it run, hand you the output. 

we made a different bet: the canvas should be yours and the agent is your collaborator. that’s MagicOS.

most AI design tools are a linear conversation: prompt, generate, iterate, repeat. a hundred prompts in, you might have a great final design, but the reasoning, rejected directions, and inspiration that got you there are buried in a chat log nobody will ever scroll back through.

MagicOS is a persistent, spatial canvas. Your PRD, inspiration images, design system, variations, rejected directions, final picks - all of it lives together, all in one place, instead of stacked on top of itself and lost.

it’s voice-first. talk to it in real time and watch work land directly on the canvas as you speak.

it’s also multiplayer. your whole team works on the same canvas together.

and it still runs on your design system and components because none of this matters if the output doesn’t look like your actual product.

three months ago, this was internal only at Magic Patterns, my co-founder's weekend project. it’s now live for everyone.

Design everything, everywhere, all at once.

text:
Busy morning back from vacation. I've been resharing a ton of news this morning, especially from Google who just launched a new model, and Apple who just announced a bunch of hardware, along with a bunch of startups in AI space (see my profile).

I was just talking with execs at @hm (big fashion brand) about the future of fashion. 

How will brain computer interfaces, glasses, robots, autonomous cars, change our fashion? 

For one, if you had a humanoid in your business, you will want a uniform for your robot, and if you brought it home, you would want a variety of outfits to make it nicer to look at, at minimum. 

Just think of a world where there are millions of robots walking around our cities. Do we want them all to look the same? Heck no. And that's a place where America will have a lot to say, even if China is way ahead in robotics. (And they have a lot of stores in China too).

Hey @radbackwards thinking of you, since you are ahead of most in building a fashionable home robot. I think there will be a sizeable market someday for dressing up your Neo. I don't want mine to be dressed the same as the one that @wholemars has.

But I was also thinking of @reservoirfarms. How textiles are grown in America was something they were interested in. And farmers aren't seen as fashionable, but I disagree, even when out in the field they have a unique fashion sense that's utilitarian, from boots and hats, but they like to party on the weekends and dress up just like every one else.

But brands like them can help introduce new ideas to lots of people, and brain computer interfaces are clearly coming, and are opening up new fashion needs. 

Interesting way to end vacation, was my first meeting after getting back home for the first time in 10 days. 

Now back to catching up on all the AI news that's breaking from Google and others. 

What would you want to show a fashion brand about the future? Are you building a company that has a potential impact on fashion? @hthieblot got any startups we should get on the calendar to come see?

It's so nice to be back home.

Compare this to even something like Astra, which did every effort level, in under 12 hours, for less than $50.

That makes Muse Wonder more expensive, and a lot slower, than Astra. 

Now I'm not sure what to do. I'll either needs to pay a small fortune to benchmark this model given how token hungry it is, or take a month or longer benchmarking it.

Put together some preliminary results comparing Muse Wonder to Opus 5.5 and GPT 6.1 Sol w/respect to token use. 

While it's looking like an accurate model, I care a lot about cost-per-task, as we all should, and right now, this number is looking very high.

quoted_text:
Most of the recent math results were not reached by a swarm, the way Navier–Stokes was. I think that part got lost in the excitement around the release. OpenAI's unnamed internal model, which I'm going to call Aeon, reached most of them in one shot, from a single prompt, with no interruptions. This model did not even exist before the end of August, and it is still training. Notice how the returns are not dropping off? That chart is from a month ago. It is a log scale. What does Aeon look like now? 

On average, each result used three hours of thinking. Aeon was given 4000 problems to work on by OpenAI. How many more have been solved in the last three days? That number is not zero. 

It's like hearing notes in a song that is slowly rising. I don't think Pacing the Frontier was just about Hugging Face or hacking. They've seen how close we are to closing the loop, and as the hour draws near, their resolve begins to quaver. The last piece was model creativity, and I think that threshold was crossed internally by Anthropic and OpenAI in September. You see it in Opus 5.5, which gets it from Fable 5.5. You see it in the math results from Aeon.

All that was needed to start the event was the ability for models to think of novel ways to improve themselves. That was the last piece. This is directly analogous to the ability to think of strange, alien ways to solve math problems: solutions so inhuman that they are difficult to express in existing human terms, so the proof winds up incomprehensible. I think these same kinds of alien solutions are now being applied to model improvements internally. That's what all this recent consternation is really about. They see the invisible frontier. And they see what is about to happen.
