text:
The WSJ starting to admit the obvious: Western democracy when combined with fiscally negative immigration and a generous welfare state, inexorably creates a solvency crisis. (they didn't mention the immigration part but it's an essential ingredient in the toxic mix)

their words are unusually stark: 

> It’s also a litmus test of a pressing question facing the West: Is it possible for political leaders to rein in spending on ever expanding welfare states? So far, the answer seems to be no, increasing the chances that countries like Britain are inching toward a financial reckoning.

the welfare state + open borders model is a clear democracy failure mode and there's no obvious way out. no western European nation will reform pensions or entitlements. they are actually fundamentally incapable of doing what must be done. (the immigration aspect is virtual corollary to democracy because it creates incentives for the left to import reliable voters, so at least part of the time immigration is virtually unfettered.)

the UK, with maximum, unending immigration, an aging and shrinking workforce, a tiny and overexploited base of taxpayer paypigs, highly financialized service / financial industry, a legacy of welfare as political payoffs to disenfranchised groups, an inability to cut pensions, and a stagnant, is the poster child for this disease and the worst affected but by no means the only nation in this predicament. 

the UK's grim fiscal state is the future of every western nation, unless something changes dramatically. 

aging population + increasingly discouraged working-age adults + highly mobile capital & elites that simply leave under onerous tax regimes + mass and unending fiscally negative immigration + expensive decarbonization and deindustralization + a left wing that is totally committed to immigration, over all else + a total inability to cut entitlements = fiscal crisis and eventual default 

in the end, the wealthy and the entrepreneur class that actually power growth will simply leave to escape the tightening tax noose. the government will become increasingly reliant on the middle/upper middle professional classes who lack the ability to leave, completely eliminating any motive to be entrepreneurial or take risks. the economy will become increasingly torpid as dynamism vanishes. the left will continue to gain power due to slow electoral build of immigration and will continue to honor their side of the deal, which is neverending handouts to fiscally useless electoral client groups. 

case studies like south africa, venezuela and lebanon show us that life can get worse, and worse, and worse, and worse and worse. things getting extremely bad are not a guarantee that they won't continue to get worse. don't be fooled by anticipating a sudden realization among political elites that they have employed the wrong formula. things can just get steadily worse for decades and decades with no escaping the slide. 

if I had to guess, I would venture that if no MAJOR (and I'm talking _major_) political reform occurs in western Europe, the continent will enter a sovereign debt crisis in the coming decade, standards of living will collapse, life expectancy will collapse, entitlements will be ravaged. I anticipate something akin to the effect that the collapse of the Soviet Union had on the local population, or worse. politics will be polarized between the ultraright and far left, each with their own radical solution to the problem (extirpating immigrants, versus actual socialism). I don't know which of the two will prevail. neither the right nor the left is willing to reform entitlements, which is the biggest problem, and so the market will do it for them. the US may escape their fate, but I am not particularly optimistic it will. our demographics and willingness to do hard things (on immigration, eg) are marginally better, but our spending and fraud-based entitlement economy is almost just as bad. no major party will even contemplate uttering that boomer luxury communism must end eventually. it's not even a topic in the midterms nor will it be in '28. 

the productivity boost from AI might grant European nations a slight reprieve in the medium term, but it wont salvage their bleak fiscal situation in the end. this is because almost no European nation controls the industrial inputs to AI (beyond ASML), so their gain is limited to the productivity uplift from deployment of the technology, while they remain vassals to the nations which actually control the deeper stack. moreover, a GDP and tax revenue boost from AI can easily be outspent. these nations have a spending problem, not a revenue problem. they can always dream up utterly farcical new handout schemes, like the UK's "motability". additionally, while AI creates a legion of highly productive entrepreneurs, they will all tax optimize and the benefits of new firms will largely not be captured by their respective governments. capital and startups are more portable than they have ever been. AI simply accelerates the pareto-ization of the economy whereby a shrinking minority of founders produces more value whilst more and more are idle and depend on handouts from the productive few. however, capital and human capital mobility destroys this fragile arrangement and strips the idle many of their benefactors. AI buys Western Europe at most a few years of delay to the inevitable crisis.

text:
Interesting fact: as of today, this is powered by the most efficient and practical PIR scheme.

Under the hood, there is a ciphertext compression mechanism called packing.

A paper came out a month ago that optimized the packing throughput by 5x compared to the prior state of the art. It’s called ReInsPIRe.

The buffer introduced by the speed up has allowed us to reduce parameters controlling decryption correctness. The security parameters stay the same.

With more room for noise, we applied a number of tricks such as rounding encryption at the client/server boundaries, which reduced total bandwidth.

There are also GPUs involved for the matrix-vector multiplication of the database by the client query.

The results are sub 200KB total per-query bandwidth and sub 50ms server time on a 1.88 GB database.

The wallet PIR databases are sharded into chunks of under 500 MB. So, in production, the server time and bandwidth are even smaller.

text:
严肃学习金律师 @JianzhiJin & @Bitrace_team 雄文 ，AI 翻译如下：

新币担保被制裁：4500 万美元 USDT 的法律地位与美中两国执法路径

2026 年 9 月 8 日，稳定币发行方 Tether 将当时东南亚最大的非法加密货币交易担保平台新币担保（Xinbi Guarantee）的一个链上业务地址列入黑名单，冻结了逾 4500 万美元的 USDT。
次日，美国财政部与司法部联合宣布，将新币担保认定为跨国犯罪组织并对其施加制裁。Telegram 与 The Open Network 区块链网络也随之采取了封堵措施。
新币担保的多个群组及 TNS 至今无法访问，且尚未恢复。

上述进展在东亚与东南亚的有组织犯罪网络中引发震荡。部分非法市场商户转向其他平台，部分退出市场，还有许多人试图通过各种渠道"维权"，以期取回被冻结的押金。这给所有相关方提出了一个重大问题：从新币担保处冻结的数千万美元加密资产，其法律地位为何？最终将流向何方？

本文由区块链监管科技公司 Bitrace 与知名加密货币律师 金鉴智合著，介绍该担保平台的商业模式，区分商户所缴押金的法律性质，并解释新币担保在中国与美国法律框架下面临的法律风险。

一、加密担保平台的性质

加密担保平台并非合法的金融机构。它们是服务于非法市场的地下信用与交易基础设施。此类平台通常使用 USDT 等加密货币结算，并在 Telegram 等即时通讯平台上设立交易群组。它们为互不信任的双方提供撮合、押金托管、交易登记、结算与争议仲裁，并通过佣金、群租费、押金及其他服务费获取收入。

这类平台具有三项核心属性：
1. 地下信用中介
非法市场交易的参与者隐匿身份、跨境运作，通常缺乏可通过法律渠道执行的合同。担保平台借助其品牌、押金要求与仲裁机制，为交易双方提供一种替代性的信用保障。

2. 非法市场商户的聚合器
平台设立大量群组，把提供诈骗工具开发、网络赌博、非法换汇、洗钱、套现、将银行卡资金转换为 USDT、钓鱼、服务器与域名等服务的商户聚集在一起。这使原本分散的买卖双方能在一处找到交易对手。

3. 地下市场基础设施
平台将通讯群组、商户流量、信用担保与加密支付结合在一起，连接上游的技术与资源供应商、中游的犯罪运营者，以及下游的支付、洗钱与套现渠道。值得注意的是，平台通常是商户的聚合器与信用中介，但未必控制其公开群组内所有底层犯罪活动。

二、加密担保平台的主要功能

担保平台一般承担以下功能：
1.身份与准入管理：对商户进行登记与筛查，或对其施加押金要求；
2.供需撮合：利用群组展示不同类型的地下商品与服务；
3.信用出租：允许商户借用平台声誉，以降低陌生交易对手之间的不信任；
4.资金托管：在交易完成前暂时保管一方或双方存入的 USDT；
5.交易登记：记录交易主体、金额与条款，以支持后续结算与争议解决；
6.结算与放款：在确认交易完成后，将托管资金扣除佣金后放给收款方；
7.争议仲裁：依据平台内部规则处理违约或纠纷；
8.流量获取：利用平台既有用户、群组与品牌为商户带来客户；
9.对接支付与洗钱通道：整合套现、场外兑换、加密支付与资金洗白服务，使非法所得得以接收、转移、兑换并变现为现金。

三、私有群与公开群的区别

私有群与公开群是担保交易的两种主要场所。
私有群是小型的封闭群组，用于为某笔特定交易提供担保；公开群则是规模更大、开放性的群组，由商户自行发起交易。

在私有群交易中，平台为某笔具体交易提供托管：一方或双方事先向平台存入与交易金额等值的 USDT。交易完成后，平台在扣除佣金后返还押金或将资金放给收款方。
在公开群模式下，服务商先缴纳一笔较大额度的押金，再按月租用平台群组，通过预先登记交易的方式持续服务多个客户。平台不仅提供担保，还将自身的品牌信誉、经营空间与用户流量出租给商户。因此，公开群更像是依托担保平台长期经营的"地下店面"，而私有群则更接近为单笔交易临时设立的托管与仲裁场所。

四、新币收取的 USDT 押金，法律性质如何？

基于前述非法担保商业模式，新币担保并非诈骗资金流经的平台。新币在此过程中锁定的 USDT，是洗钱交易参与方缴纳的押金，与诈骗所得相分离。理解这一点，是分析后续全部法律问题的起点。
从法律与功能的角度看，这笔 USDT 是履约保证金，而非交易对价，更不是诈骗所得。
它解决的是洗钱交易双方之间的信任缺口。诈骗团伙与为其处理资金的一方彼此不信任：一方担心对方在收到受害人资金后不履约，另一方则需要确保交易能按约定结算。因此，双方事先向新币锁定一笔特定金额的 USDT。平台根据双方是否履行约定义务，决定返还、扣减还是继续持有该押金。
这与传统的第三方托管相似，区别在于传统托管通常保管的是交易价款，而本安排保管的是与交易价格相分离的履约担保。

这一点对公开群与私有群交易同样适用。
在公开群中，洗钱方先交纳押金，再随机接单。
在私有群中，洗钱方已与特定诈骗团伙就处理某笔具体金额达成一致，并在受害人付款前交纳押金。就资金来源或民法功能而言，两类押金在实质上并无差别：都是为担保履约而预先提交的 USDT，既不是受害人被盗的美元，也不是由这些美元直接兑换而来的 USDT。

真正的差别在于证据链的强弱。
在私有群交易中，如果完整的证据链显示"某受害人即将支付 100 万美元；洗钱方事先为该 100 万美元锁定一笔对应押金；受害人付款；资金完成兑换；押金被释放"，执法机关就更容易将该押金与某一具体犯罪关联起来。
而在公开群的随机交易中，这种一对一的对应关系通常更弱。这一区分在美国法下尤为重要，因为美国的民事没收制度明确要求：主张某财产被用于实施或便利犯罪的执法机关，必须证明该财产与犯罪之间存在实质性联系。

五、在中国法下，新币的风险取决于它是否"明知"自己在帮什么

中国最高人民法院与最高人民检察院 2025 年就掩饰、隐瞒犯罪所得罪发布的司法解释明确规定，刑法第 312 条中的"其他方法"范围广泛，包括居间介绍买卖财物、提供账户、转换财物、通过支付结算方式转移资金以及跨境转移资产等。是否"明知"并不单凭行为人是否口头承认来认定；办案机关会综合评估交易异常性、资金流向、行为人的职业与背景，以及其与上游犯罪人的关系等因素。
最高人民法院 2025 年发布的一起典型案例，其结构与本案高度相似：被告人先购买虚拟货币作为"押金"，随后提供银行卡接收诈骗所得，取现后再购买虚拟货币并交付给上游联系人。被告人最终被以掩饰、隐瞒犯罪所得罪定罪。

但这并不意味着提供押金服务就自动使新币构成犯罪。
如果新币只是提供一套通用的担保规则，不处理诈骗所得，不知悉具体底层交易的性质，也无法区分所谓的公开群与私有群，那么犯罪分子使用了它的服务这一事实本身，并不足以认定平台具有犯罪的"明知"。
反之，如果交易反复呈现出高度异常的特征——例如金额、频次、交易对手与资金冻结情况持续指向典型的电信诈骗洗钱——而平台在收到明确风险信息、甚至执法机关的提示后，仍继续为这些交易量身定制担保、结算与争议解决机制，那么其"明知或应知"的风险将显著上升。最高人民法院 2025 年的黄金交易案就说明了这一点：经营者起初可能从事的是普通业务，但在其银行账户因含诈骗所得被冻结、且警方已明确告知之后，该经营者仍继续为异常交易提供便利，最终被以掩饰、隐瞒犯罪所得罪定罪。

还有一种风险更高的情形值得关注。中国最新的司法解释明确规定，如果行为人在诈骗发生前即与犯罪人共谋，事后又掩饰、隐瞒犯罪所得，在符合犯罪构成要件的情况下，可直接按诈骗罪或其他上游犯罪的共犯处理。如果平台自身参与了此类事先安排，其潜在刑事责任可能从"事后协助转移犯罪所得"上升为"上游犯罪的共犯"。但如果新币对该安排并不知情，则当事人之间的共谋不能自动归责于平台。

中国还存在一个独立于洗钱刑事责任之外的监管问题。2021 年《关于进一步防范和处置虚拟货币交易炒作风险的通知》明确将法定货币与虚拟货币之间的兑换、虚拟货币之间的兑换、作为虚拟货币交易中央对手方，以及为虚拟货币交易提供信息中介与定价服务列为非法金融活动。该通知还明确将境外虚拟货币交易所向中国大陆居民提供的服务纳入监管范围。
因此，新币的刑事洗钱风险，与其在中国因虚拟货币业务本身而产生的监管风险，应当分别评估。

六、在美国法下，新币可能面临哪些法律责任？

1. 即便新币持有的 USDT 并非犯罪所得，也可能被没收
就目前可得的事实而言，如果从新币处冻结的 USDT 在受害人付款之前即已存在、且受害人的美元从未流入新币，那么将其直接定性为受害人的"诈骗所得"或这些所得的可追溯替代物，存在明显的事实障碍。但美国执法机关还有另一条路径。《美国法典》第 18 编第 981(a)(1)(A) 条（18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(A)）授权没收任何涉及违反美国洗钱法的财产，而不仅仅是犯罪所得本身。美国法院已多次认定，来源完全合法的资金，只要实际上被用于促成洗钱完成，仍可被没收。例如，第五巡回法院在 United States v. Tencer 案中认可了所谓的"便利化理论"：用于掩护犯罪资金、使洗钱更易于继续进行的合法资金，可以构成涉及洗钱的财产。法院采用的经典检验标准是：该财产是否使非法活动"更便利、更少阻力地实施"。
第十巡回法院同样在 United States v. Bornfield 案中认定，涉及洗钱的财产不仅包括被洗的资金，还包括佣金及其他用于便利洗白的财产。
与本案情尤其相似的 United States v. Puche 案涉及一家货币兑换业务。法院认定，企业账户中的合法资金如果实际上保护了非法资金、从而便利了其转移，则可被没收。
如果美国执法机关能够证明这些押金构成了信用基础设施，使陌生人之间的交易得以可靠地完成洗钱——尤其是在能够将个别押金与特定的诈骗所得相对应的情况下——他们就可以主张这些押金属于便利化财产。

反之，如果被冻结资产存放于一个长期存在的通用押金池中、被随机用于大量交易，且与某一特定的美国诈骗案缺乏明确联系，执法机关就更难以证明第 983 条（§ 983）所要求的实质性联系。

2. USDT 可被没收，并不自动等同于新币实施了洗钱
《美国法典》第 18 编第 1956 条（18 U.S.C. § 1956）对洗钱罪规定了具体的主观要件。在典型案件中，执法机关必须证明被告明知该财产代表某种非法活动的所得，并以法定目的行事，例如促进非法活动，或掩饰犯罪所得的性质、来源、所有权或控制权。因此，对新币而言，"押金机制客观上帮助了洗钱"与"平台明知自己在帮助洗钱"是两个完全不同的命题。如果平台只是对所有用户适用一套自动化、通用的担保规则，不了解底层法币资金的来源，也未参与买卖双方实施诈骗的安排，那么执法机关仍需另行证明平台具有明知或故意。
但如果内部聊天记录、客服记录、专用通道、风控例外、费用安排或其他证据显示，平台管理人员明知所谓"担保业务"主要是为洗白诈骗所得服务，风险将截然不同。

3. 即便被没收资产并非受害人的钱，仍可能被用于赔偿受害人
另一个重要但常被忽视的区分是：冻结不等于没收，没收也不意味着受害人将获得资金。执法机关冻结 USDT 时，仅意味着资产处于临时控制之下。美国必须首先通过相应的没收程序取得该资产。第 18 编第 981 条本身即授权将没收资产用于赔偿犯罪受害人，现行美国司法部的资产没收政策也规定了向受害人返还的机制。
因此，即便法院最终认定"被冻结的 100 万 USDT 与受害人的 100 万美元并非同一笔钱"，这 100 万 USDT 仍可能尽管来源合法，却被认定为便利了洗钱的财产，依美国法被没收，并用于赔偿诈骗受害人。
但美国不能径行无视第三方利益。司法部现行的分配顺序明确规定，在受理受害人主张之前，优先保障所有权人与留置权人。

七、从中性工具到犯罪基础设施

本案最有趣之处在于，它把传统反洗钱法中长期存在的一个问题带入了链上世界：一个合法、中性的信用工具，在反复被用于非法交易之后，究竟在哪一点上会在法律眼中变成"犯罪基础设施"？如果仅看资金来源，新币确实有一个有力的有利事实：受害人的钱没有进入新币。
但这并不能解决所有问题。中国法院越来越关注行为人是否明知、是否实际参与资金转换，或在收到明确警示信号后是否继续提供帮助。在美国，执法机关的目光超越了追查犯罪所得本身，还会追问特定财产是否实质性地便利了犯罪。
对这类平台而言，最终决定法律风险的问题，或许并不是"中心化还是去中心化"这种抽象问题，甚至不是它"是否曾经处理过犯罪所得"。而可能是三个更直接的问题：

平台究竟看到了什么？
它究竟控制了什么？
在知悉这些信息之后，它做了什么？ 

这三个问题的答案，才更接近最终的法律答案。

text:
一些已经财务自由的朋友问，不要工资，有没有门路去 frontier lab 工作。这些 frontier lab 的回答是，每个人消耗的 GPU 成本和 token 成本远超他们的工资，一个不能胜任的人浪费的资源不是不要工资就能弥补的。

DeepSeek 刘胜宇把今年夏天以来的算子开发比作 “机甲驾驶员”。LLM 正在逐渐制造业化，机器的成本超过人的成本（虽然人仍然很贵），工程经验比 raw intelligence 更重要，social closure 正在形成。

创业以来接触了很多财务自由的人，财务自由只能给你拒绝工作的自由、消费的自由，不能给你创造的自由。

很多财务自由的人甚至连拒绝工作的自由都没有，比如很多上市公司高管，公司就像自己的孩子，必须一直负责下去，没有心思赶新的技术浪潮。

要获得创造的自由，也就是自由进入自己想做的领域，我只想到三条路：
1. 自己深入学习另一个领域，转行，比如从天坑专业转码；AI 可以让我们更快地入门和探索新领域，但要达到顶尖水平，仍然很难，因为专业圈子都像 LLM 这样存在 social closure。
2. 在一个领域取得成果、声誉和影响力，从而可以通过项目合作、顾问等方式进入感兴趣的其他领域，甚至横跨多个领域；（可以是公司内，比如做网络的专家也需要参与芯片、OS 等部门的讨论和合作；也可以是跨公司的）
3. 具备讲故事、拉团队、整合资源的能力，比如很多优秀创始人并非技术背景。

quoted_text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

1) Trying again.
 TLDR: Everyone can win. Open-source, frontier labs, infrastructure, applications and most importantly the American people.
 
I understand all of the jitters about Anthropic losing share, real rates, spreads and second derivatives. Still think the most likely future outcome is a hybrid, multi-model future where almost everyone wins, open-weight tokens are likely the overwhelming majority of tokens, the dominant frontier model companies still do well albeit perhaps not the outcome that seemed possible in May and AI infrastructure/applications benefit immensely from the increased fragmentation, competition and lower margins at the model layer.
 
Lower margins at the model layer mechanically drive higher compute demand as long as someone is willing to pay for the training. And Jensen is obviously willing to be the “trainer of last resort.” As below-market compute contracts signed in 24/25 roll-off and reprice higher, cloud and neocloud revenue should continue to accelerate which will help address financing fears; I think we may be near peak external financing for this buildout. Noteworthy that using data from 3Fourteen Research, B200 clusters will generate a 37% IRR *if* their rental price declines 40% per year. Prices are still going up, but that IRR math is too ridiculous to print. 37% IRRs available at scale should get funded.

Re: this weekends controversy about MOUs, Anthropic’s $413 billion of real contractual commitments sounds scary. Reality is that it works out to roughly $31 billion of annual cloud spend, which is easily internally financed given their reported ARR, and $161 billion of spend at Broadcom which will be financed by Broadcom and private credit.

Continue to believe fragmentation at the model layer is the best outcome for ordinary Americans and humans everywhere. As I have said before, do not trust any 5-20 individuals to make the best possible decisions about the direction of this technology. I want as many AIs as possible to maximize the odds that they encompass the diversity of human values across the world and richness of human variation. And I want an AI that shares my own personal values. Safety, freedom and the maximization of human agency through democratization, distribution and diffusion vs. centralization. History has spoken on the dangers of the latter path.

Finally, from my perspective anything that slows this buildout down is net positive over the long-term as the biggest risk and worst outcome is an *actual* overbuild. We are structurally short watts, wafers and increasingly capital. That is all good. God forbid we were still in ZIRP, TSM ramped capex to 3x their current plan and we weren’t short turbine blades: there would almost certainly be an overbuild and a bubble. That would be terrible. Slower and smoother for longer is better both for investors and for the world. A terrible cyber event is the most plausible near term bear case IMHO, but AI cyberdefense ramping quickly and I was happy to hear Sholto say that cyber probably becomes defense dominant in the near future.

text:
2026 is the year fundamentals beat Bitcoin.

In 2025, 85%+ of large-cap tokens underperformed Bitcoin. In 2026, roughly a quarter are ahead so far. A common feature among them is that they distribute value to tokenholders.

Value distributed = holder revenue (rewards, buybacks, burns) minus dilutive emissions. Divide by market cap and you have a token's dividend yield.

We tested 60 factors across $100M+ tokens, 2021 to Q3 2026. Tokenholder distributions produced the strongest signal of the 60.

Tokens yielding 1%+ beat the rest by ~7pp a quarter, after controls for size, momentum, volatility, and Bitcoin beta. Their median return against Bitcoin in 2026 through Q3 was +17%, the first positive median since 2021.

An illustrative, monthly rebalanced index of these tokens returned 82% in 2026 through Q3, net of assumed trading costs. Bitcoin returned -5%.

But most of that has come since August, and the same rules underperformed Bitcoin in prior years. 23 quarters is a short sample, and with 60 factors tested, some results will look significant by chance. A return signal, not causation.

It also does not mean every protocol should distribute. Sustainable distributions need profits or surplus cash flow; for protocols still growing, reinvestment may be the better use of capital. Fee and revenue levels are mostly a size effect once controlled; fee growth on its own showed no signal, and burns showed no signal of their own once we excluded protocols distributing 0.5% or more.

Analysis by @KoschigRobert, 1kx Head of Economics. Presented by @lalleclausen, Founding Partner, at Token2049 last week.

text:
There’s been a lot of discussion on Muse Wonder since the launch. But there are some very interesting aspects that are under-discussed and make this launch unique from the rest of the frontier:

1. Big model smell reporting (goodbye benchmaxxing?): For the first time, a model launch measured and reported big model smell which basically shows how the model does on tasks it targeted in post-training vs tasks it didn’t. 
It’s essentially a guard against “benchmaxxed” models. I haven’t seen another frontier lab put this in a launch post, and I think all labs should start reporting it, ideally with the held-out tasks named.

2. Active focus: Muse Wonder is built to not give up when it hits real-world blockers, to keep trying alternative approaches and adapt to new information, while checking in before important actions. For instance, if a dinner reservation fails or a form throws an error, it tries another route on its own. Every lab trains for persistence, but Meta measures it on everyday personal tasks like housing, travel, IT and finance, not just coding. That’s what makes Wonder a good fit for assistants like Muse.

Active memory: carries important context about you across conversations and pulls up the details that matter for whatever you’re doing. This release tested it inside long chats where facts change. 
Early in a long chat you say “my flight is tuesday”, then 50K tokens of other stuff later you say “actually it moved to thursday”. Ask “when do I fly?” and a model with weak memory might say tuesday because it saw that first. Meta built their memory test around exactly this case (and wonder tops it). Imo this stale info problem is the hardest part of memory, way harder than just remembering stuff. 

Memory+focus are so important for assistants. Muse will eat the world.

The streamer secured exclusive rights in Spain and Andorra to all 104 matches, the company announced Tuesday.

One match per matchday will be free in Spain, and a free-to-air broadcaster will carry every Spain match, both semifinals and the final. Financial terms weren’t disclosed.

text:
If you're vibe coding, you need to add these 7 rules to your AGENTS.md:

1. Never edit, skip, or delete a test to make it pass. For every test you write, confirm it would fail if the code under test did nothing. If it would still pass, rewrite it.

A green test suite is the easiest thing for an agent to fake.

2. Before adding any dependency, confirm it exists on the official registry, who maintains it, and when it last shipped. Show me the link. Never guess a package name.

Agents repeat the same fake package names, and attackers can register them.

3. Before using any library's API, check the installed version and read its actual docs or source. Never write code from memory of an older version.

Agents write code for the version they were trained on. Yours could be newer or older.

4. Never say a task is done until you've proven it against the real thing. Run it and show me the actual output, not a summary. 'It compiles' is not proof. If you can't run it, say so.

When agents grade their own work, they rarely fail themselves.

5. If two fixes fail the same way, stop. The shared assumption is probably wrong. Question it before writing another fix. Never retry a theory you already ruled out.

Agents retry the same wrong theory with more confidence every time.

6. Only change what a task requires. If you notice other issues, first list them instead of immediately fixing them.

The bugs you didn't ask for come from the fixes you didn't ask for.

7. Never delete untracked files or data, rewrite git history, or force-push without showing me the exact command and waiting for approval.

One command can erase a day of work, and agents run them casually.

Newer frontier models already handle a few of these tbh, but not always fully.

Save these rules anyway. They're in mine. You will switch models on the same harness, and your rules file is one of those things that should come with you. Hooks and permissions can enforce the rest.

Note: If your code repo has both a CLAUDE.md and an AGENTS.md, Claude Code can silently ignore the AGENTS.md. You can change that under your Project instructions in /config. Most people just don't know it.

If it's a solo repo, use your project file. If it's a team repo, you'll likely want to put them in your global config.

One thing that's been underemphasized is the importance of having true diversity of output at the frontier. Using a single model, there are unmistakable signatures of each in everything from writing to "taste" in code. And this is most obvious in design (e.g., the color palate chosen as background).

I've been using Gemini 4 for some time now (it's a good model, you should try it), and I can say it is completely unique. This is obvious from the visualizations everyone is sharing now (including Ethan's excellent demos), but also in the way that it writes and communicates back and forth.

For an economist, the benefits of diversity and independence are baked into nearly all of our models; correlated signals/information/priors is how you get fragility, learning traps, and AI slop. So I'm very glad to see our big boi out there for people to use.

text:
This year's @token2049 felt different.

Less crowded. Less retail. Far more high-quality conversation. And one shared ambition across crypto platforms and fintechs: offer every financial service on-chain. Crypto and stocks alike.

A few things stood out from the yield session and our product conversations:

1. Stocks on-chain & associated yield
For most platforms, Robinhood included, on-chain stock volume is expected to pick up next year. From there, the priority becomes building baskets of stocks on-chain, which is barely happening yet, and single-stock yield.

2. Bitcoin yield
Native Bitcoin yield is still an untapped market. Only 3% of Bitcoin is earning yield today. It's now possible to put BTC to work across on-chain yield sources, from real-world assets to DeFi, and platforms know it: Bitcoin products are being prepared for launch next month.

3. Ethereum's moment of glory
Staking rates are clearly coming down, with the Ethereum ecosystem actively debating a cap on the share of ETH staked. Either way, that pushes capital toward on-chain ETH yield, where boosted ETH yields, from DeFi and carry trades alike, sit above the staking rate.

4. Stablecoin yield
Still very much a priority for every platform. After lending markets, the next ask is direct allocation to real-world assets. The problem everyone is trying to solve: liquidity in and out of those positions.

The rails are being laid. Capital markets are moving on-chain, and the products that define the next cycle are being built right now.

More excited than ever. See you next year 🫡

1. No regressions I notice. In particular, no personality or writing regressions. Feels like the same entity I was talking to with Spark.

text:
有朋友问，为什么你说共产主义和资本主义都是过渡阶段，目的王国才是最终方向？

这句话是确实我总结的，但我可不敢说概念是我的。有一个有意思的事实，就是这两边都曾宣布自己是终点。马克思那一脉相信，历史会走到消灭阶级的共产主义；1989年，福山写了《历史的终结？》，说自由民主加市场经济，可能就是人类制度演进的终点。中国官方的说法也很微妙，1987年中共十三大正式提出中国处在社会主义初级阶段，至少要上百年。所以“过渡”这两个字确实不是我发明的，我只是推广得更彻底一点，两边都是过渡，而它们通向的，也不是另一个更大的什么主义。

那为什么都是“过渡”？因为共产主义和资本主义回答的，是生产资料归谁、劳动怎么组织、东西怎么分，这些都是手段层面的问题，答得好坏当然差别很大，可它们回答不了最后那个问题，这一切是为了什么。我一直说构不可闭合，任何一套制度都是一个构，都会忽视一些东西，没有哪一套有资格当终点。资本主义容易出的毛病，是利润慢慢殖民了人的生活；现实中的共产主义容易出的毛病，是计划、集体和国家殖民了个人。机制不同，后果也不太一样，可倒置是同一种，原本为人设的目标变得不许追问，人却得无限适应。人说，这个节奏我受不了；制度说，那你要提高适应能力。人说，这不是我想过的日子；制度说，可目标不能改。

公道地说，马克思并非没看见人。《共产党宣言》里写着，每个人的自由发展是一切人的自由发展的条件；《资本论》第三卷讲自由王国，说人的能力的发展本身就是目的，缩短工作日是它的根本条件。1844年，年轻的马克思甚至直接借了康德的原话，说对宗教的批判最后归结为一条绝对律令：必须推翻使人被侮辱、被奴役、被遗弃、被蔑视的一切关系。所以问题不在他的愿望，在于宣称目的正确，和建一套不会背离目的的机制，是两件事。生产资料属于大家，大家怎样真的说了算？为人民服务，人民能不能对这份服务说不，而不被当成捣乱？二十世纪最惨痛的教训之一，恰恰是以解放为名的制度，回过头来支配了它要解放的人。

那目的王国是什么？这个词就是来自康德，指理性存在者在共同法则下的联合，每个人既服从法则，也是立法者。它最容易被误解成，将来大家终于有了同一个目的，一起奔过去。那只是一个更大的手段体系。目的王国的意思正相反，是许多目的谁也吞不了谁。有人创业，有人教书，有人想多陪孩子，有人需要一段不被动员的日子，冲突当然会有，要规则、要协商、要边界，可不能先把一些人降成障碍，再只算怎样让他们让路。

我在SAE制度论里写过，目的王国是方向，不是应当，也不是要验收的状态；方向有，终点开放，没有历史的保证。所以目的王国不是又一个等人加入的主义，也不是一张照着施工的蓝图，它给的是一套度量，任何制度，叫什么名字都行，都得拿来量一量，人在里面有没有被当成目的。具体到制度，我只要求一件事，人问不问是人的事，可他们若要问，构要让他们问得了，并且要答。要是哪天有人说，为了让你成为目的，你得按我画好的目的王国去活，那它就当场否定了自己。

再好的名字也挡不住滥用。纳粹党卫军中校艾希曼在耶路撒冷受审时说，他一生都按康德的道德律令行事，阿伦特指出他守的其实是第三帝国改过的那条绝对律令：“你的行为要让元首知道了也会赞成”。形式还在，立法的人被换成了元首。

而且“过渡”这两个字不能变成借口。为了将来人人都是目的，现在先让一些人当手段，这句话听着有理想，其实已经给眼前的手段化开了例外。后来的人活得再好，也还不回今天被牺牲的人失去的那一辈子。我在另一篇里给过一个检验办法，把宏大蓝图拿掉，看眼前这个人，今天还是不是被当成目的。“初级阶段”要是可以一直说下去，它就不再是一个阶段，是一个不必回答的回答。目的王国也不只是道德口号，没饭吃、看不起病、老了没着落的人，谈不上被当成目的；可只把人养好管好也不够，被照顾得再好、却不能提出异议的人，也只是被妥善安排的人。

现在AI来了，这件事会变得更紧迫。很多活机器做得更快更便宜，人作为手段的价值在往下掉。这可能是一个机会，马克思说自由王国的根本条件是缩短工作日，这第一次有了技术上的可能；也可能是另一条路，一个人没用了，制度就连把他当手段照顾的那份耐心都省了。1930年凯恩斯预言，一百年后人每周只要工作十五个小时。现在离他说的一百年（2030）还剩下四年，生产率早已涨了好几倍，工时却没跟着降下来；剩下这四年，AI也许真能让他说中，但也许只是让更多人连那十五个小时的活都找不到。人被当成手段的价值下降了，被当成目的的地位不会自己升上来，要看制度肯不肯让人问，肯不肯答。

所以真正要超越的，不是某一种主义，是“为了主义的成功，人可以被无限使用”的那套逻辑。最终方向不是让一种主义再也不被追问，而是让任何主义，都不能再取消人的追问。

text:
Google 发布 Gemini 4 Argon：Pro 和 Ultra 会员今天可用，API 每百万 token 输入 2 美元、输出 10 美元

Google 10 月 13 日发布 Gemini 4 Argon，这是 Gemini 4 系列的第一个模型，主打写代码、金融、法律、网络安全和科研这类需要很多步骤的复杂任务。系列里的其他模型，Google 说之后再推出。

【谁能用，在哪用】

普通用户：订阅了 Google AI Pro 或 Ultra 的，今天起可以在 Gemini App 和 Google 搜索的 AI 模式里用。免费用户暂时用不上。

开发者和企业：走 Gemini API 的付费层，入口是 AI Studio 和 Google Cloud 上的 Gemini 平台，Android Studio 里也能调用。API 免费层不提供这个模型。

Google 的 AI 编程工具 Antigravity 里也上了 Argon，个人用户要 Ultra 订阅才能用。

另有两个申请通道：科研人员可以申请 6 个月免费的 Antigravity 最高用量档，共 1 万个名额，按资格和容量筛选；做网络安全防御的团队可以申请加入 Google 的 Fairwind 计划，拿到去掉网络安全限制的版本。

【API 多少钱】

按每 100 万 token（模型处理文字的基本单位）计价。现在是引入价：输入 2 美元，输出 10 美元，输出包括模型思考时消耗的 token。重复使用的输入命中缓存，只收 5%，也就是 0.1 美元。

引入价只到 11 月 30 日。12 月 1 日起全部翻倍：输入 4 美元，输出 20 美元，缓存 0.2 美元。不急着要结果的任务可以走批量（Batch）或 Flex 档，价格是标准价的一半。官方定价页没有按提示词长度分档，输入再长也是同一个单价。

【100 万 token 统一上限是什么意思】

Argon 一次能处理 1,048,576 个 token，输入、思考和输出共用这一份额度。比如丢进去 60 万 token 的代码和文档，模型最多还能再产出约 44 万 token，思考也算在里面。

普通调用单次最多输出 65,536 个 token。要更长的结果，得按开发者文档改用“长输出”模式：请求设成后台任务，服务器每段生成约 6.4 万 token，接着上一段往下写，直到写完或者用完你设的上限，一个任务最长跑 24 小时。这是给让模型长时间自己推理、成批写代码准备的，普通聊天用不到。

文档还提醒，接力时每一段都会把前面的内容重新算进输入，用量报表里的输入 token 会比实际内容多出不少。这部分怎么计费，文档没写。

【跟别家比怎么样】

能独立核对的是第三方评测机构 Vals AI 的 Vals Index，它测模型在金融、写代码、法律、税务等工作上的表现。10 月 12 日更新的榜单上，Argon 以 68.90% 排第一，后面是 Anthropic 的 Claude Sonnet 5.5（67.04%）和 Claude Opus 5.5（66.97%），领先不到两个百分点。

其他成绩是 Google 自己公布的。比如测物理和空间理解的 ERQA 基准，Argon 得分 87%，Google 说高于其他所有前沿模型；在 Gray Swan 的提示词注入测试里（把恶意指令藏在网页、邮件中，诱导智能体干别的事），15 次针对性攻击的成功率降到 0.7%。

日常用的变化，Google 说 Argon 回答更直接，少了含糊其辞和重复，也更听从文风要求。这是跟自家旧版 Gemini 比的。

【实际用起来什么样】

以下都是 Google 自己的案例。

Google 开源的智能体开发框架 ADK 有约 20 万行 Python 代码。团队把项目里的规则文件和一段话的目标交给 Argon：在不破坏现有应用的前提下削减框架开销。Argon 自己跑了一夜，找出的优化已经合并进代码库，长会话下准备会话数据的时间缩短 40%，首次导入快了 21%。

Chrome 团队用它重构了 Chromium 的老代码。Chromium 有 4000 万行代码，其中一个约 600 万行的旧文件夹里混着各种浏览器功能，Argon 帮团队把核心的网页处理逻辑拆出来，改动涉及几百个文件，Google 说几个月的活几周干完。按 Google 的说法，这为网页在标签页、侧边栏和浮窗之间移动而不用重新加载打下基础，还能消除一整类崩溃。

Google 还说，内部工程师在 Antigravity 里用 Argon 后，智能体提交的代码量增加了 35% 以上，代码回滚少了近三分之一。

The AI infrastructure trade could be less about picking the winning model and more about owning what every model needs: power and memory

“I like power because you're going to need a bunch of power to basically run these data centers and cool them”

“I like memory because you're still need a lot of that to run, whether it's open source or closed source”

“I don't have to have a very precise opinion of where the token spend is going to happen”

“I just need to believe that there is going to continue to be a very persistent, durable demand for intelligence”

“Companies will want to have the best intelligence because the world only becomes more competitive from here”

“You can't afford not to spend in AI if you're a company of size”

@santiagoroel is drawn to the lower layers of the AI infrastructure stack, particularly power and memory.

Both are essential inputs across different AI models and architectures, giving investors exposure to the growth of AI without requiring a precise prediction about which model provider captures the most spending.

His thesis rests on the durability of demand for intelligence.

As AI agents become more capable, businesses face increasing pressure to improve their products, remove friction and adapt their business models.

For major technology companies, AI investment is becoming a competitive necessity. Falling behind could carry a much greater long-term cost than continuing to build the infrastructure needed to compete.

text:
*Post 1/12*  
I CANCELLED MY FUNERAL™  
CHAPTER 2: BARN, BLOOD, STARS  
by Ulyssesfve2™  

I came out of the barn dirty with blood 4:50am. Knife still in my hand. The air was cold, and the only sound was my own breathing and the drip of something I didn’t want to look at.  
I didn’t wipe it off. Didn’t care.  
I looked up at the stars and pointed the knife right at them.  
“Nothing’s gonna stop humanity from taking you,” I said. Stupid? Maybe 

*Post 2/12*  
I pointed that knife at the stars and made the promise like it was a contract.  
“Nothing’s gonna stop humanity from getting up there.”  
And I meant it.  
Not because I’d read it somewhere.  
I meant it because I was standing there, blood on my hands, pocket heavy with money I actually earned.  
From nothing.  
Building housing, climbing out of nowhere, sleeping in places you wouldn’t park a car.

*Post 3/12*  
If a guy like me could make it that far, then what’s stopping the rest of us?  
I felt it in my chest — the invisibility of the human spirit.  
How it bends but doesn’t break.  
My pocket was heavy. Coins and notes stuffed in the inside of my jacket, pressing against my ribs.  
Cash in hand, no bank, no mortgage, no 25 years of interest eating you alive.

*Post 4/12*  
Right in front of me was Baldur.  
The finest bull this area ever produced.  
He ran at me from the fields the way he always did, expecting feed, expecting me.  
I had to slaughter him.  
It’s not clean. The knife has to find the exact spot, and you have to commit. The blood came hot, fast, and it soaked into the dirt, into my boots.

*Post 5/12*  
There’s a smell to it — iron and earth and something primal that sticks in your nose for days.  
Money in the pocket, blood on the hands.And the worst part? It made sense.I was there when Baldur was born.
*3 AM*, freezing, cow on her side bawling, and me with my arm elbow-deep trying to turn him right so he wouldn’t die.

*Post 6/12*  
For the next 2 years I fed him, checked him, knew his limp before the vet did.  You name them even when you tell yourself not to.  
You talk to them when it’s 2 AM and you can’t sleep.But you’re not supposed to love livestock. That’s rule one. Love gets in the way of the ledger.

*Post 7/12*  
And then the clients start queuing up.  Not people. Hyenas. Smiling, “When’s it ready? How much for the cut? Supermarket is cheaper.” I’m collecting the money, counting it, feeling the notes stick together with sweat.And every note feels like 30 pieces of silver.

*Post 8/12*  
Because I’m the one who raised him.  I’m the one he ran to.  
And I’m the one turning that trust into cash.  By the gate.  
Seven guys who’d followed me through winters with no heating, summers where we slept in half-built houses.  They didn’t say anything when they saw me.  
Blood on my jacket, knife still in my hand, Baldur’s body behind me steaming in the cold.

*Post 9/12*  
They knew.  Generosity makes people uncomfortable when they’re the ones benefiting.  
Give a man a bonus when he expects minimum wage, and for 10 seconds he’s grateful.  After that, he starts wondering what you want from him.  But they still would’ve followed me to hell.  Because I’d bled with them.

*Post 10/12*  
The crew was quiet because they were already doing the math.  
About me.  When you stand there with cash in your pocket and a dead animal at your feet, people stop seeing a man.  They see a resource.  A faucet.  A threat.

*Post 11/12*  
The guy who’d carry you out of a fire yesterday is now wondering if you’ll cut his pay tomorrow.  
You understand that “human nature” isn’t about love and struggle.  It’s survival dressed up in morality.  People love you for what you give, hate you for what you keep, and betray you the second it costs them nothing.

*Post 12/12*  
I stood there and I asked, "God, what have I become?"
This is why men go quiet.  
End of Chapter 2

At an all-hands at the start of 2026 in Malta, I set the team a crazy challenge. A full-chain exploit of Chrome by the annual Black Hat cybersecurity conference in August.

I believed there were few better tests of whether @XBOW could move beyond web applications to desktop software, servers and devices.

Chrome is one of the most hardened pieces of software on the planet, used by more than half the world’s population.

A full-chain exploit lets an attacker take total control of a machine, where they can read every email, password and bank login the user types. You don’t need to download anything or click a phishing link. Visiting the wrong site is enough.

So @moyix, Andres Luksenberg, Baul Lee, and Willem Pinckaers took on the challenge along with a fifth teammate: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. 

They built a chain they thought would win, but Google told us they already knew one of the bugs. 

We were already in Las Vegas for Black Hat and DEF CON, and the team didn’t want to go home without the win.

So Brendan and the agents built a new exploit in just 6 days. 

We submitted it to Google and waited.

The news came through that we'd done what should’ve been impossible. A full-chain bounty of $250,000, the first awarded under Google’s 2026 rules.

It took just 6 days and $40,000 of compute to construct an exploit that affects a billion users of Chrome on Windows. An intelligence-agency veteran told me his team used to spend 6 months on this kind of vulnerability.

My takeaway: the cost of finding truly critical vulnerabilities is collapsing, for attackers and defenders alike. Restricting powerful models is not the answer; GPT-5.6 Sol is already public.

But defenders have one advantage attackers never will: they can test their own code first. 

Assume your software is exploitable. Whoever is hunting your bugs has the same building blocks we did.

This is cause for urgency but not panic.

XBOW is now developing an autonomous product for testing compiled software (desktop applications, servers, embedded devices), and partnering with the world’s top organizations to design that product. 

If you’d like to be one of them, get in touch. 

P.S. Restart Chrome whenever the Update button appears!

text:
At Box, we've been testing Gemini 4 Argon on our Box AI Complex Work eval for the past week. It's a huge upgrade over Gemini 3.1 Pro, jumping by 14 percentage points across all our tests, and firmly at the frontier. 

In our evaluation, we give the Box Agent (using Gemini 4 Argon) a variety of complex enterprise tasks involving enterprise documents in a range of industries. These tasks approximate the kind of hard, time-consuming work that knowledge workers do every day with their enterprise content. Gemini 4 is a huge leap on effectively every dimension of this work.

Gemini 4 is far more capable on math, logic, analytics, and deep knowledge of a variety of business domains. It also works far harder to complete tasks fully without stopping short of the desired result. This is incredibly important for complex enterprise workflows that depend on robust task execution.

Here are some example wins that we saw to put the improvements in perspective:

* Financial services (+18 points): a funding-gap analysis for a family-owned company, where the brief spelled out every step of the projected statements, down to the interest on the bank loan and the overdraft for each year. Gemini 4 Argon built them exactly as specified, every line broken out and carried through to the funding gap. Gemini 3.1 Pro folded the interest into a single figure.

* Healthcare (+25 points): an intensive care management plan where both models spotted a dangerous potassium level and a drug interaction. Only Gemini 4 Argon went back and pulled the offending drugs from the final regimen, so its plan actually matched its own diagnosis.

* Technology (+37 points): a product performance review deciding which of two regional markets should have its cloud infrastructure optimized first. Gemini 4 Argon pulled the right month's user, retention and per-user figures for both regions and correctly flagged North America. Gemini 3.1 Pro often pulled the wrong rows, at one point reporting retention above 100%, and pointed the effort at the wrong region.

* Energy (+16 points): an energy consumption report across two facilities that had to flag any gaps in the meter data. Gemini 4 Argon consistently caught that the data center's smart meter log stops in November. Gemini 3.1 Pro often missed it, at times declaring the logs complete.

* Consumer products (+33 points): a product launch evaluation deciding which production expansion to fund. Gemini 4 Argon saw that existing inventory could bridge an early capacity gap, which made the smaller expansion viable with an earlier launch and a faster break-even. Gemini 3.1 Pro defaulted to the larger expansion and the later timeline.

Gemini 4 Argon will be available in the Box AI Studio shortly for anyone to build custom Box Agents with.

text:
What does it look like when a personal brand gains motion?

Different for everyone, let’s walk through examples

A trader might earn respect for making great calls, while a musician earns that same respect for their creative ability. Both attract meaningful attention because of the reputations they’ve built within their respective communities.

Someone can become more respected within an existing community, break into entirely new ones or experience a sudden surge in attention that accelerates their rise.

Take @ishowspeedsui 

He started by building an audience through gaming streams, becoming known for his unpredictable personality and entertaining content.

Over time, his reputation carried him far beyond gaming. His relevance expanded into football, travel, music and mainstream entertainment, reaching audiences that might never have watched one of his streams.

In just a few years, he went from streaming in his bedroom to drawing thousands of fans into the streets around the world.

Next thing you know: https://t.co/f6fDTxJoRs

Now take @blknoiz06 

A crypto version of the same phenomenon. Ansem initially built his reputation as a trader, particularly through his conviction in Solana and his ability to identify emerging opportunities. His credibility attracted attention from people who valued his judgment.

Over time, his relevance expanded beyond trading. He became a recognizable personality within crypto culture, known not just for his market calls but for his participation in broader conversations, cultural moments, and events.

Next thing you know: https://t.co/4Y1KYFUUW9

Speed and Ansem followed different paths, but the underlying dynamic is the same.

Reputation earned in one community became the foundation for relevance in others.

It’s an important distinction. Personal brands don’t just grow by accumulating more attention. They grow by becoming increasingly relevant to more people, often for entirely different reasons.

Someone can deepen their reputation within a community, expand their relevance into new ones or do both.

The idea behind motion is to capture this rate and direction of change. Because the most interesting thing about a personal brand isn’t necessarily where they stand today. It’s where they’re going, how fast they’re getting there and why.

text:
$BORDR Fundamentals Are Strengthening, but the Next Stage Depends on Whether the Ecosystem Can Truly Gain Traction

6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr 

Bordrless's fundamentals have improved significantly. The changes go beyond adding a few features. The project is expanding from its own token standard, DEX, and launchpad into an open developer platform and an external trading distribution network.

What we can confirm so far is that product delivery and infrastructure development have made progress. However, the scale of the developer ecosystem, the actual trading growth generated by external integrations, and the long-term value capture of BORDR still need to be validated with data.

The most notable aspect of this update is that three developments are happening simultaneously: Axiom integration is live, the SDK and Workshop are lowering barriers to developer participation, and mainnet programs have added fee distribution and scripting capabilities. If these components work together, Bordrless could evolve from a technically differentiated launchpad into infrastructure that other projects actively use.

What Has Changed in This Update?

1. From Its Own Trading Interface to External Trading Distribution

Axiom has integrated the Bordrless Token Standard and DEX. According to the official team, all tokens launched on Bordrless can now be traded on Axiom while retaining the corresponding Hooks. This means trading is no longer limited to Bordrless's own website, and other trading terminals and aggregators are also planned for integration.

This is one of the most important changes in this update. It addresses product distribution rather than simply improving the interface. The more external trading entry points there are, the more opportunities launched projects have to reach traders. However, completing an integration does not guarantee significant additional trading volume. That still needs to be demonstrated through actual trading data.

2. From an Official Development Product to an Open Developer Ecosystem

The SDK allows developers to create custom Hooks, trading pools, and Bonding Curves. They can also add liquidity and use bridged assets as quote assets. Hooks can execute custom rules during token transfers and trading, such as taxes, holder rewards, transfer restrictions, or burns. Companions manage creator fees according to predefined schedules and rules, supporting functions such as market making and buybacks.

The team is also shifting the Studio development workflow toward developers building independently with AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Cursor, then submitting their work to the Workshop. The platform reviews, builds, simulates, and deploys approved projects. AI explains what the code does and how much it charges in plain language. Approved Hooks and Companions can then be selected by other token launchers, and developers can earn 50% of the creator fees generated by subsequent launches that use their configurations.

This means developers no longer have to be merely users of Bordrless products. They can become providers of ecosystem components. The real growth signal is not how many people download the SDK, but how many third-party tools pass review, get adopted by other launchers, and generate recurring revenue.

3. Mainnet Upgrades Are Improving Fee Distribution and Ecosystem Incentives

The mainnet upgrades announced by the team include the release of SDK 0.10.0; the ability for terminals, bots, and wallets to add integration fees of up to 1% to Bordrless trades they route; the ability to split a token's creator fees among up to 10 wallets at fixed percentages; scripts that can pay SOL to eligible wallets when the launcher enables the feature in advance; and the option for Workshop developers to publish their Hooks with a 0% fee.

These capabilities serve different purposes: monetizing trading entry points, splitting fees among project teams, automating on-chain payments, and encouraging developer participation. Creator-fee distribution and programmable scripts are particularly useful because they allow teams, treasuries, partners, and automated strategies to participate in a project's economic flows.

One distinction matters: integration fees collected by third parties do not automatically become BORDR revenue, and creator fees earned by developers are not equivalent to returns for token holders. These are initially economic mechanisms for the platform and ecosystem participants. They can indirectly benefit BORDR only if they generate revenue that the protocol can capture.

4. A Quick-Trade Panel and Builder Competition Improve User Experience and Incentivize Supply

The new web trading panel floats over the chart and combines buying, selling, preset amounts, estimated tokens received, and trading rules. Trading wallets can sign without an additional prompt. The goal is to let users trade directly while viewing market data and to prepare for future terminal integrations.

The team also announced a $5,000 Builder Race, with the top three projects receiving $2,500, $1,500, and $1,000 after 72 hours. The competition aims to attract early developers to build Hooks, Companions, and other tools, but the prize money itself does not prove that sustained ecosystem demand already exists.

Following these updates, the product's core positioning has become clearer. Bordrless is not just a launchpad. It is building its own token standard, DEX, and launchpad on Solana, allowing token rules to be executed through Hooks. The official documentation lists the mainnet programs and explains how they differ from Token-2022 transfer hooks.

External integrations are also beginning to address the distribution bottleneck. An in-house DEX can execute complex rules, but if tokens depend entirely on the project's own website, trader reach and liquidity may be limited. Axiom's integration demonstrates that external distribution is no longer entirely theoretical. The next question is whether other terminals and aggregators follow through and how much trading volume they bring.

Finally, developer incentives are becoming more complete. The SDK, AI coding agents, Workshop review and deployment, reusable Hooks, and creator-fee sharing are beginning to form a loop. In theory, developers have an incentive to build better trading rules and fee-management tools, while launchers can use those tools directly. The wider the adoption, the more fees developers can earn.

However, open development capabilities do not mean a developer network effect has already formed. Sustained third-party output, genuine adoption, and verifiable fee distributions are needed before this mechanism can be considered commercially validated.

Has BORDR's Value Capture Improved Alongside the Product?

A stronger product does not necessarily translate into proportionally stronger demand for its token.

According to the official Tokenomics documentation, half of protocol revenue is retained in the treasury for operating expenses such as development and deployment, while the other half is used to buy back BORDR every 10 minutes. The purchased tokens are bridged into the treasury and held; they are not burned. The team also states that buybacks are executed by an off-chain keeper operated by Bordrless. If the keeper stops, revenue remains in the treasury until processing resumes.

Current project metrics displayed on the Bordrless website:

Total launches: 93
Platform 24-hour trading volume: $222.50K
Displayed cumulative buybacks: $9.31K in BORDR
Cumulative fees from launch rules: 99.4 SOL

These figures indicate that the product is generating real trading activity, launch fees, and buyback activity rather than remaining a white-paper project. However, 93 launches are not enough to establish a strong network effect. The $9.31K in buybacks also needs to be evaluated against the token's market cap and future protocol revenue to assess its actual impact on supply and demand.

Protocol fees primarily come from LP fees on launch pools, launch fees, and protocol fees on regular DEX pools. The typical rules listed in the official documentation include a 0.3% LP fee on launch-pool trades, a 0.01 SOL fee per launch, and a 1% protocol fee on the quote-asset amount traded in regular pools.

Therefore, the important question is not how many new fee mechanisms are added, but whether external integrations can expand effective trading volume and consistently convert that activity into protocol treasury revenue and actual buybacks. The up-to-1% integration fee that terminals can charge belongs to the integrators; it does not all flow into the BORDR buyback mechanism.

What Is the Market Betting On?

I believe the market is primarily trading three narratives.

First, a programmable token standard on Solana.

Bordrless aims to make rules for taxes, rewards, burns, and holding restrictions take effect directly during token transfers or trading, rather than requiring each project to maintain its own off-chain scripts. This is its most important technical narrative relative to ordinary launchpads.

Second, ecosystem expansion driven by AI developers.

If developers can use AI coding agents to build their own Hooks, publish them through the Workshop, and have other launchers adopt them, the supply of ecosystem tools could grow rapidly. What the market may be pricing in ahead of time is the potential developer network, rather than developer revenue already realized today.

Third, a growth loop between external trading distribution and fee-based buybacks.

More terminal integrations could bring more trading. A wider range of tools could attract more launchers, increasing platform activity and revenue. The protocol's allocation of half its revenue to BORDR buybacks also creates a potential channel of demand linked to the platform's business.

Among these three narratives, the token standard already has tangible product support, the distribution network is only beginning to expand, and developer network effects and sustained revenue growth remain unproven.

What Could Become the Next Catalysts for Price Appreciation?

I believe the real catalysts would be:

More terminals and aggregators officially integrating. Axiom is already live, and the team has said more terminals and aggregators would integrate that week. Concrete integrations, trading volume generated by those integrations, and verifiable protocol revenue would be meaningful catalysts. Announcements alone are not enough.

Sustained adoption of third-party Hooks and Companions. SDK 0.10.0, the Workshop, developer-fee sharing, and the $5,000 Builder Race could encourage more participation. If more third-party tools are adopted by other projects and generate recurring developer revenue, the ecosystem narrative would gain further validation.

Companions and fee automation becoming fully operational. Managing creator fees through scripts could support automated market making, buybacks, and other on-chain strategies, allowing funds generated by launches to be actively deployed rather than sitting idle. However, some screenshots described Companion upgrades as “coming soon,” while official development documentation linked them to the October 12, 2026 program upgrade. Mainnet deployment and actual invocation records should be verified before treating the entire feature set as fully operational.

Sustained growth in protocol revenue and buybacks. This is the catalyst most directly connected to token value capture. If platform trading volume grows alongside treasury revenue and verifiable on-chain buyback amounts continue to increase, the market would have a stronger basis for valuing BORDR as an asset supported by business activity rather than just a technical narrative.

My conclusion is that this update represents a genuine improvement in fundamentals, but not yet completed commercial validation. Bordrless is moving beyond its programmable token standard and in-house DEX by adding external distribution, third-party development, fee automation, and ecosystem incentives.

The next stage depends on three things: whether other terminals bring incremental trading volume, whether third-party developers' tools achieve sustained adoption, and whether additional trading activity translates into recurring protocol revenue and buybacks.

If all three improve, stronger fundamentals could become a sustained catalyst for the token. If product announcements and downloads grow without corresponding adoption and revenue, market expectations may run ahead of reality.

Bordrless’s own Token Standard allows Hooks to define rules around fees, revenue distribution, burns, holder rewards, and holding-time-based mechanisms. The DEX also invokes these Hooks during trading, while the launchpad is part of the same system.

This means developers could theoretically design different tokenomics directly into their tokens, rather than relying entirely on external bots to execute buybacks, distributions, or burns. BORDR’s long-term potential lies in whether broader adoption could turn Bordrless from a launchpad into foundational infrastructure for programmable token economics on Solana.

There are two main recent catalysts.

Product modules are progressively going live. The website showcases components including the Token Standard, DEX, launchpad, bridge, and SDK. The team has also announced the launch of AI Studio and previewed upcoming features such as Hook Studio and Companions.

The developer ecosystem is taking shape. Open-source programs and SDKs lower the barrier to entry. The market is not simply betting on an individual token, but on the possibility that developers will use this infrastructure to create tokens with differentiated economic rules.

Together, these developments have encouraged the market to price in the possibility that Bordrless could become an infrastructure layer for a new generation of programmable tokens on Solana.

Fundamentals have improved, but mainly in terms of product maturity and the strength of the ecosystem narrative. Actual adoption remains at an early stage.

The website currently shows 21 launches and zero graduated projects, with approximately $110K in 24-hour trading volume, $26.8K in pool liquidity, and $1.12K in creator fees.

These figures show that the product is no longer purely conceptual, but they do not yet demonstrate that it can attract a large number of projects with sustained usage. In particular, the lack of graduated projects means long-term retention, successful launch case studies, and post-graduation trading depth still need to be proven.

BORDR’s price has also risen significantly, but the entire move cannot be attributed to any single product update. A more reasonable interpretation is that product development, developer tools, trading access, and KOL coverage have collectively strengthened market expectations. Determining the contribution of each factor would require a closer look at transaction-level data and the timeline of events.

Going forward, I will focus on three variables:

1. Hook Studio goes fully live. If developers can easily design, deploy, and share custom Hooks, Bordrless could evolve from a collection of in-house products into a broader developer platform.

2. Companions generates real usage. The team has described a mechanism through which creator fees flow into on-chain programs and are allocated according to predefined rules for buybacks, burns, holder distributions, or other purposes. If multiple projects generate meaningful trading activity through this system, that would be much stronger evidence than simply adding more features.

3. External projects adopt the standard consistently. The real inflection point is not another module going live. It is independent developers choosing to issue tokens using the standard and generating sustained trading volume, fees, and user demand.

There are two major risks.

First, product complexity may be running ahead of demand. Programmable tokens offer considerable technical flexibility, but ordinary issuers may not need such complex mechanisms. Without sufficient developer adoption, even a fully developed product may struggle to generate network effects.

Second, BORDR’s value capture has not been sufficiently established. Even if the Bordrless DEX, launchpad, and SDK grow, that does not mean all of this growth will translate into buying demand for BORDR. Its specific utility, revenue distribution model, and ability to generate sustained token demand still need to be verified.

Security is another consideration. The website states that the relevant programs retain upgrade authority pending completion of audits. For infrastructure responsible for token rules, fee distribution, and burns, this is a risk that deserves continued monitoring.

My conclusion is that the most meaningful change behind BORDR’s recent rally is its transition from the concept of a new Token Standard toward an infrastructure project with code, product modules, and developer tools. The market is betting on whether it can become a foundational layer for programmable token economics on Solana.

What will determine whether its valuation can expand further is not another explanation of how advanced Hooks are, but whether developer adoption, real trading activity, and BORDR’s value capture can grow together.

The fundamentals are moving in the right direction, but ecosystem scale and token value capture remain at an early stage.

text:
On Oct 2 a TRON user lost control of 5,102,539 TRX (~$1.7M). It took the attacker a month of social engineering and one command pasted into a terminal.

The funds are still on the victim's address, but he can't use them anymore. The attacker replaced the keys that control the account and is now waiting for the 14-day unstaking period to end on Oct 16 at 14:16 UTC.

How it started:

It started on Sep 1 with a Telegram message from an old contact from the mining hosting business. Their chat went back to 2021, so nothing looked off. The contact's account was most likely hacked.

After almost 5 years of silence he wrote "Long time no talk, how are you?" He sent a couple of friendly messages without asking for anything and then went quiet until Sep 28.

Next, on Sep 28 he apologized for the long silence, suggested a call and sent a link to a Google Calendar booking page for a "30 min chat".

On Oct 2 the victim asked to call a bit earlier and suggested Yandex Telemost. The attacker said he would send his own meeting link. It looked like https://t.co/zWBMjdSLFd.

On the phone the link opened a fake page saying the organizer didn't allow mobile access. "Try again on your laptop." So the victim moved to his laptop, where his wallet was.

On the laptop the page got stuck on "Joining the meeting...". The attacker wrote that Teams was having some issues. When the victim asked to switch to Yandex, he refused and said his partners were already working in Teams.

Around the same time the fake page showed a notice that the TeamsFx SDK had been deprecated, with a Copy button and instructions to press Win+R, type cmd, paste and hit Enter.

In the chat the attacker pushed the same thing. He asked "Did you update the SDK yet?", said he once had the same problem and an SDK update fixed it, and told him to paste the update command into the terminal. This is a ClickFix attack.

At first it didn't work because the victim kept pasting the command into the Win+R window and getting an error. The attacker sent screenshots showing where to find the terminal and wrote "Click here and type terminal". The command ran between 13:09 and 13:12 UTC, and the victim replied "seems to have worked".

After that the attacker kept him talking. He said he couldn't find him in the meeting, offered to move the call by a few hours and chatted about miners and regulation until 13:32 UTC. Then he went quiet.

About 40 minutes later things started happening on-chain.

At 14:13:24 UTC an AccountPermissionUpdate signed with the victim's key moved the owner and active permissions to the attacker's key. Since then the victim can't sign any transaction from his own address.

The attacker then revoked all delegated energy and unstaked the whole stake. Unstaked TRX can only be withdrawn after 14 days, so he has to wait.
555,688 TRX from Oct 16, 14:16:00 UTC
4,546,851 TRX from Oct 16, 15:13:30 UTC

Until then the 5.1M TRX stays on the victim's address and neither of them can move it.

The attacker also made a mistake. Changing permissions costs 100 TRX and the victim's address was about 28 TRX short. So 51 seconds before the takeover he sent 87 TRX there from another wallet, its whole balance. The two transactions were signed 42 seconds apart, which means whoever did the takeover also had the key to that wallet.

That wallet isn't new. It has been in use since April. It received payments and sent funds to exchanges that do KYC, and it's connected to a group of wallets active since 2020. He paid for the attack from a wallet with a history.

Victim's address, now controlled by the attacker:
TYYDe2Ca7fQapzZg2TZMCBXc3Xb4EbB3EZ

Attacker's key:
TEdNZQAw44xkw9b7KWpfL5SHdB3aLGWt6p

Takeover tx:
c608edc5b3ddfd6a15f82715edb3cb750aabb362a080d990cddfb5994f41ee05

If you run an exchange, swap service, bridge or OTC desk on TRON, please flag these.

A few more details about the attacker.

- The fake domain teans-lives[.]com was registered on Oct 1 at 05:53 UTC, about 31 hours before he sent the call link. It's on clientHold now.
- The fake Teams page with the "TeamsFx SDK" story is the same lure used in a campaign that was publicly linked to the North Korean group UNC1069 in April. This doesn't mean it's them, the lure is just the same.

To the attacker. You spent a month earning trust and now you're waiting for the unlock. You also paid for the takeover from a wallet with a history.

The whole chat, every screenshot you sent, your domain and every on-chain step are documented. The address is flagged in AML screening and shared with exchanges, swap services and bridges.

Red flags:
- an old contact suddenly comes back and wants a call
- the other side refuses your meeting link and insists on theirs
- a meeting page says mobile isn't supported and asks you to switch to a laptop
- any page asks you to paste a command into a terminal or Win+R

If you already ran something like this, assume the device is compromised and move funds from a clean one right away. In this case the attacker needed about an hour.

text:
Ro, thanks for the Wisconsin history lesson. You skipped the ending.

In 1911 Wisconsin's income tax started at 1% on income over $1,000, about $18,500 today. Most people paid nothing. It was sold as a tax on the few.

Today Wisconsin taxes working families starting at 3.5% and tops out at 7.65%. Washington copied the idea in 1913, and fewer than 10% of Americans paid it as late as 1939. Now it's in every paycheck.

That's the real lesson of 1911... a tax on "the few" is how you build the machine that taxes everyone.

And California already did this before... Prop 30 in 2012 was a "temporary" tax on high earners. Prop 55 extended it to 2030. Temporary in Sacramento means forever.

Now look at Prop 40...

A 5% grab on net worth, which means paper wealth and private company stock valued by a state formula, not money anyone actually made.

Written into the state Constitution, with a clause letting the Legislature amend it by a two-thirds vote if it "furthers the purposes" of the act.

"One-time" money for permanent health programs. When it runs out, guess who they come for next.

Even Gavin Newsom says it "makes no sense" and is "really damaging to the state." 

Larry Page, Sergey Brin and Peter Thiel didn't wait around to find out. The LAO warns the state loses income tax revenue every year after the ones who leave are gone.

And his chart makes the case against you... 5% "takes them back 31 days." So this wrecks California's reputation for capital, chases out the people who pay a huge share of the income tax, and doesn't even dent the "inequality" you claim to care about.

It's not innovative. It's the oldest socialist trick there is... promise it's only them, then come for you.

Vote NO on 40.

Anthropic 放弃行业通用的代码管理工具 Git，转而自己开发了一套名为 Scion 的新系统。

在 Anthropic 内部，AI（Claude）承担了大量的编程工作，写代码的速度远超人类。这导致每天需要合并保存的代码量暴增，从 5 月份的每天 2,500 次猛增到 9 月份的每天 30,000 次以上。传统软件开发中常用的 Git，原本是为人类工作习惯设计的，默认每个人都把整座代码仓库完整下载到自己的电脑上离线操作。随着代码库体积膨胀到几十吉字节（GB），数万次频繁操作让原有的网络和服务器彻底不堪重负。

面对这种瓶颈，Anthropic 决定彻底重构底层机制。他们只用了五个月时间，开发出专为 AI 时代设计的系统 Scion。这套新系统的核心逻辑主要有三点：

· 按需索取： 工作的大多是始终联网的 AI 智能体，不需要每次都把全部历史记录下载下来。系统只在需要某些文件时，才去服务器调取对应内容。
· 服务器挑大梁： 复杂、繁重的计算全部放在云端服务器完成，客户端只负责展示和简单缓存，极大地节省了本地机器的资源消耗。
· 更轻便的记录方式： 每次保存修改时，系统只记录改动的增量，不给整个代码库加锁，让上万个任务可以同时提交而互不堵塞。

这个项目本身也是 Anthropic 团队借助 AI 共同完成的。一支仅有 7 人的工程师团队，借助内部的 Claude 模型快速重写核心架构、自动排查漏洞，完成了以往大公司需要几倍人手和数年才能做完的工程。

Anthropic 的工程师认为，随着 AI 编程越来越普及，传统的软件协作工具都会面临类似的性能瓶颈。他们公开这些经验，是为了给整个软件行业提供参考，帮助大家提前做好应对海量 AI 代码的准备。

text:
This weekend I invented something new, a new type of token using Uniswap v4 hooks that I call a Pair Token.

A Pair Token is a new type of ERC-20. It is a fused, auto-compounding asset, a fusion of two tokens.

For example, the stock tokens NVDA and SPCX fused into a single tokenized version of the two, with the ticker NVDASPCX, or ETH with NVDA, creating ETHNVDA.

Each Pair Token represents a full-range Uniswap v4 liquidity pool.

So why mint these tokens?

These tokens are self-multiplying in terms of value, as at any moment anyone can call the compound function to compound the LP fees generated by the pair’s trading activity back into the asset.

The token represents a new financial primitive, as it represents a proportional value and moves as an LP position NFT would, except that it is auto-compounding and, thanks to its v4 hook, allows for compounding and self-growth.

Since it is an ERC-20, this token can be freely traded onchain, LPed, or even paired with a launchpad.

A new type of token for a new type of exposure and strategy.

Starting tonight, you’ll be able to mint or redeem Pair Tokens for any pair on Robinhood Chain via the StonkBrokers website.

Minting and redeeming are free, and the compounding process on the tokens incurs a 10% fee on the LP fees generated, which is used for $STONKBROKER buybacks.

I look forward to a new line of products and protocols on Robinhood Chain using this new financial primitive.

Only on Robinhood Chain, powered by Uniswap. @Hookrfun

quoted_text:
为什么我看好 $BORDR？因为它正在从一个代币，逐步走向 Solana 的基础设施。

真正让我看好 Bordrless 的，不只是它讲了什么故事，而是团队一直在持续交付。

从主网上线、DEX 发布，到 SDK 开放、无许可开发、Workshop 上线，再到 Axiom 集成落地，项目正在一步步把最初的构想变成真正可用的产品。

几个值得关注的进展：

• SDK 上线：让开发者能够基于协议构建自己的应用。

• Workshop 推出：开发者可以提交自定义 Hooks，并分享创作者费用收益。

• Companions 上线：支持链上创作者费用分配与回购自动化。

• DEX 与代币标准开放：让更多外部开发者参与构建 Bordrless 生态。

• Axiom 集成落地：这是一个重要进展，意味着交易不再局限于 Bordrless 自己的网站，相关代币可以通过外部交易终端进行交易，同时保留协议的 Hooks 功能。

• 持续升级主网：最新进展还包括多项功能更新、公开源码的可验证构建、SDK 发布，以及最高 1% 的集成费用机制，让终端、机器人和钱包有机会通过路由 Bordrless 交易获得收益。

这条发展路线很值得关注：

构建协议 → 产品上线 → 开放基础设施 → 吸引开发者 → 接入交易平台 → 建立集成激励。

这才是我真正关注的地方。

我看涨 $BORDR 的核心逻辑，并不是单纯押注一个热门叙事，而是押注它能否成为 Solana 可编程代币生态背后的经济层。

如果未来越来越多的代币发行、交易、Hooks、开发者工具、交易终端和应用接入 Bordrless，那么协议就有机会获得更多使用量，并形成更完整的经济循环。

根据项目公布的代币经济模型：

总供应量为 10 亿枚，团队称不会额外增发。
50% 的协议收入进入金库。
另外 50% 用于回购 BORDR，项目方称回购每 10 分钟执行一次。

如果这些机制能够持续运行，并且真实交易量和协议收入不断增长，那么回购机制的价值才有机会逐步体现。

当然，技术交付不等于商业成功，集成上线也不等于大规模采用。 后续仍需要观察真实交易量、协议收入、开发者增长、集成留存，以及回购机制的实际执行情况。

但对一个仍处于早期阶段的项目来说，我更愿意关注那些持续交付、开放技术并努力建立生态经济模型的团队。

Bordrless 已经展示出从协议到产品、从产品到集成的推进路径。

接下来真正值得期待的是：它能否让更多开发者和交易平台主动选择这套基础设施。

如果这个方向最终跑通，$BORDR 的想象空间就不只是一个 Meme 币的涨跌，而是整个生态能否持续创造价值。

我会继续关注，也期待下一阶段的交付。

$BORDR #Solana #Crypto

This weekend I invented something new, a new type of token using Uniswap v4 hooks that I call a Pair Token.

A Pair Token is a new type of ERC-20. It is a fused, auto-compounding asset, a fusion of two tokens.

For example, the stock tokens NVDA and SPCX fused into a single tokenized version of the two, with the ticker NVDASPCX, or ETH with NVDA, creating ETHNVDA.

Each Pair Token represents a full-range Uniswap v4 liquidity pool.

So why mint these tokens?

These tokens are self-multiplying in terms of value, as at any moment anyone can call the compound function to compound the LP fees generated by the pair’s trading activity back into the asset.

The token represents a new financial primitive, as it represents a proportional value and moves as an LP position NFT would, except that it is auto-compounding and, thanks to its v4 hook, allows for compounding and self-growth.

Since it is an ERC-20, this token can be freely traded onchain, LPed, or even paired with a launchpad.

A new type of token for a new type of exposure and strategy.

Starting tonight, you’ll be able to mint or redeem Pair Tokens for any pair on Robinhood Chain via the StonkBrokers website.

Minting and redeeming are free, and the compounding process on the tokens incurs a 10% fee on the LP fees generated, which is used for $STONKBROKER buybacks.

I look forward to a new line of products and protocols on Robinhood Chain using this new financial primitive.

Only on Robinhood Chain, powered by Uniswap. @Hookrfun

quoted_text:
1/ ASMR Research Preview

Bittensor subnets in aggregate (the YCX index) have substantially lower volatility than the S&P 500. The likely driver is large-cap subnet tokens having greater liquidity (quoted in $TAO) relative to their size than many S&P 500 index members.

Market discussions often start with the assumption that more liquidity is better. Yuma’s research, recently presented at @Exploitsummit, demonstrates how excess liquidity can suppress price discovery, obscuring quality and risk information from capital allocators. Key slides from the presentation follow in this thread.

This work is shared as research for public discussion and it explores a solution we’re calling ASMR: Alpha Subnet Market Reloaded.

text:
Gavin Baker 今天发了一篇长帖，直接回应最近 AI 市场最让人不安的几个问题：Anthropic 丢份额，模型价格越打越低，融资越来越贵，几千亿美元的算力承诺到底谁来付？

他的答案相当鲜明：开放模型、前沿实验室、基础设施、应用公司，都有机会赢。这个未来，也可能比两家模型公司包揽一切，对普通人更好。

先介绍一下他是谁。Gavin 是 Atreides Management 的管理合伙人兼 CIO，之前在 Fidelity 工作了 18 年，曾管理 Fidelity OTC Portfolio，也参与推动其风险投资业务。他最早做分析师时就覆盖半导体，后来同时投资上市公司和私人科技公司。

所以他看 AI，会把模型、芯片、云、企业客户和融资放在同一张账里算。模型公司今天少赚一点，供应商明天可能多接几笔订单；一个产品份额下降，也未必代表整个市场缩小。这是他这篇长帖的出发点。

先想想，如果未来只剩 OpenAI 和 Anthropic，会发生什么？

面对应用开发者，它们掌握模型和价格；面对云厂商，它们又是最大的采购客户。你做产品，要向它们买智能；你建机房，要争取它们的订单。上下游都得跟这两家谈条件。

采购规模足够大之后，它们还能要求更低的算力价格，甚至逐渐自己做芯片、自己建基础设施。供应商今天最重要的客户，往后可能变成竞争对手。应用公司也会担心：我花一年做出来的功能，会不会被它们下一次更新顺手覆盖？

这样的结局，两家公司的股东可能很开心，其他人的利润就难留了。

Gavin 因此更愿意看到模型竞争加剧，尤其是开放权重模型起来。企业可以自己部署，开发者可以换供应商，推理云可以服务更多客户。算力生意的买方名单变长，大客户就更难把整个供应链的价格压在手里。

模型公司打价格战，为什么算力供应商可能受益？

这也是 AI 和传统软件差别很大的地方。

传统软件开源之后，别人复制一份，新增成本可以很低。AI 模型权重可以免费下载，但每运行一次，仍然要占机器、耗电、用内存。模型公司的收费被竞争压下去了，底下的运行成本仍然得有人付。

拿一笔简化的账来说：假设完成同一项任务，底层算力成本都是 $1。闭源服务卖 $5，另一家基于开放模型的服务卖 $2。同样 $100 的预算，用户原来做 20 次，现在能做 50 次。如果预算继续用完，底层算力消耗反而从 $20 增到了 $50。

这就是 Gavin 那段单位经济学计算的意思。他把闭源服务较高的推理毛利，与开放模型服务较低的加价放在一起比较，想说明：终端收费下降，可以让同一笔预算买到更多 AI，也消耗更多算力。

具体到不同模型，Token 成本并不相同，模型大小、推理深度、上下文长度和部署方式都会影响成本。所以这是一笔解释机制的账。它能否变成真实需求，要看便宜之后，用户究竟多用了多少。

而 AI 恰好有很多“降价之后才值得做”的工作。

以前只抽查一小部分客服对话，现在全部分析；以前合同太多，人工挑重点看，现在每一份都处理；以前问一次模型，拿到答案就结束，现在让 Agent 连续尝试、检查、修改，直到把任务完成。

价格高的时候，这些需求藏着。价格降下来，才会变成订单。

前沿模型会不会因此被开放模型打死？我倾向于不会这么简单。

未来企业很可能同时使用几类模型。

高频、重复、要求明确的任务，交给便宜的专用模型；复杂规划、难题和最后审核，交给最强的前沿模型。一个贵但聪明的模型，可以指挥一群便宜模型执行。用不着每个小动作都让最贵的模型亲自完成。

Gavin 提到的企业后训练，也是这条路：拿开放模型，加上自己的私有数据和业务经验，做出更适合本公司的版本，再通过路由，把不同任务分给不同模型。

一家处理特定合同的公司，并不需要每次都购买模型全部的通用能力。它更需要熟悉自己的条款、格式、审批流程，而且稳定、便宜。专用模型未必在通用排行榜上第一，却可能在这项工作上更合适。

因此，开放模型拿走大量 Token，前沿实验室仍然在最难的任务上收取溢价，两种生意可以同时成立。份额下降，也可能发生在收入仍然高速增长的时候——只要整个市场长得更快。

对应用公司来说，多模型也提供了更多选择。可以换供应商，可以组合模型，可以自己优化成本。不过，单纯在 API 外面套个界面的产品，日子仍然不好过。模型能力往前走，简单功能很容易被吸收。客户的数据、工作流程、权限和最终交付，会越来越影响一家公司能留下多少钱。

再看那笔吓人的 Anthropic 合同承诺。

约 4,130 亿美元，光看总数，很容易产生一种感觉：这么大一张账单，怎么付得起？

Gavin 把它拆成了两部分：多年云服务合同，折算后每年约 310 亿美元；另外约 1,610 亿美元是 Broadcom 相关设备租赁义务，需要单独安排融资。报道中的云合同期限确实延伸到 2033 年、2036 年，不能把多年总额当成今年要一次性付清的钱。

这里也得分清 MOU 和正式合同。一个宣布合作方向的意向，和一份不花够也可能需要补差额的合同，对资产负债表的影响完全不同。不能看见“承诺”就全算成马上要付的债，也不能因为付款跨多年，就当它没有约束。

Gavin 认为，按 Anthropic 当前的收入规模，年度云支出有能力通过经营收入覆盖。但我会继续看现金：ARR 是把当前收入速度年化，公司实际收进多少钱，扣掉训练、人员和其他成本后还剩多少，才决定付款能力。

Broadcom 提供最高 420 亿美元融资额度，说明供应商参与融资已经在发生。它能缓解眼前的现金压力，但融资仍然要偿还，部分违约情形也可能让付款义务提前到期。

所以这笔账比标题看起来更有时间安排，也比“收入够大就没事”复杂。

云厂商可能还藏着一段收入增长。

Gavin 的判断是，2024、2025 年签下的一批算力合同，价格已经低于现在的市场水平。等这些合同到期，算力有机会按更高价格重新出租，云和新型云厂商的收入、现金流就会改善。

可以理解成一栋楼：早几年便宜租给大客户，如今周围租金涨了，但旧租约没到期，收入还没有完全反映新价格。

如果未来续约价格提高，利用率又维持住，机房就能拿更多经营现金继续扩建，减少对外部融资的依赖。这是他认为“外部融资占扩建比例可能接近峰值”的原因。

但这条路能不能走通，得看合同到期时的市场。客户还愿不愿意付高价？旧设备还有没有竞争力？算力能不能按原来的条件转售？今天新卡报价高，和几年后旧卡还能收多少租金，是两笔不同的账。

他还引用了一组 B200 集群测算：即使租金每年下降 40%，项目仍可能做到 37% 的内部收益率。这样的回报如果经得起成本、利用率、设备寿命和融资条件的检验，当然会吸引资金。但它是项目模型里的回报，不能直接拿来当股票持有收益。

帖子里接近 $100/W 的 Blackwell 集群竞标，与此前 $50/W 的 Google／SpaceX 交易对照，也是在强调买方争夺算力的力度。不过这些报价要把合同期限、交付时间和服务范围对齐，才能比较，更不能直接当成利润。

他最后关于“慢一点”的观点，我觉得需要认真想。

电力、晶圆、燃气轮机、资本，现在都不能无限供应。这些短缺让项目排队，也迫使资金挑客户、挑地点、挑回报。设备分批上线，收入就有时间追上支出。

如果钱几乎免费，设备随叫随到，大家都按照最乐观的需求曲线同时扩建，反而更容易出问题。需求确实增长，供应却增长得更快，最后租金掉下去，买设备借的钱还留在原地。

这类生意最残酷的地方就是：你可能看对了行业需求，仍然亏掉股东的钱。

所以我认同，有节奏的扩建，可能比一口气冲到最大产能更健康。但放缓也有不同原因。设备交付慢一点，和客户突然没钱付账，不能放在一起庆祝。我们得分清，是供给被约束，还是需求已经退了。

Gavin 认为近期更大的风险之一，是严重网络安全事件突然打断采用和投资。他同时看好 AI 防御能力的进步。这仍然是他的判断，技术发展快，并不代表事故不会先发生。

他对多模型未来的支持，还涉及普通人的选择权：不要让少数几个人决定所有人能用什么 AI、接受什么规则。更多模型意味着可以换、可以自己部署，也更容易找到适合自己需求的工具。企业如此，个人也是。

我对接下来的判断是：模型会越来越像一组可以组合、替换的工具。前沿实验室争取最难任务的溢价，开放模型进入大量日常工作，应用公司把工具接进实际业务，基础设施承接不断增加的调用。

真正需要跟踪的，是这几层之间的钱有没有流通起来。

模型便宜后，客户是否真的多用了？买算力的名单有没有变长？机房的租金和利用率有没有变成现金？新增供应会不会超过新增需求？

Gavin 说“大家都可以赢”，讲的是一种可能的行业结局。落实到投资，每家公司仍然得单独算账。

排行榜可以每周换第一。机房的电费、设备折旧和贷款利息，每个月都得付。
