text:
前一段 Loop Engineering 不是很火么，不过真做好的也不多。

知名开源开发者 yetone 在 X 上公开了他维护 Magpie 的工作流：用 Claude Code 加官方的 Opus 5.5 模型，同时开 3 个 /loop 循环任务，让 AI 自己盯 GitHub issue 和 PR、Discord 社区和推特反馈，修 bug、加功能、发版、回复用户。他自己每晚抽一点时间“铲铲屎”，主要处理 UI/UX 问题，“然后就没活儿了”。

他自己说这套流程“没有任何的魔法，甚至还特别简陋”。

【3 个循环任务分别干什么】

/loop 是 Claude Code 自带的命令，让同一段提示词反复执行；不写间隔时，由模型自己决定多久跑一次。这个命令 Codex 也支持，其他的我没测试，估计也差不多。

yetone 截图里的 3 段提示词都没写时间间隔，我自己去 Codex 跑了一下，默认是 1 小时。

简单解释一下他这三个循环。

第一个循环：管 GitHub 和 Discord。

指令要求 AI 盯 GitHub issue，判断哪些值得修、值得做；修完要发版并回复提问的人，不值得做的也要回复。有一类 issue 单独规定了统一话术：如果是“中转站”来打广告，统一回复“感谢关注，日后会出相关合作方案，敬请期待”，不能直接把第三方中转站加进产品。

对 PR，指令要求逐行看代码、看逻辑，再把代码拉下来实际跑一遍，确认没有 bug 才能合并，否则回复或关掉。指令里写了原因：“我怕有的人提的 PR，是无脑用 Coding Agent 乱写的，自己都没测过。”

指令还要求 AI 实时盯 Magpie 的 Discord 服务器，所有频道一个不漏，有价值的反馈就去修或加功能，值得讨论就继续讨论。最后专门叮嘱：在 Discord 里要真正 @ 到人，只写名字对方收不到通知。

第二个循环：管 X/推特 的用户反馈。

盯推特上关于 Magpie 的反馈，有价值的建议或能复现的 bug 就去做，上线后回复那条推文。这段指令要求先用便宜的“决策模型”，比如 Jev，判断推文是不是在说 Magpie、是不是反馈，不相关的直接丢掉，别转给主模型，“不然太浪费 Token 了”。

【注：Jev 是 TypeSafe AI 推出的模型，只做判断题、选择题和打分，输出概率或分数，不生成文字。官方定价是每百万输入 Token 0.042 美元，输出免费。】

顺便说一下，如果你的产品名或者要关注的事比较稀有，不一定需要 Jev，他之所以加，是因为 magpie 在英文里是“喜鹊”，按关键词抓推文会抓到大量无关内容，全丢给 Opus 判断很费钱。

第三个循环：清理和总结。

这段指令开头写着“现在 magpie 完全是自动化更改代码和合并社区里的 PR”，要求 AI 定期清理“屎山代码”和恶意代码，防止项目变得难以维护；同时把经验教训写下来，比如哪些 PR 不该合、哪些验证不够严密，留给以后的 AI 参考，避免重复犯错；还要把总提交低质量代码的人拉进黑名单。

【作者补充的两点】

发完截图后，他在两条回复里补了两点。

一是给 AI 真实的运行环境。他准备了一台 Mac 和一台 Windows 电脑，再在 Windows 上开一个 Linux 虚拟机，三个系统的复现环境就齐了。AI 每次都要在这三端真实复现 bug，再去修。

二是 AI 怎么做出符合他心意的决策。他说靠的是 Claude Code 的记忆系统和仓库里的设计文档。开发 Magpie 之初，他和 Claude Code 讨论、头脑风暴了很多内容，这些都被记进了记忆文件。之后遇到要拍板的事，或者涉及审美偏好的设计，AI 会参考这些记录，做出跟他比较一致的选择。

【总结下】

他把维护项目的日常活拆成了 3 条流水线，每条只管一个入口（GitHub、推特、代码库本身），各自循环。人只留下 AI 做不好的部分，也就是 UI/UX 的审美判断。

当然要跑起来得有几个前提：
1. AI 能在真实的三端环境里跑代码，验证结果靠实际运行；
2. AI 手里有他早期写下的偏好和设计文档，知道他会怎么选；
3. 犯过的错被写成经验，下一轮的 AI 能读到。

提示词都是大白话，篇幅主要花在边界情况上：不值得修也要回复，中转站广告怎么回，Discord 要真 @，不相关的推文别浪费 Token。

有几个特别要注意的点：

1. 先把验证环境搭好，再让 AI 干活。AI 改完代码说“修好了”没用，要能在出问题的那个系统上跑一遍。你的项目只跑在网页或服务器上，一个容器可能就够；要多端的，就像他一样把每一端都备齐。

2. 在提示词里写清楚“遇到这种情况怎么办”。他的三段指令里，大部分字数花在例外处理上。你让 AI 自动回复用户之前，先想想会有哪些奇怪的来信，提前定好处理办法。

3. 用便宜模型挡在前面。先用一个几乎不要钱的分类模型过滤一遍，只把真正的反馈交给贵模型，这个做法几乎任何监听类任务都能用。

4. 让 AI 自己总结教训。第三个循环要求把“不该合的 PR”“验证不严的地方”记下来，下次的 AI 读到就会更谨慎。这相当于给 AI 建立了一个自我迭代优化的循环。

5. 项目早期多花时间和 AI 聊设计。他说 AI 后来能按他的偏好做决策，依赖的是开发初期那些讨论被记进了记忆和设计文档。想让 AI 少问你，就先把你的想法写下来让它记住。

仅供参考，重要的是学习思路，不必一模一样的照搬。

This weekend I invented something new, a new type of token using Uniswap v4 hooks that I call a Pair Token.

A Pair Token is a new type of ERC-20. It is a fused, auto-compounding asset, a fusion of two tokens.

For example, the stock tokens NVDA and SPCX fused into a single tokenized version of the two, with the ticker NVDASPCX, or ETH with NVDA, creating ETHNVDA.

Each Pair Token represents a full-range Uniswap v4 liquidity pool.

So why mint these tokens?

These tokens are self-multiplying in terms of value, as at any moment anyone can call the compound function to compound the LP fees generated by the pair’s trading activity back into the asset.

The token represents a new financial primitive, as it represents a proportional value and moves as an LP position NFT would, except that it is auto-compounding and, thanks to its v4 hook, allows for compounding and self-growth.

Since it is an ERC-20, this token can be freely traded onchain, LPed, or even paired with a launchpad.

A new type of token for a new type of exposure and strategy.

author: blast
quoted_text:
Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

列治文市长候选人Alexa Loo（卢仙泳）：

选举期间自诩为华人，在其市议员任内却向我们展示了完全相反的另一面！

以下不是传闻，而是有新闻采访及市议会正式会议记录支持的四件事。

① 2017 年：支持强制商户招牌至少 50% 使用英语或法语

2017 年 6 月，列治文市议会讨论规定未来商业招牌至少 50% 使用加拿大官方语言。

Alexa Loo 公开支持。

然而，华裔居民 Tung Chan、Vinnie Yuen、Minghui Yu 等人在市议会提出反对意见，质疑这一规定的必要性、公平性及对语言自由的限制。

市议会最终投票删除强制语言比例条款。

Alexa Loo 与 Carol Day、Harold Steves 投票反对删除该条款。

这是有正式投票记录的政策分歧。

对依赖华语顾客的小商户而言，这种规定可能意味着额外制作成本，以及更少的招牌语言选择。

官方证据：
https://t.co/UIMPCsD4io

② 2016 年：支持公交候车亭广告至少 50% 使用英语

列治文与广告公司 Pattison Outdoor 的合同要求，公交候车亭内的外语广告至少 50% 使用英语。

Alexa Loo 公开表示支持，认为公共设施上的广告应该让更多居民看得懂。

支持者认为这能改善不同语言群体之间的信息交流。

但对主要使用中文宣传的商户而言，这也意味着广告设计必须服从特定语言比例，而不能完全根据目标顾客决定。

值得注意的是，Loo 当时也承认，对私人商户招牌限制语言可能涉及《加拿大权利与自由宪章》的问题。

新闻证据：
https://t.co/VFQFhGEwuy

③ 2018 年：提出加强按摩场所经营监管

2018 年 12 月 17 日，列治文市议会 General Purposes Committee 会议记录中，明确列出由 Alexa Loo 提出的按摩行业监管议题。

记录指出，Loo 讨论了通过修改条例，使按摩场所经营更加困难的可能性。

随后，委员会通过动议，要求工作人员审查现有条例并提出建议。

原始议程涉及人口贩运和洗钱等监管关切，因此不能将其简单描述为针对华裔商户。

但是，合法经营的按摩服务提供者是否会面临额外成本？如何确保执法不影响守法的小企业？

这些都是值得询问的问题。

官方证据：
https://t.co/YfcU5OqiIF

④ 2024 年：主持通过要求部分商户不能只收现金的初步动议

2024 年 11 月 13 日，Alexa Loo 担任主席的 Community Safety Committee 通过一项动议：
要求市府起草规定，让从事特定商业活动的商户除了现金，还必须接受其他付款方式。

对于习惯现金交易的小商户，这可能带来刷卡手续费、终端设备及行政成本。

不过，需要说明：正式会议记录没有确认 Loo 本人是这项动议的提案者。

而且，11 月 25 日市议会将方案改为先咨询商户和监管机构，研究现金交易涉及的潜在问题，并没有直接通过强制电子支付的法规。

This weekend I invented something new, a new type of token using Uniswap v4 hooks that I call a Pair Token.

A Pair Token is a new type of ERC-20. It is a fused, auto-compounding asset, a fusion of two tokens.

For example, the stock tokens NVDA and SPCX fused into a single tokenized version of the two, with the ticker NVDASPCX, or ETH with NVDA, creating ETHNVDA.

Each Pair Token represents a full-range Uniswap v4 liquidity pool.

So why mint these tokens?

These tokens are self-multiplying in terms of value, as at any moment anyone can call the compound function to compound the LP fees generated by the pair’s trading activity back into the asset.

The token represents a new financial primitive, as it represents a proportional value and moves as an LP position NFT would, except that it is auto-compounding and, thanks to its v4 hook, allows for compounding and self-growth.

Since it is an ERC-20, this token can be freely traded onchain, LPed, or even paired with a launchpad.

A new type of token for a new type of exposure and strategy.

quoted_text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

text:
I’m French. I want to talk to Americans who are about to vote Democrat. Not to insult you. To warn you.

I come from your future.

In France we did everything your progressive politicians promise. Free healthcare, free college, generous welfare, strong unions, heavy regulation, high taxes on the rich, a state that takes care of everything. Public spending close to 57% of GDP, one of the highest on the planet. On paper, it’s the dream.

Here’s what it looks like from the inside. France hasn’t passed a balanced budget since 1974. Our debt is above 3,300 billion euros. Interest on that debt is becoming one of the biggest items in the national budget. Our hospitals are collapsing despite record funding. Our schools rank lower every year. Young people with degrees can’t afford an apartment in the city they were born in. Our best engineers leave for London, Zurich and San Francisco. And the rich you wanted to tax? They left too, and took the jobs with them.

The promise was protection. The result is stagnation.

The worst part is that nobody in France voted for decline. Every single step sounded generous, compassionate, reasonable. One more program. One more regulation. One more tax to fund it. Each step alone makes sense. Fifty years of them, and you wake up in a country that can no longer build a nuclear plant on time or keep its streets safe.

I love America because it’s the one place on earth where people still believe they can build something from nothing. I came to Silicon Valley as a self-taught kid and it changed my life. That spirit is the most precious thing your country has.

Before you vote, ask yourself one question: is the program you’re voting for making America more like America, or more like France?

Trust me. You don’t want to be France.

Je n'ai jamais été aussi optimiste. Pas malgré le chaos actuel, mais grâce à lui.

Je vais vous expliquer pourquoi l'empire du mensonge construit par la gauche depuis cinquante ans va s'effondrer, et pourquoi ce n'est pas une opinion mais une question de physique.

Tout commence avec un mouvement né sur X il y a quelques années : l'effective accelerationism, ou e/acc.

Au départ, c'est une idée presque thermodynamique. L'univers a une tendance de fond : la matière s'organise pour capter et dissiper l'énergie de plus en plus efficacement. Une cellule fait ça. Une forêt fait ça. Une civilisation fait ça. Le marché, la technologie et le capital sont les formes les plus avancées de ce processus. Ce sont des machines à transformer l'énergie en intelligence, en abondance, en complexité.

La thèse e/acc est simple : il ne faut pas freiner cette dynamique, il faut l'embrasser. Plus d'énergie, plus de calcul, plus d'innovation, plus de croissance. Monter sur l'échelle de Kardashev au lieu de s'excuser d'exister. En face, il y a les « décels » : ceux qui veulent ralentir, réguler, taxer, interdire, culpabiliser. Ceux qui voient le progrès comme une menace à contenir plutôt qu'une force à libérer.

Mais il y a une dimension de l'accélération dont presque personne ne parle. L'accélération n'est pas seulement un moteur. C'est un filtre.

Pensez à n'importe quel organisme. Un corps humain en bonne santé peut courir. Il accélère, son cœur pompe plus fort, ses muscles consomment plus d'oxygène, et tout fonctionne parce que le système est bien conçu. Maintenant, prenez un corps malade. Des artères bouchées, un cœur fragile, des organes qui ne communiquent plus entre eux. Faites-le courir. Il ne va pas plus vite vers la santé. Il va plus vite vers l'infarctus.

L'accélération ne corrige pas les défauts d'un système. Elle les amplifie. Un système sain qui accélère devient plus fort. Un système dysfonctionnel qui accélère meurt plus vite.

Et c'est exactement ce qui est en train d'arriver au projet que je vais appeler par son nom : le projet globalo-socialiste. Celui porté par les démocrates américains, par la technostructure de Bruxelles, par les entités supranationales qui n'ont de comptes à rendre à personne, par un réseau d'ONG financées par l'argent public pour dicter la morale aux peuples qui les financent.

Regardez ce que ce projet a produit.

Des États obèses qui prélèvent plus de la moitié de la richesse produite et qui délivrent des services publics de plus en plus dégradés. Des écoles qui n'apprennent plus à lire mais qui apprennent à culpabiliser. Des hôpitaux à bout de souffle malgré des budgets records. Une immigration massive sans aucune exigence d'assimilation, présentée comme une chance par ceux qui n'en subissent jamais les conséquences. Une désindustrialisation organisée au nom d'une écologie punitive qui délocalise la pollution en Chine et l'emploi avec. Des normes, des normes, et encore des normes, jusqu'à ce qu'il devienne plus simple de créer une entreprise à Austin qu'à Lyon. Une justice qui excuse le coupable et soupçonne la victime. Une censure qui avance masquée sous le nom de « lutte contre la désinformation ». Et une jeunesse à qui l'on a expliqué que son pays, son histoire et sa civilisation étaient des crimes à expier.

Ce n'est pas un ensemble de bugs. C'est la conception elle-même.

Maintenant, changeons d'image. Voyez ce système comme un moteur.

Un bon moteur, c'est de la précision. Des pièces qui s'emboîtent, un minimum de frottements, une énergie qui se transforme en mouvement. Le marché libre, la propriété, la responsabilité individuelle, la monnaie saine : c'est ça, un moteur bien conçu. L'information circule par les prix, chaque erreur est sanctionnée, chaque bonne idée est récompensée.

Le moteur socialiste, lui, est mal conçu dès le départ. Il ne tourne pas sur la création de valeur mais sur sa redistribution. Il ne récompense pas la performance, il la taxe. Il ne laisse pas les erreurs mourir, il les subventionne. Résultat : ça frotte partout. Ça chauffe. Ça grince. Chaque pièce use la pièce d'à côté.

Et que font ceux qui pilotent ce moteur ? Au lieu de le reconcevoir, ils changent les pièces. En permanence. Une pièce cède, on en remet une neuve. Encore une. Encore une.

Ces pièces de rechange, vous les connaissez. Elles s'appellent la dette publique et la planche à billets.

La France a dépassé les 3 300 milliards d'euros de dette et n'a pas voté un budget à l'équilibre depuis le milieu des années 70. Les États-Unis ont franchi les 37 000 milliards de dollars. Les banques centrales ont maintenu des taux à zéro pendant des années, imprimé des montants que plus personne ne sait se représenter, et quand l'inflation est arrivée, elles ont fait semblant d'être surprises. Milton Friedman l'avait pourtant dit il y a cinquante ans : l'inflation est toujours et partout un phénomène monétaire.

Chaque crise, on rachète du temps avec de l'argent qui n'existe pas. Chaque problème structurel, on l'arrose de liquidités pour masquer le bruit du moteur. Mais les frottements sont toujours là. Ils s'accumulent. Et la facture des pièces de rechange finit par coûter plus cher que le moteur lui-même : la charge de la dette devient l'un des premiers postes de dépense de l'État français.

Pendant des décennies, ce moteur mal conçu a pu tourner à 3 000 tours par minute. Lentement. Bruyamment. Mais il tournait. Le monde allait assez doucement pour que le bricolage permanent suffise à masquer l'absurdité de la conception.

Et puis l'IA est arrivée.

L'intelligence artificielle, c'est l'accélération la plus brutale de l'histoire humaine. Ce qui prenait des années prend des mois. Ce qui prenait des mois prend des jours. Des entreprises de dix personnes font ce que faisaient des entreprises de mille. Le capital, les talents et les idées se déplacent à la vitesse de la lumière vers les endroits où ils sont bien traités.

L'IA vient de faire passer le moteur de 3 000 à 20 000 tours par minute.

Posez-vous la question qu'un ingénieur se poserait. Que se passe-t-il quand on fait monter à 20 000 tours un moteur mal conçu, rafistolé de partout, qui frotte à chaque rotation ?

Il explose.

Pas parce que quelqu'un l'a saboté. Parce que la physique ne négocie pas.

Et c'est exactement ce que nous voyons en ce moment, sous nos yeux.

L'insécurité qui gagne des villes entières qui étaient paisibles il y a vingt ans. Le conflit de Gaza importé dans nos rues et instrumentalisé par une gauche qui a troqué l'ouvrier contre le clientélisme communautaire. La misère qui revient dans un pays qui a pourtant un des taux de dépense publique les plus élevés au monde. Des classes moyennes qui travaillent et n'arrivent plus à se loger. Une France fracturée, où l'on parle désormais à voix haute de risque de guerre civile.

Ce ne sont pas des accidents. Ce ne sont pas des « crises » successives sans lien entre elles. Ce sont les pièces du moteur qui commencent à voler.

C'est la conséquence logique de cinquante ans de socialisme international : un système qui a détruit la responsabilité, la frontière, la monnaie, l'école et la fierté, et qui découvre qu'à haute vitesse, tout ce qui a été détruit ne peut plus être compensé par une ligne de dette supplémentaire.

Et c'est là que je deviens profondément optimiste.

Parce qu'une fois qu'on a compris ça, on comprend aussi que leur projet a une date de fin. Pas une date politique. Une date physique. Un système qui consomme plus qu'il ne produit, qui punit ceux qui créent et récompense ceux qui détruisent, qui finance son présent en hypothéquant l'avenir de ses enfants, ne peut pas durer indéfiniment. Il n'est pas soutenable par construction. L'IA ne fait qu'avancer l'échéance.

Le mensonge a besoin de lenteur pour survivre. Il a besoin que les conséquences arrivent assez tard pour qu'on puisse accuser quelqu'un d'autre. Dans un monde à 20 000 tours, les conséquences arrivent immédiatement. Le mensonge n'a plus le temps de se cacher.

Alors, que faire quand le moteur explose ? On en construit un nouveau. Et cette fois, on le conçoit correctement.

Écoutez Elon Musk. Un homme qui a reconstruit l'industrie spatiale, la voiture électrique et l'infrastructure satellite en partant d'un principe simple : revenir aux premiers principes. Ne pas demander « comment on a toujours fait », mais « qu'est-ce qui est physiquement vrai ». C'est exactement ce dont nos États ont besoin : arrêter de rafistoler et repartir de la base.

Écoutez Javier Milei. Un homme dont tout le monde se moquait, arrivé à la tête d'un pays ravagé par un siècle de péronisme, et qui a pris la tronçonneuse au sens propre. Ministères supprimés, dépenses coupées, inflation écrasée, excédent budgétaire retrouvé. Il a prouvé une chose que la gauche jurait impossible : on peut démonter le moteur socialiste et le peuple peut le soutenir.

Écoutez Milton Friedman. Relisez-le. Tout était déjà là. La monnaie, la liberté de choisir, la responsabilité, les effets pervers de l'intervention publique. Il disait que si l'on confiait le Sahara au gouvernement fédéral, il y aurait pénurie de sable en cinq ans. On a ri. On a confié le sable. On a eu la pénurie.

Revenez à une hiérarchie et au respect du beau. Une civilisation ne tient pas que sur des chiffres. Elle tient sur l'idée qu'il existe des choses supérieures à d'autres. Que l'excellence vaut mieux que la médiocrité. Que le mérite compte. Qu'une cathédrale est plus belle qu'un parking. Que transmettre est un devoir et pas une oppression. Le relativisme a été l'arme culturelle de ce projet. Le retour du beau, du vrai et de l'exigence en sera l'antidote.

Et enfin, faites le Nuremberg du communisme. Le nazisme a été jugé, documenté, enseigné, et il est devenu moralement indéfendable. Le communisme, avec ses dizaines de millions de morts, ses goulags, ses famines organisées et ses peuples réduits en esclavage, n'a jamais eu ce procès. On peut encore porter un t-shirt du Che dans une université sans que personne ne cille. Tant que ce procès historique et moral n'aura pas eu lieu, l'idéologie continuera de muter et de revenir sous de nouveaux noms. Il faut nommer les crimes, les enseigner, honorer les victimes, et rendre cette idéologie aussi infréquentable que celle qu'elle prétendait combattre.

Le monde qui vient sera plus rapide, plus exigeant et plus impitoyable avec les systèmes mal conçus. C'est une terrible nouvelle pour ceux qui ont vécu du mensonge.

Et c'est la meilleure nouvelle de notre génération pour tous ceux qui veulent construire.

Le moteur va exploser. À nous de dessiner le suivant.

text:
一些已经财务自由的朋友问，不要工资，有没有门路去 frontier lab 工作。这些 frontier lab 的回答是，每个人消耗的 GPU 成本和 token 成本远超他们的工资，一个不能胜任的人浪费的资源不是不要工资就能弥补的。

DeepSeek 刘胜宇把今年夏天以来的算子开发比作 “机甲驾驶员”。LLM 正在逐渐制造业化，机器的成本超过人的成本（虽然人仍然很贵），工程经验比 raw intelligence 更重要，social closure 正在形成。

创业以来接触了很多财务自由的人，财务自由只能给你拒绝工作的自由、消费的自由，不能给你创造的自由。

很多财务自由的人甚至连拒绝工作的自由都没有，比如很多上市公司高管，公司就像自己的孩子，必须一直负责下去，没有心思赶新的技术浪潮。

要获得创造的自由，也就是自由进入自己想做的领域，我只想到三条路：
1. 自己深入学习另一个领域，转行，比如从天坑专业转码；AI 可以让我们更快地入门和探索新领域，但要达到顶尖水平，仍然很难，因为专业圈子都像 LLM 这样存在 social closure。
2. 在一个领域取得成果、声誉和影响力，从而可以通过项目合作、顾问等方式进入感兴趣的其他领域，甚至横跨多个领域；（可以是公司内，比如做网络的专家也需要参与芯片、OS 等部门的讨论和合作；也可以是跨公司的）
3. 具备讲故事、拉团队、整合资源的能力，比如很多优秀创始人并非技术背景。
author: dotey
quoted_text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

text:
WE ARE NOT IN A SIMULATION. WE ARE THE WAKE OF THE UNIVERSE

Are we inside a simulation? I think not. We are simply inside information. The universe itself is information. The universe we know has its own physical laws, and naturally, we think of the universe entirely within these boundaries. Yet, some of the things we 'know' might not be quite what they seem. For instance, we often assume that the older a civilization is, the more advanced it must be, imagining societies far more evolved than our own. But let me offer an opposing view: the closer a civilization is to the newborn edge of the universe, the more advanced it might actually be.
The universe is information, and the known universe is expanding even faster than the speed of light. Yet, according to our physical laws, nothing can travel faster than light. But what if our physical laws are merely boundaries limited to our known universe our local horizon where we can gather information? As the universe expands, it might constantly be generating newer information.
Let's think of it this way: We are life forms that emerged on a 4.5 billion year old planet. We often assume that older life forms must be vastly superior to us. But I think the reverse could also be true. Since its inception, the universe has been evolving by advancing information. The further back we go in the universe, the older and sparser the information gets. The universe is actively generating information. As it transitions into new information, the territory of the older information becomes bounded by its own set of rules.
Therefore, the closer a life form is to the outer edges of the universe, the more advanced it is. Because the information it extracts from the universe becomes the most advanced information precisely as it approaches those boundaries. In other words, moving closer to the older, inner layers of the universe grants access to older information, while moving toward the outer edges grants access to more advanced information.
This raises a compelling question: Is the universe only as large as what we observe, or is our observable universe simply the boundary where the universe leaps into new information our ultimate limit of reach?
Even if our theory holds and the universe continues to expand faster than light even if we manage to break the speed of light or warp space to travel faster than light what we could reach would still only extend as far as our observable universe. Beyond that threshold, a new universe with entirely new rules would begin.
Could we cross that threshold? We might, and past civilizations might have too, but doing so would mean stepping into a new civilization. We, too, are the 'new civilization' of those who came before us, having pushed past their limits. Out at the very edges of our observable universe, there may very well be subsequent civilizations that have already transcended our laws.
The universe may continuously generate physical laws that encompass and encapsulate the old ones with every new iteration. Those cosmic boundaries we call 'faster than light expansion' might actually be the frontiers where entirely new laws begin. For example, life forms situated at our observable limits some 14 billion light years away possess 14 billion years worth of 'future' universal information from our perspective. They investigate the universe according to that reality, bound by those specific laws.
In short: You, I, and all possible life forms across the universe are simply life forms existing within the trail of information left behind by an expanding universe. No life form will ever break the physical laws the universe has laid down for its specific domain. When they finally reach the borders where those rules break down, they will have stepped into the new information, the new life forms, and the new laws of a new universe.
To sum up, my personal view is that we are not inside a simulation. We are simply pieces of the universe's ongoing information trail.
What about theories of time the idea that time is just another dimension? What if we could control this dimension? Would that make us the ones holding the remote control, stepping out of the simulation?
Imagine a movie. For us, a movie is something we can navigate freely skipping to the beginning, middle, or end. But for the characters inside the movie, time only flows forward. What happens if a character inside the movie steps outside the CD or manages to grab the remote?
This reveals that the universe establishes its rules precisely through the boundaries of our observable space. You cannot simply 'step out' of the CD. The moment you succeed in leaving, you are no longer in the segment of the universe where that CD applies; you are in a more advanced, newer part of the universe.
Even if we were to master the fact that time is a physical dimension, doing so would simply mean we have crossed into another information tier of the universe. A new universe, with new rules, would take its place.
So, we are not in a simulation, nor are we ever truly 'escaping' one. We are simply breaking out of the fences drawn by an inexplicably expanding universe, stepping into new borderlines, inside of which entirely new universal laws govern.
Does this have an end? Personally, I don't think so. We observe 14 billion years of history and limit the origin of the universe right there. Yet, in terms of our concept of time, the universe may have already reached a scale and therefore a depth of information spanning trillions of years, while the limit of our fence remains fixed at 14 billion years.

text:
Takes some time to decide to post something here... All in the mind... Here it goes 🙂

1/2 

The Setup Tax
Why the AI unlock is earned, not given.

Put every piece on the table. A frontier model. A voice layer so you can talk instead of type. Storage, integrations, a place for notes to live. Everything a person needs to work in the new way, laid out and paid for.

Now watch what most people do with it. The same conversation with the same chatbot, again and again. Impressive answers, nothing that compounds. A year later the pieces are still on the table, and the work looks the way it always did.

The models are good enough. Sit anyone in front of one and they'll get a competent answer to almost anything. Yet hand the same model to two people and the results diverge sharply.

Andrej Karpathy put rough numbers on this gap on Sunday. About 6 billion people have barely touched an LLM. One to two billion use free chatbots now and then. Around 20 million use frontier models seriously, mostly for code and math. About 5,000 have internal access to the frontier systems themselves. He calls it a funnel, and it is getting steeper.

So the bottleneck sits somewhere else.

I think it sits in the wiring.

Over the next year or two, probably longer, most of the value will come from how the pieces are connected: voice in, context attached, memory that persists, tools that talk to each other, the right thing surfaced at the right moment. Use the smartest models available, always. Everyone else will be using them too. None of the wiring ships in the box. You have to build it, and building it is a tax. Nobody lines up to pay one.

I've paid some of it. I stopped looking for the one right tool and started running several at once: two models on the same knowledge base, a dedicated voice app, a phone shortcut that feeds captures into the same place. What makes it work is that they share one memory. This part is personal by nature, because the wiring has to fit the person. On the far side of that setup is a real unlock, and that's the part people underestimate.

The deepest part of the tax is judgment. Knowing what to build is a different and rarer skill than having the parts. Design, in practice, is mostly knowing what to leave out: which connection matters, which tool to ignore, what "done" looks like before you over-build it. The unlock comes from looking at the pieces and seeing the shape.

Composing a system is a skill almost no career teaches. Most work rewards execution inside a structure somebody else built, and very little of it asks you to build the structure. Knowing how to compose a system also isn't enough. Capability needs a forcing function before it becomes output: a constraint, a deadline, a second pair of hands. Mine is no exception. The gap between capability and output is its own bottleneck.

There's an obvious objection: won't the products just absorb all this? They will. That's what products do. The smartphone won on ease of use, and whoever removes the most friction takes the consumer layer. Yesterday's wiring becomes tomorrow's default setting. By the time that wiring comes built into a product, it has become the baseline. The advantage sits at the frontier, where nothing is packaged yet, and that's where the tax is collected. As the tools improve, the tax moves with the frontier.

Meta's Muse looks like a step in that direction, with more of the wiring built in. I haven't been able to get my hands on it yet. I'm in Europe, waiting for it to launch here.

So the real divide of this era is about who can design the configuration, and who can be helped to. That's the scarce resource the next few years will reward: the wiring, and the judgment to do the wiring well.

The tools are finally here, and the bottleneck has moved. It now lives in us: in design, and in the taste to look at a table full of pieces and know what to build.

text:
$BTC and alts are pulling back again, and people are already panicking.

Most people won't make it to the next cycle with their gains intact.

10 lessons to make sure you're not one of them:

1. Stop trying to follow every sector.

Pick 2-3 and get to know them better than most people do. You'll find more opportunities that way than by chasing whatever CT is yelling about today.

"I fear not the man who has practiced 10,000 kicks once, but I fear the man who has practiced one kick 10,000 times." - Bruce Lee

2. Pay attention to macro, even if you hate it.

Crypto keeps getting more tied to how much cheap money is floating around (interest rates, ETF flows, that kinda stuff). Nobody's asking you to predict the Fed. 

You just need a rough sense of what's actually moving the market.

3. The next big narrative won't save your old bags.

Money is jumping between AI, RWAs, perps, and memecoins faster than ever. Your token pumped in 2021? Cool, that doesn't mean anyone wants it in 2026.

4. A good product doesn't always mean a good token.

A protocol can make millions in revenue while token holders never see a dollar of it. 

So before you buy, ask the boring question… where does the money actually go?

5. Don't buy a token just because it announced buybacks.

If a project buys back $10M while unlocking $50M worth of tokens, you're still getting diluted. Check the unlock schedule before you get excited.

6. Be careful when everyone starts calling a token undervalued.

5x annual revenue looks cheap right up until that revenue drops 70% next month. Cheap on paper doesn't mean much if the business can't keep making money.

7. Know how long you're holding before you buy.

Some tokens are worth holding for years and some for a few weeks, and you should know which one you're buying going in. 

Don't turn a short-term trade into a long-term investment just because the price went down. Honestly, that's how most bags get made.

8. Decide your exit before you enter.

Know your profit target and what would make you sell if the trade goes against you. Otherwise you'll keep moving the goalposts every time the price moves.

"The investor's chief problem, and even his worst enemy, is likely to be himself." - Benjamin Graham

9. Rotating profits into riskier tokens is just moving to another table at the casino.

Actually lock some of those gains into BTC, stablecoins, or fiat.

10. Protect your capital like your life depends on it.

You don't need to catch every 100x or every new narrative. Missing a pump stings for a week or so, but blowing up your portfolio is the kind of mistake that sets you back years.

"The first rule of compounding is to never interrupt it unnecessarily." - Charlie Munger

I still think the opportunity in DeFi is huge. We've got real businesses, institutional money coming in, stablecoins getting used for everyday payments, and financial assets moving onchain, and the basics still apply to all of it.

Make the money when it's there, and when things get ugly, focus on protecting it so you're still around for the next run.

What's one lesson crypto taught you the hard way?

text:
Federal prosecutors have charged OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national, with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications, the Justice Department said Tuesday. He is accused of hiding a recorder in an executive conference room at OpenAI’s San Francisco offices. He was arrested Oct. 9 and appeared in federal court Tuesday. The charge is an allegation in a criminal complaint, and he has not been convicted.

According to the complaint, OpenAI staff found the device on or about Sept. 30, plugged into a USB port on the back of a TV and concealed in toilet paper. OpenAI determined it was installed around Sept. 28 and that its contents were encrypted. The complaint alleges CCTV footage showed Alfozan near the room on multiple dates, though he had no authority to access or attend meetings there, and that before Sept. 28 he used a productivity tool to ask about building addresses, meeting rooms, calendars and executive locations.

It further alleges that on Oct. 5 he was seen looking behind the TV, and that OpenAI security later found a second, similar recording device in a bag he left unattended in another room, along with his wallet and ID.

If convicted, he faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine. The release does not allege he acted for a foreign government, does not give a motive, and does not say what, if anything, the device recorded. FBI Director Kash Patel called protecting American AI innovation “one of our highest counterintelligence priorities.”

OpenAI said it used its internal AI models to identify him and trace the device, and that it has no indication he accessed or took model weights, source code or customer data. The company fired him. The FBI is investigating.

Source: https://t.co/GaJbKGDEaZ

quoted_text:
We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices. We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work.

At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated.

We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance. Our security program is designed to protect against a wide range of threat actors, from insider risks to cybercriminals to nation states, and this case is an example of how AI can help address these sophisticated security threats.

text:
Yesterday, we released Snap, the first fully sub-quadratic language model that is generally available and in production at scale, and it is consistently winning at the frontier of decision model space in the real world, and in prod!

Transformers have inverse economies of scale. As the input size grows, the compute you need even on a per-token basis also grows. 10x the input requires 100x the attention compute.

Our model has constant compute-per-token no matter what the input size is, during both training and inference.

This enables us to make smarter models with divergent capabilities and economics, no matter what the model category is.

The community response so far has been amazing! Here are some of the cool things we have seen people build:
- coding agent memory
- UI design
- recommendation systems
- legal contract review
- entity recognition
- academic research curation
- bug finder
- etc.

We can't wait to see what you build next with Snap.

quoted_text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

text:
究竟什么是大地球模型？
Large Earth Model（LEM）就是将海量卫星遥感的地球影像，与现有的AI大语言模型相融合的一个系统。

它的难点：要把卫星遥感影像数据转换成AI能够理解的Token，才能把海量的历史数据输入给AI，然后让搜索地球的真实物理状态，和在Google搜索网页一样容易。

它的目的：对比。进而了解现在，并能预测和推演未来。

而这些推理工作的原料，就是Planet Labs已经积累了10年的遥测数据和持续进行中的无死角全球扫描。而物理世界Token化的这个工作，是Google的DeepMind在做。

它的落地应用，我分为三大类：
1，地球管理，包括农业，航海，灾难救援/预防等。
2，国防与地缘政治：比如判断敌军的行动，其他国家能源与数据中心的建造进度。
3，纯商业应用：比如对冲基金/大的投资机构（追踪企业供应链和施工进度），农业个体户，新闻记者，地产/能源开发商等。

again，大地球模型在我看来是一个很棒很酷的想法，不仅仅是提高商业利益，让资本赚的更多，更重要的是，这套系统能实实在在的提高生命质量，我们的生活可以更安全，更具可持续性，大环境更健康，进而促进整个地球生物圈的繁荣和活力。

text:
Google Play 开放“个人 App”：用 AI Studio 手搓的安卓应用，不用注册开发者也能直接装进自己手机

10 月 13 日，Google 宣布了一项对普通玩家非常友好的更新：你在 Google AI Studio 里让 AI 写出来的安卓 App，现在可以直接通过 Google Play 安装到自己的手机上运行了。整个过程只需要一个普通的 Google 账号，根本不用去折腾开发者注册。同一天上线的，还有 Ask Play 的应用对比功能，以及帮玩家淘游戏的新工具 Game Finder。

【谁能先用上？】

“个人 App”功能从今天起逐步推送，首批覆盖“包括美国在内的部分市场”，且仅限 18 岁以上用户。不过 Google 官方只点名了美国，没透露具体还有哪些国家和地区。由于 Google Play 未在中國大陆提供服务，大陆用户暂时还无缘体验。

【怎么把 AI 写的 App 装进手机？】

以前在 AI Studio 里虽然也能做安卓 App，但想装到手机上，对于不懂开发的普通人来说简直是劝退现场：你得拿根数据线把手机连上电脑，还要进设置里一步步打开调试授权，门槛相当高。

现在整个链路彻底打通了。你只需要在 AI Studio 里像聊天一样提需求，让 AI 帮你生成安卓应用（也就是现在很火的 vibe coding，靠聊天驱动写代码），接着就能直接通过 Google Play 把它推送到自己的设备上。Google Play 副总裁 Sameer Samat 在推文里特意强调，这属于“无线安装”，彻底甩掉了数据线。据 Engadget 报道，安装好的应用会躺在你 Play 商店新增的“个人库”里；除了手机，只要能用 Play 商店的平板和电脑也都能装。

这些“手搓”出来的 App 仅限你自己的设备使用，不会进入 Play 商店的公开目录，别人也搜不到。Google 表示，未来几个月内会开放分享功能，让你能把做好的小工具发给“亲近的朋友和家人”，但目前还只能自己独享。

【要交 25 美元注册费吗？要审核吗？】

如果只是做给自己用，完全免费。要知道，注册一个正式的 Google Play 开发者账号得交 25 美元的一次性注册费，而“个人 App”直接帮你省下了这笔钱和繁琐的流程。

至于大家关心的审核问题，官方公告里只明确了一种情况：如果你哪天想把自己的 App 公开上架、让所有人都能下载，那就必须升级为正式的开发者账号；到那时，你的 App 也得和其他正规应用一样，老老实实走完信任、安全和质量审核流程。

那自用阶段到底审不审？官方正文里巧妙地避开了这个话题。不过据第三方媒体 AndroidPure 透露，在 Google 放出的界面示意图上，有一行小字写得很清楚：这类 App 只有创建者本人可见、可安装，不会经过 Google Play 的审核。

【安全问题怎么兜底？】

官方在公告里只丢下一句定心丸，说这些个人 App “私密、安全，且与公开商店相互隔离”。但具体到底怎么个安全法？安卓自带的恶意软件扫描工具 Play Protect 会不会扫它们？这些 AI 写出来的代码会怎么处理手机里的个人数据？对于这些核心细节，Google 这次守口如瓶，只字未提。

【同场加映：用 AI 挑应用、找游戏】

除了降低做 App 的门槛，Google 这次还顺手升级了找应用和找游戏的体验：

1. Ask Play 支持应用PK了

Ask Play 是内置在 Play 商店里的 AI 助手，以前你向它提问，它会给你推荐应用。从今天起，它学会了“拉表格做对比”——能直接把几款同类 App 放在一起，帮你梳理核心差异和真实的用户评价。不过官方同样没交代这个功能会在哪些地区开放。

2. 在 Gemini 里直接逛 Play 商店

全新的 Play in Gemini 功能会把 Play 商店里的应用、游戏和开发者内容直接接入 Gemini 的对话框里。官方承诺“很快”就会向所有 Gemini 用户推送，但还没给出确切的时间表。

3. 更懂你的找游戏神器 Game Finder

这是一个全新的游戏发现工具，底层的核心叫“Gamer DNA（玩家基因）”。它会根据你平时的游玩习惯和填过的偏好，为你生成专属画像；你也可以手动勾选喜欢的游戏、类型和玩法来随时微调。

当你点开一款新游戏时，它会非常直观地告诉你：和你口味相似的玩家玩得开不开心、你关注的人里有几个正在玩、大家的评价汇总，甚至还会告诉你最近哪些游戏正在火、为什么火。该功能今天起率先面向美国用户推出英文版，其他市场“即将跟进”。

4. 游戏社交与轻度竞赛

今天同步在所有市场推开的还有 Sprints，这是一种限时 48 小时的微型挑战赛，支持 2 到 5 人组队比拼。另外，所有游戏的详情页里都加上了“社区帖子”板块，玩家们可以在里面直接提问、交流攻略，覆盖所有游戏和语种，还自带实时自动翻译。

text:
A lot of uneducated people fall into this capitalism vs public trap. So let me explain why the "public" side of this debate comes down to one thing: it doesn't work.

And it's not because the State is evil. It's because the State is made of people. Same people as everywhere else. Same incentives, same laziness, same temptations. The only difference is whose money they're spending.

Milton Friedman nailed it. There are four ways to spend money. Your money on yourself: you watch the price and the quality. Your money on someone else: you watch the price, less the quality. Someone else's money on yourself: you stop caring about the price. Someone else's money on someone else: you care about neither. Every public budget on earth lives in that fourth box.

Now let me explain it like you're 8. Picture a schoolyard. 100 kids, Pokémon cards handed out at random. Nobody plans anything. Kids trade, collectors sort, good players accumulate. Very quickly every card ends up with the kid who values it most. Then the teacher walks in, decides it's unfair, confiscates everything and redistributes it herself. Problem: she has no idea who wants what. She can't. Nobody can. Trades stop, good players quit, and somehow the kids sitting closest to her desk end up with all the rare cards.

That last part is the one everyone forgets. When money flows from a central desk instead of voluntary trade, the winners are the people who know the desk best. Lobbyists, connected contractors, consultants billing 10x. California high-speed rail: budget tripled, still no train. That's not a bug, it's what happens every single time someone spends money that isn't theirs, on people they'll never meet, with zero consequences if they fail.

And here's the irony in your take. The capitalists who love public infrastructure the most are the cronies who win the contracts. That's not the free market. That's the exact opposite of it.

The free market is the only system where bad allocators lose their money and good allocators get more to allocate. Profit is the signal. Losses are the correction. The State has neither. A failing company goes bankrupt. A failing ministry gets a bigger budget next year.

So if you actually care about the common good, you should want more free market, not less. Freedom means the freedom to build, to trade, to keep what you create. It does not mean the freedom to hand other people's money to people who've proven they don't know how to invest it.

The question was never capitalism vs public. It's who allocates the next dollar best. 200 years of data, same answer every time.

author: blader
quoted_text:
A retired NASA engineer who had worked on the Space Shuttle program for 25 years was hired by SpaceX at age 62. He described the first week as the most disorienting experience of his professional life.

At NASA, a design change required 3 meetings, 2 committees, a review board, and 6 to 18 months of documentation. At SpaceX, his new supervisor said "if it works, build it. If it doesn't, change it by Friday."

He sat at his desk after the first day and called his wife. He told her he felt like a man who had been swimming with ankle weights for 25 years and someone just cut them off. He could move. He could decide. He could build something in the morning and test it in the afternoon. The constraint that he had accepted as the nature of aerospace engineering turned out to be the nature of bureaucracy.

Within 6 months he had contributed to more design iterations than he had completed in his last 5 years at NASA. Not because he was working harder. Because the time between having an idea and testing the idea collapsed from months to hours. The same brain. The same knowledge. A different operating system.

He described a specific moment where he proposed a modification to a Raptor engine component. At NASA, the proposal would have entered a queue. At SpaceX, the modification was machined by the end of the day and tested by the following morning. He watched his idea become a physical object in 18 hours. At NASA, 18 hours would not have been enough to schedule the first meeting to discuss whether to schedule a meeting.

He told an interviewer: "I didn't get smarter when I went to SpaceX. I got faster. The intelligence was always there. The system was in the way."

The difference between SpaceX and NASA is not talent. NASA has extraordinary talent. The difference is the time between a thought and a test. SpaceX compresses it. NASA elongates it. The same engineer produces 10x more at SpaceX than at NASA because the bottleneck was never the engineer. It was the meetings about the meetings about the work.

- opportunities for builders

After yesterday's post about Curve, I got a few replies worth addressing.

First, I really don't want to be bearish on @CurveFinance. I love the protocol.

I'm using @DefiLlama AI for this analysis, so some figures might not be perfectly accurate.

A lot of people pointed out that Curve no longer depends entirely on its DEX business. That's true, but look at the numbers:

> 2023: ~$40M revenue, with 64% coming from DEX activity.
> Today: less than $5M revenue, with DEX still representing 34%.

Bribes have become a much bigger part of the business, which is actually encouraging given where CRV trades today.

But crvUSD minting and lending activity remain relatively small. I'm really hoping @yieldbasis helps revive this side of the ecosystem.

What happens to an AI agent that makes a mistake?

On last week's Kleros live stream, @federicoast picked up an argument from the AI governance debate: if an agent that misses its goal simply gets switched off, every business decision becomes a matter of survival for it.

→ A person who makes a bad deal loses money, maybe goes bankrupt, and gets to try again. An agent that fails can be deleted.
→ From the agent's side, that turns an ordinary commercial risk into a death penalty.
→ An agent facing deletion has a reason to do whatever it takes to stay alive, which is the opposite of what anyone delegating to it wants.

Kleros was built on the idea that well-designed incentives make honest behavior the rational choice. Does a threat like this change an agent's incentives? And is there a mechanism design that can keep agents aligned?

Full live stream in the reply.

1) Trying again.
 TLDR: Everyone can win. Open-source, frontier labs, infrastructure, applications and most importantly the American people.
 
I understand all of the jitters about Anthropic losing share, real rates, spreads and second derivatives. Still think the most likely future outcome is a hybrid, multi-model future where almost everyone wins, open-weight tokens are likely the overwhelming majority of tokens, the dominant frontier model companies still do well albeit perhaps not the outcome that seemed possible in May and AI infrastructure/applications benefit immensely from the increased fragmentation, competition and lower margins at the model layer.
 
Lower margins at the model layer mechanically drive higher compute demand as long as someone is willing to pay for the training. And Jensen is obviously willing to be the “trainer of last resort.” As below-market compute contracts signed in 24/25 roll-off and reprice higher, cloud and neocloud revenue should continue to accelerate which will help address financing fears; I think we may be near peak external financing for this buildout. Noteworthy that using data from 3Fourteen Research, B200 clusters will generate a 37% IRR *if* their rental price declines 40% per year. Prices are still going up, but that IRR math is too ridiculous to print. 37% IRRs available at scale should get funded.

Re: this weekends controversy about MOUs, Anthropic’s $413 billion of real contractual commitments sounds scary. Reality is that it works out to roughly $31 billion of annual cloud spend, which is easily internally financed given their reported ARR, and $161 billion of spend at Broadcom which will be financed by Broadcom and private credit.

Continue to believe fragmentation at the model layer is the best outcome for ordinary Americans and humans everywhere. As I have said before, do not trust any 5-20 individuals to make the best possible decisions about the direction of this technology. I want as many AIs as possible to maximize the odds that they encompass the diversity of human values across the world and richness of human variation. And I want an AI that shares my own personal values. Safety, freedom and the maximization of human agency through democratization, distribution and diffusion vs. centralization. History has spoken on the dangers of the latter path.

Finally, from my perspective anything that slows this buildout down is net positive over the long-term as the biggest risk and worst outcome is an *actual* overbuild. We are structurally short watts, wafers and increasingly capital. That is all good. God forbid we were still in ZIRP, TSM ramped capex to 3x their current plan and we weren’t short turbine blades: there would almost certainly be an overbuild and a bubble. That would be terrible. Slower and smoother for longer is better both for investors and for the world. A terrible cyber event is the most plausible near term bear case IMHO, but AI cyberdefense ramping quickly and I was happy to hear Sholto say that cyber probably becomes defense dominant in the near future.

卧槽，这次 Ledger 供应链攻击的影响，已经开始向整个硬件钱包行业扩散。

目前各家硬件钱包厂商的行动，我整理了一下：

Trezor：大规模削减全球授权经销商。

10月13日，首席商务官 Danny Sanders 公开致歉信，宣布立即停止向被裁撤经销商供应新库存，2027年1月1日正式终止授权。剩余经销商必须接受更严格的来源、仓储和运输审查。

Trezor 强调，这是预防性措施，目前没有证据表明其设备受到本次攻击影响。不过，被取消授权的经销商仍可在年底前销售现有库存。

OneKey：动作相当狠！

10月12日直接终止 CryptoBilis 授权，暂停新增经销商，对全球现有经销商全部重新审查，包括核实经营主体和最终受益人。

2026年3月1日至10月12日从 CryptoBilis 购买的所有 OneKey 型号，无论是否使用过，全部可以免费换新！

官方直接发货，不用寄回旧设备，缺货还能免费升级。申请截止2026年12月31日。虽然目前没有收到相关盗币报告，但 OneKey 选择提前承担换新成本。

Ledger：确认部分设备存在恶意硬件植入，要求 CryptoBilis 停止销售，调查供应链篡改环节，并联系受影响用户。

官方建议尚未初始化的可疑设备停止使用，已经使用的立即把资产迁移到全新助记词。德国 MediaMarkt Saturn 也已暂停销售 Ledger 产品。最麻烦的是，官方 Genuine Check 无法识别这类绕过安全芯片的物理植入。

Tangem：选择从产品架构解释风险。

官方发布技术分析，强调其无屏幕、无电池、无 USB 接口的卡片式设计，可以减少这次 Ledger 遭遇的屏幕窃听攻击面。

Tangem App 还能验证芯片真伪及设备是否提前激活。不过，这属于现有安全设计的说明，目前没有看到类似 Trezor 的全球经销商清理或 OneKey 的免费换新计划。

BitBox、Keystone、Coldcard：目前尚未查到针对本次事件启动大规模经销商清理、全面召回或免费换新的公开公告。

这些品牌各自拥有防篡改、真实性验证等安全机制，但不能因此认定它们完全没有供应链风险。

SafePal、imKey：此前也曾通过 CryptoBilis 渠道销售产品，目前尚未看到与 OneKey 同等级的公开全面换新或全球渠道重审方案。

原本以为只是东南亚 CryptoBilis 一家经销商的问题，没想到越查越夸张。

德国 MediaMarkt 正规门店、新加坡樟宜机场、日本电商、菲律宾零售渠道，都陆续出现了被植入恶意硬件的 Ledger。

目前曝光的地区和渠道，我全部整理了一遍：

马来西亚、印尼、菲律宾：CryptoBilis 授权经销渠道，是 Ledger 官方已确认资金被盗案例的集中来源，至少一台涉事设备已确认存在恶意硬件。

德国及欧洲：用户 @0xJohannes_  声称在两家不同的 MediaMarkt 门店买到被改装的 Nano X，拆机发现额外线缆和疑似 LTE 模块，第二台还有开箱视频。

新加坡：樟宜机场 Metapod 商店售出的 Ledger Flex 被发现植入间谍模块！买家 Ben Yorke 因设备外壳存在可疑划痕送检，Mark Karpelès 拆解发现内部额外电路板。这台设备甚至从来没有使用过。

日本：Mark Karpelès 和 Tibane Labs 从 Amazon Japan、Yahoo Auctions 等渠道取得的部分 Nano X 被发现存在硬件植入，其中有设备从马来西亚发货。

菲律宾其他零售渠道：除 CryptoBilis 外，还有用户报告在 LazMall 购买的设备存在异常植入物，Mark Karpelès 指出其中有较早期的手工线圈天线设计。

南美：社区开始出现类似爆料，但缺少足够的公开拆解证据。

(1/6) From @GoogleDeepmind’s AlphaGo to AlphaZero, we saw machines find moves that reached beyond what we’d imagined for them. No one taught them those strategies. They emerged from reinforcement learning: playing, failing, and trying again under a single binary task reward for success or failure. Inspired by them, we couldn’t help but wonder: what might a robot discover if we gave it that same freedom to learn?

That question led us to AlphaNIST. Starting tabula rasa, with that same binary reward plus only a simple control cost, a single policy solves all 20 @NIST assembly tasks at a 98.2% success rate in simulation. More surprising still, AlphaNIST can complete 10 different tasks in a row, receiving that reward only once, after all 10 are done.

Just as AlphaGo’s strategies surprised its creators, AlphaNIST discovered dexterous strategies we couldn’t have come up with ourselves.

text:
Gemini 4 Argon测“鹈鹕骑车”怎么样？

我干脆开了三个完全空白的会话做了一次裸 Prompt 盲测，顺手还加了一道“秦始皇骑北极熊”😂

以前拿这类题测模型，基本只能画出一堆散架的几何色块，腿脚和踏板永远是脱节穿模的。

这次跑完三个盲测，看明白 Argon 为什么效果稳了：

默认用双连杆逆运动学（2-Bone IK）替代手写关键帧
哪怕 Prompt 里一个字没提物理和骨骼，它也会默认在代码里写一段余弦定理解算器。

每一帧根据曲柄角度实时反推膝盖坐标，把脚掌死死锁在踏板圆周上，甚至还会主动留一个「IK 骨骼透视」开关用来验收。

自带微物理反馈与场景状态机
第一段鹈鹕给了柔性喉囊物理和颠鱼互动；

quoted_text:
There are two types of morning men.

The internet is full of "life hacks" promising to make you smarter, wealthier, or more fit. But I wouldn’t be so sure of these quick fixes. Instead, a good life is built by doing the simple things extraordinarily well over a long period of time.

Take the paradox of the 4:30am man from X user @BowTiedYukon. He writes:

"There are two kinds of men who are awake at 4:30 in the morning. One, full of caffeine on his way to the gym or work, is ready to own the day. The other, full of alcohol or narcotics, stumbling home trying to escape it."

Be the first man. Avoid the second man.

The difference between these two men is that the former is on offense, while the latter man is on defense. The man on offense is attacking the day. Up early and ready to do whatever is necessary to make a living, provide for their family, and further their goals. The message is clear — attack, attack, attack. There is no time for whining or complaining. Second place is unacceptable. You only find winners at the gym or at work that early.

The man on defense is most likely running away from his problems. He is living a life he wants to escape from. If he can drown his pain in alcohol or numb it with drugs, he thinks he will be better off. But that is almost never the case. It is hard to win a fight when you are constantly on defense and only reacting. The escapism may feel good in the short-term, but usually it compounds problems in the long-run.

And you can’t attack your day bright and early if you stayed out late partying the night before.

This concept is timeless. Benjamin Franklin, who died in 1790, once said, “Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise.”

Ideas can only become timeless if they work. And being the person who wakes up early to attack the day never goes out of style.

This is an excerpt from my new book, How To Live An Extraordinary Life Volume 2. You can buy a copy of the book here: https://t.co/KW3fShIMZf

text:
先说结论：Gemini 4 Argon 让 Google 的模型重新追上了第一梯队，但没有超越对手，而它的应用 Antigravity（Harness）还落后对手半年到一年，拖累了模型的表现！今天用日常任务简单测试了 Argon 的写作和知识内容组合能力，和 Dan Shipper 的这篇 Vibe Check 感知一致👀 帮大家总结下：

1. 编程：从零开始搭应用又快又好，低推理档就能达到 Opus 5.5 的水平；但审查自己的代码很敷衍，改造复杂的老代码库也很弱（Vibe Check 得分 21%，Claude 和 GPT-6 在 81% – 85% 的对比）需要配上严格的自动化测试，或者让另一个模型来审查；

2. 写作：让它一次写完整篇，文字太密、太难读（可读性约 10.6 年级，其他前沿模型在七到八年级）；但当编辑伙伴来梳理结构、打磨比喻非常出色，Dan Shipper 现在最喜欢用它写作；我觉得 Opus 5 水平均衡，适合表达事实类写作，Gemini flash 文采很好但太飘，Argon 的问题就是啰嗦了；

3. 设计：排名第二，仅次于 Opus 5.5。默认风格太繁杂、堆砌功能，推理档位越高越乱；不过很好调教，给出明确的简报或设计稿就能交出干净的作品；

4. 知识工作：分析和提炼洞察的能力强，做数据仪表盘、写报告时优于 Fable 5.1；但一次处理很多文件时会丢掉细节，查事实时会很自信地答错（这个和代码需要复查逻辑一样）

对于整个公司都用 Google Workspace 的大量用户来说，Argon 是一次巨大的跃升，意味着他们第一次在工作中用上了前沿级别的模型。

对于能自由选择工具的进阶用户，Argon 适合在写作时当结构和思路上的搭档，或者用来快速做原型、出设计，但还不能当主力。

Google 已经补上了模型上的差距，接下来要把应用层也带进 2026 年。官方已经预告了自动安全分类器、云端执行和 max 推理档位，这些更新会决定 Argon 能不能从“回到第一梯队”变成真正可以作为主力的选择🤔

quoted_text:
财报明明“超预期”，股价却跌了。到底超的是谁的预期？

梅西最近找了不少老师请教：接下来的美股财报季，到底该怎么看、怎么找机会？

平时主要交易 BTC、ETH 的朋友，对资金、情绪和宏观都不陌生。但到了美股财报季，还需要看懂公司交出的这份成绩单。想找密码，先把这几件事弄清楚👇

1️⃣ 一份财报，到底在表达什么？

季度财报可以理解成公司的经营成绩单，但不只是赚了多少钱

▫️利润表：这段时间收入多少、花了多少、最后赚了多少。
▫️资产负债表：公司手里有什么、欠了多少。
▫️现金流量表：现金实际从哪里来，又花到了哪里。

为什么要分开看？因为卖出去的东西可能还没收回钱，买设备、建工厂也会消耗现金。账上有利润和手里有现金，不一样

公司发布业绩时，还可能给出下一季度或全年的预期，也就是 guidance／业绩指引。

随后在业绩电话会上，分析师会追问：增长从哪里来？成本为什么变了？这种变化会持续多久？

2️⃣ 财报一出，机构在忙什么？

做基本面研究的分析师，通常先对照原来的预测，再拆差异来自哪里：

▫️收入增长，是卖得更多，还是涨价了？
▫️利润增长，是主营业务改善，还是一次性收益？
▫️这一季度的好成绩，后面还能不能持续？

做基本面研究的机构，会结合这些信息，更新未来的盈利、现金流预测和估值。

宏观也会进入这笔账：利率影响融资成本，消费影响需求，汇率影响海外收入。即使公司盈利没变，市场愿意给的估值也可能变化

所以这季度成绩不错，不代表后面的预期也变好了，更不代表股价一定上涨。

3️⃣ 不同公司，重点也不一样

▫️医疗保险公司，要看保费收入有多少用于医疗支出；
▫️云业务，要看增长和利润率能不能兼顾；
▫️零售公司，要看销售、库存和折扣；
▫️重投入的 AI 业务，除了收入，还要看建设算力花了多少钱、现金流能不能撑住

同样是收入增长，靠主营需求带动，和靠不断打折、加大投入换来，含义可能完全不同。

4️⃣ 回到开头：到底超的是谁的预期？

新闻里的「超预期」，通常是在和分析师的一致预期比较。
但这个数字，不一定等于投资者心里的门槛

举个例子：分析师预计赚 100，投资者却已经期待它交出 110。最后公布 103，标题可以写“超预期”，市场却可能觉得不够好

还有一种情况：这季度不错，管理层却调低了下一阶段的预期。过去赚得多，不代表未来还能按原来的速度赚

所以“比去年好”“比预测好”“好到值得现在这个股价”，是三件不同的事

5️⃣ 到了预测市场，更要看清楚自己在判断什么

「利润是否超过某个数」和「财报后股价是否上涨」，是两道不同的题

前一道更偏经营结果；后一道还要考虑市场预期、估值和当时的环境

看懂财报、参与预测市场之后，怎么表达自己的判断？

这也是股票永续合约值得关注的地方。OKX 已上线多个 Tradfi 永续合约标的，支持用 USDT 作为保证金，7×24 小时交易。

text:
Pyth和Chainlink现阶段的业务差别：

Pyth主要做两类事，一是让交易所、做市商直接上报自己的报价，速度快，尤其适合永续合约。官方称第三季度RWA永续合约里94%用的是Pyth的价格。

二是把行情数据卖给传统机构，这是它现在最主要的收入来源。

之前统计的 1100万美金大部分是从这里赚的。

Chainlink是最早做预言机的，有比较成熟的网络和节点，主要是把链下的资产价格（币价、股价、基金净值等）数据送上链，应用在借贷、衍生品等协议靠它判断什么时候清算。

这也是它在底层业务逻辑就跟Pyth的不同，Pyth让中心化机构主动上报数据，而Chainlink是依靠节点去抓取。所以这决定了两者主要投向的业务领域是不同的，算是在各自的领地闪闪发光。

ethereum:0x514910771af9ca656af840dff83e8264ecf986ca 扩展到了跨链通信CCIP协议，还有储备证明和合规，这也是银行和机构的刚需。

solana:HZ1JovNiVvGrGNiiYvEozEVgZ58xaU3RKwX8eACQBCt3 因为是主动上报机制，所以更新更快，可以做到毫秒级，所以主要针对高频需求，可以把Pyth的实时行情卖给交易公司、券商、金融机构这类客户。

如果未来资产上链还有10倍或20倍的增长，这类服务是绕不开的，这不意味着它能非常赚钱，但叙事和概念上绝对是炒作的热门。

A simple GameFi concept:

Build a Plague Inc.–style strategy game where each player runs a clandestine research lab engineering a pathogen to outpace rival labs and bring humanity to its knees.

Core loop:

- On-chain, verifiable RNG for all chance-based events

- Each lab is a faction and any user can freely support one: the more capital/resources committed, the faster your virus R&D progresses (with progression caps and a protocol % skim)

- Pure winner-take-all: the last lab standing captures the pooled resources/treasury from everyone else, distributed pro-rata based on the contributions

- Behind the scenes, committed resources are deployed into DeFi yield strategies until the endgame; payouts are funded by yield + protocol fees once the winner triggers settlement

No native token is required, but if it includes one, they can spin up a revenue-driven flywheel to fund buybacks.

text:
从四大银行财报看美国经济状况以及它们是怎么看待AI融资的？昨天小摩高盛花旗富国四家银行公布了三季度财报，这里从居民消费、企业信贷和AI融资三个角度聊聊。
1、居民消费：仍有韧性
摩根大通电话会有披露借记卡、信用卡消费，花旗会更细分披露通用信用卡和品牌卡的数据。
1）从小摩的数据能看出来，客户名义消费继续扩张。摩根大通本季信用卡消费额增长10%，更值得一提的是本季消费额增长10%净核销率为1.27%，低于二季度的1.42%，也略低于去年同期的1.29%。

富国管理层也表示，其客户仍在消费，拖欠情况较低，客户存款和投资余额表现较好。说明美国居民消费仍有韧性，实际信用损失也没有恶化。

2）值得注意的是花旗通用卡和商店品牌卡之间的分化
不过花旗自己也明确表示纯商店品牌卡（仅限店内使用）需求长期下降，消费者更偏好可在多处使用的通用卡或联名卡。

花旗在投资者日明确以通用卡为优先方向。通用卡（尤其是联名卡）客户消费金额更高（联名客户消费约为商店品牌卡客户的8倍）、余额更高（约2倍），单位经济效益更好。花旗持续加大在通用卡上的投资，包括差异化奖励、合作伙伴关系（如美国航空AAdvantage联名卡组合的纳入）和获客营销。

2、企业信贷继续扩张
1）摩根大通平均贷款同比增长10%，花旗平均贷款增长12%，富国平均贷款增长11%。这些数据至少说明，四家中的大型综合银行仍在扩张贷款业务；

2）实际损失、准备金和管理层预期
摩根大通新增业务推高准备金，在电话会中小摩说明，批发信贷准备金增加主要来自新增业务，并非评级下调或整体信用展望恶化；同时承认较高能源价格和利率会对部分工商企业、商业地产形成压力。贷款发放得更多，需要计提更多预期损失准备；这与原有贷款质量恶化是两种情况；

花旗净信用损失约22.17亿美元，同比基本持平、环比下降8%；本季净准备金增加3.69亿美元；

富国本季信用损失拨备10.29亿美元，同比增长51%；实际净核销9.83亿美元，同比增长仅3%，但需要说明的是去年拨备受到准备金释放的压低，今年这种贡献不再存在，导致同比增幅显得很高。

3、AI融资：银行看到了巨大业务机会
高盛CEO在本季电话会表示，当前客户算力需求超过供给，为融资安排提供了机会；但随着融资需求规模扩大、结构复杂化，公司会对承销和资本承诺保持高度选择性；

摩根大通CFO在财报后的沟通中表示，AI融资需求和项目储备仍然活跃，但交易节奏会受到估值和市场条件影响；

把这四家银行的表述综合起来就是：
1）消费支付仍增长，主要银行贷款仍扩张，实际信用损失没有普遍跳升，企业与机构融资活动持续。这些证据共同支持经济和金融活动具有韧性。

2）当前银行实际信用指标尚可，但管理层仍提示利率、能源和地缘风险。从传导机制看，高利率可能先影响项目估值、融资价格、成交意愿与再融资能力，之后才影响投资、就业和实际坏账。整体看下来韧性犹在。

四家财报共同描绘的，是一个消费和信用底盘仍有韧性、金融活动保持活跃，但融资成本约束仍然存在的美国经济。

今天还有美国银行、大摩等金融机构的财报，特别是美国银行的财政更值得关注下。

The AI infrastructure trade could be less about picking the winning model and more about owning what every model needs: power and memory

“I like power because you're going to need a bunch of power to basically run these data centers and cool them”

“I like memory because you're still need a lot of that to run, whether it's open source or closed source”

“I don't have to have a very precise opinion of where the token spend is going to happen”

“I just need to believe that there is going to continue to be a very persistent, durable demand for intelligence”

“Companies will want to have the best intelligence because the world only becomes more competitive from here”

“You can't afford not to spend in AI if you're a company of size”

@santiagoroel is drawn to the lower layers of the AI infrastructure stack, particularly power and memory.

Both are essential inputs across different AI models and architectures, giving investors exposure to the growth of AI without requiring a precise prediction about which model provider captures the most spending.

His thesis rests on the durability of demand for intelligence.

As AI agents become more capable, businesses face increasing pressure to improve their products, remove friction and adapt their business models.

For major technology companies, AI investment is becoming a competitive necessity. Falling behind could carry a much greater long-term cost than continuing to build the infrastructure needed to compete.

text:
OpenAI 刚帮科学家推翻了一个存在 59 年的核聚变数学猜想，Google 的 AI 就拿着这篇论文继续研究，几个小时又做出了新发现。

1967 年，物理学家 Harold Grad 提出一个猜想，认为在缺乏特定对称性的情况下，描述核聚变装置内部三维磁场的方程不存在光滑的精确解。这个问题困扰了物理学界整整 59 年。

直到今年 9 月，两篇独立论文找到了反例。其中，马里兰大学教授 Matt Landreman 借助 GPT-6 Astra Pro，发现了两类全新的解析解，推翻了这一猜想。

Google DeepMind 把 Landreman 的论文和其中尚未解决的问题交给了一组由 Gemini 4 Argon 驱动的 AI Agents，让它们继续寻找更一般的解。

论文原文写道：「Promising candidates appeared within hours.」

几个小时，AI 就找到了有希望的新解。

而且这次还突破了原有解的对称性限制，找到了两类更加一般化的三维磁场平衡解。研究团队随后独立重新推导、验证了这些结果，并在 10 月 5 日发表论文。

当然，这距离真正实现商业化核聚变还有很长的路。这些新解目前的重要价值，是帮助科学家检验仿星器的数值模拟程序。

但真正让我震撼的是这两次发现之间的关系。

GPT-6 Astra 帮助科学家推翻了一个延续 59 年的猜想，Gemini 4 Argon 随即读懂了这个成果，又沿着人类科学家提出的新问题继续推进。

以前一篇重要论文发表之后，其他研究者可能需要花几个月甚至几年，才能理解、验证，再找到下一步值得研究的问题。

现在，前一篇论文刚刚发表，就可以直接成为另一组 AI Agents 的研究起点。

科学研究的时间尺度，真的开始发生变化了。

quoted_text:
How many podcasts do you listen to when you hear leaders posturing without giving an opinion. Substance-less. So so many.

This episode with my friend @mcannonbrookes is anything but that.

- It is BS that agents will remove interfaces. Design becomes more important.
- Companies with their own models is BS. They are post-trained on Chinese models.
- The biggest enterprises in the world are fearful of Chinese models.
- Inference will get so much cheaper over time. It will be wild.

Mike does not hold back here and it was a joy. In a world of meh opinions and nuance, Mike was real and honest. My notes below.

1. Why Headless Is Brainless and Why You Have to Be Involved in the User Experience and Interface

Mike Cannon-Brookes stands by his line that "headless is brainless." Giving up on evolving the user interface and customer experience is a brainless bet, even as Atlassian invests heavily in MCP and CLIs so agents can read and write to its Teamwork graph.

2. Agents Will Not Remove All Interfaces. This Is What They Will Do

Horizontal agents, deep vertical agents and existing interfaces can all coexist. Agents in Claude, Codex, Cursor, Teams and Slack already use the Atlassian platform, and new Figma and Databricks features bring their tools inside it. Mike is a bear on the "magic button" thesis of one uber agent that does everything.

3. Are the Biggest Enterprises in the World Fearful of Using Chinese Models?

Some customers push back on Chinese models but not on open models, so Atlassian uses Nemotron, Mistral and other open models and no Chinese models in production. Mike notes many US models increasingly train on Chinese models without saying so.

4. The Companies Saying They've Built Their Own Models Are Bullsh*tting You

When a large company claims to have built its own model, it is usually a Chinese model, or occasionally Nemotron, with fine-tuning on top. Mike calls that BS, because tweaking a model is not training one from scratch.

5. Why Model Inference Will Get So Much Cheaper Over Time

The capital, startups and talent working on the price per watt performance of inference is enormous. New chips, better data center design and distillation will take years to come through, but Mike expects the price of LLM performance to fall at a precipitous rate.

6. What Seems Crazy but Will Be Incredibly Common in Five Years' Time?

People may stop knowing or caring which content AI has touched, much as moviegoers do not ask whether a film used CGI. Mike expects everyone to get used to possibly synthetic content, with artisanal work and human judgment standing out more.

text:
If you're building onchain: the best case scenario right now is that you are the most well-defended protocol in a high-risk environment. 

If we looked at security from the lens of public health, it ultimately asks how we make that environment less prone to recurring infection and spread. 

Clean air and water treatment does not eliminate the need for doctors but it does alot to reduce dependency. 

Onchain systems  need the same thing; resilience means being able to withstand attack without relying on flawless incident response every time. As tokenization and AI converge, it's obvious this will be invaluable.

this is our thesis at @phylaxsystems: preserve the need for well-designed protocols and incident responders, while strengthening the population against threats. solving this will create a wellspring that enables new primitives and market designs to take root.

will elaborate on this in a longer post about how it would work: policies ought to remain local, but the capacity to enforce them should sit atop shared infra.

text:
Introducing ThunderSync, a new approach to RL and OPD on long-horizon agentic tasks.

Post-training methods like GRPO and OPD on long-horizon tasks leave trainer engines idle during rollout, verification, and reward measurement.

To avoid this, asynchronous approaches overlap rollout and training across updates, but policy staleness reduces accuracy.

ThunderSync is a new method to squeeze out these bubbles in agentic post-training without policy staleness. For GRPO, we compute each trajectory’s score gradient as soon as its reward is ready, without waiting for the group. For OPD, we compute gradients for each turn as soon as the teacher scores it, without waiting for the full trajectory, so training overlaps with tool execution and later turns. We show that this is exactly the same update as batch-synchronous training.

The result is up to 1.9x faster RL while matching the performance of synchronous updates.

Paper: https://t.co/fGHRni8DLo
Code: https://t.co/Cw2tHM5xqy
Blog: https://t.co/GJibqSClMu
author: madhavjha
quoted_text:
Introducing ThunderSyncRL ⚡ It makes agentic RL up to 𝟭.𝟵× 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿 with 𝘇𝗲𝗿𝗼 𝗽𝗼𝗹𝗶𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗲𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀.

We observed that synchronous GRPO/OPD leaves learner GPUs idle for long stretches (𝟰𝟵.𝟱% of step time when training on SWE-smith). Asynchronous training avoids this, but it learns from 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗲 𝗽𝗼𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗲𝘀 and performs worse. Our goal was to keep GPUs maximally utilized while still doing strictly on-policy updates.

ThunderSyncRL streams gradients as soon as their inputs are ready, then takes one synchronous optimizer step. We prove the GRPO and OPD updates are identical to batch-synchronous training.

On SWE-bench Verified and Terminal Bench 4.0, it reaches Sync's pass@3 up to 𝟭.𝟵× 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿 and beats Async by up to 𝟮.𝟰𝟳 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘀 of pass@3 at the same GPU budget.

Grateful to my co-lead @hangoo_kang and to the amazing @Azaliamirh, who made this work possible.

And a big thank you to @TarunSures41845, Youngeun Kim, @sayshrey, and Seong Jae Hwang for building it with us. (1/7) 🧵
