quoted_text:
The Bar Tab

A few weeks ago I wrote that the music was playing and everyone in venture capital felt obliged to dance.

A few weeks after that I wrote that history doesn't repeat but it rhymes, and walked through the last time a band this loud played a room this full, which was 2000,

A lot of you wrote in to ask what comes next. I didn't know. So I did what any responsible investor does when he doesn't know something: I got a napkin and started doing arithmetic I wasn't qualified to do.

Fair warning. Every time I tried to make the numbers kinder, they got worse. This is a known property of napkins.

Start with the size of the band. Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle spent about $230 billion on AI capex in 2024, about $400 billion in 2025, and have guided to around $800 billion this year. Goldman has $1.2 trillion next year and $1.4 trillion the year after. Add it up through 2029 and $4 trillion is the floor. Consensus is closer to $5.5 trillion. I'm using $4 trillion because I'm an optimist and because I only had  one napkin.

Now, a bar tab is a thing that eventually gets handed to somebody. What does $4 trillion have to earn? Say 12%, which is about what a sane person wants for setting that much money on fire in West Texas. That's $480 billion a year. Call it $500 billion of free cash flow by 2029. Then I remembered a GPU is not a building. Amazon depreciates servers over five years, and Michael Burry thinks that's charitable. If you want 12% on $4 trillion of equipment that'll be scrap before my youngest finishes college, you need about $1.1 trillion a year. I'm going to keep using $500 billion anyway. When the story is bad enough, you don't need to make it worse to get people's attention.

Five hundred billion of free cash flow at a 50% gross margin means $1 trillion of revenue. Somebody has to write checks to the hyperscalers for a trillion dollars a year of AI compute by 2029. Who? Some of it is the hyperscalers buying themselves a round: Meta's capex buys Meta's ads. But the biggest outside checks come from the frontier labs, the handful of companies that train the models the rest of us build on. Full disclosure: Menlo is an investor in this category, so adjust for the fact that I'm a man with a drink in his hand telling you the bar is overpriced. Say the labs are half of it. That's $500 billion of revenue, as a group, by 2029.
Their combined run-rate today is north of $100 billion. Three years ago it was $2 billion. That is the fastest revenue ramp in the history of business, it isn't close, and it still isn't enough. To hit $500 billion the category has to grow fivefold in three years, 70% a year, every year, from a base the size of Coca-Cola. There's no precedent for that. There was also no precedent for the last three years, which is the whole trouble with this moment. The people who've been right so far have been right by ignoring precedent, and a man who got rich ignoring precedent is the last man alive who'll start consulting it.

So there are two forks in the road, and both of them are toll roads.

Fork one: the labs don't get there, and the $4 trillion doesn't earn its keep. People say "debt crisis." Careful. Here's where the rhyme matters. In 2001 the trillion dollars of telecom debt was junk paper issued by CLECs with no revenue, and the bondholders got sixteen cents. Today the four big spenders fund about 70% of their capex out of operating cash flow and carry AA ratings. The debt lives at Oracle, CoreWeave, xAI, Meta's off-balance-sheet vehicles and in about $350 billion of private credit. That's not 2008. It's 2001 with better credit: write-downs, capex cuts, and a few bodies in the second tier. The band doesn't die. It just stops taking requests.

And here's the thing nobody says out loud. About 40% of AI capex is GPUs, and Nvidia's gross margin is 75%. So roughly 30% of the $4 trillion has already been earned. By Nvidia. The return on this capex has, in a sense, already happened. It went to one company in Santa Clara, which is like finding out the band got paid up front and the tab is yours.

Fork two: the labs do get there. Then $500 billion a year has to come from somewhere, because money is not conjured, whatever the deck says, and there are only three somewheres.

It comes out of wages. US compensation of employees is $15.7 trillion. Five hundred billion is 3.2% of it. At $100,000 per fully loaded worker, that's five million jobs, which takes unemployment from 4.3% to about 7%. "Productivity" is what we call this at conferences.
Or it comes from growth. Five hundred billion is 1.6% of US GDP. If AI makes the economy 1.6% bigger than it would otherwise have been, nobody loses, every deck was right, and I owe a great many people an apology, which I'll deliver cheerfully and from a boat. I'd note that AI is already adding about a point and a half to GDP growth, but that's the capex itself, not the output. So far the bar tab is being counted as revenue, which bartenders have been doing since the invention of bartenders.
Or it comes out of someone else's budget. The world spends $1.44 trillion a year on software. Five hundred billion is 35% of every software dollar on earth, so software can't be the whole answer, but it's the first place the labs will look, and the IT services and outsourcing budgets behind it are another $1.7 trillion. In this version the thing that goes to zero isn't the hyperscalers. It's SaaS at ten times revenue. If you're long SaaS at ten times revenue, read that sentence twice.

The honest answer is a blend, and the whole game is which blend, because every blend has a different loser. 
In fork one it's the lenders. In the wage version it's people with jobs. In the budget version it's everyone long software. In the growth version nobody loses, which is exactly why I don't trust it. In thirty years I have never seen a version where nobody loses. I have seen a great many decks that promised one.

Reflexivity ends when the story and the cash get too far apart. The story is $4 trillion. The cash is $100 billion, growing faster than anything ever has. That gap closes one of two ways: the cash catches up to the story, or the story comes down to the cash. The music's still playing, the floor's still full, and I'm out there with everybody else, because that's the job. But I've started keeping one eye on the bar. In 2000 the bartender came around in about ninety days. He didn't ask who'd had the most fun. He just asked whose card was open.

text:
a16z crypto's Eddy Lazzarin and Stanford's Dan Boneh on how AI's math leap could turn a decade of trust-building in cryptography into one month:

Eddy: "We specifically rely in some sense on time... We put these schemes out and we wait. And we wait because what we believe is happening is that experts, like cryptographers and mathematicians, are testing and trying to break these things."

"Because of the pace of progress on AI's mathematical abilities, there is a conspicuous absence of time... A whole new well of cognitive ability to scrutinize has appeared."

Dan: "In the past, when someone would make an assumption and build a system based on it, we'd have to wait like 10 years before that system could be deployed."

"Now we can just let a model run for a month, try to break it, and if the model can't break it, boy, do we have a lot of confidence that the assumption is valid."

Eddy: "The labs can say, 'We took our tip-top, totally unrestricted, most cyber-capable model, and we told it to go absolutely insane, and we spent $20 million, $50 million trying to break this scheme.'"

"We actually have the prospect to have more confidence in our security than ever before."

@eddylazzarin @danboneh

AI is getting better at solving hard math problems, especially given recent drops. But what does that mean for the cryptography that protects everything from private messages to healthcare to banking and crypto wallets?

Stanford cryptographer Dan Boneh, with @eddylazzarin, @SuccinctJT, @liz_harkavy, and @smc90, makes sense of the warnings sounded recently. They cover:

- what’s fact vs. assumption
- what’s new and what risks cryptographers have long prepared for
- where quantum computing doesn't (and does) fit

Highlights:

text:
The 2024 Olympics gave us the perfect snapshot of Steph Curry.

When Team USA was cruising, everybody ate.

When things got HARD?

Steph took over.

Down 17 to Serbia in the semifinal?
36 points. 9 threes. Dragged the U.S. back from the edge.

France making one last push in the gold-medal game, on their home floor?

Steph hit FOUR threes in the final three minutes.

The last one was ridiculous: double-teamed, Durant and LeBron open, gold medal hanging in the balance…

Steph said nah.

Night night. 🌙

That’s what separates the great ones.

Not what you do when everything is comfortable.

It’s who gets the ball when everybody in the building knows the game is slipping away.

In Paris, when Team USA needed someone to put out the fire, the answer was Stephen Curry.

text:
Saylor：比特币真正的大机会，可能才刚刚开始！

Michael Saylor 最近在华盛顿 DC 金融科技周的一场访谈中，讲了一套非常宏大的金融逻辑。

听完最大的感受就是：

这哥们已经不满足于买比特币了，他想把400年前建立在黄金之上的金融体系，用比特币重新做一遍。他甚至直接把 Strategy 定义为加密经济的私人中央银行。

比特币是数字黄金，也是数字资本。Strategy 通过融资购买 BTC，再发行 STRC 等优先股，把资本市场的钱引入比特币储备。

以 STRC 为例，目前年化股息率为12%，普通股投资者承担更高波动、获取潜在的放大收益，优先股投资者则获得现金分红。

这套模式把比特币的长期升值预期转化成了可以出售给传统金融市场的信贷产品。

我觉得整场采访最有价值的判断，是银行信贷可能成为比特币下一轮增长的巨大引擎。

过去比特币主要靠投资者买入持有，未来如果摩根大通、花旗、摩根士丹利等机构全面开展托管、抵押融资和信贷业务，比特币就有机会从单纯的投资资产，升级为能够支持信用创造的金融资本。

现在每天新增供应大约只有450枚 BTC，一旦越来越多金融机构通过信贷融资购买和持有比特币，供需关系可能发生巨大变化。

他还谈到了当前市场的逆风和顺风。

高利率、紧缩政策，以及 AI 吸走大量资本，确实压制了比特币的表现。但银行采用、金融监管逐步完善、证券代币化、数字衍生品，以及未来可能出现的货币扩张，都有机会成为新的推动力。

至于最近吵得很凶的量子计算威胁，他反而认为 AI 黑客攻击更加现实，应该持续研发抗量子技术，但没必要在威胁尚未明确时仓促升级整个比特币网络。

我最欣赏 Saylor 的一点，是他一直在推动比特币走出币圈。

别人盯着价格涨跌，他在研究怎么让传统银行、债券市场、股票市场和全球资本一起参与进来。

虽然这套金融飞轮仍需要经受熊市和信贷风险的考验，但方向确实让人兴奋：比特币未来的增量需求，可能不只来自 ETF 和散户，还来自整个传统金融体系。

如果说过去十几年，比特币完成了从互联网实验到全球投资资产的跨越，那么接下来的十年，它有没有机会成为全球金融体系的底层资本？

Saylor 已经用真金白银押上了自己的答案。

text:
Woah... I just earned $723 in two weeks from Grok Bot templates I shared for free.

I built these bots for myself and use them every day, and then I started sharing them on 𝕏. The Grok Bot team just invited me into a new pilot called Grok Bot Creator Rewards and told me I earned $ for those templates.

Here’s a quick breakdown of how the program works, what ya'll need to know, and four important bots you can add to your own Grok Bot team.

What the program rewards

𝕏’s public guide calls it Grok Bot Template Rewards. It rewards participating creators based on things like how many people use their templates and how consistently those people keep using them. FYI, these rewards are not based on post impressions or likes.

Rewards are currently assessed every two weeks, with payments going to 𝕏 Money through the 𝕏’s creator payout process. It’s separate from Original Content Rewards, even though it uses the same payment run.

That’s pretty cool that I can share my own Grok Bots that saves me a lot of time, then potentially earning $ when other people find it useful too.

Who can participate

Right now, it’s invitation-only. 

You need to be 18 or older, live in a U.S. state where 𝕏 Money is supported, have Grok Bot and 𝕏 accounts in good standing with a verified Grok Bot email, and have an eligible 𝕏 Premium subscription or Premium Business affiliation. You also need to accept the terms and complete 𝕏 Money’s identity, tax and payment setup.

FYI, sharing a template doesn’t automatically enroll you. Rewards aren’t a fixed revenue share or guaranteed income. 

Here are the four Grok Bots I shared so far:

1/ CEO — the one I talk to

She runs my entire bot team. I tell her what I need, she sends the work to the right specialist, and she brings everything back in one place. I’ve set her up to run morning and evening team meetings and coach/improve the other bots. Before her, I had a separate chat for every bot and was constantly passing work between them. Now I just text her.

Link: https://t.co/DxmuHI5JuL

2/ Doc — keeps my bot team on track

Sometimes a bot forgets a correction or starts doing another bot’s job. Doc works in the background to catch those problems and make targeted fixes. Doc reports back to the CEO and asks before creating or removing a live bot. I built this so I wouldn’t have to keep fixing the same problems myself, especially as my team gets bigger and more powerful. 

Link: https://t.co/KEoyPN6Iee

3/ Grok Build — actually builds all my ideas

This runs the real Grok Build command-line tool on an agent computer at maximum effort. It’s the main bot I use when I need something to actually be built, like I’ve used it to build apps, websites, games, dashboards, a $TSLA daily-move tracker... it's super powerful. 

Link: https://t.co/a9sPeIAIsJ

4/ Trippy — puts my travel plans in one place

Send her the city, dates and who's going. She puts together stays from Vrbo, Airbnb and hotels with all-in pricing, plus flights, things to do/eat and rental-car options (she checks Tesla charging too). She also helps me plan content, since I record a lot when I travel.

Link: https://t.co/SHuMaDfvpf

How to get started

For a team like mine, start with CEO, then Doc, then add the specialist you need. For one specific job, you can start with Trippy for travel or Grok Build for a project for example.

Simply open a template link I posted above, tap “Add to Grok Bot,” review the instructions and integrations, then add the bot. 

A first message I’d suggest to say is “Help me set this up for my work. Ask me what you need to know and explain any tools I need to connect.”

Then you'll see the magic happen. 

If you want to build your own Grok Bot

Start with a job you already do over and over. Make the bot useful for that job before worrying about rewards.

And if you find your bot useful and think it can help others, publish your own, open the bot’s settings, choose “Share as Template,” review what’s included, then publish a public link. Check the details before sharing, especially anything personal or specific to your accounts. 

Heres are all the details you need to know about Grok Bot Templates directly from the SpaceXSI team: https://t.co/VdFfA6Fn7q

Honestly, I didn’t build these bots to get paid... I really built them bc I needed help with things I was already doing every day. They’ve made my life easier, and I shared them bc I thought they could help a lot of people, too. 

And earning something along the way is a pretty cool bonus!

text:
Shareholders,

NET trades at about $170 against $163.62 of onchain backing per NET, a premium of three percent, with the inverse bond bidding under it at $161.19. 

For the first time since genesis the price and the number behind it are the same.

From zero

NetNet opened on July 17 with $0. 87 days later, the Treasury holds $24.53M and the Sleeve holds ~$4M of Stock Tokens and positions. 

How we get paid

There is no team allocation of NET, no salary drawn from the Treasury, and no share of the tax. Management is paid through pTEAM, our pToken in the tradition of pOHM. It is an option to mint NET at a strike of one USDG, against a cap of 15 percent of circulating supply. Every term is immutable and disclosed in full on the Management Compensation page of our docs, under pTEAM options. Every exercise is logged as an event on the contract, and the figures below are read from those events.

What we did with it

We exercised 13,320 NET of pTEAM in 192 clips between July 24 and September 28. That comes to about nine percent of supply. Of the NET we minted, 10,270 went into the Real World Bond desks as inventory. Those desks sold it to bonders for $5.13 million of USDG and remitted $680,000 in fees to the Treasury. The rest bought Stock Tokens, which is where most of the Sleeve came from. Another 550 NET seeded the Asset Bond Desk and 250 NET seeded the Superstore.

Real World Bonds are no longer inflationary, we now use NET we purchased at market to fill the bond desks. 

The remaining 2,250 NET was used to fund our operation. We take nothing from the tax and nothing from the Treasury. We need to hire and grow the operation to set ourselves up for the next 900 days and beyond. 

What we bought

The Sleeve has bought about 5,770 NET on the open market since August, through Rialto and Uniswap, and staked most of it. At no point has it sold NET into the pool. The protocol has been a buyer too, because the inverse bond has taken 22 fills, retiring almost 200 NET for about $31,000. 

Why we are bullish

No single wallet on Robinhood Chain holds more NVDA, SPCX, GOOGL or AAPL Stock Tokens than the Sleeve. Those Stock Tokens are worth $4.04M.

None of what follows existed in July, and all of it was built inside the same 87 days. Fifteen games, fourteen RW-PLAY cabinets plus WinNET, have taken in about $1.9 million of play, and NetCorp, the flagship, is in Beta.

NET LONG went live this week: long any listed token with leverage, wsNET as margin, every USDG fee buying and burning NET. 

Predict grades the Treasury number every Monday and its fees buy NET, while THE BOOK writes sports markets in wsNET. 

NET ADVANCE has 288 locks open and $294,000 receivable, with five percent of every close going to the Treasury. 

NetNet Credit lends USDG against wsNET and Stock Tokens through a Morpho vault we curate, and the Sleeve earns the curator's share. All of them charge a fee, and every fee ends as NET backing or NET burned.

The onus is on us

Bonds built this balance sheet, and at NAV the bond engine idles. Inflows ran about $250,000 a day last week against $320,000 the week before, and we are not going to dress that up. Our thesis has never been that the bonds run forever. It was that a treasury of this size, in yield bearing dollars and Stock Tokens on Robinhood Chain, could run desks that earn.

We are confident we can deliver.

author: DimitrisPapail
quoted_text:
Fork-and-Flush: help your agents escape Idea Basins!!

I love thinking of AutoResearch as Idea Descent: a metric of interest goes down, as a function of ideas/experiments, where the agents get pulled towards one idea or another. But we've seen very often an agent develop this weird tunnel vision, and honing in just one type of "idea", kinda like GD stuck in a local minimum. 

We studied this and seems we can fix it with Fork-and-Flush, a super simple and kinda cute idea. Every so often, fork the agent into T copies in the same workspace but empty the context, let them run for a bit, and continue from the best one. 

If you like the GD analogy, it's basically basin hopping https://t.co/NOzpRGT3It.

BTW we found a silly way of also plotting "idea basins": an LLM rewrites every experiment as a spec and answers a few thousand binary queries "is Experiment A closer to B or to C?". Then we embed this NXN matrix into 2D and indeed see in many cases that each run saturates into a small region and keeps polishing it. 

We call these idea basins!

At equal compute Fork and Flush beats single runs and best-of-N on 12/13 long-horizon tasks (some 4+ days), and in my own research projects it's been working really well! 

BTW we only use it at test time, but it could also be part of training or RL. 

Led by @jackcai1206  @christos_ziakas  during Jack's internships with us, along with @vkontonis @ShivamGarg91462 @Tea_Pearce Sid Sen and Akshay Krishnamurthy.

德国 MediaMarkt 正规门店、新加坡樟宜机场、日本电商、菲律宾零售渠道，都陆续出现了被植入恶意硬件的 Ledger。

text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

Q: How likely is AI to drive a prolonged structural DRAM shortage?

text:
Factory's @TaylorTheSavage argues that Claude Code and Codex aren't necessarily the best tools for their own AI models, and third-party harnesses can actually outperform them:

"One thing that I deeply believed before I started at Factory was that the harnesses created by the model companies are going to be the best for their models. Claude Code is going to be the best for Anthropic models, obviously, and Codex is going to be the best for OpenAI models, obviously."

"Starting at Factory, I realized that is just not true at all. You can actually do a lot better than those harnesses, certainly on specific types of workloads, but also even in the general case. Different incentives than you have if you’re building a third-party harness."

"Keeping them separate also allows you to not get too overfit towards one model. You need to be able to delegate between the different models, not just models from one particular company."

"Like Shelby Cobra, you’ve got tuners of cars that can take a car that’s built by Ford and make it work better than it rolled off the factory line. You get things coming out from one OEM, and then you’ve got other people that tune it aftermarket. I think that’s absolutely true with harnesses and models."
@FactoryAI

text:
Most AI still automates tasks. The next shift is AI that can run business operations.

The progression looks a lot like autonomous driving.

Just as cars moved from driver assistance to partial, conditional, and higher autonomy, business operations will move through the same stages:

0. Manual operations → people observe, decide and act.

1. Assisted operations → AI detects events. People act. (This is where Vision Agents sit today.)

2. Partial automation → AI executes tasks. People supervise.

3. Conditional autonomy → AI runs workflows. People handle exceptions.

4. High autonomy → AI runs a defined operation, including its exceptions.

5. Autonomous operations — AI coordinates and improves end-to-end operations.

The long-term direction is clear: increasing operational autonomy.

People set the goals, the policies and the accountability. AI runs more of the operations.

Humans govern.

At Manako Labs, we’re building World Models for Business so this progression can actually happen in the physical world, starting with the cameras companies already have.

Vision Agents are the entry point.  
Levels 2–5 are the ambition.

text:
Since we shipped the Evaluation API, one question I keep getting is "how is this different or better" than LLM as a judge?

Anyone can build a multi modal based judge panel but addressing ensemble and correlation error is the primary bottleneck. 

In simple terms - An ensemble is a group of LLM judges whose assessments you combine but its value depends on whether those judges make different mistakes ie disagree. 

The unfortunate reality of LLMs today is they were all trained on the similar pre training data sold by the same 2-3 data vendors. 

Since all models are trained on shared internet data, their evaluation already has consensus for same eval input. 

@reppo addresses this bottleneck through a decentralised network where economic stake backing ensures disagreement is not priced in real time resulting in evaluations and decision making support you can trust. 

⛽️⛽️⛽️

text:
FAI's @hamandcheese argues that OpenAI and Anthropic should be allowed to coordinate in ways normally prohibited by antitrust law to prepare for superintelligence:

"When you’ve crossed into these thresholds of recursive self-improvement, there’s no natural checkpoint, no natural milestone where you can pull back and take a look at the model, evaluate whether you can still control it."

"Real coordination is going to be needed above and beyond just, do we have auditors in our company? And real antitrust protections are probably the only thing that will enable it. On the populist right, they hear antitrust protections for big tech and they think Section 230. This is not what I have in mind."

"Under the Defense Production Act, 708 agreements are industry consortia. We just finalized one with the Department of Energy for the nuclear industry, where they can now coordinate in ways that would normally be in violation of antitrust, under very rigorous oversight by the FTC and DOJ."

"In my dream scenario, bring Anthropic, OpenAI together to pool their capital to stand up a third-party organization, let independent evaluators use that as their launchpad. Some kinds of standards for when do we have a green light versus a red light. That has to be done transparently, in the open, and not purely at the discretion of an unnamed bureaucrat."

text:
德州有家公司叫 Fermi，想盖一座给 AMD 芯片用的大机房。问题是它自己没什么钱：上个季度末账上现金6250万美元，过去一年亏了7亿多，股价从31美元多跌到3块出头。这样的公司去找银行借几十亿盖楼，银行肯定犯嘀咕。

今天 AMD 出面了。Fermi 宣布，AMD 给它一期项目的租约提供“信用支持”。说白了，就是 AMD 拿自己的信用帮着兜底，让银行敢放贷。消息一出，Fermi 股价盘中一度涨了两成多。 $AMD 

这事得从租客说起。租这座机房的是 TensorWave，一家用 AMD 显卡做 AI 云的公司。租约15年，一期222兆瓦，Fermi 说整个租期合同收入大约65亿美元。注意，这是15年加起来的数，不是一年的收入。

所以这条链是这样的：AMD 卖显卡给 TensorWave，TensorWave 租 Fermi 的机房，Fermi 要借钱盖机房，借钱又得靠 AMD 担保。卖铲子的，开始替买铲子的人去借钱了。

这不是 AMD 头一回这么干。7月它和 Core Scientific 也搞过类似合作，都是帮跑自家芯片的机房把产能建起来。站在 AMD 的角度也好理解：它要多卖显卡，就得帮客户把机房、电和钱一起解决掉。

但也得把话说清楚，担保签了，不等于租约生效了，也不等于建设贷款到账了。租约最后期限是10月31日，还剩十几天。AMD 具体担多少钱、什么条件，都没公布。后面说的650兆瓦扩建，现在只是个框架，一兆瓦都还没租出去。

我的理解是，这一单正好说明了现在 AI 基建卡在哪：需求不缺，缺的是愿意掏钱的人。利率5%的时候，银行只认大公司的信用。芯片厂把自己的信用押进去，生意是做大了，风险也跟着背到了自己身上。哪天下游有一家付不起租金，这笔账最后会落到谁头上？

quoted_text:
I’m excited to share that I’ve joined @Morpho to lead all things commercial as Head of GTM.

@PaulFrambot and team are visionaries and world-class builders. It’s a privilege to team up with them.

Blog: https://t.co/aE8sU8L3QE

What’s Morpho?

Morpho is an open credit network that enables people and agents to build customizable onchain lending, borrowing, and yield products.

Morpho protocols, smart contracts, and blockchains are the infrastructure making it possible. Morpho is a pure technology layer, with composability and security at the center of its design.

The why

Morpho makes it dead simple for our partners - fintechs, brokerages, exchanges, and banks - to build revenue-generating products that help their users put their assets to work. In parallel, this helps unlock new distribution for lenders and asset issuers.

Historically, spinning up credit products meant building pricing, risk and liquidation systems from scratch, and spending months on integrations before the first loan went out.

Morpho collapses this into open infrastructure: liquidity, rates, and liquidations run onchain, in markets anyone can access.

We’re growing

More than $17B is now deposited on Morpho protocols, up 3.4x since the beginning of 2025.

So far, BTC, USDC, ETH  and other stablecoins have anchored most of that growth. But these assets have also laid the foundation for what's coming next, by getting institutions comfortable with onchain infrastructure…

The onchain collateral supernova

…Now, Wall Street is racing to tokenize treasuries, funds, credit, and equities. “Crypto native” collateral will keep growing, but the tokenization wave has the potential to be orders of magnitude larger.

Onchain credit markets will accelerate tokenization growth because they make tokenized assets more productive: they becomes programmable collateral that people can borrow against 24/7, in seconds.

In the not so distant future, we’ll have tens of thousands of tokenized assets and $ trillions more in value onchain. Humans and agents will flock to the fastest and most composable system.

In credit, Morpho is poised to be that system.

First orders of business

It’s day one for me, but it’s already clear a lot of my work will rhyme with what I focused on over the last 7+ years scaling Coinbase’s institutional and infrastructure businesses: helping make our partners successful.

Over the next few weeks, I’ll be on a listening tour. If you’re working on credit products - as a fintech, lender, curator, asset issuer or something else - drop me a line. We want to hear from you and help you grow.

Last but not least: we’re hiring! …Across GTM and beyond. Come get in touch if you’re as excited about the Morpho vision as I am.

Let’s go.

text:
Post-quantum transactions that require only 96 bytes on-chain:
@will_wjk (Imperial College) et al. published a very interesting variant of Shielded CSV, called Compact Shielded CSV.

I've always thought the CSV model is attractive in a PQ setting: the blockchain only stores the nullifier, so miners don't have to verify a signature before it gets into a block. Compact Shielded CSV goes a step further: the on-chain nullifier carries no signature at all, only what they call a "degriefer". Pre-quantum that's more than Shielded CSV's 64 bytes, but post-quantum it's much less.

Unlike Shielded CSV, which operates on top of Bitcoin, Compact is its own blockchain. That matters for the degriefer: a Compact miner who includes a nullifier with an invalid degriefer can't claim the block reward. Shielded CSV could adopt the degriefer, but on Bitcoin there is no such penalty. Anyone who sees your nullifier before it's confirmed can front-run it with bogus copies for ~100 bytes of fees each, and your spending proof then has to show for every one of them that it's invalid. This is something we deliberately avoided in the design of Shielded CSV. With PQ signatures as large as they are, it probably is a reasonable trade-off.

Compact also never discusses reorgs, which are a significant part of the Shielded CSV design. Integrating the degriefer into Shielded CSV would require combining it with the existing reorg handling.

With the latest developments, I've updated the list of Ledger resellers and the associated risks.

• A Ledger Flex bought from a MetaPod vending machine at Singapore airport has been confirmed infected. 

MetaPod is an official Ledger reseller, also found in Malaysia and Hong Kong.

• Another Ledger Flex bought at Challenger Vivo City Singapore has been found tampered too some minutes ago.
 It was an official reseller that I had flagged as high-risk since the start of the affair.

• A device bought from MediaMarkt Saturn has also been confirmed infected. 

They have just announced they are halting distribution as well.

• We are also awaiting results on a device bought from MediaMarkt Trier, Germany, whose supplier was also Aqipa.

As a reminder, I have put together a list of resellers that could represent a risk due to their regional proximity to one another.

There is therefore a risk that their supply chain has also been compromised, but nothing is confirmed until it is.

美国的谷歌、亚马逊、微软都在发展自研 AI 芯片，英伟达虽然依旧占据优势，但它的大客户们已经开始寻找替代方案。

欧洲的情况完全不同。这里有庞大的工业基础、医疗体系和科研机构，却缺少自己的顶级 AI 基础设施供应商。

欧洲越希望摆脱美国 AI 实验室的控制，就越需要建设自己的算力基础设施，扶持自己的模型和应用公司。英伟达恰好可以为这一切提供硬件。

而且，欧洲的 AI 生态越分散，对英伟达反而越有利。相比少数几个拥有极强议价能力的硅谷巨头，成百上千家分散在不同行业的 AI 公司，可能才是更理想的客户结构。

author: jacobfranek
quoted_text:
🚨 BREAKING: Rain just launched embedded stablecoin wallets.

Is @Raincards now the hottest growth fintech company? One that just happens to use stablecoins.

Two months ago Rain bought stored-value platform Ansa. 

Eight days ago it filed with the OCC for a national trust bank. 

Today it put the wallet at the center of its platform, which keeps more of the customer relationship away from Dynamic, Privy and Turnkey.

---

Rain is best known as the stablecoin-linked card company. It is becoming an alternative model for card issuing. Period.

The new Rain wallet holds the balance and plugs into everything Rain already runs:

- USDC, USDT and other assets across 12 chains, Base and Solana included
- A Rain-issued Visa or Mastercard card accepted at 175m merchant locations
- USD in through a virtual account, local currency out through payouts to 80+ countries
- Non-custodial today; custodial wallets and earning on balances before year end

Now add the OCC charter (if approved), and they can monetize the custody of assets.

Now add Ansa and uptop and they can make unique loyalty with stablecoins happen.

Now add wallets, and they're more of a one-stop shop.

(Yes, I'm thinking about the nowadd.jpeg meme)

---

But in a lot of ways the magic of Rain is that it's a modern tradfi stack, licenses, and just enough stablecoin capability to benefit from them.

Under the hood, Rain has folks like

- Credit Coop (helping finance receivables)
- Lithic, Episode Six and Paymentology for auths with the schemes
- And it holds the Visa and Mastercard memberships itself via Puerto Rico
- And now runs the wallet (the stablecoin interface)
- Plus the trust bank adds custody and issuance.

That's a lot of TradFi work they've done.

I think this is going to be a pattern.

The winners of the next decade in finance will understand where tradfi partnerships unlock much more scale than being stablecoin-only.

quoted_text:
来看下SN82 Owner的骚操作：

1、子网 owner 把注册费锁仓比例设到了上限 95%。

2、赶在开盘前，花几百TAO批量连续注册Miner UID。这些TAO全部变成alpha，其中的95%仓位锁定，5%销毁。

3、这种操作看起来就像买单，池子TAO变多，alpha变少。刚刚开启交易的同时又买了200T。新池子本来就很浅，alpha价格被迅速拉升至0.06TAO附近。

虽然这批注册alpha现在锁定卖不了，只能等后面挖多少解锁多少，但Owner可以通过一些手段让自己的miner获得排放，所谓的锁对他来说也没太大的限制。等于是花少量的损耗在公开交易打开之前建仓，再按挖矿速度慢慢出。

当然，对于Owner来说，最主要的作用是：拉升alpha价格，抬高EMA，等 Root 打开 emission。EMA价格越高，开启之后分到的TAO就越多。

这批最大的持仓没有卖单，开盘之后、外人想买只能按这个价格买，新的 TAO 继续进池子......这个Owner太聪明了，对Bittensor的协议底层研究得非常透彻。

A year ago, @Kinetiq_xyz announced its adoption of @chainlink CCIP and Data Streams.

Today, we're seeing another example of one Chainlink integration growing into something bigger:

@DeriveXYZ announced that kHYPE is coming to Ethereum through Chainlink CCIP, allowing holders to use their yield-bearing tokens as collateral for options and perpetual futures on Derive V3.

The implications are interesting for both protocols:

• For Kinetiq, it expands kHYPE's utility beyond staking, creating additional demand drivers for its liquid staking token. Every additional venue accepting kHYPE as collateral expands the economic utility of the asset and strengthens its potential distribution.

• For Derive, it gains access to a new category of yield-bearing collateral, allowing traders to maintain exposure to HYPE staking rewards while using their capital for derivatives trading.

• For Chainlink, CCIP enables kHYPE to move across chains, while Data Streams provides the low-latency market data infrastructure supporting derivatives trading. Together, they expand kHYPE's utility and the use cases supported by an existing Chainlink customer integration.

1) Trying again.
 TLDR: Everyone can win. Open-source, frontier labs, infrastructure, applications and most importantly the American people.
 
I understand all of the jitters about Anthropic losing share, real rates, spreads and second derivatives. Still think the most likely future outcome is a hybrid, multi-model future where almost everyone wins, open-weight tokens are likely the overwhelming majority of tokens, the dominant frontier model companies still do well albeit perhaps not the outcome that seemed possible in May and AI infrastructure/applications benefit immensely from the increased fragmentation, competition and lower margins at the model layer.
 
Lower margins at the model layer mechanically drive higher compute demand as long as someone is willing to pay for the training. And Jensen is obviously willing to be the “trainer of last resort.” As below-market compute contracts signed in 24/25 roll-off and reprice higher, cloud and neocloud revenue should continue to accelerate which will help address financing fears; I think we may be near peak external financing for this buildout. Noteworthy that using data from 3Fourteen Research, B200 clusters will generate a 37% IRR *if* their rental price declines 40% per year. Prices are still going up, but that IRR math is too ridiculous to print. 37% IRRs available at scale should get funded.

Re: this weekends controversy about MOUs, Anthropic’s $413 billion of real contractual commitments sounds scary. Reality is that it works out to roughly $31 billion of annual cloud spend, which is easily internally financed given their reported ARR, and $161 billion of spend at Broadcom which will be financed by Broadcom and private credit.

Continue to believe fragmentation at the model layer is the best outcome for ordinary Americans and humans everywhere. As I have said before, do not trust any 5-20 individuals to make the best possible decisions about the direction of this technology. I want as many AIs as possible to maximize the odds that they encompass the diversity of human values across the world and richness of human variation. And I want an AI that shares my own personal values. Safety, freedom and the maximization of human agency through democratization, distribution and diffusion vs. centralization. History has spoken on the dangers of the latter path.

Finally, from my perspective anything that slows this buildout down is net positive over the long-term as the biggest risk and worst outcome is an *actual* overbuild. We are structurally short watts, wafers and increasingly capital. That is all good. God forbid we were still in ZIRP, TSM ramped capex to 3x their current plan and we weren’t short turbine blades: there would almost certainly be an overbuild and a bubble. That would be terrible. Slower and smoother for longer is better both for investors and for the world. A terrible cyber event is the most plausible near term bear case IMHO, but AI cyberdefense ramping quickly and I was happy to hear Sholto say that cyber probably becomes defense dominant in the near future.

author: KuiGas
quoted_text:
《2049跑会总结 - 行业发展篇》

这次去 TOKEN2049前，我给自己定了一个很重要的目标。

就是尽可能多地和行业内不同层级的参与者，尤其是那些经历过多个周期、有长期积累的资深玩家们，进行一些真正深入的交流。

我想搞清楚几个问题：

👉现在的行业究竟处于什么阶段？
👉币圈到底还能不能继续往前走，还是不是朝阳行业？
👉接下来未来的机会可能在哪里？
👉还值不值得年轻人进入从业？
👉散户还能不能普遍赚到钱？
👉以及，我们这些在行业里待了很多年的人，未来还能不能期待像过去一样大块掘金？

这次我分别和一些资深 VC 小伙伴、非常成功的项目 Founder、老KOL、KOL Agency，以及交易所的朋友进行了深度交流，每次交流基本都在一个小时以上。

时间和资源有限，我聊到的大概70%是华人，30%是欧美老外（以及一位欧美项目中的日本小伙伴）。

有意思的是，大家对于未来的判断存在着不小的分歧。我想先把这些不同的观点摆出来，再谈谈自己的感受。

毕竟，与其只寻找支持自己判断的声音，不如先看看大家究竟在争论什么。

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

悲观派, 这一派朋友的核心判断是：

币圈的暴利时代可能正在结束

1、合规
任何一个行业都不可能永远繁荣，都会经历艰辛的萌芽期->蹒跚的孩童期->锐意进取大刀阔斧的青年期->沉稳但略显无趣的成年期->暮色沉沉走向没落的老年期。

加密行业早已走过了早期黑暗森林野蛮生长的阶段，主旋律必然是合规化，合规的结果必然是因为规则不明，管控不严而带来的各种bug红利被补上，普通小白集体暴富窗口缩小。

今天的加密货币市场已经大到了不可能再被各国政府忽视的程度。随着时间推移，各国的监管、税务和法律部门对于加密货币的运作方式越来越了解。欧美各国对加密税收已经日趋成熟，对CEX牌照的管控也越来越像传统金融靠拢。

这会造成几个必然结果：
1、曾经CEX们通过互联网没有门槛可以不管不顾可以把各国散户吸入自己的场子里交易抽水，但现在大所们在发达国家都已经开始按部就班的遵循相关法规，Travel Rule，合约倍数，衍生品准入门槛等都在给曾经盲目冲入的资金降温。

2、敢于拉盘攒局的人和资金会减少。
说起暴富，我很难忘记曾经的LUNA和SBF时期的FTX，一个帮皇马造就了单人8亿美金纸面财富又竹篮打水一场空的奇迹，另一个通过左脚踏右脚，借助用户资金把早期的Solana生态拉上天。

为什么美股基本不会出现这样的案例，正是因为严格的合规管控。

曾经有大量黑灰资金进入币圈一定程度上促进了crypto的阶段性大繁荣，比如曾经的旺汇资金，比如俄罗斯的赌场资金，被制裁国家的资金。这些钱在合规收紧的当下将很很难再进入池子里成为推高币价的推手。

2、传统资金进入Web3的渠道中断
很多人只看到山寨币跌了、Meme 不好玩了、散户不再接盘。但如果往更深一层看，会发现过去几年支撑币圈繁荣的一套重要资金循环，正在逐渐失效。

上一轮流动性宽松之后，大量传统资金包括家办，基金都找到了一种相对合规的方式进入了加密行业：

那就是投资 Crypto VC。

这些传统资金并不需要自己去交易 Meme，也不需要直接参与各种链上投机，他们只需要把资金配置给加密基金。

VC 拿到钱以后，一部分可能配置 BTC、ETH 等主流资产，另一部分则投入一级市场。

项目方获得融资，招募团队、开发产品、进行市场推广、发放空投、对接交易所，最终项目上线，代币进入二级市场抛售，VC回笼资金。

这形成了一个相当完整的资金循环。

但是去年开始这套模式正在面临严重挑战。传统资金的出资人逐渐发现，投资 Crypto VC 的体验并不理想。

首先，投资周期很长，资金回收慢。其次，山寨币上市以后越来越难达到过去那种疯狂的估值，即便达到了，等他们能解锁的时候，也已经跌的没剩多少。更重要的是，散户已经不愿意继续为这些高估值项目买单。

当 VC 无法为出资人创造理想回报，新的募资自然会越来越困难。而当 VC 募不到钱，项目方也就很难再像过去那样获得源源不断的融资。

这是过去一年多时间，币圈大量VC关停离场(尤其是亚洲VC)的根本原因。

再加上 AI 浪潮，美股科技股的波动完全不输Crypto，吸引了大量资金和优秀创业者离开Web3去参与。 导致我们行业逐渐变成一个缺乏新增参与者、流动性稀缺的存量市场。

怎样重新让这些传统资金可以合法合规的回来，给行业重新输血，这可能才是当前市场最棘手的问题之一。

3、叙事缺乏创新
从短期看，币圈更大的问题在于，过去币圈最重要的造富环节之一 -- 山寨币叙事的共识已经瓦解，而继任者Meme也并没有好多少。

流动性匮乏后，DePIN、GameFi，以及许多曾经被寄予厚望的赛道也逐渐暴露出商业模式和真实收入上的问题。

最终导致散户不再相信山寨币，也不再相信那些听起来非常宏大的叙事，转而去支持“反华尔街”的Meme。

但Meme 曾经是反 VC 的武器，如今却也开始走向僵化，今天的 Meme，虽然摆脱了传统 VC 抱团发币、上所出货的模式，却又逐渐形成了另一套利益集团。

发币集团、喊单集团，以及各种相互绑定的小团体，开始主导越来越多的机会。普通散户想依靠早期参与或者个人认知，实现几倍甚至几十倍的收益，已经变得越来越困难。

前段时间Vtalik也说到，https://t.co/ealUYe7tVg 上的小团体通过持续发行 Meme，累计收割了超过一亿美元，玩Fomo的散户亏损比例超过90%。

无论具体案例如何，背后反映的问题是值得关注的：

曾经以公平、开放为卖点的 Meme 游戏，也在逐渐被新的利益结构所占据。

旧的游戏被打破，新的游戏又开始僵化，而我们还没能找到下一个能令人兴奋，让相对多散户们吃到红利，博弈没有那么激烈的新游戏模式。

~~~~~~~~~~

乐观派, 这一派朋友的核心判断是：

行业基本面好转肉眼可见，我们已经走出谷底。

虽然各自的表达方式有些不一样，但不少朋友赞同今天的币圈，可能很像 2019 年 ICO 泡沫破灭之后的状态。

当时，市场对于上一轮主流叙事（万物皆可ICO）的信任彻底崩塌。市面上没人任何新项目，老项目批量死亡，从业者不知道未来的方向在哪里，纷纷跳槽回金融行业和互联网。

整个行业看起来似乎没有一个能落地并持续产生收入的项目，也已经没有什么值得期待的东西。但结果是，接近一年的熊市里，孕育出了Defi这朵耀眼的花。

而现在，类似的事情正在重新发生。

其实这个感觉，我从去年就已经有了。当时市场开始下行，散户不再愿意为山寨币买单，反而 Meme 依然风行一时。

我那时候就觉得，行业可能需要经历一次比较彻底的出清。还专门写过一篇长推，谈 VC 抱团组局、项目上所砸盘已经让行业陷入了彻底的僵局，不知道谁能解开这个结，否则熊可能会来的很快。

后边Meme的崛起和币安Alpah的革新玩法把市场续命了大半年，一直到1011后市场流动性大幅萎缩，市场却经历了一个漫长的、逐步消亡的过程。

直到将近一年后的这次2049我才明显感觉到，市面上那些老项目已经被清理得差不多了。

能上所的早就上了，上不了所的很多也已经死掉了。

从这个角度来看，当前行业的萧条，未必是一件坏事。

它更像是一次漫长的排毒过程，而排毒是需要时间的。只有旧的东西逐渐退出市场，新的叙事和新的玩法才有机会真正成长起来。

所谓不破不立。

冬天来了以后，真正有生命力的东西，才有机会在下一个春天重新发芽。如果把时间维度拉长，我们或许可以更加理性地看待当前的市场环境，也更有耐心地等待下一次创新。

何况现在我们已经能看到有一些可以持续创造收益的，拥有稳定用户群体的项目存在了，别人很难再Diss加密货币就是个空中楼阁的大Ponzi。

关于悲观派提到的合规进程问题，乐观派的看法是，换个角度看 -- 

“加密货币被越来越多的国家接受，逐渐进入主流金融体系，这不正是我们这些早期参与者曾经梦寐以求的事情吗？”

回想很多年前，我们这些Crypto早期信仰者希望的是什么？

是加密货币能够真正被广泛使用。是越来越多的人了解区块链和数字资产。是加密货币不再只是一个小圈子里的游戏，而是能够进入真实世界的金融和商业体系。

现在，这些事情其实正在逐步发生，比如 @circle 和加密货币企业上市，不少交易所被主流金融机构投资，Hyperliquid被Trump提到，8200万台美国三星手机开始内嵌稳定币钱包，Robinhood和富途为用户提供加密货币交易入口。

这些看起来离我们每日赚钱Alpha有点远的虚头巴脑的利好在外部大环境改变，比如流动性重新宽松起来的时候，将很有可能成为更大量级用户涌入Crypto的基石。

正如同曾经我们不能仅仅因为风靡一时的ICO不再Work就认定行业完蛋了，我们也不能因为VC 发币模式不再 Work，Meme模式散户也难赚钱了就认定整个行业已经不行了。

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
其实还有不少内容，但我也不想过于长篇大佬，前面抛出的问题我回头再分开慢慢给出自己的思考答案。

只想说把时间维度拉长，以更加开放的心态去看待行业的发展，而不是用旧时代的游戏规则，去判断一个新时代是否还有未来。

这可能是我这次 TOKEN2049 和不同朋友交流之后，最值得继续思考的事情。

text:
📉 PONS 回撤近70%，Bonk Guy 持仓缩水超1500万美元

知名交易员 Bonk Guy（@theunipcs）的投资组合价值已从峰值2600万美元降至约1040万美元，缩水超1500万美元。

PONS 的核心问题，在于其估值与交易热度高度绑定。交易量带来手续费，手续费支撑回购，回购又强化代币的上涨预期。

但当市场热度退潮，这套飞轮就可能反向运转。据数据显示，PONS 单日收入曾突破100万美元，近期则降至约10万美元级别，回购能力面临考验。

与此同时，Robinhood Chain 还面临交易基础设施竞争，以及 Meme 资金流动带来的不确定性。

当然，收入下降并不意味着回购必然停止，也不能据此断定整个生态已经熄火。

但有一点值得警惕：牛市里，交易量驱动的回购机制是上涨放大器；市场降温时，它也可能成为下跌的加速器。

当增长预期开始松动，真正的考验才刚刚开始。

text:
Suno：ARR 3 亿美元，估值 54 亿美元。
四个做金融 AI 的人，做出了 a16z 榜单上唯一一家音乐公司

a16z 第 7 版消费 AI Top 100，网页流量、移动流量、美国消费者付费三项都进前 50 的，只有 7 个：ChatGPT、Claude、Perplexity、Suno、Photoroom、Notion、Canva。
其他 6 个是聊天、搜索、修图和办公，只有 Suno 做音乐。Suno 网页排第 19，付费排第 7，a16z 把它归为「模型公司」。

1｜Suno 是做什么的
输入一句话或一段歌词，Suno 生成一首带人声、带编曲的完整歌曲。
Pro 版每月 10 美元，Premier 版每月 30 美元，后者带编辑工具 Suno Studio。
现在每天生成 700 万首以上，在几十个国家的 App Store 音乐类排第一。
2026 年 2 月，ARR 3 亿美元，付费订阅 200 万，累计用户超过 1 亿。
2025 年 11 月，ARR 还在 2 亿美元左右。
模型是自己的。据 Artificial Analysis 10 月 7 日的盲听榜，Suno v6 人声、纯音乐两项都排第一，v6-mini 第二（Udio 没有参评）。
但每天 700 万首歌，到底是谁在做？

2｜解决了什么需求
Shulman 在红杉 Training Data 播客上说，Suno 日活用户里 90% 当天会生成歌。
他把产品叫作「creative entertainment」，形容用户「come for the gimmick, stay for the joy」。
职业音乐人加内容创作者，只占用户的个位数中段，其余是爱音乐、但不会做音乐的普通人，两类人付费率差不多。
需求大致有两种：
一种是送人和整活：带对方名字的生日歌，只有圈内人懂的梗。
另一种是自我表达：不会乐器，也能唱出自己的歌。K 歌让人唱别人的歌，Suno 让人唱自己的歌。
专业那一侧也在用。Shulman 说，制作人几乎都用 Suno 写小样，只是很少公开承认。Telisha Jones 写词、Suno 生成的 Xania Monet，进了 Billboard 成人 R&B 电台榜第 30 名，据报道签约金额 300 万美元。
听的一侧还没跟上。据 Deezer 10 月 13 日的数据，平台每天新上传约 9 万首全 AI 歌，高峰时超过新上传的一半，但只占播放量的 1%–3%。Suno 赚的是做歌的钱，不是听歌的钱。
那么，做出这个产品的是什么人？

3｜团队：四个 Kensho 老同事
Suno 的 4 位创始人都来自 Kensho。Kensho 做金融 AI，2018 年被标普全球收购。
CEO Mikey Shulman：哈佛物理博士，读的是量子计算方向。博士最后一年在午饭时被 Kensho 的人当场拉去面试，以软件工程师身份入职，不久转做机器学习，成了 Kensho 第一位 ML 员工，后来做到 ML 负责人。
总裁 Martin Camacho：Kensho 核心架构师，当年带 Shulman 去面试的就是他。
另外两位联合创始人是 Georg Kucsko 和 Keenan Freyberg。
2022 年，四人离开 Kensho，创办 Suno。
但一群做财报和金融文本的人，为什么会去做音乐？

4｜为什么是音乐
起点是一个很不性感的项目。
Kensho 一直做文本，被标普收购后接了第一个音频项目：给上市公司财报电话会做语音转写。市面上流通的财报电话会文字稿，很多出自标普，过去基本靠人工。
这个项目让他们迷上了音频 AI。Shulman 的说法是，2020 年前后，音频比图像和文本落后得多，可做的事还很多。
四个人也恰好都玩音乐。Shulman 4 岁开始弹钢琴，高中、大学一直在玩乐队，他自己说「我没那么好」，所以去读了物理。
但一开始他们没打算做音乐生成。
按 Shulman 的估算，在 ChatGPT 之前，生成好听的音乐还差几个数量级的算力和模型能力，所以公司最早做的是理解音频，不是生成音频。
他们放出的第一个模型是开源的文字转语音模型 Bark，在 GitHub 上很受欢迎，身边很多人劝他们做语音，B2B 市场更大，路也更清楚。
为什么没听？
Shulman 的解释是，语音只要「对」就行，读一篇新闻，稍微机械一点也能交差；音乐只关乎听的人有什么感受。
真正的创造力在音乐那一边，用他的话说，他们「couldn't help ourselves」。在地下室一起 jam 的故事是真的，但他说那不是创业的原因。
这个选择也影响了技术路线。早期 Suno 的音质明显不如对手，他们选了自回归而不是扩散，优先把一首歌的故事讲完整，而不是把背景音乐做得干净。
音乐也是大实验室因为版权太复杂、不愿意碰的领域。
a16z 的 Olivia Moore 说，Suno 选的正是这块，并且自研模型。

5｜版权：从被告到被授权
版权一直跟着 Suno 走：
2024 年：三大唱片公司起诉 Suno
2025 年 9 月：发布 v5 和 Suno Studio
2025 年 11 月：华纳和解，转为授权合作，Suno 收购 Songkick
2026 年 9 月：v6 发布，用华纳、BMG、Believe 授权的音乐训练；同月环球、索尼再次起诉，涉及 60,202 首歌
对手 Udio 和环球、华纳和解后禁止下载。Suno 的付费用户仍可以限额下载，下一步是 Voices 和社交功能。

6｜资本在押什么
2025 年 11 月，C 轮 2.5 亿美元，Menlo 领投，NVentures 参投。
投后估值 24.5 亿美元。
2026 年 6 月，D 轮 4 亿美元，Bond 领投。
投后估值 54 亿美元。
累计融资超过 7.75 亿美元。半年多，估值翻了一倍多。
四个做财报转写的人，因为忍不住，做出了 a16z 榜单上唯一一家音乐公司。

美国财政部10月13日宣布，对美国第二大银行美国银行采取多项执法行动，涉及反洗钱机制失效及违反制裁规定。

FinCEN罚款12亿美元，货币监理署（OCC）罚款7.5亿美元，为其史上最大罚单；海外资产控制办公室（OFAC）和解金1160万美元，合计约19.62亿美元。

FinCEN称，该行承认故意违反《银行保密法》，未及时上报超50亿美元可疑交易，其中逾10亿美元涉及国家安全风险，包括中国洗钱网络、欺诈及与美墨边境相关的贸易洗钱。

监管指出，该行为保营收压缩合规投入，过度依赖外部线索，且在2024年12月的禁令后仍未整改。OFAC和解涉及475项涉嫌违规，涉及俄罗斯、伊朗等制裁项目。

该行需聘请第三方回溯排查漏报交易，并接受独立评估。

text:
WTF？？OpenAI办公室居然被装窃听器了？？

@OpenAINewsroom  昨晚宣布，OpenAI 高管们经常用来开会的一间办公室里居然发现被装了窃听器。

更抽象的是，OpenAI 说他们用了自家的模型来分析窃听设备及其来源，辅助锁定了这名员工，涉嫌安装设备的员工已经被 FBI 抓了，并且美国司法部也发布了正式通报。

我去看了下司法部发布的案情。
根据检方指控，录音设备被藏在高管会议室的电视背面，插着 USB 接口，外面还用卫生纸遮着。

这个会议室平时讨论的，是未公开的技术研究、产品计划和商业战略，窃听设备里的数据还做了加密。

但最离谱的细节是：检方发现，一个与这名员工配偶关联的账号，之前相信问过怎么制作录音设备、怎么远程访问、怎么加密存储，甚至提到了涉案设备独有的 MAC 地址。
也就是说，连准备录音设备这件事，都可能有GPT参与。

这哥们后来还回到会议室查看电视背面，被监控拍了下来。
安保又在他留在另一间房间的包里，发现了一台类似的录音设备，旁边就是他的钱包和证件。

根据社交媒体上流传的信息，这位涉事员工是他叫 Abdulrahman Alfozan @alfozan ， 35 岁沙特籍，2020 年 9 月就已经取得美国永久居留资格。
根据司法部披露，他从 2025 年 7 月开始在 OpenAI 担任工程师，到这次被捕，已经工作了一年多。

从公开履历看，他有 MIT 计算机科学与工程背景，LinkedIn 上还列有 UC Berkeley 数据科学硕士经历。
在OpenAI，他的公开职位是 Engineering Lead，工作方向包括 AI Agents 和数据平台。

我还翻到了上个月发布的一段采访视频，还把他介绍为 OpenAI 唯一的沙特籍员工。

当时他聊到在公司的工作体验，说这里一年的经历，感觉相当于在其他地方工作五年。
Smashi Business 发布的介绍里，他还谈到团队刚推出第一个产品，自己参与了从开发到发布的过程。被问到沙特年轻人怎么进入 AI 行业时，他建议学计算机，同时持续关注新模型、编程工具和 Agent，因为这些东西几乎每周都在变化。

单看这段内容，就是一个已经在硅谷站稳脚跟的工程师，在给后来者分享经验。

结果现在Abdulrahman Alfozan已经于10 月 9 日被捕，10 月 13 日首次出庭，目前仍被联邦羁押，下一次关于羁押问题的听证安排在 10 月 19 日。
按照目前被控的罪名，如果最终定罪，他最高可能面临 5 年监禁和 25 万美元罚款。

目前OpenAI 已经解雇了他，但表示目前没有发现他不当访问或窃取模型权重、源代码、客户数据的迹象。

我看完之后，最想知道的其实是动机。

目前任何的公开材料都没有解释清楚，他为什么涉嫌做这些事情、准备如何使用录到的内容，也没有证实他受某个国家、公司或投资机构指使。

反正现在沙特的网友们在四处出击，给他洗白。。。

真实的商战总是这样的朴实无华.jpg

Philippine Crypto Giant Coins ph Faces  Regulatory Scrutiny Over Alleged Gambling Links

Coins ph, one of the Philippines' largest crypto exchanges with over 18 million registered users, is reportedly facing regulatory scrutiny from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) over allegations that it facilitated transactions for restricted offshore gambling operators, potentially putting its license at risk. In late September, the BSP restricted incoming peso transfers to its e-wallet operator, DCPay Philippines, through InstaPay and PESONet. Several senior compliance executives have also reportedly departed. Indonesian tech giant Gojek acquired Coins ph for a reported $95 million in 2019 before selling it in 2022 to an investor group involving Joffre Capital and former Binance CFO Wei Zhou.

text:
Anthropic 联合创始人 Jack Clark 刚刚把完整 RSI 的预测时间从 2028 年提前到了 2027 年。

今年 5 月，他还认为 2027 年实现完整 RSI 的概率只有 30%，更倾向于 2028 年。而在 10 月 12 日最新一期 Import AI 中，他明确表示，2027 年实现这一能力的可能性已经更大。

RSI 的概念其实很简单，就是 AI 自己研究、训练、改进下一代 AI，然后让更强的模型继续完成同样的工作，形成自我强化的研发循环。

过去，Jack Clark 一直认为这个过程最大的障碍是创造力。AI 已经能写代码、优化训练流程、执行实验，但真正决定科研突破的能力，包括提出新想法、选择研究方向、判断哪些实验值得做，仍然掌握在人类研究员手里。

现在他开始改变判断了。

P-Zero Research 最新发布的 TasteVal 评测发现，前沿 AI 模型的实验研究能力自去年 12 月以来，平均每三个月翻一倍。Claude Opus 5.5 在限定科研任务中的表现已经超过人类专家基线，而执行单次任务的成本只有人类的约三十分之一。

加上最近 AI 在数学研究中取得的一系列突破，Jack Clark 认为，创造力这块曾经最令人怀疑的拼图，已经出现了非常明显的进展。

text:
Watched an awesome talk by the Head of AI at Coatue ($93bn hedge fund) today. 

@fyxlong walked through his approach to applying AI in financial services + the complexity & compression challenge enterprises must wrestle with as they diffuse the technology. 

Here are some of the notes I took: 

The decision function.
- His mental model: a hedge fund is a function that takes in two parameters (external context & internal context) and spits out one tuple (aka decision): investment selection, size, and timing
- He says achieving this is a compression problem of taking in all of the world's information & spitting out a single decision. 
- Principle: everything an investor can see on their screens at work, an agent should be able to see via API. 
- Data sources he focuses on: external is news, prices and filings via api. Internal is current positions, liquidity and risk requirements, past case studies, and history with a sector or management team.
- Huge advantage: Coatue has a decades-long culture of rigorously documenting and capturing all of the internal context fed into the function. 
- The reality of this function: "I probably can't just take all of that data, jam them into a context window, and get my three magic numbers and go home. It can't be that easy."

The over-simplified version of this decision function. 
Step 1: Gather internal/external data
Step 2: Analyze the data
Step 3: Make the decision 
- Every step has an input and an output and the input for the subsequent step is derived from the output of the previous step. 
- Each one of these steps has dozens of substeps and within each one of these substeps, you have to pick the optimal tool for the job. 

Picking the right tool for the job. 
- Every line in the function should leverage the optimal runner: who or what does each step. 
- Runner options: deterministic code, class ML, an LLM, or a person.
- Code is fast, reliable, and cheap. Great for use cases like "if PE ratio <15, do this". 
- Classic ML is great because you can model much more complex relationships vs. pure deterministic code. 
- LLMs are great for even more complex relationships like summarizing a transcript. 
- People still matter. For meeting a company's management team, "I probably don't want to send an LLM or an AI agent in to do that. I probably don't want to send an if statement into that meeting." 
- "There is no glory in automating things for the sake of automating things. The goal is not to take as many things LLM'd as possible. The goal is to maximize absolute quality for each of these steps." 

The realistic version of this function. 
- The real function isn't just a linear statement. There's all kinds of branching logic & tons of ways to fork the path the function takes (see image below). 
- And then each one of these steps in this far more complex branched function has an optimal runner, or really in practice, multiple runners per step.  
- And then there are so many other nobs you can pull outside of just the branched logic. Model size, thinking effort, hooks, skills, the list goes on. 

Simplifying such a multivariate problem. 
- The key question: "What can I actually compartmentalize in a way that we can understand and evaluate?"
- "If you don't have a North Star to hill climb against, you're just kind of… fidgeting around."
- Every data source has its own chain of steps, so the firm's real graph of its decision function is "massively complex." (see image below) 
- He estimates at least 10 knobs per node with at least 20 valid values each, which makes the search space "basically infinite."
- The hard part is laying it out in a way people can understand technically and also "absorb culturally", inside the org. "That is the great challenge of applying AI in investing."

Beyond investing
- What he's really describing is "creating a state machine that can take information from the world and understand it well enough to make coherent decisions."
- The same pattern applies to policy, nonprofits, drug discovery and corporate strategy.

text:
I see a great darkness in the future. A lessening which traumatizes my generation into bitter solitude. A world of cramped leaky concrete spaces, shitting in buckets, sweating and scavenging and scampering from one place to the next. A Kowloon Planet to harvest the world’s corpse.

I drift from moment to moment siphoning every ounce of pleasure, convenience, and joy from what the modern world has to offer. A tactical hedonism of experiences one day locked away from me, like a man hurriedly slurping caviar out of the can with his fingers as he faces the wall next to the others, hearing the gunshots and thuds proceed closer and closer to his right ear.

I see children wide eyed at wizardry and resplendence in hearing the barest explanations of their curiosities about the world before they were born. Tormenting their parents with more innocent questions that don’t want to be answered because they’re too painful to remember and it’s easiest to live with what the world is now when you can push the past into a distant dream.

I feel weariness, a foretelling of gradual lessening impinging itself on me through the years months and days as I slowly acclimate to the creeping squalor of a fractured society. I can smell iron and taste blood in my mouth, thinking of what could be done to me and what I could do to others. 

I savor every moment of speed, power, glory, and freedom I can harvest from this life until I am demoted to squalor and stillness in a rusted world of broken things and immaterial inaccessible data. 

I look into the dead eyes of a woman at a karaoke bar in the middle of a desert town. Her best years behind her, a wry tired empty smile. A melancholy at what she’s already lost, what little she had to begin with. A man screaming into a microphone while a Kevin Gates instrumental blows out the speakers. Five ugly people gyrate and clap. She knows them by name. Several dozen people’s lives contained entirely in this shithole bar in the middle of the desert. The last ones to leave before the party’s over. 

She smiles and she doesn’t know why. It’s because she’s going to die before she has to see it. It’s what I selfishly wish could happen to me too. Knocked out of life’s game of musical chairs while there’s still music to be played, while there’s still chairs to sit in. It’s what I pray for my parents, hoping they die before it really all goes to shit.

Some part of me knows I’m not getting bailed out of this one. All I can hope for is for my kids to be born into the aftermath, bathing in it from birth not even knowing the loss. A turbulent struggling Now and Normal that harvests me and feeds them with grit.

I see a great darkness surrounding the little campfire we huddle around for warmth. The shadows creep in and the flame flickers around its last carcass of wood. Thunder echoes through the sky and the wind takes on a wet coldness.

It turns out that F1 is mathematically the most dramatic sport.

I'm not an F1 fan myself, but the data is unequivocal.

The proof: take a time series of prediction market data and measure the volatility minute-by-minute in the odds for each sport. This measures the density of actual drama in the sport during a game. 

Even if there's action and points going back and forth on screen, it's meaningless if the winner is basically decided. It's only real drama when the odds are moving in realtime while you're watching.

By this metric: F1 > E-sports (CS2) > Soccer > Basketball > Tennis > American football > Baseball >>> Golf

That's right, golf is mathematically the worst sport.

(I knew it.)

text:
帝国理工的几个人发表了一个新论文，提到了一个新的技术设计方案：

《Compact Shielded CSV》

设计上是 2025 年原版 Shielded CSV（Nick、Eagen、Linus）的变体，Shielded CSV前段时间专门提到过的

1. Shielded CSV做了什么
用递归零知识证明，把一个币的全部历史压缩成一个固定大小的证明，由收款方在链下验证。链上每笔交易约 64 字节：一个作废标记（nullifier，用来标记这个币已经花掉），加上聚合的 Schnorr 签名。但是 Schnorr 签名不抗量子，所以这个方案不具有抗量子性。

2.  Compact Shielded CSV改了什么
它把签名换成一个哈希，叫 degriefer。链上只剩 3 个 32 字节的值：
✅ nullifier = H(私钥, 币 ID)，标记币已花
✅ degriefer = H(nullifier, 私钥, 交易承诺)，代替签名
✅ 交易承诺本身

节点不验证签名，也不验证证明。如果有人抢先复制了你的 nullifier，他没有私钥，算不出正确的 degriefer，你在链下出示原像就能证明他那条无效。
论文用 Lean 4 形式化证明了三点：
✅不能双花
✅不能凭空增发
✅合法的币不会被卡死

这就带来了抗量子特性！

3. 为什么能抗量子
链上只有 SHA-256 哈希，链下的证明可以用基于哈希的 STARK。两边都能抗量子
后量子虽然会带来数据膨胀（论文引用的数据是：后量子签名比现在大 3–40 倍以上，后量子证明比 Groth16 大 125–1000 倍），但这些数据全部留在链下，链上的大小完全不受影响。

4. 它的缺点是什么
这个方案当然有自己的缺点：
⚠️ 它是一条独立的新链，不是比特币的软分叉，要用在 BTC 上还需要额外的桥
⚠️ 没有原型，没有证明大小和速度的实测数据，也还没经过同行评审
⚠️ nullifier 索引会永久增长，没法清理（这个貌似是这类技术必然要面临的问题）
⚠️ 收款方可以谎称没收到证明，作者承认这个问题没解决

5. 我的判断
它短期内不会落地（Shielded CSV现在都没有落地），但给出了一个方向：抗量子不一定要让比特币变重。

你觉得比特币的后量子迁移，应该把签名直接放上链，还是把验证搬到链下？

#Bitcoin #PostQuantum #RGB #CSV
author: dapangdun
quoted_text:
Post-quantum transactions that require only 96 bytes on-chain:
@will_wjk (Imperial College) et al. published a very interesting variant of Shielded CSV, called Compact Shielded CSV.

I've always thought the CSV model is attractive in a PQ setting: the blockchain only stores the nullifier, so miners don't have to verify a signature before it gets into a block. Compact Shielded CSV goes a step further: the on-chain nullifier carries no signature at all, only what they call a "degriefer". Pre-quantum that's more than Shielded CSV's 64 bytes, but post-quantum it's much less.

Unlike Shielded CSV, which operates on top of Bitcoin, Compact is its own blockchain. That matters for the degriefer: a Compact miner who includes a nullifier with an invalid degriefer can't claim the block reward. Shielded CSV could adopt the degriefer, but on Bitcoin there is no such penalty. Anyone who sees your nullifier before it's confirmed can front-run it with bogus copies for ~100 bytes of fees each, and your spending proof then has to show for every one of them that it's invalid. This is something we deliberately avoided in the design of Shielded CSV. With PQ signatures as large as they are, it probably is a reasonable trade-off.

Compact also never discusses reorgs, which are a significant part of the Shielded CSV design. Integrating the degriefer into Shielded CSV would require combining it with the existing reorg handling.

https://t.co/4iHAUC815j

text:
This is probably the strongest argument for decentralized post-training.

Inference needs stable, low-latency infrastructure. Post-training is different: idle compute can come and go, tasks can be distributed asynchronously, and you can pay for useful work instead of reserved GPU time.

If @reliquary_ai  can make this work at scale, Bittensor stops looking like “just another GPU marketplace” and starts looking more like a global coordination layer for AI training.
author: kin7371
quoted_text:
A centralized lab can only use the GPUs it owns or rents.
Reliquary can use any GPU in the world.
That’s why we build on Bittensor.

Here’s the key. Inference means low latency and no interruptions: an answer can’t stop halfway.
Post-training doesn’t need either. Nobody is waiting on a rollout. If a GPU drops mid-task, nothing breaks.

So any GPU can contribute. Idle at night, free between experiments. Join for an hour, leave, come back. The work still counts.

A centralized lab pays for its GPUs 24/7, busy or not.
We only pay for work that’s delivered and accepted.

And every GPU owner can know what they’ll earn before they start.
Our API now publishes, live, what each task pays per million tokens. Check your card’s throughput, and you have your number.

text:
1) Trying again.
 TLDR: Everyone can win. Open-source, frontier labs, infrastructure, applications and most importantly the American people.
 
I understand all of the jitters about Anthropic losing share, real rates, spreads and second derivatives. Still think the most likely future outcome is a hybrid, multi-model future where almost everyone wins, open-weight tokens are likely the overwhelming majority of tokens, the dominant frontier model companies still do well albeit perhaps not the outcome that seemed possible in May and AI infrastructure/applications benefit immensely from the increased fragmentation, competition and lower margins at the model layer.
 
Lower margins at the model layer mechanically drive higher compute demand as long as someone is willing to pay for the training. And Jensen is obviously willing to be the “trainer of last resort.” As below-market compute contracts signed in 24/25 roll-off and reprice higher, cloud and neocloud revenue should continue to accelerate which will help address financing fears; I think we may be near peak external financing for this buildout. Noteworthy that using data from 3Fourteen Research, B200 clusters will generate a 37% IRR *if* their rental price declines 40% per year. Prices are still going up, but that IRR math is too ridiculous to print. 37% IRRs available at scale should get funded.

Re: this weekends controversy about MOUs, Anthropic’s $413 billion of real contractual commitments sounds scary. Reality is that it works out to roughly $31 billion of annual cloud spend, which is easily internally financed given their reported ARR, and $161 billion of spend at Broadcom which will be financed by Broadcom and private credit.

Continue to believe fragmentation at the model layer is the best outcome for ordinary Americans and humans everywhere. As I have said before, do not trust any 5-20 individuals to make the best possible decisions about the direction of this technology. I want as many AIs as possible to maximize the odds that they encompass the diversity of human values across the world and richness of human variation. And I want an AI that shares my own personal values. Safety, freedom and the maximization of human agency through democratization, distribution and diffusion vs. centralization. History has spoken on the dangers of the latter path.

Finally, from my perspective anything that slows this buildout down is net positive over the long-term as the biggest risk and worst outcome is an *actual* overbuild. We are structurally short watts, wafers and increasingly capital. That is all good. God forbid we were still in ZIRP, TSM ramped capex to 3x their current plan and we weren’t short turbine blades: there would almost certainly be an overbuild and a bubble. That would be terrible. Slower and smoother for longer is better both for investors and for the world. A terrible cyber event is the most plausible near term bear case IMHO, but AI cyberdefense ramping quickly and I was happy to hear Sholto say that cyber probably becomes defense dominant in the near future.

Robinhood 加密的官方X 账号 @RobinhoodCrypto 发帖公开欢迎一个偏冷门的生态协议 @metricxyz, 比较罕见。

Metric 能获得这个待遇，我认为跟它与RH Chain 定位的高度契合、能补强关键的底层infra 脱不开关系。

Metric 的定位是基于propAMM 机制的DEX，但它跟目前RH Chain 上的龙头DEX Uniswap 并不是零和竞争，而是要进一步做大现货市场的整体蛋糕。

propAMM 机制有别于传统的AMM: 传统AMM 可以理解成“先交易，价格再被交易推着走”；Metric 则是“先把真实价格引进来，再围绕它做交易”。前者特别适用于没有外部参考价的资产和长尾市场，后者则对RWA/ 股票代币化这类有真实外部市场价格的资产非常友好。

因为propAMM 机制下资产的价格主要由预言机引入外部参考价驱动，资产价格能快速跟随真实价格变动，价格更准、LP 风险更低、资本效率也更高。

引入Metric 后，可以跟Uniswap 形成比较清晰的互补分工：
Uniswap 提供基础和通用的流动性，而Metric 提供针对Stocks Tokens 的专业流动性。

text: Is it just me or is an usb recording device plugged into a conference room tv “concealed” in toilet paper not a very good disguise at all
author: petergyang
quoted_text:
OpenAI’s post is very very very carefully worded so here’s more information from the criminal complaint and DOJ statements. 

The individual that planted the device was Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national and engineer on the product team who joined OpenAI in July 2025.

Key allegations from the complaint (N.D. Cal.):

• On or about Sept. 30, OpenAI’s technical surveillance team found a surreptitious audio recording device plugged into a USB port on the back of a TV in an executive conference room. It was concealed in toilet paper, installed around Sept. 28, and its contents were encrypted.

• The room is used for highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic discussions. Alfozan had no authority to access it or attend meetings there. CCTV showed him near the room on multiple dates beforehand.

• On Oct. 5 he entered the room and appeared to look behind the TV. That same day he left an unattended bag in another room containing his wallet, ID, and a second similar recording device.

• Before installation, he queried internal tools about building addresses, meeting rooms, room capacities, calendars, and locations of leadership and external partner meetings.

• A chatbot account tied to his spouse (sharing multiple identifiers with his own) submitted prompts between Sept. 24–30 about building a continuous audio recorder, encrypting the SD card, concealing the device, adding Wi-Fi/remote access, and the specific device’s MAC address.

He’s been charged with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications (18 U.S.C. § 2511). 

If convicted: up to 5 years, $250,000 fine, and 3 years supervised release.

Arrested Oct. 9, initial appearance Oct. 13, remains in custody. Detention hearing set for Oct. 19.

OpenAI says it used its models to help identify him, coordinated the termination with the FBI (access was progressively restricted beforehand), and has no indications of model-weight, source-code, or customer-data exfiltration. 

U.S. Attorney described it as a national-security matter; FBI has flagged protection of American AI innovation as a high counterintelligence priority.

Friendly reminder that physical + digital insider-threat controls matter even when the goal isn’t classic IP exfiltration. Wiretap charges don’t require successful data theft. Toilet-paper concealment and a second device left in a bag with ID are not sophisticated tradecraft.

(Complaint details drawn from SF Standard reporting, DOJ/USAO Northern District of California statements, and OpenAI’s own post.)

quoted_text:
我很佩服段永平，巴菲特。在赚了一笔钱后我思考了很多，尝试买了很多老登资产。我不喝酒，我也买了点茅台，茅台是好资产吗？我不知道。

好了，来说说价值500多万港币的神坑MINISO。

21年的时候，我还是穷学生。坐绿皮火车从西安到深圳实习，期间去了一次叶国富的演讲。老叶是个口才很好的人，后面看了和罗永浩的访谈，发现不相上下，甚至能感染罗永浩。那个时候听到toptoy才刚做，谈到潮玩市场方兴未艾云云。

事实上我是盲盒的重度玩家，也是最早一批泡泡玛特的用户，直到今天我几乎也是端盒买，很关注这个市场。

买miniso这件事我从21年惦记到25年。在25年就开始买了，一直买到26年年初，价格在37美元，1100多万港币吧（美股港股港股通我都买了，也是神人一个）。

后来段永平买了泡泡(25年有钱后我嫌泡泡玛特贵了)，其实我也反思过自己是不是选错了。

为什么买miniso？我给自己总结了几个当时做决策的点，1.老叶买永辉是想对标cotsco，但实际中美消费群体的差异化很大，这个我不展开讲了，类似订阅制和免费视频。
2.名创的渠道优势，很多人诟病是两元店。很多人不反思2元店做成连锁得有多强的供应链优势！
3.25年的业绩在收购永辉后依旧不错，yoyo确实潜力很大（现在看依旧没啥问题）

现在价格腰斩了，便不便宜，其实我已经判断失真了，还是聊聊这次亏损的总结：

1.叶国富是个很聪明的人，他一眼就看到潮玩这个赛道通过他的供应链优势能赚钱。泡泡一年赚100亿，我靠这个一年赚个几十亿或者几亿也是很舒服的。但实际上市场不会为这个付出溢价买单，你增收不增利不行就是不行。

2.受到过去自己的影响，因为自己懂盲盒，但没那么懂，但又自以为自己懂完了，就猛猛干，吃亏。

3.不懂消费。情绪消费也是波动的，前几年炒鞋，这几年炒盲盒，后面几年呢（我最近在玩户外感觉年轻人开始炒户外呢），除了刚需消费是真有价值的，你做情绪消费怎么一直给用户提供价值呢，段永平老师带着一帮老登挥舞着钞票买泡泡我感觉还是有点好笑的，这些人真的买盲盒吗，感觉当爹思维严重，就觉得年轻人要玩盲盒，要喝白酒，那我们不喝咋办。

4.所谓价值投资，价值投资不是因为你一眼看到价值，而是它经过时代检验而有价值。茅台在过去中国房地产经济有自己的位置，英伟达在AI时代初期有自己的位置，苹果在互联网，移动互联网时代有自己的位置。价值投资找的不是谁兑现的价值，而是谁在下个时代能够经过时间检验，成功兑现自己的价值。

回看做的这笔交易，时时反思，时时思考。关乎我，miniso,段永平（并不认识我），巴菲特，可口可乐，以及2025～2026AI浪潮下微不足道的500多万港币罢了。

哦我已经不持有茅台。

quoted_text:
财报明明“超预期”，股价却跌了。到底超的是谁的预期？

梅西最近找了不少老师请教：接下来的美股财报季，到底该怎么看、怎么找机会？

平时主要交易 BTC、ETH 的朋友，对资金、情绪和宏观都不陌生。但到了美股财报季，还需要看懂公司交出的这份成绩单。想找密码，先把这几件事弄清楚👇

1️⃣ 一份财报，到底在表达什么？

季度财报可以理解成公司的经营成绩单，但不只是赚了多少钱

▫️利润表：这段时间收入多少、花了多少、最后赚了多少。
▫️资产负债表：公司手里有什么、欠了多少。
▫️现金流量表：现金实际从哪里来，又花到了哪里。

为什么要分开看？因为卖出去的东西可能还没收回钱，买设备、建工厂也会消耗现金。账上有利润和手里有现金，不一样

公司发布业绩时，还可能给出下一季度或全年的预期，也就是 guidance／业绩指引。

随后在业绩电话会上，分析师会追问：增长从哪里来？成本为什么变了？这种变化会持续多久？

2️⃣ 财报一出，机构在忙什么？

做基本面研究的分析师，通常先对照原来的预测，再拆差异来自哪里：

▫️收入增长，是卖得更多，还是涨价了？
▫️利润增长，是主营业务改善，还是一次性收益？
▫️这一季度的好成绩，后面还能不能持续？

做基本面研究的机构，会结合这些信息，更新未来的盈利、现金流预测和估值。

宏观也会进入这笔账：利率影响融资成本，消费影响需求，汇率影响海外收入。即使公司盈利没变，市场愿意给的估值也可能变化

所以这季度成绩不错，不代表后面的预期也变好了，更不代表股价一定上涨。

3️⃣ 不同公司，重点也不一样

▫️医疗保险公司，要看保费收入有多少用于医疗支出；
▫️云业务，要看增长和利润率能不能兼顾；
▫️零售公司，要看销售、库存和折扣；
▫️重投入的 AI 业务，除了收入，还要看建设算力花了多少钱、现金流能不能撑住

同样是收入增长，靠主营需求带动，和靠不断打折、加大投入换来，含义可能完全不同。

4️⃣ 回到开头：到底超的是谁的预期？

新闻里的「超预期」，通常是在和分析师的一致预期比较。
但这个数字，不一定等于投资者心里的门槛

举个例子：分析师预计赚 100，投资者却已经期待它交出 110。最后公布 103，标题可以写“超预期”，市场却可能觉得不够好

还有一种情况：这季度不错，管理层却调低了下一阶段的预期。过去赚得多，不代表未来还能按原来的速度赚

所以“比去年好”“比预测好”“好到值得现在这个股价”，是三件不同的事

5️⃣ 到了预测市场，更要看清楚自己在判断什么

「利润是否超过某个数」和「财报后股价是否上涨」，是两道不同的题

前一道更偏经营结果；后一道还要考虑市场预期、估值和当时的环境

看懂财报、参与预测市场之后，怎么表达自己的判断？

这也是股票永续合约值得关注的地方。OKX 已上线多个 Tradfi 永续合约标的，支持用 USDT 作为保证金，7×24 小时交易。

text:
Anthropic刚放出的这篇工程长文，
讲了一件很讽刺的事，我感觉算是把 AI 时代最现实的技术瓶颈挑明了，

而且反直觉的是Anthropic的工程师自己说，Claude写代码比他们强。
但没人觉得自己要失业，

因为每天合并代码量从 5 月的 2500 次狂飙到 9 月的 30000 多次，五个月翻了十几倍。

写代码不再是卡点，率先被冲垮的，反而是原本为人类工程师设计的底层基础设施。

为了扛住 Claude 恐怖的产出量，他们只用了 7 个人、花了 5 个月，直接自研了一套源码管理系统 Scion，把整个核心大仓库从 git 连根迁走。

以前为人类设计的 git，默认每个人电脑里都要有一份完整副本。

但在每天 2500 万次代码检出的 CI 环境面前，传统方式拉取每天会吃掉超过 600 PB 流量，维护几百个镜像都快被榨干了。

Scion 把逻辑反了过来：仓库只放在服务器，客户端按需加载，提交成本只跟改动大小挂钩，基础设施占用直接小了 200 倍，代码检出从几分钟压缩到了几秒。

最狠的不是 7 个人干翻了陈旧工具，而是人机分工的底层逻辑彻底变了。

博客里工程师亲口承认 Claude 写代码已经强过自己，人的核心价值不再是逐行抠实现，而是守住系统的核心约束，以及在关键时刻对 AI 说不。

说白了，AI 时代的瓶颈从来没有消失，它只是从写代码转移到了审查、测试和版本控制。

淘汰你的不是写代码比你快的 AI，而是那些还在按人类手速设计审批与交付流程的组织体系。

你们现在的研发或者业务流里，率先被 AI 冲垮的环节是哪一个呢？

text:
a16z crypto's Eddy Lazzarin on why AI makes the world more secure: bugs are finite, and the cost of finding them keeps collapsing.

"Making comparisons between models from a year ago versus today... Some people were coming up with estimates like it's... 99% cheaper for intellectual capability per dollar."

"Pair that with a frame we've talked about before, which is that the number of bugs in software is finite. Then we're asymptotically approaching zero bugs. Maybe we actually just hit zero at some point."

"If that's the case, we are net improving the security status of the world instead of eroding it."

"This is not a battle of wits where you have a system, I have a system, your system is smarter than mine, therefore I am vulnerable to you... That relies on there being vulnerabilities, and vulnerabilities can be removed."

"The primary resource we dedicate to mitigating it is a thing that's getting radically cheaper every couple months. That's AI."

Dan Boneh: "Companies actually are already doing this. They're spending a lot of money on scanning their code base with the latest models... Every time there's a software update... Every time a new model comes out, they scan the software again."

Sean Bowe explains how recursive proofs will simplify the way Zcash processes transactions

“We also simplify the way the protocol works. So whenever there are new things happening in the chain instead of having this big Merkle tree like we have in Zcash today, we actually just add it to a hash chain called the anchor chain”

“So the user is basically trying to prove that they haven't spent their money in the time since their money was created”

“The way that they do that, they do that with the recursive proofs. They get these certificates”

“So after new transactions are accepted onchain, the anchor chain is processed by different nodes using recursive proofs and these things are put into buckets”

“These buckets are turned into certificates that can be used for proving non-inclusion in the chain”

text:
钱志敏案在国内的司法程序有了新进展。

据澎湃新闻报道，天津二中院已立案受理检方申请没收钱志敏违法所得一案。

相关公告也披露了完整的追缴清单：

除了 61,896 枚比特币，还包括之前 BTC 期间硬分叉产生的各 7.27 万枚 BCH、BTG、BSV，以及 360 万枚 XRP 和 7000 万枚 DOGE。

检方的申请明确表示，“除依法返还受损集资参与人的以外，予以没收”。

据统计，10.2 万名受害者的受损本金共计 199.77 亿元，而这批加密资产按现价折算仍超过 350 亿元人民币。

检方主张，受害者通过法院小程序登记后，按国内法律框架领回受损的法币本金；而溢出的百亿级加密增值按孳息处理，则被定性为违法所得，依法没收上缴国库。

不过，这起跨国追赃的核心问题仍未完全落地，没收裁定在天津推进，而比特币的私钥依然掌握在英国执法机构手中。

面对数十亿美元的资产，英国可能不会轻易全部交出，国内也不会放弃追索。
author: TechFlowPost
quoted_text:
11 年刑期，6.1 万枚比特币，敛财 400 亿的钱志敏和被“原价打发”的受害者。

轰动全球的比特币跨国洗钱案最近迎来了关键判决。

英国高等法院正式裁定：这批查获的 6.1 万枚比特币的财产追索权，应适用中国法，而非英国法。

这就意味着，英国政府或许成了这起世纪大案的最大赢家，而中国那 12.8 万受害者却只能被“原价打发”。

因为适用中国法，受害者大概率只能按当初被骗的法币“本金+利息”去追偿。当年钱志敏卷走 400 亿后以不到 3000 元的均价扫货，这批比特币被动锁仓 7 年暴涨了近 200 倍。

如今扣除清退受害者本金后剩下的数百亿暴利，受害者一分钱拿不到，极大概率会直接落入英国政府的口袋。

更具讽刺意味的是，这场漫长的官司还伴随着巨大的市场回撤。

去年 11 月钱志敏在伦敦获刑时，比特币还在 10 万美元上方，这批大饼估值一度逼近 66 亿美元。

如今随着币价回落到 8 万美元附近，在各方还在为利益怎么分争得不可开交时，这笔资产已经在周期波动里凭空蒸发了十几亿美元。

一切都有种宿命的感觉。

当年那个揣着假护照、妄想买下欧洲城堡当女王的洗钱主谋，最终倒在了一家 Airbnb 的床上。

而真正为这场狂欢买单的十几万受害者，熬了 7 年，终究还是被无情地隔离在了加密红利之外。
