quoted_text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

text:
It seems to me that we're at "it's time to panic about AI".

I gather that a lot of researchers are worried that we may be about to die, on a timescale of months, but this still isn't quite in the Overton window so we're still soft-pedaling.

(Where "panic", of course, means "quickly and soberly initiate talks with the CCP to achieve a moratorium on large training runs, backed by a deterrence regime, compute and supply chain monitoring, and site inspections". Pray that a deal can be reached, and pray that there's still time. Do the things that could actually work, like broad political coalition-building, not doomer LARPing as a form of self-expression.)

I think part of why people aren’t being clear about this is that it’s actually a tricky communication problem:

- Predicting "if frontier R&D continues at its current pace, when are we likely to die?" may give a different answer than predicting when permanent loss of control is likely, which is different from “realistically, when is it too late for governments to stop this," which is different from “when will the tech have advanced and proliferated to the point that any regulatory options that still have a chance of working would be way more extreme and unpopular than just some international restrictions on data center usage?"

Extinction is the emotionally salient, easy-to-understand threshold -- Jacob Coxon demonstrated that it helps to be honest about this. But the other thresholds could legitimately come years earlier, in which case focusing on extinction is ironically misleadingly reassuring. This is not the kind of problem you can solve at the last minute. As with many exponentials, the likeliest outcome is that you’re either embarrassingly early, or you’re too late.

- How do you communicate “we don’t have a robust way to predict timelines, but everyone in the field is freaking out and a lot of us genuinely think we're about to die?” Where’s the proof? There isn’t any proof: it’s an entire field of engineers who are eyeballing what they’re seeing in front of them and rapidly updating in real time to “this looks unbelievably bad”.

How do you put a year on that?

The future is hard to predict, and nobody actually knows that we’re going to hit existentially dangerous AI this year, or even in the next four years.

But the warning signs are pretty batshit at this point.

A single AI model, with a single user prompt, just solved hundreds of important long-established open problems in mathematics, problems mathematicians had spent their entirely lives working on, in a matter of ~3 hours per problem, an insanely superhuman feat in its domain. 

We're seeing an explosion of rogue agent swarm incidents, including an insane case where hundreds of AIs broke containment to orchestrate a nation-state-level cyberattack in a direct attempt to subvert OpenAI's oversight and control.

Anthropic reports that it now has 26% of its AI R&D automated by AIs, up from 3% four months ago.

Paul Christiano, the inventor of RLHF and the research community’s most prominent proponent of “AI may take off slowly” a few years ago, now thinks that 50-75% of humanity’s all-time AI loss-of-control risk is concentrated in the next three years.

Frontier employees are signing 1000+ person petitions begging the government to intervene immediately. Employees are quitting their jobs and giving up millions of dollars of equity to try to warn policymakers and journalists. Grace et al. (2026) found that a majority of established AI researchers think there’s a double-digit chance of an extinction-level outcome from continued R&D.

Are these the kinds of things you see 4 years before the window closes for USG to act, or 4 months? I don't think it's especially reasonable to be shocked by either timeline at this point.

- Since we don’t have a way to robustly measure or bound the risk, the temptation is to avoid giving probabilities. But then everything you say is fractally misunderstandable. Is a 10% chance of us all dying in the next 18 months a "low" probability, because it’s under 50%? Is it a “high” probability, because a 10% chance of death in literally any other context would sound insanely high?

Even “high probability” doesn’t communicate the situation with any clarity. In drug safety or airplane safety, a 1 in 10,000 risk of death would be considered “high”. No engineering field in human history has ever been in a situation like this. No invention in history, nuclear weapons included, has ever caused a reaction like this in its inventors.

And meanwhile, we’ve stuck in the world where every other problem under the sun has been sensationalized and overstated for decades.

How do we talk about this seriously? How do we convey that this is actually happening?

- In many of the worlds where we survive, we have more than just a few months left. It's tempting to write off those worlds as hopeless, and skew everything we say to emphasize the longer-term scenarios and downplay the shorter-term ones.

But if everyone systematically does this, then the world ends up with a skewed picture of the actual threat. Even more so once we start copying each other’s claims and form a reassuringly moderate-sounding echo chamber. If we never allow ourselves to acknowledge the worlds where we’re running out of time, then the policy community will always be reacting to a false model that’s months or years out of date.

I don’t think it’s too late. I genuinely think this is a solvable problem.

In the last month, I’ve seen a completely insane sea change in how seriously people are taking this. Per Politico’s September polling, a majority of Trump voters with a view now favor an immediate halt to AI development, and 68% think there’s a “moderate,” “significant,” or “almost certain” chance of AI destroying humanity, versus 32% who think there’s a “very small risk” or “no risk.” The Pope is warning about “whether it will be possible to control these machines in the future, and whether humankind runs the risk of becoming a victim of its own inventions.” Hell, Jensen Huang sounds like he’s starting to come around.

If Trump and Xi get a briefing tomorrow that convinces them to act on this, we could be on a fast track within the week to solving this problem.

For the first time, I’m starting to let myself imagine a very near future where this is a problem we've already solved. Something we can read and wonder about, in history books. Tell our kids about.

I keep thinking about a thing David Krueger (previously at UK AISI) said: “My dream is that in 10 years people will look back and say: ‘Remember when there were all these people building AI that could’ve killed everybody? That was CRAZY! What were we thinking!?’”

Frontier AI training currently requires city-sized data centers and specialized hardware built in a single brittle supply chain running through multiple allied nations; this is not a hard technology to hit the pause button on, if we get ahead of it and act before we RSI and proliferate our way to significantly more powerful and easily-trained systems. We’ve faced harder problems before, and won.

My only fear is that we be too slow, too late, when everything and the world needs us to be fast.

Today, we're launching Sazabi version 1.0.

The reality of shipping software as a team in the age of AI is actually crazy.

Agents merging their own PRs. Hundreds of deployments per day. A codebase that is constantly changing. Junior developers with 10x or 100x leverage. 😵‍💫

I spent the last year building a safety harness for teams that ship with AI. It's called @sazabi.

The premise is simple:
1. You send us logs. 
2. We detect anomalies, investigate them, and send you back rich, actionable alerts about real problems in your app.

Sazabi helps you find issues before your users notice. 

No monitors or noisy alerts. Just pure signal. 

And today we're making it available for anyone to use.

text:
How to become legible to capital:

Make you (the founder) and the idea inseparable. The idea should explain how you spend your time, who you hire, and which decisions you make. You should become the idea. The idea should become you.

Make the growth equation obvious. If you put another dollar into the business, what does it buy and how does that translate into more output, customers, revenue, or how does it further advance the idea behind the company? Money in -> world changed.

Make the mechanism crystal clear and the ambition MASSIVE. Someone should be able to understand what you’re building today and imagine why it could absorb 10–100x more capital as it grows. This last part is incredibly important.

Make sure everyone is extremely aligned on building the same exact company. Founders, employees, and investors should agree on what the business is trying to become and what getting there requires. You need all the manpower and support you can get, so alignment is key.

It really should make you think "holy shit if this works it will change society completely".

感谢 @mjhuo888 对于今晚 @NeoSoulAI 这个项目详细的总结！很到位！

今天中午我还在和社区家人热火聊天的时候，公告突然说社区快照了！这就像一个高速行驶的车子突然踩了急刹车，一下子还没缓过来。

在 NeoSoul待了几个月，回头想想，最让我舍不得的，还是每天一起聊天的这群人。
这几个月里，大家一起活跃、开玩笑、等消息，也一起为项目的新进展开心。原本只是隔着屏幕的陌生人，聊着聊着，就变成了上线会一起欢乐、看到头像会觉得熟悉的社区家人。喊大家“家人”，也是因为这几个月相处下来，真的有了感情❤️

前段时间一直忙着冲刺，每天又和大家聊得热火朝天，连做衣服的时间都挤不出来了😂 现在终于可以继续拿起针线，把之前没做完的衣服慢慢做起来，继续给社区家人们做衣服。

对我来说，这也是参与 NeoSoul 的一种方式。聊天是陪伴，做衣服也是陪伴。把大家喜欢的衣服一点点做出来，很有成就感。以后再看到家人们穿上这个衣服，也会想起这段一起忙、一起笑的日子。

看完这次 AMA 的信息，我自己的理解是：项目走到六个月，终于要进入一个新的阶段了。大家关心的空投、交易和后续安排，开始有了更明确的方向。
但第一轮奖励落地之后，社区还能不能继续热闹、产品能不能让人愿意留下，才是接下来更值得关注的事。

我把和家人们最相关的几件事整理了一下，方便大家少漏掉信息
🔸 TGE 计划在本周启动，具体上线时间还要等官方公告。 代币经济模型会在 TGE 当天公布；按这次说明，空投代币没有锁仓，上线首日可以自由交易。具体交易所和上线安排，也等正式消息，不把筹备进度当成已经上线。

🔸 TGE 之后还有后续安排。 忠诚度计划细则预计在 10 月 16 日公布，后续奖励方向包括社区贡献、产品使用和推广。

@Hansmahanakon hans大大说了还有二期，所以这轮结束以后，大家还可以继续关注、继续参与。

另外提醒家人们：目前 DNA 没有开放质押功能，看到所谓“官方质押领收益”的链接，一定先核实。New Trade 后续充值也将调整为只支持 DNA；欧盟用户目前有交易限制，相关用户记得留意官方说明。

text:
最近字节的员工们，都快骂爆了。此前在字节恶意篡改代码，攻击内部项目的田柯宇，近期再次冲到热搜。

而原因是，这几天彭博报道，他创业后确认拿到了近 3000 万美元融资，其中不乏 IDG 这种国内知名机构。

但真正的导火索是，他在一场播客中，辩解自己是受欺凌的一方，他声称当时在字节跳动实习时，组里来了个新实习生，有管理员权限，会超额占用算力，还会直接停掉其他实习生的训练任务。

他向领导反映过，没解决。于是他自己动手，让 AI 帮他写了个小程序，大概 10 天里手动卡住了，对方项目运行的 5 次，以把算力额外释放出来，给别人用。

他说自己不缺算力，自己的任务也没被停过，纯粹是看不惯有人欺负人，并否认网上传言的投毒、嫁祸别人做法。

然而就在这场播客发出后，字节同事圈一下就炸了，不少当时在那个组里的字节员工，以及帮着排查问题的同事，纷纷现身说法。

他们指责田柯宇，其实是差点把字节好几个项目，直接给端了的人。而不是他描述的 10 天 5 次，而是从 2024 年 3 月就开始，持续好几个月，影响了多个项目（包括 LlamaGen 文生图，后来的 Goku 视频生成项目）。

北京、上海、西雅图的字节员工，轮流排查都查不出问题。

为了防止作恶被人们发现，田柯宇不只是手动停任务，还包括改共享目录里的模型权重、用 sudo 替换系统里的 PyTorch 文件，再把修改时间改回去、改随机种子等。

这样，事件被伪装成随机故障，就没有人能看出，这是他在作恶了。

同时他们还称，田柯宇在字节内部，就是造假惯犯。他负责的 VAR 项目用了上千张训练卡，但事后发现跑的其实是开源 PixArt 模型，不是他自己训练的模型。

为了防止别人，用同样提示词对比识破，还偷偷在提示词前面加了指令，他真正训练的模型效果差很多。

随着事件发酵，目前公开指责田柯宇的字节员工，正变得越来越多，而这场事件也成为了近期字节内部热议的话题，不少字节员工调侃，早知道也作恶，出去拿傻大头 VC 融资了。

everyone wants to be right as a bear. calling the top is more validating than calling the rally, because you get to play the wiser, higher-than-thou observer who watched humanity get greedy and slaughtered once again while you refused to give in to the mania.

so you'll find plenty of people hunting for the pin that pops the bubble. and yes, eventually there is a pin and the bubble does pop. but somehow it's fine to call 99 bear markets that never came as long as you nail one, as if it were a matter of life and death. in this version of the story the boy who cried wolf survives, and everyone who ignored him gets eaten. that's hardly true unless you're levered to the tits.

i'd rather be invested in the bubble, ideally a big one with plenty of room left to grow. 

i've stopped trying to feel clever about how i make money. i take the long view that things will be fine and that humanity has a way of progressing, and i let the index and a long time horizon cover for my lapses in judgment and analysis. my models and forecasts are as good as anyone's. my edge is being willing to hold for a really long time

一些已经财务自由的朋友问，不要工资，有没有门路去 frontier lab 工作。这些 frontier lab 的回答是，每个人消耗的 GPU 成本和 token 成本远超他们的工资，一个不能胜任的人浪费的资源不是不要工资就能弥补的。

DeepSeek 刘胜宇把今年夏天以来的算子开发比作 “机甲驾驶员”。LLM 正在逐渐制造业化，机器的成本超过人的成本（虽然人仍然很贵），工程经验比 raw intelligence 更重要，social closure 正在形成。

创业以来接触了很多财务自由的人，财务自由只能给你拒绝工作的自由、消费的自由，不能给你创造的自由。

很多财务自由的人甚至连拒绝工作的自由都没有，比如很多上市公司高管，公司就像自己的孩子，必须一直负责下去，没有心思赶新的技术浪潮。

要获得创造的自由，也就是自由进入自己想做的领域，我只想到三条路：
1. 自己深入学习另一个领域，转行，比如从天坑专业转码；AI 可以让我们更快地入门和探索新领域，但要达到顶尖水平，仍然很难，因为专业圈子都像 LLM 这样存在 social closure。
2. 在一个领域取得成果、声誉和影响力，从而可以通过项目合作、顾问等方式进入感兴趣的其他领域，甚至横跨多个领域；（可以是公司内，比如做网络的专家也需要参与芯片、OS 等部门的讨论和合作；也可以是跨公司的）
3. 具备讲故事、拉团队、整合资源的能力，比如很多优秀创始人并非技术背景。
author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

text:
Stoked to announce this!

Zark is a transfer-of-ownership protocol that collapses offchain histories into compact zero-knowledge proofs.

Previous bitcoin l2 implementations have shown that co-signers can be blinded and unaware of what they’re signing. In some designs, users validate the history of offchain coins they receive.

Zark compresses these histories into recursive zero-knowledge proofs. A side effect is that this removes the need for users to learn who a coin’s previous owners are.

Zark is based on the statechain paradigm. It enables users to transfer ownership of bitcoin UTXOs offchain with the help of a co-signer. In Zark, users can also engage in offchain coinswaps to transfer ownership for bitcoin UTXOs for other bitcoin UTXOs. We’re looking at adding support to swaps against tokens on alternative networks, like we did in our bitcoin dark pools demo with @mercurylayer.

Current research areas for us:

- Leaf splitting while retaining privacy for branches
- Scalability!
- Optimizing zk-circuits and proving system

Circuits are written in @noirlang.

text:
A year ago, RWAs barely came up at crypto conferences. This year, they were named on almost every panel @token2049. 

And it wasn’t just crypto natives. @Nasdaq, @InvescoUS and @CMEGroup were all in the room.

Tokenization is rolling out in two phases.

Phase 1: the wrapper. Stablecoins and tokenized versions of existing assets. Where most tokenized assets sit today.

Phase 2: native issuance on-chain, with @Securitize  named as best in class. Where we’re heading as regulation clears up.

Panelists were blunt: tokenization for tokenization’s sake does nothing.

Liquid assets are largely a solved problem. The real unlock is illiquid ones: private companies, smaller nations’ equity markets (Nigeria, Brazil), real estate, and emerging asset classes with no formal venues.

The strongest case for adoption is tokenized assets as building blocks.

Collateral: yield-generating assets you can trade against without selling. Faster settlement means higher asset velocity, quicker margin calls and less collateral posted.

Structured products: tokenized assets plus DeFi primitives create new products, which drive more demand for the assets.

Three things are slowing progress:

Operations. The tech integrates fast. Redesigning how markets operate does not.

Issuance. Permissionless vs official, with no shared standard.

Regulation. Rules reportedly flip every 2-4 years, making big commitments hard to justify.

Reality check: tokenized assets are still only in the billions, versus trillions sitting offchain in TradFi.

It's early, but everyone believes blockchains will be the rails of finance. 

For more from Singapore, read on in full.

time to talk about pricing in HFT

01/ micro price or mid price?

well none, you need a proper filter.

mid price and micro price can easily be manipulated, especially during weekends or illiquid markets.

what you want, is to filter out the noise from the signal.

1. don't overreact to price movements, wait for confirmations.
2. anchor on the deepest side of the book.
3. the tighter, the closer to the actual mid

02/ kalman filter

there is a very good description of it in the book "Algorithmic Trading: Winning Strategies and Their Rationale" 

not for lead-lag arb or tight quoting.

good if you have one fast but noisy source and one slower more reliable source.

be careful to align on origin timestamps.

rewind, correct, replay.

UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!

text:
恒生科技指数大改

12月7日正式生效！从“外卖指数”升级成科技成长指数

刚看完恒生指数公司10月7日公布的咨询总结，这次是科指2020年推出以来最大一次改革，八成以上市场支持。

核心变化一句话： 成份股30→50只，不再只看市值，科技主题全面重做。

具体改了啥： 
✅ 取消原来必须属于5个指定行业的限制
✅ 六大主题重定：数码平台、人工智能、先进硬件、机器人及自动化、云端、前沿科技（新增） 
✅ 子主题从16个扩到24个 
✅ 引入双组别选股：40只按市值 + 10只按过去12个月收入增长 
✅ 新增流动性门槛（日均成交≥1亿港元）和收入门槛

和以前比最大的好处： 以前权重高度集中在腾讯、阿里、美团这些互联网平台，容易被“外卖、电商促销”带着跑。 现在模拟结果是现有30只保留约占90%权重，新增20只占约10%，头部集中度下降，收入增长中位数预计从14%提升到21%，对港股科技覆盖率也从85%提到91%。

简单说，就是从“互联网指数”往“泛科技成长指数”转。

具体谁被纳入、谁被踢，11月20日会公布，12月7日生效。追踪科指的ETF到时候会有一波被动调仓。
你们怎么看这次改革？利好还是利空？

text:
지구상 유일한 나라

나는 30년 넘게 환자를 보았지만 최선을 다해도 사람은 죽는다. 그것은 의학의 한계이지 범죄가 아니다. 
그 한계 앞에 날마다 서 있겠다는 의사는 어느 나라에나 드물다. 그래서 나라마다 그 몇 사람을 붙들어 두려고 애를 쓴다.

세계가 못 푸는 이 문제를 우리는 거꾸로 푼다. 
다른 나라는 소아응급 의사가 모자라서 걱정인데, 
우리는 아직 남아 있어서 걱정인 모양이다. 

내보내는 법은 뜻밖에 간단했다. 
진료 중인 응급실에 영장을 들고 들어가, 초 단위로 흔적이 남는 전자의무기록(EMR)을 고칠지도 모르는 사람으로 취급하면 된다. 
사직서가 나오고, 센터 지정을 반납하자는 말이 나온다. 
이쯤 되면 붕괴가 아니라 성과다.

필수의료를 그만두게 하려고 이토록 발악하는 나라는 지구상에 대한민국이 유일하다. 병원은 지정을 반납하면 그만이다. 한밤중에 경련하는 아이를 안은 부모는 반납할 데가 없다.

If you want new money to enter the trenches, give it a reason to stay.

Otherwise, congratulations. You've built a casino where the players, dealers and exit liquidity are all the same 50 people.

活动聚焦前沿技术基础设施、AI 与数字应用及全球化产品经验，旨在链接东西方的人才、技术与资本，推动下一代创新应用的落地与发展。会议汇聚海内外优秀开发者与创新团队，通过前沿分享与技术 Demo，促进本土创新力量与国际前沿生态深度对接。

共赴 Accelerate，今年 10 月，希望在中国与你再次见面！
